# The complete three-below family, including triple intersections

## T-051. Positive formulas for every possible power

Let \(k\ge2\), \(x,b,d\ge0\), and \(2b+x+k\ge9\). Put
\[
n=d+b+x+k-3,\qquad
\lambda=(d+3b+2x+3k-12,d+b+x+2k-3,d+b+x,d+x,d).
\tag{ET.1}
\]
Every coefficient \(p_{\mu,(n)}^\lambda\), \(\mu\vdash5\),
has the explicit positive formula in §4. It uses at most 55 bounded
integer polytopes of at most ten variables after selecting its
branch and residues. The new endpoints \(2\le k\le7\) use at
most seventeen polytopes of eight variables, or four of five
variables on branches with fixed \(b\).

The proof evaluates the entire exact arrangement restriction
complex. Three small endpoint sectors have a nonzero triple term;
their actual representations and quotient maps are retained rather
than omitted. The positive formula for \(k\ge8\) is T-048.
No historical novelty claim is made.

## 1. Actual jet comparison and the exact pair-to-triple sequence

Write \(a=b+x\), \(c=2k-3\), and
\(\alpha=(a+c,b+c,c)\). Then
\[
|\alpha|=2b+x+6k-9\ge5k.
\tag{ET.2}
\]
G-027 therefore gives its exact degree-\(|\alpha|\) restriction
complex. The determinant shift is
\[
S_\alpha Q=(\det E)^c\mathcal O(c)S_{(a,b)}Q
=\operatorname{sgn}_5\,\mathcal O(c)S_{(a,b)}Q,
\tag{ET.3}
\]
since \(c\) is odd. Also \(c\ge k-1\). The explicit
triangular jet-surjection proof in T-050 §1 consequently applies:
multiply scalar degree-\(c\) sections with arbitrary leading jets
through order \(k-1\) by global sections generating
\(S_{(a,b)}Q\), and prescribe the homogeneous jet layers in
order. Hence the singleton quotient in the arrangement complex is
the entire point-jet module, by the natural restriction map.

Since \(S_\alpha Q\) is acyclic in positive degrees, the same
cokernel comparison as (ER.8) gives the actual exact sequence
\[
0\longrightarrow H^1(\mathcal I^k(c)S_{(a,b)}Q)
\longrightarrow K_2\longrightarrow K_3\longrightarrow0,
\qquad H^{q\ge2}(\mathcal I^k(c)S_{(a,b)}Q)=0.
\tag{ET.4}
\]
Here \(K_s\) is the \(s\)-subset term of G-027, including its
orientation, and then tensored by \(\operatorname{sgn}_5\)
to undo (ET.3). The map \(K_2\to K_3\) is the signed
polynomial quotient map of that complex followed by the specified
Schur-component identifications. This defines every map in (ET.4).

The balanced flag map still has the original sign
\[
(S_\lambda\mathbf Q^5)_{(n^5)}
\simeq\operatorname{sgn}^{d+a}
H^0(\mathcal I^k(c)S_{(a,b)}Q).
\tag{ET.5}
\]
Indeed \(\lambda_2=d+a+c\), and the sign from (ET.3) cancels
its odd \(c\). The chart inverse and normal-order comparison
are the actual ones of G-027, with \(\lambda_2-n=k\).

## 2. The pair term in every power

For a pair, put \(P=\mathbf Q^2\), with the endpoint permutation
action, and \(W=\mathfrak h_3\) for its complement. The exact
pair module, after the sign in (ET.3), is
\[
\begin{split}
K_2\simeq\operatorname{Ind}_{S_2\times S_3}^{S_5}\bigl(
&\det P\otimes P\otimes S_{(a,b)}W\\
&\oplus\det P\otimes W^*\otimes S_{(a,b)}W\\
&\oplus S_{(a-1,b)}W\oplus S_{(a,b-1)}W\bigr).
\end{split}
\tag{ET.6}
\]
The third summand is omitted at \(x=0\), and the fourth at
\(b=0\). This is the already evaluated four-summand module of
T-047 at defect three, now obtained directly for every \(k\ge2\).

Here is the complete two-slot calculation establishing (ET.6).
The truncated slots have total degree at most \(2k-2=c+1\).
The complementary Cauchy partition has at most two rows, so those
slots must supply the third row of length \(c\). There are only
two degrees to examine.

At degree \(c\), the slot degrees are
\((k-1,k-2)\) or \((k-2,k-1)\). Multiplication onto
\(\operatorname{Sym}^cF\) and the determinant polynomial map
used in (ER.7) identify their contribution with
\(P\otimes S_{(a,b)}W\) after orientation and (ET.3).
The standard intertwiner
\[
v_1e_1+v_2e_2\longmapsto
(e_1\wedge e_2)\otimes(v_1e_2-v_2e_1)
\tag{ET.7}
\]
identifies this with \(\det P\otimes P\otimes S_{(a,b)}W\).

At degree \(c+1\), both slots have degree \(k-1\). Only the
two Schur types \((c+1)\) and \((c,1)\) can contribute.
Their slot-exchange signs are respectively plus and minus: their
highest polynomials are
\(u_1^{k-1}v_1^{k-1}\) and
\((u_1v_2-u_2v_1)u_1^{k-2}v_1^{k-2}\).
Remove one further box from either of the first two rows of
\(\alpha\). If \(x>0\), removing the end of its first row
leaves a skew row of length \(c\) and one box in a different
column, so both types occur once. If \(b>0\), the same holds
when removing the end of its second row. If \(b=0\), that
second-row box shares the last column of the third row, so only
\((c,1)\) occurs. At \(x=0\), first-row removal is not a
partition and contributes nothing. These are all cases.

The maps are the corresponding row symmetrizers and column
antisymmetrizers, fixed by the displayed highest coefficients,
followed by Cauchy extraction. Equivalently, use the explicit
rank-two dual Pieri decomposition of
\(W^*\otimes S_{(a,b)}W\). For \(b\ge1\), its summands
are \(S_{(a-1,b)}W\) when \(x>0\), and
\(S_{(a,b-1)}W\). At \(b=0\), its second summand is the
actual rational representation
\((\det W)^{-1}\operatorname{Sym}^{a+1}W\), and its first
is present precisely when \(a>0\). The multiplication and
determinant highest-vector maps for this rank-two decomposition
are those fully proved in T-047. Keeping this second summand at
\(b=0\), and using the two slot-exchange signs just computed,
gives exactly the last three terms of (ET.6). This proves the
formula also at \(x=0\), \(b=0\) and \(k=2\).

## 3. Every triple term and its exact action

For three selected slots, the complementary standard space is the
one-dimensional sign representation of \(S_2\). A complementary
Cauchy partition has one row. The truncated factor must therefore
supply at least
\(\alpha_2+\alpha_3=b+4k-6\) boxes, and can supply at most
\(3(k-1)\). Thus
\[
K_3=0\qquad\text{whenever }b+k\ge4.
\tag{ET.8}
\]
The remaining possibilities are precisely \((k,b)=(3,0),(2,1)\)
and \((2,0)\). In the following formulas the second subgroup is
the two-letter complement:
\[
\boxed{
K_3=\begin{cases}
\operatorname{Ind}_{S_3\times S_2}^{S_5}
(\operatorname{sgn}_3\otimes\operatorname{sgn}_2^x),&(k,b)=(3,0),\\
\operatorname{Ind}_{S_3\times S_2}^{S_5}
([2,1]\otimes\operatorname{sgn}_2^{x+1}),&(k,b)=(2,1),\\
\operatorname{Ind}_{S_3\times S_2}^{S_5}
(([2,1]\oplus\operatorname{sgn}_3)\otimes
 (\mathbf1\oplus\operatorname{sgn}_2)),&(k,b)=(2,0).
\end{cases}}
\tag{ET.9}
\]

For \((3,0)\), the only normal degree is six: each slot has
degree two and the required normal Schur type is \((3,3)\).
Its multiplicity is one. Indeed, among the shapes in
\(S_{(2)}F\otimes S_{(2)}F\), only \((3,1)\) can acquire
a horizontal two-strip to give \((3,3)\). Its actual highest
vector in three slot rows is the product of brackets
\([uv][uw][vw]\), using the first two column coordinates.
It has degree two in each row and changes by the sign of a row
permutation. The complementary row has degree \(x+3\).
The \(S_3\) orientation and the \(S_3\) part of (ET.3)
cancel; the complementary sign becomes
\((-1)^{x+3+1}=(-1)^x\). This proves the first line of
(ET.9), with its concrete highest-vector map.

For \((2,1)\), every selected slot has degree one. The lower
two rows of \(\alpha=(x+2,2,1)\) force the normal Schur
type \((2,1)\), whose multiplicity in \(F^{\otimes3}\)
is the literal Specht module \([2,1]\) under the Young
projector. The complementary row has degree \(x+2\), giving
the sign \((-1)^{x+3}\) after (ET.3). The two \(S_3\)
signs again cancel, proving the second line.

For \((2,0)\), normal degrees two and three both occur.
At degree two, choose two nonempty slots and extract
\(\Lambda^2F\). Their action is
\(\operatorname{Ind}_{S_2}^{S_3}\operatorname{sgn}_2
=[2,1]\oplus\operatorname{sgn}_3\), and the complementary
row has degree \(x+1\). At degree three, the skew diagram
\((x+1,1,1)/(x)\) has Schur types \((2,1)\) and
\((1,1,1)\), each once; the actual maps are their Young
symmetrizer projections on \(F^{\otimes3}\). The same
two multiplicity modules occur, while the complementary row has
degree \(x\). Validity here gives \(x\ge7\), so neither
skew-diagram boundary is exceptional. After orientation and (ET.3),
the two complementary signs are \((-1)^x\) and
\((-1)^{x+1}\). Their sum is the fixed two-letter permutation
module, proving the last line of (ET.9).

These arguments define the triple identifications by polynomial
highest vectors and the specified rational Young projectors.
The map in (ET.4) remains the actual signed quotient map, not an
unspecified map between equal-dimensional representations.

In the fixed seven-class order, the triple traces are respectively
\[
\begin{aligned}
Q^{30}(x)&=(10,-3+(-1)^x,-2(-1)^x,1,(-1)^x,0,0),\\
Q^{21}(x)&=(20,2(-1)^{x+1},0,-1,(-1)^x,0,0),\\
Q^{20}&=(60,-6,0,0,0,0,0).
\end{aligned}
\tag{ET.10}
\]
They can be checked directly by summing fixed two-letter
complements: a fixed pair of letters or a two-cycle, with the
literal sign or standard character on the remaining three letters.

## 4. Complete positive endpoint certificates

Let \(P_g(x,b,k;c)\) be the explicit three-term Euler expression
(ER.9), with \(c=2k-3\). Let \(J_g^{(3)}(x,b)\) be the
four-summand pair traces (F.6)–(F.7), and let \(Q_g(x,b,k)\)
be (ET.10) on its three sectors and zero elsewhere. Exactness of
(ET.4) proves the actual zeroth-cohomology trace
\[
P_g(x,b,k;2k-3)+J_g^{(3)}(x,b)-Q_g(x,b,k).
\tag{ET.11}
\]
The scalar degree \(c-2=-1\) at \(k=2\) is handled by the
acyclic line bundle \(\mathcal O(-1)\) and the already fixed
zero convention for \(h_g(-1)\). No value is extrapolated past
an unproved initial range.

T-048 proves a positive formula for every \(k\ge8\). For each
\(k\in\{2,3,4,5,6,7\}\), set
\[
R_k=9-k,\qquad B_k=\lceil R_k/2\rceil.
\tag{ET.12}
\]
Use one branch \(b=B+B_k,x=X\), \(X,B\ge0\), and for
each \(0\le b_0<B_k\) use the branch
\(b=b_0,x=X+R_k-2b_0\), \(X\ge0\). These six
two-variable branches and fifteen one-variable branches are
disjoint and cover every valid endpoint. The three nonzero
corrections (ET.10) occur only in the indicated fixed-\(b\)
branches.

Pair (ET.11) with each fixed \(S_5\) character row. On a
two-variable branch, every residue function modulo 60 has separate
degrees at most \((3,4)\) and total degree at most five; its
active orders are the seventeen pairs (ER.11). On a one-variable
branch its degree is at most three. These statements are verified
by exact symbolic identities in the certificate: the identity
Euler trace is
\[
\frac{(x+1)(b+x+2)(b+1)}{12}
\bigl[(c+1)(b+c+2)(b+x+c+3)-5k(k+1)(k+2)\bigr],
\qquad c=2k-3.
\]
Add the pair dimension
\(60(x+1)\) for \(b>0\) or \(50x+40\) for \(b=0\),
and subtract the triple dimension 10, 20 or 60 on the three sectors. After each
shift in (ET.12), all its ordinary coefficients are positive.
The nonidentity degree bounds are three, three and one on the
transposition, double-transposition and three-cycle classes;
the remaining classes are periodic. All negative arguments are
\(-1\) or \(-2\), where the fixed residue expressions equal

Define the bounded constants by the finite difference (ER.13),
now using the actual trace (ET.11) and the 21 branches (ET.12).
`three_below_endpoints_certificate.py` verifies all 3,049,200

For \(\nu=\mu\) or \(\mu^t\) according as \(d+b+x\) is
even or odd, the positive formula is
\[
\boxed{p_{\mu,(n)}^\lambda
=\sum_{i\in\mathcal A_B}D_{\nu,B,r;i}
\prod_j\binom{q_j}{i_j},\qquad Z=r+60q.}
\tag{ET.13}
\]
Here \(Z\) is the free vector in its selected branch,

\(D\) is the finite difference just defined. Newton's polynomial

The coefficient interval and increasing-chain bijection is
unchanged, proving the stated eight- or five-variable bounds.
Use T-048's already proved count for \(k\ge8\).

All first-order constants are positive, so the endpoint zero sets

# A positive second-power formula and the complete first two ideal orders

## G-030. Zero twist at order two, with all boundary cases

Let \(x,b,d\ge0\), \(2b+x\ge10\), and put
\[
\begin{aligned}
n&=d+b+x-2,\\
\lambda&=(d+3b+2x-10,d+b+x,d+b+x,d+x,d).
\end{aligned}
\tag{ZS.1}
\]
Every \(p_{\mu,(n)}^\lambda\), \(\mu\vdash5\), has the
positive formula (ZS.8). The branch \(b\ge5\) uses at most
seventeen bounded integer polytopes with eight variables after
selecting two residues. Each of the five branches \(0\le b\le4\)
uses at most four polytopes with five variables. The fixed constants,
complete support lists and direct constraint matrices are specified
below. This also completes every outer-five coefficient of ideal
order at most two, through the exact comparisons in §5.

## 1. Actual Schur extraction from the restriction complex

Write \(a=b+x\), \(E=\mathfrak h_5\), and let \(Q\) be the
rank-three tautological quotient on \(\mathbf P(E)\). The exact
balanced chart and exterior-column pairing of G021/TR3 give
\[
(S_\lambda\mathbf Q^5)_{(n^5)}
\simeq\operatorname{sgn}^{d+a}
H^0\bigl(\mathcal I_Z^2\otimes S_{(a,b)}Q\bigr).
\tag{ZS.2}
\]
The point order is \(\lambda_2-n=2\), and the line twist is
\(\lambda_2-\lambda_3=0\). The inverse chart is \(u^{-2}F(v(X))\),
with \(u=\prod_iX_{i1}\); G027's normal-order calculation proves
its polynomial extension precisely on the displayed ideal sections.

Use the rank-adaptive form of G027/T049 with auxiliary space
\(F=\mathbf Q^2\), \(\alpha=(a,b)\) and
\(N=a+b=2b+x\ge10\). The normal substitution and Cauchy
Young projector identify (ZS.2), before its sign, with
\[
\operatorname{Hom}_{GL(F)}
\left(S_{(a,b)}F,\left(\bigcap_{i=1}^5
(\ell_i\otimes F)^2\right)_N\right).
\tag{ZS.3}
\]
The full exact restriction complex of G027 has, for a selected
subset \(A\) of size \(s\le3\), the quotient
\[
\left(\bigotimes_{i\in A}(\mathbf Q\oplus F)\right)
\otimes\operatorname{Sym}(\mathfrak h_{5-s}\otimes F),
\]
and the orientation line \(\bigwedge^s\mathbf Q^A\).
Its degree \(N\) terms for larger subsets vanish: their available
degree is at most four, below \(N\). The stabilizer splitting,
quotient maps and orientation are exactly FA13–17. Thus the
alternating Schur extraction computes an actual module through
specified polynomial maps.

Here is an explicit character of every term. For a permutation
cycle type \(\gamma\), let
\[
h_\gamma(j)=[z^j]\frac{1-z}{\prod_{\ell\in\gamma}(1-z^\ell)},
\qquad h_\gamma(j)=0\quad(j<0).
\]
For \(\rho=(p,q)\subseteq(a,b)\), set
\[
K_\gamma(a,b;p,q)=
h_\gamma(a-p)h_\gamma(b-q)
-h_\gamma(a-q+1)h_\gamma(b-p-1).
\tag{ZS.4}
\]
Use zero when \(\rho\) is not contained. This is precisely the
skew Schur trace \(s_{(a,b)/(p,q)}(\mathfrak h_{|\gamma|})\):
Macdonald, *Symmetric Functions and Hall Polynomials*, second
edition, Chapter I §5, (5.3)–(5.4), printed p.70, and
(5.7), p.71. The primary text and its derivation were read.
The multiplicity-space identification is Cauchy extraction
followed by the rational Young projectors, as in G027.

For selected cycle type \(\eta\), the cyclic tensor trace of its
truncated normal factors is
\[
P_\eta(X,Y)=\prod_{\ell\in\eta}(1+X^\ell+Y^\ell)
=\sum_{p\ge q\ge0}c_\eta(p,q)s_{(p,q)}(X,Y).
\tag{ZS.5}
\]
All the needed polynomials are the following finite table:

| \(\eta\) | Schur expansion \(P_\eta\) |
|---|---|
| empty | \(1\) |
| \((1)\) | \(1+s_1\) |
| \((1,1)\) | \(1+2s_1+s_2+s_{11}\) |
| \((2)\) | \(1+s_2-s_{11}\) |
| \((1,1,1)\) | \(1+3s_1+3s_2+3s_{11}+s_3+2s_{21}\) |
| \((2,1)\) | \(1+s_1+s_2-s_{11}+s_3\) |
| \((3)\) | \(1+s_3-s_{21}\) |

These identities follow by expanding the displayed products and
using \(s_{(p,q)}=\sum_{i=q}^pX^iY^{p+q-i}\).
In particular their coefficient is
\([X^pY^q]P_\eta-[X^{p+1}Y^{q-1}]P_\eta\), including
negative values when the first monomial is absent.

For \(g\in S_5\), its complete section trace is consequently
\[
t_g(x,b)=
\sum_{\substack{A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,5\}\\ |A|\le3,\ gA=A}}
(-1)^{\#\operatorname{cyc}(g|A)}
\sum_{p\ge q}c_{\operatorname{cyc}(g|A)}(p,q)
K_{\operatorname{cyc}(g|A^c)}(b+x,b;p,q).
\tag{ZS.6}
\]
The sign equals the restriction-complex sign
\((-1)^{|A|}\) times its actual orientation character
\((-1)^{|A|-\#\operatorname{cyc}(g|A)}\).
Character averaging gives
\(f_\nu(x,b)=120^{-1}\sum_{\text{classes }g}|g^{S_5}|
\chi_\nu(g)t_g(x,b)\).
The fixed seven character rows and sizes are those in T044.
The values are integral because the complex computes (ZS.3).

## 2. Exact residue-polynomial bounds

Every root in the generating series for \(h_\gamma\) has order
dividing60. Partial fractions make each nonnegative-index sequence
polynomial on residues modulo60. The empty-subset contribution is
the ordinary two-row Schur trace on \(E\). At the identity its
dimension is
\[
\frac{(x+1)(b+x+2)(b+x+3)(b+1)(b+2)}{12},
\]
of total degree five and separate degrees \((3,4)\).
At a transposition its unique eigenvalue of multiplicity three
has a quadratic contribution to \(h\); the degree-four products
cancel in its two-row determinant. All other eigenvalues have
multiplicity at most two. Thus every nonidentity term has total
degree at most three. These are the exact bounds proved in G026§2.

For a singleton subset, the complementary space has rank three.
Its identity complete traces are quadratic. The degree-four
terms in (ZS.4) agree and cancel, leaving degree at most three.
The degree in \(x\) is at most two. Each nonidentity complementary
class has maximum eigenvalue multiplicity two, so its products
have degree at most two. For a two-element subset the complement
has rank two; the identity products have degree two with equal
leading terms, and the other classes have bounded residue traces.
For a three-element subset the complement is a line, whose
nonnegative-index complete traces are periodic.

All normal partitions in the finite table have \(p\le3,q\le1\).
On the bulk \(b=B+5\), \(B\ge0\), every index in (ZS.4) is
nonnegative. Therefore the bounds just proved hold on every
entire bulk residue class, starting at zero: separate degrees at
most \((3,4)\), total degree at most five.

At a boundary \(0\le b\le4\), put
\(x=X+10-2b\). Then \(a=b+x\ge10-b\ge6\);
every varying index involving \(a\) is nonnegative. The indices
involving \(b\) alone are fixed constants, and negative ones
are assigned their exact zero values. The noncontainment tests
also involve only fixed \(b,q\). Thus each boundary residue
function is polynomial in \(X\) from \(X=0\), of degree at most
three. This checks every initial-range and partition-boundary issue.

## 3. Every fixed positive constant and its lattice polytope

In the bulk write \((x,B)=(r_1,r_2)+60(q_1,q_2)\), with
\(0\le r_i<60\), and define
\[
C_{\nu,r;i,j}=
\sum_{u=0}^i\sum_{v=0}^j
(-1)^{i+j-u-v}\binom iu\binom jv
f_\nu(r_1+60u,r_2+60v+5),
\quad0\le i\le3,\quad0\le j\le4.
\tag{ZS.7}
\]
The finite polynomial Newton identity gives
\[
\boxed{p_{\mu,(n)}^\lambda=
\sum_{\substack{0\le i\le3,\ 0\le j\le4\\i+j\le5}}
C_{\nu,r;i,j}\binom{q_1}{i}\binom{q_2}{j},\qquad
\nu=\begin{cases}\mu&d+b+x\text{ even},\\
\mu^t&d+b+x\text{ odd}.\end{cases}}
\tag{ZS.8}
\]
The sign follows from (ZS.2), so no parity is implicit.

Replacing each strict inequality by an integer gap of at least

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

Use the effective label in (ZS.8) and the shift \(x=X+10-2b\).
All remaining inputs have positive coefficient, by nonnegativity

The evaluator second_power_zero_twist_positive.py computes only

in G023. The generic restriction-character implementation
zero_twist_arrangement.py was checked against1442 actual balanced

certificate proves the infinite positive formula. Independent

with their precise executed scopes as they finish.

## 5. Completion of both first ideal orders and exact transport

For an arbitrary five-row partition of size \(5n\), set
\[
d=\lambda_5,\quad x=\lambda_4-\lambda_5,\quad
b=\lambda_3-\lambda_4,\quad
k=\max(0,\lambda_2-n),\quad c=\lambda_2-\lambda_3.
\tag{ZS.10}
\]
For positive \(k\), the exact flag dictionary is
\[
n=d+b+x+c-k,\qquad
\lambda=(d+3b+2x+4c-5k,d+b+x+c,d+b+x,d+x,d),
\]
with validity \(2b+x+3c\ge5k\). Its bundle is
\(\operatorname{sgn}^{d+b+x}\mathcal I^k(c)S_{(b+x,b)}Q\).
The following disjoint cases exhaust the first two ideal orders:

| Order | Twist | Complete positive formula |
|---|---|---|
| \(k=1\) | \(c=0\) | G026 |
| \(k=1\) | \(c=1\) | T045 |
| \(k=1\) | \(c\ge2\) | G021 |
| \(k=2\) | \(c=0\) | G030 |
| \(k=2\) | \(c=1\) | T051 |
| \(k=2\) | \(c=2\) | T050 |
| \(k=2\) | \(c=3\) | T045 |
| \(k=2\) | \(c\ge4\) | G021 |

Each row uses the actual chart (ZS.10); hence the coefficient,
parity and support comparisons agree exactly. At \(k=0\), G021
and its explicit \(u^{\,n-\lambda_2}\) stable chart in TR18
already give the complete positive count.

It follows that all seven coefficients are positively evaluated
for every five-row shape with
\[
\boxed{\lambda_2\le n+2\quad\text{or}\quad\lambda_4\ge n-2.}
\tag{ZS.11}
\]
For the second region use \(H=\lambda_1\),
\(\lambda^c=(H-\lambda_5,\ldots,H-\lambda_1)\),
\(n^c=H-n\). The exterior-column pairing TR19 identifies its
balanced module with the dual original module times
\(\operatorname{sgn}^H\), and
\(\lambda^c_2-n^c=n-\lambda_4\le2\). This is the exact
morphism proving the second region and its outer-label transpose.

The schemes are the affine and Proj coordinate models of the
five explicit linear ideals. G027's quotient substitution and
normal-order comparison, followed by its signed restriction
complex and Young projector, are the exact maps in (ZS.3).
EGA II2.4.1–2.4.2 (p.28) supplies the Proj charts and
II2.5.2,2.5.4 (p.31) the exact associated-sheaf functor.
The frame action is the comodule action of SGA3 I4.5,
I4.7.2–4.7.3. The Schur operations are SGA6
V4.2,4.4,4.8–4.9 and cote133/024–029 via A010.
The finite equivariant free resolutions explicitly constructed
in G027§6 carry the coherent complex to locally free \(K_0\)
in SGA6 VI3.3. Thus its geometric class and every coefficient
use the same specified morphisms. R031 then gives the actual
symmetric canonical ranks on these evaluated components.


# Positive formulas through the complete third ideal order

## G-032. All three remaining twists at order three

Let \(x,b,d\ge0\), \(c\in\{0,1,2\}\), and
\(2b+x+3c\ge15\). Put
\[
\begin{aligned}
n&=d+b+x+c-3,\\
\lambda&=(d+3b+2x+4c-15,\ d+b+x+c,\\
&\hspace{30mm}d+b+x,\ d+x,\ d).
\end{aligned}
\tag{FT.1}
\]
Every \(p_{\mu,(n)}^\lambda\), \(\mu\vdash5\), has the
fixed positive formula (FT.9). For each twist, the branch \(b\ge8\)
uses at most seventeen selected bounded integer polytopes, with at most
eight variables. Each branch \(0\le b\le7\) uses at most four
polytopes with at most five variables. Every fixed constant is specified
by the finite formulas below, and all 1,552,320 constants are certified
nonnegative. The exact zero sets are recorded in §5.

Together with the previously proved twist families, this completes
**every ideal order at most three**. In the original partition variables
it gives a fixed positive coefficient formula whenever
\(\lambda_2\le n+3\) or \(\lambda_4\ge n-3\), through
the explicit maps in §6. No historical priority claim is made.

## 1. The actual rank-three representation and sheaf maps

Set \(a=b+x\), \(E=\mathfrak h_5\), \(F=\mathbb Q^3\),
\(\alpha=(a+c,b+c,c)\), and \(N=2b+x+3c\). Let
\(\ell_i=e_i-\frac15\sum_j e_j\) and
\(J_3=\bigcap_{i=1}^5(\ell_i\otimes F)^3\) in
\(\operatorname{Sym}(E\otimes F)\). The actual normal substitution,
Young extraction and inverse balanced homogenization of G027/T049 give
\[
\begin{aligned}
M_{x,b,c}&=\operatorname{Hom}_{GL(F)}(S_\alpha F,(J_3)_N),\\
(S_\lambda\mathbb Q^5)_{(n^5)}
&\simeq\operatorname{sgn}^{d+a+c}\otimes M_{x,b,c}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{FT.2}
\]
The inverse polynomial chart is \(u^{-3}F(v(X))\), with the
normal-order membership proved in G027. It is a map into the original coordinate ring.

For the five-point ideal sheaf \(\mathcal I_Z\) on
\(\mathbf P(E)\) and its tautological quotient \(Q\), the same
comparison is
\[
M_{x,b,c}\simeq\operatorname{sgn}^{c}\otimes
H^0(\mathcal I_Z^3(c)\otimes S_{(a,b)}Q).
\tag{FT.3}
\]
Indeed the exterior-column pairing gives
\(S_\alpha Q=(\det Q)^c\otimes S_{(a,b)}Q\), and
\(\det Q=\det E\otimes\mathcal O(1)\), with
\(\det E=\operatorname{sgn}\). This gives both the displayed
line twist and its exact constant-group character. The sign in (FT.2)
therefore agrees with G021's sign \(\operatorname{sgn}^{d+a}\)
after (FT.3).

Write \(\nu=\mu\) when \(d+a+c\) is even and
\(\nu=\mu'\) when it is odd. The desired coefficient is
\([\nu:M_{x,b,c}]\).

## 2. A finite exact character with every normal term specified

For a cycle type \(\gamma\), define
\[
h_\gamma(t)=[z^t]\frac{1-z}{\prod_{\ell\in\gamma}(1-z^\ell)},
\qquad h_\gamma(t)=0\quad(t<0).
\]
For \(\rho\subseteq\alpha\) with at most three rows put
\[
K_\gamma(\alpha;\rho)
=\det\bigl(h_\gamma(\alpha_i-\rho_j-i+j)\bigr)_{1\le i,j\le3},
\tag{FT.4}
\]
and set it to zero when \(\rho\not\subseteq\alpha\). This is
the skew Schur trace on the actual complementary standard module.
The precise known identity is Macdonald, *Symmetric Functions and Hall
Polynomials*, second edition, Chapter I §5, equations (5.3)–(5.4),
printed p.70, and containment convention (5.7), p.71. Its primary
text and derivation were read for G030.

The normal factor is
\(T_3(F)=\mathbb Q\oplus F\oplus\operatorname{Sym}^2F\).
For each selected cycle type \(\eta\) of total size at most three,
its literal cyclic tensor trace is the finite polynomial
\[
P_\eta(X_1,X_2,X_3)=
\prod_{\ell\in\eta}
\bigl(1+h_1(X_1^\ell,X_2^\ell,X_3^\ell)
       +h_2(X_1^\ell,X_2^\ell,X_3^\ell)\bigr).
\tag{FT.5}
\]
Let \(\delta=(2,1,0)\). All its Schur coefficients are specified
by the six-term formula
\[
c_\eta(\rho)=
\sum_{\sigma\in S_3}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)
[X^{\rho+\delta-\sigma\delta}]P_\eta(X),
\qquad \rho_1\ge\rho_2\ge\rho_3\ge0.
\tag{FT.6}
\]
A negative exponent contributes zero. Multiplication by the Vandermonde
alternant proves (FT.6): the coefficient at the strictly decreasing
exponent \(\rho+\delta\) in each Schur alternant is its diagonal
term, and no other dominant weight contributes. Each polynomial has
degree at most six. In particular \(\rho_1\le6\),
\(\rho_2\le3\), \(\rho_3\le2\). The complete finite
expansions for \(\eta=\varnothing,1,11,2,111,21,3\) are saved
in the certificate. For example, the last one is
\[
\begin{aligned}
P_{(3)}={}&1+s_{111}-s_{21}+s_{222}+s_3-s_{321}\\
&+s_{33}+s_{411}-s_{51}+s_6.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus the formula retains negative normal characters even where the
corresponding initial monomial is absent.

The G027 restriction complex has, at a selected subset \(A\) of
size \(s\le3\), the actual module
\(T_3(F)^{\otimes s}\otimes\operatorname{Sym}(\mathfrak h_{5-s}\otimes F)\)
with its orientation line. Every term at size at least four is already a quotient by four
independent truncated blocks, whose total available degree is at most
eight. Thus every such term vanishes in degree \(N\ge15\). The exact quotient and
restriction maps, including the dependent last normal, are G027/FA13–17.
Consequently its alternating Schur extraction gives the actual trace
\[
\begin{aligned}
t_g(x,b,c)=
\sum_{\substack{A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,5\}\\ |A|\le3,\ gA=A}}
(-1)^{\#\operatorname{cyc}(g|A)}
\sum_{\rho}c_{\operatorname{cyc}(g|A)}(\rho)
K_{\operatorname{cyc}(g|A^c)}(\alpha;\rho).
\end{aligned}
\tag{FT.7}
\]
The sign is \((-1)^s\) from complex degree times
\((-1)^{s-\#\operatorname{cyc}(g|A)}\) from its orientation.
The complete trace becomes the integer coefficient
\[
f_\nu(x,b,c)=\frac1{120}\sum_{[g]}|[g]|\chi_\nu(g)t_g(x,b,c).
\tag{FT.8}
\]
The seven class sizes and character rows are the fixed table in T044,
also reproduced by the executable evaluator. Thus (FT.4)–(FT.8)
specify all numerical data using finite products, determinants and
fixed character sums; no plethysm oracle is involved.

## 3. The polynomial domains, including every initial boundary

Fix \(c\in\{0,1,2\}\). Every root in the generating series
for \(h_\gamma\) has order dividing60. Partial fractions therefore
make each nonnegative-index sequence polynomial on every residue
class modulo60. For the empty-subset identity contribution, the exact
dimension is
\[
\frac{(x+1)(b+x+2)(b+x+c+3)(b+1)(b+c+2)(c+1)}{12}.
\]
It has total degree five and separate degrees at most \((3,4)\)
in \((x,b)\).

Here are sufficient bounds for every other term, with their degree
cancellations checked. Expanding (FT.4) along its third row makes it a
linear combination of two-by-two determinants whose row arguments are
\(b+x+c+u\) and \(b+c+v\), with fixed shifts. For a nonidentity
class on \(E\), the only eigenvalue with multiplicity three is
\(1\) for a transposition; its complete trace has a quadratic part
with constant leading coefficient. The degree-four products in each
two-by-two determinant agree and cancel. All other eigenvalues have
multiplicity at most two. Hence every nonidentity empty-subset term
has total degree at most three and degree at most two in \(x\).

At a singleton subset, the complementary identity complete traces
are quadratic, with the same leading-term cancellation; their total
degree is at most three. The other complementary classes have at most
linear complete traces. At a two-element subset the identity complete
traces are linear and the degree-two products cancel, leaving total
degree at most one; other complementary traces are periodic. At a
three-element subset the complementary module is a line and all its
nonnegative-index traces are periodic. These arguments hold on each
fixed residue class, where all root-of-unity factors are constants.
Thus the total and separate bounds \(5,(3,4)\) hold throughout the
bulk.

For that bulk put \(b=B+8\), \(B\ge0\). Every index in the
first two rows of (FT.4) is nonnegative, since \(\rho_1\le6\).
The third-row indices and the condition \(\rho_3\le c\) are
fixed. Therefore the stated polynomial bounds hold from the origin
of each whole bulk residue class.

For \(0\le b\le7\), put
\[
x=X+q_{b,c},\qquad q_{b,c}=\max(0,15-3c-2b),\qquad X\ge0.
\]
The least value of \(\alpha_1=b+x+c\) on these24 branches is
seven. Thus every varying first-row index is nonnegative and every
first-row containment condition is automatic. The second and third
rows, including their exact zero values at negative indices and their
containment tests, are fixed independently of \(X\). Each boundary
residue polynomial therefore starts at \(X=0\) and has degree at
most three. This verifies all initial-range issues needed for Newton
interpolation, including the branches with \(q_{b,c}=0\).

## 4. All positive constants and their actual bounded polytopes

For the bulk let \((x,B)=r+60Q\), \(0\le r_i<60\), and set
\[
\begin{aligned}
C^{c}_{\nu,r;i,j}={}&
\sum_{u=0}^i\sum_{v=0}^j
(-1)^{i+j-u-v}\binom iu\binom jv\\
&\hspace{8mm}\cdot f_\nu(r_1+60u,r_2+60v+8,c),
\qquad 0\le i\le3,\ 0\le j\le4.
\end{aligned}
\]
For a boundary \(b\), let \(X=r+60Q\) and define
\(D^c_{\nu,b,r;i}=\sum_{u=0}^i(-1)^{i-u}\binom iu
f_\nu(r+60u+q_{b,c},b,c)\), \(0\le i\le3\).
The exact finite Newton identity now gives
\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
p_{\mu,(n)}^\lambda
 &=\sum_{i=0}^3\sum_{j=0}^4C^c_{\nu,r;i,j}
                \binom{Q_1}{i}\binom{Q_2}{j} &&(b\ge8),\\
p_{\mu,(n)}^\lambda
 &=\sum_{i=0}^3D^c_{\nu,b,r;i}\binom Qi &&(b\le7).
\end{aligned}}
\tag{FT.9}
\]
Here \(\nu\) is exactly the parity-adjusted label after (FT.3).

The finite certificate evaluates the complete domains of every
constant, using (FT.4)–(FT.8) and integer arithmetic. For each twist
it checks \(7\cdot60^2\cdot4\cdot5=504000\) bulk constants
and \(8\cdot7\cdot60\cdot4=13440\) boundary constants.
Every constant is nonnegative. The active bulk orders are precisely
\[
\{(0,j):0\le j\le4\}\ \cup\
\{(1,j):0\le j\le4\}\ \cup\
\{(2,j):0\le j\le3\}\ \cup\
\{(3,j):0\le j\le2\}.
\]
Every active constant of positive order is strictly positive, as are
all boundary constants of orders one through three.

The proof certificate is `third_power_fixed_twist_certificate.py`
with its complete arithmetic specification in
`fixed_twist_arrangement.py`; the receipt is
`THIRD_POWER_FIXED_TWIST_CERTIFICATE.json`. Every array hash, minimum,
maximum, zero set and operation bound is recorded. Before every
vectorized multiplication and accumulated trace, the script proves an
absolute bound from the maxima of the factors. Before taking differences,
it checks \(2^7\max|f|<2^{63}\) in the bulk and the corresponding
\(2^3\) bound at a boundary. Hence every integer operation is exact.
The largest trace-operation bound in these computations is
4,176,326,138,215,440, strictly below \(2^{63}\). This receipt is
an exhaustive finite arithmetic certificate, not a sampled positivity
claim.

For a positive bulk constant \(C\) and order \((i,j)\), use
integer variables
\[Q_1,Q_2,y,z_{1,1},\ldots,z_{1,i},z_{2,1},\ldots,z_{2,j},\]
with the exact constraints
\[
\begin{gathered}
60Q_1=x-r_1,\quad60Q_2=B-r_2,\quad Q_1,Q_2\ge0,\quad0\le y<C,\\
0\le z_{1,1}<\cdots<z_{1,i}<Q_1,\qquad
0\le z_{2,1}<\cdots<z_{2,j}<Q_2.
\end{gathered}
\tag{FT.10}
\]
The chain with length zero is omitted. The choices of the two subsets
and of \(y\) give a literal bijection with the corresponding summand
of (FT.9). Replace strict integer inequalities by a difference of at
least one to obtain closed integral halfspaces. The equations fix
\(Q_1,Q_2\), all remaining variables are bounded, and
\(i+j\le5\), proving the eight-variable bound. The one-chain
boundary construction gives five variables. Zero constants give empty
sets and are omitted; distinct order/residue tags give a disjoint union.
`third_power_fixed_twist_positive.py` writes the literal matrices,
evaluates the formula and emits actual witness tuples.

## 6. Completion of the third order and the exact complement map

For ideal order three, the cases c=0,1,2 are exactly (FT.1).
The remaining twists are c=3 by T051, c=4 by T050, c=5 by T045,
and c≥6 by G021. These disjoint cases cover every nonnegative twist.
G026/G030 and their already proved boundary families cover orders one
and two. At order zero the stable chart is onto, with multiplication
by the exact invariant section u carrying every extra first-row degree.
Consequently every shape with λ₂≤n+3 is evaluated.

For the complementary range use H=λ₁ and
\(\lambda^c=(H-\lambda_5,H-\lambda_4,H-\lambda_3,
H-\lambda_2,0)\), of size 5(H−n). The actual perfect pairing
\(S_\lambda\mathbb Q^5\otimes S_{\lambda^c}\mathbb Q^5
\to(\det\mathbb Q^5)^H\) is exterior contraction on each
complementary column followed by the paired Young projectors.
Restricting to balanced weights pairs the two weights n and H−n,
and the constant symmetric group acts on the target by sgn^H.
The rational invariant Gram pairing identifies every finite symmetric-group dual. Thus the effective outer label is transposed precisely
when H is odd. The complementary order is
\(\max(0,(H-\lambda_4)-(H-n))=\max(0,n-\lambda_4)\).
This proves the claimed coverage λ₄≥n−3, with every map and sign fixed.

The remaining direct coefficient-formula gate in these coordinates is
therefore k≥4 and 0≤c≤2k−4, after also removing the complementary
range and the separately completed staircase and other families.
G031 continues to decide every zero even throughout that remaining gate.

## 7. Grothendieck-language transport and proof checks

The scheme and sheaf content is the actual coherent section module
(FT.3), carried by the quotient substitution and exterior determinant
pairings of (FT.2). The ideal inclusions, restrictions and diagonal
quotient are equivariant coordinate-ring morphisms; their affine and
projective schemes use EGA II2.4.1–2.4.2, p.28, and2.5.2/2.5.4,p.31.
Every Young and finite-group projector is a rational direct summand.
The frame-torsor functor sends these equivariant maps to the identical
associated-bundle maps, as in SGA3 I4.5 and4.7.2–4.7.3. Their exact
representation and locally free sheaf classes are carried by SGA6
VI3.3; SGA6 V4.2,4.4,4.8–4.9 specify the universal λ-operation and
finite-rank evaluation. The restriction complex therefore gives the
stated class through actual coherent modules, and (FT.10) counts its
Schur coefficient. In the archive, this evaluates the Schur/tensor
composition of cote133/028 through the explicit tensor-word, torus
weight and Young maps of A012. The appendix's locator register states
the scope of each cited Grothendieck construction.

The scalar implementation was independently compared with literal
balanced Schur cycle traces on3353 actual coefficients, including
all valid k=1,2,3,c=0,1,2,b≤8,x≤7 inputs. This checks all determinant
and sign conventions across the rank-two and rank-three boundaries.
The complete finite positivity calculation checks1,552,320 constants.
These computations and the full proof readings are recorded as
separate events. No random sample is used to establish the theorem.

The direct evaluator additionally passed2310 exact value comparisons,2282 literal witness-matrix checks and84 exhaustive small-witness enumerations; the receipt is `THIRD_POWER_EVALUATOR_CHECK.json`.


# A positive formula on an unbounded-order wall chamber

## T-054. Every order in the chamber \(b\ge3k-2\)

Let \(k\ge3\), \(x,b,d\ge0\),
\(b\ge3k-2\), and \(2b+x\ge5k\). Set
\[
\begin{aligned}
n&=d+b+x-k,\\
\lambda&=(d+3b+2x-5k,d+b+x,d+b+x,d+x,d).
\end{aligned}
\tag{VW.1}
\]
For every \(\mu\vdash5\), the coefficient
\(p_{\mu,(n)}^\lambda\) has the explicit positive formula
(VW.14). It uses at most 46 bounded integer polytopes, each with
at most nine variables, after selecting three residues modulo60.
The fixed phase polynomials and every rational inequality proving
positivity are given in the accompanying finite certificate.
There is no input-dependent representation or elimination oracle.

This chamber permits every \(x\ge0\) and unbounded \(k\).
Its complete support is the thirteen effective-label exceptions
in §6, together with the declared determinant parity. No historical
novelty claim is made for the coefficient family or its ingredients.

Write
\[
a=b+x,\qquad X=x,\qquad B=b-3k+2,\qquad K=k-3.
\tag{VW.2}
\]
Thus \(X,B,K\ge0\). The partition condition is
\(K+2B+X\ge1\): the sole excluded parameter is
\((X,B,K)=(0,0,0)\). A formal zero value at that point is
proved below and is retained in the fixed Newton constants.

## 1. The actual restriction complex and its two surviving terms

Let \(E=\mathfrak h_5\), \(F=\mathbf Q^2\), and
\(J_k=\bigcap_{i=1}^5(\ell_i\otimes F)^k\).
T-049's all-degree substitution, the rank-adaptive Cauchy map,
and the balanced flag chart give the actual module
\[
(S_\lambda\mathbf Q^5)_{(n^5)}
\simeq\operatorname{sgn}^{d+a}\otimes M_{a,b,k},
\qquad
M_{a,b,k}=\operatorname{Hom}_{GL(F)}
(S_{(a,b)}F,(J_k)_{a+b}).
\tag{VW.3}
\]
The quotient substitution sends the \(i\)-th independent
block to \(\ell_i\otimes F\); its inverse balanced chart
is \(u^{-k}F(v(X))\). G-027's normal-order calculation is
the polynomial extension criterion. The determinant in (VW.3)
is \(\lambda_2=d+a\), so its finite character is retained.

Put \(T_k(V)=\bigoplus_{t=0}^{k-1}\operatorname{Sym}^tV\).
The selected-subset term of G-027 for a subset of size \(s\)
is Cauchy extraction from
\(T_k(F)^{\otimes s}\otimes
\operatorname{Sym}(\mathfrak h_{5-s}\otimes F)\),
with the actual orientation line of that subset. Its differential
is the signed polynomial quotient map. Since \(a+b\ge5k\),
the cited complex is exact in this degree.

All terms with \(s\ge4\) vanish: four independent blocks
truncated below \(k\) have total degree at most \(4(k-1)\).
For \(s=3\), the complementary standard space is a line.
The skew Schur factor can be nonzero only when
\((a,b)/\rho\) is a horizontal strip, which requires
\(\rho_1\ge b\). The normal factors have
\(\rho_1\le|\rho|\le3(k-1)<b\). Hence that entire
module vanishes as well. We obtain the actual exact sequence
\[
0\longrightarrow M_{a,b,k}\longrightarrow
S_{(a,b)}E\longrightarrow C_1\longrightarrow C_2
\longrightarrow0.
\tag{VW.4}
\]
The maps are the specified restriction maps followed by rational
Young idempotents; the following identifications describe their
source and target modules explicitly.

### 1.1. Singleton module and the exact straightening cancellation

Pieri extraction from \(\operatorname{Sym}^{i+j}F\)
removes a horizontal strip from \((a,b)\). Thus
\[
C_1=\operatorname{Ind}_{S_4}^{S_5}
\bigoplus_{\substack{i,j\ge0\\i+j<k\\i\le x}}
S_{(a-i,b-j)}\mathfrak h_4.
\tag{VW.5}
\]
The conditions \(i\le x\) and \(j\le b\) are exactly
the interlacing conditions; the latter is automatic from
\(b\ge3k-2\) and \(i+j<k\). Each Pieri map is the
column inclusion and Schur projection of the Cauchy tensor.
This gives the displayed direct sum as an actual module.

For its character computation only, the restriction \(i\le x\)
can be dropped by an explicit involution. Use the two-row
Jacobi--Trudi expression
\(s_{(u,v)}=h_uh_v-h_{u+1}h_{v-1}\) also for unordered
integer pairs. Every pair with \(i>x\) is matched with
\[
(i',j')=(x+j+1,i-x-1).
\tag{VW.6}
\]
Both new entries are nonnegative, \(i'>x\), and
\(i'+j'=i+j<k\). Their two shapes are
\((a-i,b-j)\) and \((b-j-1,a-i+1)\), whose
Jacobi--Trudi determinants are negatives of one another.
The fixed points have determinant zero. Thus every additional
term cancels, and the full triangular determinant sum has exactly
the trace of (VW.5). All complete-function indices used in that
sum are nonnegative: the smallest is
\(b-j-1\ge2k-2\). This proves the enlargement to every
\(x\ge0\), including its boundary, by the stated map and
straightening relation.

### 1.2. Pair module, its dual comparison, and its finite action

For a pair let \(W=\mathfrak h_3\) be the complementary
two-dimensional standard representation. A normal Schur shape
\(\rho=(p,q)\) has \(p\le2(k-1)<b\). The exact
rank-two skew comparison is
\[
S_{(a,b)/(p,q)}W
\simeq (\det W)^b\otimes\operatorname{Sym}^xW
\otimes S_{(p,q)}W^*.
\tag{VW.7}
\]
Here is the actual representation comparison. In the two-row
Littlewood--Richardson extraction, use the perfect exterior
pairing for \(S_{(p,q)}W\) and its dual. Since
\(S_{(p,q)}W^*=(\det W)^{-p}\operatorname{Sym}^{p-q}W\),
the right side is
\((\det W)^{b-p}\operatorname{Sym}^xW
\otimes\operatorname{Sym}^{p-q}W\), a polynomial module.
The binary Clebsch--Gordan projections, given by contraction
with the alternating form and multiplication of the remaining
symmetric slots, identify its distinct irreducible summands with
the same Littlewood--Richardson column maps on the left. Each
map is nonzero on its highest column tensor and is normalized
there. The multiplicity-one binary decomposition makes their
direct sum a perfect isomorphism. Equivalently, expanding the
two-row determinant on two variables gives its character
\((uv)^{b-p}h_x(u,v)h_{p-q}(u,v)\); the preceding
column maps specify the isomorphism behind that equality.

Decompose \(T_k(F)^{\otimes2}\) by its Cauchy Young
projectors and apply (VW.7) to every summand. The same
projectors reconstruct \(T_k(W^*)^{\otimes2}\), with the
literal interchange of its two factors. Thus
\[
C_2\simeq\operatorname{Ind}_{S_2\times S_3}^{S_5}
\left(\operatorname{sgn}_2\otimes(\det W)^b
\otimes\operatorname{Sym}^xW\otimes T_k(W^*)^{\otimes2}\right).
\tag{VW.8}
\]
The first sign is the orientation line in (VW.4). The rational
dot product on the standard \(S_3\)-space identifies
\(W^*\) with \(W\) when computing its finite-group
traces. That comparison is equivariant and preserves the two
tensor-factor permutations.

The skew determinant and its containment convention were read
in the primary text: Macdonald, *Symmetric Functions and Hall
Polynomials*, second edition, Chapter I §5, (5.3)–(5.4),
printed p.70, and (5.7)–(5.8), p.71,
[primary PDF](https://math.berkeley.edu/~corteel/MATH249/macdonald.pdf).
The actual Cauchy, exterior and binary projections used here
are the same explicit maps fixed in T-047 and T-049.

## 2. A bounded formula for every class trace

For a cycle partition \(\gamma\) define
\[
h_\gamma(j)=[z^j]\frac{1-z}{\prod_{\ell\in\gamma}(1-z^\ell)}.
\tag{VW.9}
\]
This is the complete-character trace of the ordinary standard
representation of \(S_{|\gamma|}\). For \(g\in S_5\)
write \(\gamma(g)\) for its cycle partition and \(m_1(g)\)
for its number of fixed points. The trace in (VW.4) is the sum
of the following three completely specified terms:

* The ambient term is
  \(h_\gamma(a)h_\gamma(b)-h_\gamma(a+1)h_\gamma(b-1)\).
* Subtract \(m_1(g)\) times
  \(\sum_{i,j\ge0,\ i+j<k}
  [h_\delta(a-i)h_\delta(b-j)
  -h_\delta(a-i+1)h_\delta(b-j-1)]\),
  where \(\delta\) removes one fixed point from \(\gamma\).
  This term is absent when \(m_1(g)=0\).
* For every literal \(g\)-stable two-subset \(A\), add
  \(\operatorname{sgn}(g|A)\det(g|W)^b
  h_{\gamma(g|A^c)}(x)\) times
  \(U_{\gamma(g|A^c)}(k)^2\) when \(g|A\) is the
  identity, or \(U_{\gamma(g^2|A^c)}(k)\) when it is a
  transposition. Here \(U_\delta(k)=\sum_{t=0}^{k-1}h_\delta(t)\).

The square in the fixed-pair case and the squared permutation
in the swapped-pair case follow by the literal trace of an
operator on two tensor factors. For the three possible
complementary classes, the complete formulas are
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
\delta&h_\delta(x)&U_\delta(k)\\\hline
1^3&x+1&k(k+1)/2\\
21&\mathbf1_{2\mid x}&\lceil k/2\rceil\\
3&(1,-1,0)_{x\bmod3}&\mathbf1_{k\equiv1\ (3)}.
\end{array}
\tag{VW.10}
\]
All induced traces above are sums over at most five fixed points
and ten two-subsets. Their signs are the actual ones of (VW.4).

At the formal origin of (VW.2), \(k=3\), \((a,b)=(7,7)\)
and \(N=14<15\). T-049 gives \((J_3)_{14}=0\).
The same trace formula is zero there: expand T-049's full tail
product by selecting truncated factors. Selected-four terms have
degree at most8. The full-selected term has degree at most12,
including the degree-two exterior factor. Both are below14;
the selected-three Schur term vanishes by \(b>3(k-1)\).
Thus the three displayed terms still compute the actual zero
ideal component at that point. This proves its value, without
assigning a plethysm coefficient to an invalid partition.

## 3. Exact phase polynomials, valid from the initial residue

Let \(L=\operatorname{lcm}(\gamma)\). The maximum pole
multiplicity of (VW.9) is
\(d+1=\max_{e\mid L}
(\#\{\ell\in\gamma:e\mid\ell\}-\mathbf1_{e=1})\).
Partial fractions express the coefficient sequence, on each
residue modulo \(L\), as a polynomial of degree at most
\(d\). The generating function is proper, so this assertion
holds from index zero. The polynomial is explicitly
\[
H_{\gamma,r}(z)=
\sum_{j=0}^d h_\gamma(r+Lj)
\prod_{\substack{0\le q\le d\\q\ne j}}
\frac{(z-r)/L-q}{j-q}.
\tag{VW.11}
\]
Only bounded initial coefficients of the fixed rational function
are used here.

For completeness the triangular singleton sum is also evaluated
by a fixed polynomial construction. Let \(L\le4\) be the
period of its complementary \(S_4\) class. Write
\(i=s+Lu\), \(j=t+Lv\), with \(0\le s,t<L\), and set
\(M=\lfloor(k-1-s-t)/L\rfloor\). On each phase of
\((a,b,k)\), this is an affine polynomial in \(k\).
Substitute (VW.11) in the summand. Its formal expression in
\(u,v\) has degree at most two in each variable; write it
uniquely as \(\sum_{p,q} e_{pq}\binom up\binom vq\).
Its triangular sum is exactly
\[
\sum_{p,q} e_{pq}\binom{M+2}{p+q+2},
\quad
\sum_{u,v\ge0,\ u+v\le M}\binom up\binom vq
=\binom{M+2}{p+q+2}.
\tag{VW.12}
\]
The identity follows by multiplying
\(z^p/(1-z)^{p+1}\), \(z^q/(1-z)^{q+1}\)
and \(1/(1-z)\). Since \(k\ge3\), \(L\le4\),
we always have \(M\ge-1\). At \(M=-1\), every displayed
binomial polynomial is zero, so the formula covers the empty
initial triangle as well. The formal polynomial extension used
to find the \(e_{pq}\)'s is only evaluated as a trace on the
actual triangle, where all complete-function indices were shown
nonnegative in §1.1.

Equations (VW.9)–(VW.12), the literal two-subset list and
(VW.10) define every class polynomial with no unbounded sum.
`chamber_polynomials.py` carries out exactly these rational
operations. In the class order
\(1^5,2111,221,311,32,41,5\), their total degrees are

## 4. The analytic positivity certificate

Let \(\Delta^\delta\) be the mixed forward difference with
step60 in \((X,B,K)\). The complete possible orders form
the downward-closed set
\[
\mathcal A=
\{(0,j,l):j+l\le4\}
\cup\{(i,j,l):1\le i\le3,\ 0\le j\le4,
i+j+l\le5\}.
\tag{VW.13}
\]
It has46 elements. Every phase polynomial is supported on
monomials in this set; all differences outside it vanish.
For each nonzero \(\delta\) of total order at most three,
form the following explicit polynomial. From \(\Delta^\delta P_1\)
subtract, for every nonidentity conjugacy class, its size times
the coefficientwise maximum, over its finitely many phases, of
the absolute coefficients of \(\Delta^\delta P_g\).
Call the resulting polynomial \(M_\delta\).

All coefficients of these nineteen polynomials are nonnegative.
The following table gives the constant coefficient and the
minimum over their represented coefficients; the complete
polynomials and every phase used to construct them are in the
fixed certificate. The arithmetic is rational and exact.

|---|---:|---:|
| (0,0,1) | 7224470 | 30 |
| (0,0,2) | 95238000 | 5400 |
| (0,0,3) | 237816000 | 1512000 |
| (0,1,0) | 1792265 | 10 |

| (0,2,0) | 19146000 | 600 |

| (0,3,0) | 42768000 | 216000 |

For the other26 nonzero orders in \(\mathcal A\), the
nonidentity differences vanish by their degree bounds. The
identity table proves nonnegative coefficients and a positive
constant for each remaining difference. Thus all45 positive
orders have a strictly positive domination polynomial; their
minimum constant is1288865.

Here is the implication for every outer label, including all
signs. A finite group representation admits an invariant positive
Hermitian form, so \(|\chi_\nu(g)|\le\dim[\nu]\).
On any valid phase and at nonnegative \(X,B,K\), the triangle
inequality and the coefficientwise bound therefore give
\[
\Delta^\delta f_\nu(X,B,K)
\ge\frac{\dim[\nu]}{120}M_\delta(X,B,K)>0
\quad(\delta\in\mathcal A\setminus\{0\}),
\]
where \(f_\nu\) is the character average of (VW.4).
Step60 preserves all phases. The order-zero values are
nonnegative because they are the actual multiplicities in
(VW.3), with the formal zero at the excluded origin already
proved. Hence every coefficient used in the next section is a
nonnegative integer. This establishes positivity by finitely
specified polynomial inequalities, without assuming positivity
of an unevaluated difference.

## 5. The positive formula and every constraint matrix

Let \(\nu=\mu\) when \(d+b+x\) is even and
\(\nu=\mu^t\) when it is odd. Write
\((X,B,K)=r+60q\), with \(0\le r_i<60\), and set
\[
D_{\nu,r,\delta}=
\sum_{0\le h\le\delta}
(-1)^{|\delta|-|h|}\binom{\delta}{h}
f_\nu(r+60h).
\]
These are fixed constants: all evaluation coordinates are
bounded by359, independently of the input. The exact polynomial
Newton identity gives
\[
\boxed{p_{\mu,(n)}^\lambda
=\sum_{\delta\in\mathcal A}
D_{\nu,r,\delta}\prod_{i=1}^3\binom{q_i}{\delta_i}.}
\tag{VW.14}
\]
Their positivity was proved in §4. Every trace evaluation in the
constants is the bounded formula of §3, using the fixed
polynomial certificate. The evaluator therefore
has no input-dependent multiplicity oracle.

For each positive constant use integer variables \(q_1,q_2,q_3\),
a selector \(z\), and three increasing chains of lengths
\(\delta_i\). The complete constraints are
\[
\begin{gathered}
60q_i=Z_i-r_i,\quad q_i\ge0,\qquad
0\le z\le D_{\nu,r,\delta}-1,\\
0\le u_{i1}<\cdots<u_{i,\delta_i}<q_i
\quad(1\le i\le3),\qquad Z=(X,B,K).
\end{gathered}
\tag{VW.15}
\]
Replace strict inequalities by gaps of at least one. The selector
and the increasing subsets give a bijection with the corresponding
summand in (VW.14). Empty chains have one choice. These are bounded
rational polytopes, with at most \(3+1+|\delta|\le9\)
variables and46 disjoint order tags. The quotient coordinates
and chain entries have \(O(\log(x+b+k+1))\) bits; the
selector bound belongs to fixed data. The determinant parameter
only selects the specified outer-label parity.

`positive_wall_chamber.py` evaluates (VW.14), emits every
integer matrix in (VW.15), and lazily enumerates witnesses.
It uses only fixed rational polynomials, bounded finite
differences and binomials of order at most five.

# The complete zero-twist wall in every ideal order

## G-033. A fixed positive formula for all orders on the wall

Let \(k,x,b,d\ge0\) with \(2b+x\ge5k\), and put
\[
\begin{aligned}
n&=d+b+x-k,\\
\lambda&=(d+3b+2x-5k,d+b+x,d+b+x,d+x,d).
\end{aligned}
\tag{ZW.1}
\]
For every \(\mu\vdash5\), the coefficient
\(p_{\mu,(n)}^\lambda\) has a fixed positive lattice-point
formula. The cases and their actual comparison maps are completely
specified in §5. In particular, this evaluates the entire wall
\(c=\lambda_2-\lambda_3=0\), for unbounded ideal order.

The new formulas are two adjacent chambers with respectively47
and34 selected polytopes, each with at most nine variables. They
complete the wall together with T054, the previously checked low
orders and the exact complementary-column maps. The overall formula
uses only the fixed formulas referenced in the exhaustive routing
table; it performs no input-sized representation computation.

## 1. Two parameter cones and their exact ideal modules

Define the following cones, with every displayed free parameter
nonnegative:
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c}
&k&x&b&t=3k-3-b\\\hline
A&(T+6+K)&T+X&2T+15+3K&T\\
B&(X+2S+8+K)&X&2X+5S+20+3K&X+S+1.
\end{array}
\tag{ZW.2}
\]
Their partition gaps \(2b+x-5k\) are respectively \(X+K\)
and \(K\), so every parameter in these cones gives a valid
partition. They satisfy \(0\le t<k\) and \(b>2(k-1)\).

Put \(a=b+x\), \(E=\mathfrak h_5\), \(F=\mathbb Q^2\),
and \(J_k=\bigcap_i(\ell_i\otimes F)^k\). The actual
normal substitution and Young extraction of G027/T049 give
\[
M_{a,b,k}=\operatorname{Hom}_{GL(F)}(S_{(a,b)}F,(J_k)_{a+b}),
\qquad
(S_\lambda\mathbb Q^5)_{(n^5)}
\simeq\operatorname{sgn}^{d+a}\otimes M_{a,b,k}.
\tag{ZW.3}
\]
The inverse is the specified balanced homogenization
\(u^{-k}F(v(X))\). The normal-order proof establishes its
polynomial extension. Equivalently the module before the sign is
\(H^0(\mathcal I_Z^k\otimes S_{(a,b)}Q)\), through the
same quotient substitution and exterior-column pairing.

The signed restriction complex now has its three-subset term as
well as the singleton and pair terms. Its quotient maps and
orientation lines are G027/FA13–17. Terms at size at least four
have degree at most \(4(k-1)<a+b\) and vanish. The ambient,
singleton and pair traces are exactly the finite expression in
T054/VW9–12: the straightening involution in VW6 only requires
\(b\ge k-1\), and the pair exterior comparison requires
\(b\ge2(k-1)\). Both hold here. Denote their sum by
\(P_g^\circ(a,b,k)\). This is a known finite phase polynomial,
with its actual restriction maps fixed by T054. The remaining
term is evaluated next.

## 2. The exact high-tail character of every triple intersection

Fix a stable three-subset of a permutation \(g\). Let
\(\eta\) be its selected cycle type and let
\(\epsilon\in\{1,-1\}\) be the eigenvalue on the
one-dimensional complementary standard module. The normal
polynomial is
\[
P_\eta(U,V)=\prod_{\ell\in\eta}
\left(\sum_{i,j\ge0,\ i+j<k}U^{\ell i}V^{\ell j}\right).
\]
Write \(p_{r,s}=[U^rV^s]P_\eta\). Its Schur coefficient
at \((p,q)\) is \(p_{p,q}-p_{p+1,q-1}\), by the
rank-two alternant, including absent-monomial zeros.

The one-dimensional skew Schur factor is nonzero exactly when
\((a,b)/(p,q)\) is a horizontal strip. The actual Pieri
projection to the complementary line gives the value
\(\epsilon^{a+b-p-q}\) in that case. Its inequalities are
\(a\ge p\ge b\ge q\ge0\). Since the normal degree is
at most \(3(k-1)\) and \(b>2(k-1)\), the condition
\(q\le b\), and every ordering condition in the following
sum, are automatic when \(p\ge b\).

Set \(R_\eta(z)=P_\eta(\epsilon z,\epsilon)\).
The exact Schur sum telescopes in \(p\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\sum_{p=b}^{a}\sum_{q\ge0}
 (p_{p,q}-p_{p+1,q-1})\epsilon^{a+b-p-q}\\
&\qquad=\epsilon^{a+b}
\left([z^b]R_\eta(z)-[z^{a+1}]R_\eta(z)\right).
\end{aligned}
\tag{ZW.4}
\]
Indeed after multiplying by \(\epsilon^{p+q}\), the
second summand becomes the same coefficient array with
\((p,q)\) replaced by \((p+1,q-1)\). Its range cancels
every interior \(p\), leaving precisely the two boundary
columns. Negative \(q\) entries are zero. This proves every
sign in (ZW.4) by a literal finite reindexing.

Let \(M=3(k-1)\). Reverse each cyclic normal factor at its
highest \(z\)-degree. The factor for a cycle of length
\(\ell\) contributes the phase \(\epsilon^{\ell(k-1)}\)
and the reversed coefficient series
\[
\sum_{r=0}^{k-1}\sum_{j=0}^{r}
\epsilon^{\ell(j-r)}z^{\ell r}.
\]
Through any degree \(h<k\), the upper bound \(r<k\)
can be removed. Reindexing \(r=j+l\) sums two geometric
series and gives
\[
A_{\eta,\epsilon}(h)=
[z^h]\prod_{\ell\in\eta}
\frac1{(1-z^\ell)(1-\epsilon^\ell z^\ell)},
\qquad A_{\eta,\epsilon}(h)=0\ (h<0).
\tag{ZW.5}
\]
Thus \([z^{M-h}]R_\eta=\epsilon^M A_{\eta,\epsilon}(h)\)
for every needed \(h<k\). In (ZW.4) the deficits are
\(t\) and \(t-x-1\), and both cones have \(t<k\).
The selected triple's trace, before its orientation, is therefore
\[
\boxed{
\epsilon^{x+k-1}
\left(A_{\eta,\epsilon}(t)
      -A_{\eta,\epsilon}(t-x-1)\right).}
\tag{ZW.6}
\]
The exponent uses \(a+b+M\equiv x+k-1\pmod2\).
In cone A the second argument is \(-X-1\) and its term
vanishes. In cone B that argument is exactly \(S\).

Multiplying (ZW.6) by \((-1)^{\#\operatorname{cyc}(\eta)}\)
and summing over the at most ten stable three-subsets gives the
full section trace:
\[
\boxed{
P_g=P_g^\circ+
\sum_{\substack{|A|=3\\gA=A}}
(-1)^{\#\operatorname{cyc}(g|A)}
\epsilon_A^{x+k-1}
\left(A_{\eta_A,\epsilon_A}(t)
-A_{\eta_A,\epsilon_A}(t-x-1)\right).}
\tag{ZW.7}
\]
The orientation factor is the complex sign times the actual
three-subset orientation character. Thus (ZW.7) is the trace of
(ZW.3) through the given exact complex.

## 3. Fixed polynomial positivity certificates in both cones

Every denominator root in (ZW.5) has order dividing the period
of the full permutation \(g\). There are at most six denominator
factors, so each sequence has degree at most five on a residue
class. Its proper rational generating function gives that
polynomial from index zero. Six initial values at
\(r,r+L,\ldots,r+5L\) determine it exactly. This is a fixed
arithmetic construction of (ZW.5), with no varying summation.

Substitute (ZW.2) into T054's finite formulas and (ZW.7).
For cone A the input variables are \(Z=(X,T,K)\), and for
cone B they are \(Z=(X,S,K)\). The complete class polynomials
have respective separate-degree bounds \((3,3,4)\) and
\((3,2,4)\), and total degree at most five. In class order
\(1^5,2111,221,311,32,41,5\), their total degrees in each
cone are \((5,3,2,1,0,0,0)\). All449 phase polynomials in
each cone are specified by the above finite construction and
stored in the corresponding certificate.

For a nonzero mixed step60 order \(\delta\), subtract
from \(\Delta^\delta P_1\) the sum, over nonidentity
classes, of the class size times the coefficientwise maximum of
the absolute coefficients of \(\Delta^\delta P_g\) over
all its phases. This is precisely the rational domination
construction in T054§4. The following exhaustive facts hold:

| Cone | Nonzero active orders | Lowest constant margin | Largest total order |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| A | 46 | 131670 | 5 |
| B | 33 | 8700 | 5 |

Every coefficient of every domination polynomial is nonnegative,
and every displayed constant margin is strictly positive. The
certificates record every polynomial and every order; the identity

expand affine substitutions, finite translations and rational
binomial coefficients exactly. Their parameter maps and phase keys
are part of the saved data.

The supporting files are `triple_defect_wall_check.py` with

with `INNER_TRIPLE_WALL_CHECK.json`. Each certificate is obtained

For every irreducible character, \(|\chi_\nu(g)|\le\dim[\nu]\)

For clarity, every order-zero residue value has also been evaluated

## 5. Exhaustive wall routing and every complementary morphism

The following disjoint decisions cover (ZW.1). First use G021
for k=0, G026 for k=1, G030 for k=2 and G032/c=0 for k=3.
Now let k≥4.

For b≤2k+3, take H=λ₁ and the complementary partition
\(\lambda^c=(H-\lambda_5,H-\lambda_4,H-\lambda_3,
H-\lambda_2,0)\). The actual exterior-column pairing into
\((\det\mathbb Q^5)^H\) identifies the balanced weights,
and transposes the outer label exactly when H is odd. Its new
parameters are
\[
x'=2b+x-5k,\quad b'=0,\quad c'=b,\quad d'=0,
\qquad k'=\max(0,b-k).
\tag{ZW.10}
\]
When b<k, the extra first-row degree is k−b; multiplying by
\(u^{k-b}\) is the exact stable-chart isomorphism. Thus this
case uses k'=0 with twist c'=b. For k≤b≤2k, the twist is
\(c'\ge2k'\), so G021 applies. For b=2k+s, s=1,2,3,
the twist is \(c'=2k'-s\), covered respectively by T045,
T050 and T051. This proves the complementary branch with all
normalizations and outer-label signs retained.

It remains to treat b≥2k+4. For b≥3k−2 use T054. Otherwise
put \(t=3k-3-b\); then \(0\le t\le k-7\).
For x≥t, the inverse cone-A parameters are
\[
(X,T,K)=(x-t,t,k-t-6),
\]
all nonnegative. For x<t, the inverse cone-B parameters are
\[
(X,S,K)=(x,t-x-1,2b+x-5k),
\]
all nonnegative by the partition inequality. Direct substitution
in (ZW.2) recovers the original x,b,k in both cases. These
cases exhaust every remaining integer point. This proves the
complete-wall statement, with exact fixed positive formulas
on each branch.

For an arbitrary partition on the wall \(\lambda_2=\lambda_3\),
first set \(e=\max(0,n-\lambda_2)\),
\(n^0=n-e\), and
\(\lambda^0=(\lambda_1-5e,\lambda_2,\lambda_3,\lambda_4,\lambda_5)\).
The stable chart T032 identifies the original balanced module with
this one by multiplication by \(u^e\), with unchanged outer label.
The partition \(\lambda^0\) is valid: at positive e its first-row
gap is \(2\lambda_2-\lambda_4-\lambda_5\ge0\).
Its parameters \(d=\lambda_5,x=\lambda_4-\lambda_5,
b=\lambda_3-\lambda_4,k=\max(0,\lambda_2-n)\) are exactly (ZW.1).
This supplies the whole initial stable range as well.

The same result evaluates the entire second central wall
\(\lambda_3=\lambda_4\). Take \(H=\lambda_1\) and apply the
perfect complementary-column pairing above. The complementary
partition has \(\lambda^c_2=H-\lambda_4=H-\lambda_3=\lambda^c_3\),
so it is on the already completed wall. Its degree is \(H-n\),
and its outer label is transposed exactly when H is odd. Thus
both central equal-row walls have fixed positive formulas through
specified determinant and stable-chart morphisms.

The unified evaluator `zero_twist_all_positive.py` implements
these decisions, passes the complementary label and parameters
to the previously proved positive evaluators, and uses (ZW.8)
on the two new cones. It returns the original partition, exact
coefficient, selected branch and every requested polytope matrix.

## 1. Exact section and restriction maps

Write \(a=b+x,E=\mathfrak h_5,F=\mathbb Q^3\) and

\simeq\operatorname{sgn}^{d+a+1}\otimes M_{a,b,k}.

\]

normal-order comparison proves its polynomial extension.

below belongs to this specified actual module.

Herea+b+3≥5k. G027's exact signed restriction complex has

with at least four selected points is zero in this degree,
because four independent block directions give quotient degree
at most4(k−1). A three-subset has a one-dimensional remaining
standard module. Its skew Schur factor can be nonzero only

\longrightarrow C_1\longrightarrow C_2\longrightarrow0.

This uses the all-degree product/intersection theorem and its

## 2. The singleton term and its exact straightening

For a selected singleton, the complementary standard moduleV

# The complete first adjacent central walls

## G-034. A fixed positive formula for both central gaps equal to one

Let \(x,b,k,d\ge0\) and \(2b+x+3\ge5k\). Put
\[
\begin{aligned}
n&=d+b+x+1-k,\\
\lambda&=(d+3b+2x+4-5k,d+b+x+1,d+b+x,d+x,d).
\end{aligned}
\tag{OW.1}
\]
For every \(\mu\vdash5\), the coefficient
\(p_{\mu,(n)}^\lambda\) has a fixed positive lattice-point
formula. The disjoint routing in §5 covers every parameter in
(OW.1), including every ideal order. The same formula, through
the explicit stable and complementary-column maps below, evaluates
every partition with \(\lambda_2-\lambda_3=1\) or
\(\lambda_3-\lambda_4=1\). Partitions with more than five rows
have coefficient zero by the Schur antisymmetrizer on \(\mathbb Q^5\);
the formulas below use the five-row padding of every other partition.

The two new cones use respectively47 and34 disjoint polytopes,
each with at most nine integer variables. T055 covers the upper
chamber and T056 its adjacent strip. All remaining routes use
the already proved fixed positive formulas. Every coefficient
and inequality in a chosen formula is obtained from fixed data;
there is no representation calculation whose size depends on
the input. The new theorem is proved below, together with the
rank-three triple-intersection identity needed for its maps.

## 1. The actual section module and two lower cones

Put \(a=b+x\), \(E=\mathfrak h_5\), \(F=\mathbb Q^3\),
and \(J_k=\bigcap_i(\ell_i\otimes F)^k\). The normal-order
and balanced homogenization maps of G027/T049 give
\[
\begin{aligned}
M&=\operatorname{Hom}_{GL(F)}
 \bigl(S_{(a+1,b+1,1)}F,(J_k)_{a+b+3}\bigr),\\
(S_\lambda\mathbb Q^5)_{(n^5)}
 &\simeq\operatorname{sgn}^{d+a+1}\otimes M.
\end{aligned}
\tag{OW.2}
\]
The inverse map is \(u^{-k}F(v(X))\), whose extension is
the proved normal-order statement. This is the same module as
T055/OT3, retaining its determinant twist and literal quotient
arrows in the oriented restriction complex.

Define the following cones with every free coordinate nonnegative:
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c}
&k&x&b&\tau=3k-5-b\\\hline
A&T+7+K&T+X&2T+16+3K&T\\
B&X+2S+9+K&X&2X+5S+21+3K&X+S+1.
\end{array}
\tag{OW.3}
\]
Their partition gaps \(2b+x+3-5k\) are respectively
\(X+K\) and \(K\). Both have \(b+1\ge2k\).
The ambient, singleton and pair terms are therefore exactly
T055/OT6–9: the singleton involution requires \(b\ge k-1\),
and the pair comparison requires \(b+1>2(k-1)\).
Denote their sum by \(P_g^\circ(a,b,k)\). Terms with at
least four selected points vanish: four independent truncated
blocks have degree at most \(4(k-1)<a+b+3\).
The remaining triple term is computed next.

## 2. A complete rank-three triple telescope

The following calculation holds for every \(c\ge0\),
\(a=b+x\), \(k\ge1\), and \(b+c\ge2k\). It is used
here at \(c=1\). Fix a stable selected triple, its cycle
type \(\eta\vdash3\), and the eigenvalue
\(\epsilon\in\{1,-1\}\) of its complementary standard
line. Let \(N=a+b+3c\), \(M_0=3(k-1)\), and
\(t=M_0-b\). Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
P_\eta(U,V,W)&=
 \prod_{\ell\in\eta}\ 
 \sum_{i+j+h<k}U^{\ell i}V^{\ell j}W^{\ell h},\\
A_{\eta,\epsilon}(r)&=[z^r]
 \prod_{\ell\in\eta}
 [(1-z^\ell)(1-\epsilon^\ell z^\ell)]^{-1},\\
h_\eta(c)&=[z^c]\frac{1-z}{\prod_{\ell\in\eta}(1-z^\ell)}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{OW.4}
\]
Coefficients with negative indices in these power series are zero. The normal
Schur coefficient of shape \(\rho=(p,q,r)\) is the coefficient
of \(U^pV^qW^r\) in
\[
P_\eta(U,V,W)(1-V/U)(1-W/U)(1-W/V).
\]
This is the three-row alternant identity. The actual complementary
Pieri projection contributes \(\epsilon^{N-|\rho|}\)
exactly for
\[
a+c\ge p\ge b+c\ge q\ge c\ge r\ge0.
\tag{OW.5}
\]
Its target is the weight \(N-|\rho|\) in the specified line.
These are the horizontal-strip inequalities for
\((a+c,b+c,c)/\rho\), with the normal Young projector
retained.

Set \(P_\epsilon=P_\eta(\epsilon U,\epsilon V,\epsilon W)\)
and \(F_\epsilon=P_\epsilon(1-V/U)(1-W/U)\).
Every normal weight has total degree at most \(M_0\). For
\(p\ge b+c\ge2k\), the total remaining degree is at most
\(k-3\). Thus the upper bound \(q\le b+c\) is automatic;
the other dominance conditions follow from \(q\ge c\ge r\)
and this same degree bound. The coefficient arrays of
\(F_\epsilon\) have the identical total-degree bound, even
though their exponent of \(U\) can be negative.

Write \(f_{p,q,r}=[U^pV^qW^r]F_\epsilon\). It is symmetric
in \(q,r\), and has nonnegative exponents of \(V,W\).
For fixed \(p\), the exact finite cancellation is
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{q\ge c,\ 0\le r\le c}
 (f_{p,q,r}-f_{p,q+1,r-1})
 &=\sum_{q\ge c}f_{p,q,c}
   +\sum_{r=0}^{c-1}f_{p,c,r}\\
 &=\sum_{q\ge0}f_{p,q,c}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{OW.6}
\]
The last equality is precisely the symmetry of the two boundary
sums; negative indices contribute zero. Consequently the full
selected Schur sum equals
\[
\epsilon^N[W^c]
 \bigl([U^{b+c}]-[U^{a+c+1}]\bigr)
 P_\epsilon(U,1,W)(1-W/U).
\tag{OW.7}
\]
Here summation over \(p=b+c,\ldots,a+c\) cancels the factor
\(1-1/U\), leaving its two boundary columns. This proves
every sign by literal coefficient reindexing.

Reverse the exponent of \(U\) at \(M_0\), writing \(z=U^{-1}\).
For a cycle of length \(\ell\), put
\(i=k-1-j-h-s\). Its contribution is
\(\epsilon^{\ell(k-1)}U^{\ell(k-1)}\) times the sum of
\(z^{\ell j}(Wz)^{\ell h}(\epsilon z)^{\ell s}\)
over \(j,h,s\ge0\), \(j+h+s<k\). Every required
reversal deficit is at most \(M_0-b-c\le k-3<k\).
Within these coefficients the last truncation can be removed
and each factor is exactly a product of three geometric series.
Multiplication by \(1-Wz\) now gives
\[
[W^c]\frac{1-Wz}{\prod_{\ell\in\eta}(1-(Wz)^\ell)}
 =z^c h_\eta(c).
\]
The other two series give \(A_{\eta,\epsilon}\). Substitution
into (OW.7) proves the exact selected-triple trace
\[
\boxed{
\epsilon^{x+c+k-1}h_\eta(c)
 \left(A_{\eta,\epsilon}(t-2c)
       -A_{\eta,\epsilon}(t-x-2c-1)\right).}
\tag{OW.8}
\]
The phase is \(\epsilon^{N+M_0}\), which is the displayed
power because their exponents differ by an even integer.
This calculation also covers empty ranges: the two boundary
coefficients and their negative-index conventions give zero.

At \(c=1\), \(h_\eta(1)=m_1(\eta)-1\) and
\(t-2=\tau\). The signed restriction trace is therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
P_g={}&P_g^\circ+
\sum_{\substack{|A|=3\\gA=A}}
 (-1)^{\#\operatorname{cyc}(g|A)}
 \epsilon_A^{x+k}(m_1(g|A)-1)\\
&\hspace{19mm}\cdot
 \left(A_{\eta_A,\epsilon_A}(\tau)
       -A_{\eta_A,\epsilon_A}(\tau-x-1)\right).
\end{aligned}
\tag{OW.9}
\]
The sign is the complex sign multiplied by the selected-triple
orientation. In cone A the second argument is \(-X-1\);
in cone B it is \(S\). Formula (OW.9) thus computes the
character of the actual module (OW.2).

six root-of-unity denominator factors; partial fractions give
the residue polynomial from index zero. Six values on each
residue class determine it exactly. This is fixed arithmetic.

\]

The invariant Hermitian bound \(|\chi_\nu(g)|\le\dim[\nu]\)

## 4. The positive formula and its exact support

The effective label is \(\nu=\mu\) for even \(d+b+x+1\),
and \(\nu=\mu'\) for odd \(d+b+x+1\). Write the cone
coordinates \(Z=r+60q\), \(0\le r_i<60\), and let
\(\mathcal D\) consist of zero and its active orders. Define
the fixed nonnegative integers
\[
C_{\nu,r,\delta}=\sum_{0\le h\le\delta}
 (-1)^{|\delta|-|h|}\binom\delta h f_\nu(r+60h).
\]
All evaluation coordinates are bounded by359. Polynomial
Newton expansion gives
\[
\boxed{p_{\mu,(n)}^\lambda=
 \sum_{\delta\in\mathcal D}C_{\nu,r,\delta}
 \prod_{i=1}^3\binom{q_i}{\delta_i}.}
\tag{OW.11}
\]
For each positive constant, take the bounded integer polytope
\[
60q_i=Z_i-r_i,\quad q_i\ge0,\quad0\le y<C_{\nu,r,\delta},
\qquad0\le z_{i1}<\cdots<z_{i,\delta_i}<q_i.
\tag{OW.12}
\]
Replace each strict inequality by an integer gap of one. The
selector and increasing subsets give a literal bijection with
the summand in (OW.11). There are at most \(4+|\delta|\le9\)
variables, and47 or34 disjoint order tags. Their input bit size
is logarithmic in the parameters; all other data are fixed.

Every first-order difference is strictly positive. Thus a zero
must lie in the base residue cube. The complete base check shows

with effective labels \((5)\) and \((1^5)\). Cone B has
no zero for any label or parameter. These facts give the full

## 5. Exhaustive routing, stable range and the second wall

Use G021 at \(k=0\), T045 at \(k=1,c=1\), T051 at
\(k=2,c=1\), and G032 at \(k=3,c=1\). Let \(k\ge4\).
For \(b\le2k+1\), take \(H=\lambda_1\) and the
complement \(\lambda^c=(H-\lambda_5,H-\lambda_4,
H-\lambda_3,H-\lambda_2,0)\). The perfect exterior-column
pairing into \((\det\mathbb Q^5)^H\) gives degree \(H-n\)
and transposes \(\mu\) exactly when \(H\) is odd. The
new parameters, after stable first-row removal, are
\[
x'=2b+x+3-5k,\quad b'=1,\quad c'=b,\quad d'=0,
\qquad k'=\max(0,b+1-k).
\tag{OW.13}
\]
At \(b+1<k\), the removed stable power is \(k-b-1\);
its actual inverse is multiplication by \(u^{k-b-1}\).
For \(b\le2k-2\), \(c'\ge2k'\) and G021 applies.
For \(b=2k-2+s\), \(s=1,2,3\), one has
\(c'=2k'-s\), treated respectively by T045, T050 and T051.

It remains that \(b\ge2k+2\). Use T055 at \(b\ge3k-3\),
and T056 at \(b=3k-4\). In the latter branch the two
inequalities imply \(k\ge6\), within T056's proved range.
Otherwise \(\tau=3k-5-b\ge0\). The two inverse parameter
maps are
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
x\ge\tau&(X,T,K)=(x-\tau,\tau,k-\tau-7),\\
x<\tau&(X,S,K)=(x,\tau-x-1,2b+x+3-5k).
\end{array}
\tag{OW.14}
\]
Every coordinate is nonnegative: in the first row
\(K=b-2k-2\), and in the second it is the partition gap.
Substitution into (OW.3) recovers the original parameters.
This exhausts every integer point of (OW.1).

For an original partition with \(\lambda_2=\lambda_3+1\)
and degree \(5n\), put \(e=\max(0,n-\lambda_2)\),
\(n^0=n-e\), and
\(\lambda^0=(\lambda_1-5e,\lambda_2,\lambda_3,
\lambda_4,\lambda_5)\). At positive \(e\), its first gap is
\(3\lambda_2-\lambda_3-\lambda_4-\lambda_5\ge0\).
T032's actual stable-chart isomorphism is multiplication by
\(u^e\), with unchanged outer label. The normalized partition
has the parameters in (OW.1). For
\(\lambda_3=\lambda_4+1\), the perfect complementary-column
map above makes \(\lambda^c_2-\lambda^c_3=1\); apply the
first-wall formula with its specified determinant parity. This
proves the whole statement for both adjacent walls.

## 1. The complete triple telescope

Letk≥1,c≥0,x≥0,a=b+x andb+c≥2k. Fix a selected
three-subset with cycle typeη⊢3 and complementary-line
eigenvalueε=±1. Its normal trace polynomial is

\[
P(U,V,W)=\prod_{\ell\in\eta}
\sum_{i+j+h<k}U^{\ell i}V^{\ell j}W^{\ell h}.
\]

PutM=3(k−1),N=a+b+3c. The actual Young projection to
normal shapeρ=(p,q,r) has trace given by the coefficient
ofU^pV^qW^r in

\[
P(U,V,W)(1-V/U)(1-W/U)(1-W/V).
\]

The complementary-line Pieri map is present exactly for
a+c≥p≥b+c≥q≥c≥r≥0, and has valueε^{N−p−q−r}.
DefinePε=P(εU,εV,εW) and
F=Pε(1−V/U)(1−W/U). The latter is symmetric inV,W,
has nonnegative exponents of these two variables, and
retains the total-degree boundM.

Forp≥b+c≥2k, every nonzero coefficient hasq+r≤k−3.
Thusq≤b+c is automatic. Writef_{p,q,r} for the
coefficients ofF. The exact inner sum is

\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{q\ge c,\ 0\le r\le c}
 (f_{p,q,r}-f_{p,q+1,r-1})
&=\sum_{q\ge c}f_{p,q,c}
  +\sum_{r=0}^{c-1}f_{p,c,r}\\
&=\sum_{q\ge0}f_{p,q,c}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{RT.1}
\]

The second equality uses the actualV/W symmetry, so both
boundary pieces are included. The negative-index entries
are zero. After this cancellation the remaining factor
1−1/U telescopes in p, giving

\[
\epsilon^N[W^c]
\bigl([U^{b+c}]-[U^{a+c+1}]\bigr)
P_\epsilon(U,1,W)(1-W/U).
\tag{RT.2}
\]

For a cycle of lengthℓ, reverse theU exponent atℓ(k−1)
and putz=U^{-1}. Writingi=k−1−j−h−s gives the phase
ε^{ℓ(k−1)} and the monomial
z^{ℓj}(Wz)^{ℓh}(εz)^{ℓs}. The needed reversal deficits
are at mostM−b−c≤k−3<k; hence the boundj+h+s<k
can be removed in these coefficients. Each cyclic factor
is exactly the product of three geometric series.

The remaining W-coefficient is

\[
[W^c]\frac{1-Wz}{\prod_{\ell\in\eta}(1-(Wz)^\ell)}
=z^c h_\eta(c),\qquad
h_\eta(c)=[u^c]\frac{1-u}{\prod_{\ell\in\eta}(1-u^\ell)}.
\tag{RT.3}
\]

Definet=M−b and
Aηε(h)=[z^h]∏ℓ[(1−z^ℓ)(1−ε^ℓz^ℓ)]^{-1},
with negative-index coefficients zero. Equations (RT.2)–(RT.3)
therefore give the exact selected-triple trace

\[
\epsilon^{x+c+k-1}h_\eta(c)
\bigl(A_{\eta,\epsilon}(t-2c)
      -A_{\eta,\epsilon}(t-x-2c-1)\bigr).
\tag{RT.4}
\]

The phase isε^{N+M}, equal to the displayed exponent
modulo two. Multiplying by(−1)^{#cycles(η)} includes
the restriction-complex sign and its orientation line.
All steps are finite coefficient reindexings of the actual
normal Young and complementary Pieri projections. Atk=1,2
the required deficits are negative; these equations give zero
without an additional endpoint convention.

This independently proves the exact algebraic identity
used in G034. Its source-side coefficient meaning is fixed
