# The complete normalized region below the ideal order

## G-035. Every normalized coefficient with c<k

Let \(x,b,k,c,d\) be nonnegative integers satisfying
\[
c<k,\qquad b+c\ge2k,\qquad2b+x+3c\ge5k.
\tag{NB.1}
\]
Set
\[
\begin{aligned}
n&=d+b+x+c-k,\\
\lambda&=(d+3b+2x+4c-5k,d+b+x+c,d+b+x,d+x,d).
\end{aligned}
\tag{NB.2}
\]
For every \(\mu\vdash5\), \(p_{\mu,(n)}^\lambda\) has a
fixed positive formula with at most152 selected bounded integer
polytopes, each with at most eleven variables. The complete disjoint
routing is in §5. It treats every point of (NB.1), including small
orders and every boundary. Its formulas require only fixed rational
polynomial data, residue selection and bounded-order binomial
evaluation; no input-sized representation computation occurs.

The new ingredients are two four-variable cones, three adjacent
three-variable strips and six low-order boundary pieces. Their actual
restriction maps, all phase formulas and all positivity certificates
are specified below. G033 and G034 supply the completed \(c=0,1\)
routes, while T058 supplies the four-variable upper cone.

## 1. Exact parameters and the full restricted character

Put
\[
C=c,\qquad R=k-c\ge1,\qquad b_0=b-c.
\]
Then (NB.1) is exactly
\[
b_0\ge2R,\qquad2b_0+x\ge5R.
\tag{NB.3}
\]
These equalities follow by the displayed integral substitution and
its inverse \((c,k,b)=(C,C+R,C+b_0)\). They do not change the
original module. With \(a=b+x\), \(F=\mathbb Q^3\), and
\(J_k=\bigcap_i(\ell_i\otimes F)^k\), its exact form is
\[
\begin{aligned}
M&=\operatorname{Hom}_{GL(F)}
 \bigl(S_{(a+c,b+c,c)}F,(J_k)_{2b+x+3c}\bigr),\\
(S_\lambda\mathbb Q^5)_{(n^5)}
&\simeq\operatorname{sgn}^{d+b+x+c}\otimes M.
\end{aligned}
\tag{NB.4}
\]
The maps are G027/T049's normal substitution, rational Young
projection and balanced inverse \(u^{-k}F(v(X))\), with its proved
polynomial extension. The oriented restriction complex has literal
quotient maps. Terms of size at least four vanish by degree
\(4(k-1)<2b+x+3c\).

Let \(P_g^\circ\) denote its ambient, singleton and pair trace.
The singleton is exactly T058/GU5 and T057's proved \(c<k\)
formula. The pair is T058/GU6–9, including the explicit exterior
minor maps, rational highest-space isomorphism and selected-slot
permutations. Their proofs require only \(c<k\) and
\(b+c\ge2k\), not the upper-cone inequality.

For a stable selected triple, let \(\eta\vdash3\) be its cycle
type and \(\epsilon=\pm1\) its complementary-line eigenvalue.
Define \(A_{\eta,\epsilon}\) and \(h_\eta\) by G034/OW4,
with zero coefficients at negative indices. Set
\(\tau=3R-3-b_0\). G034's complete rank-three telescope gives
the exact full trace
\[
\begin{aligned}
P_g={}&P_g^\circ+
\sum_{\substack{|A|=3\\gA=A}}
(-1)^{\#\operatorname{cyc}(g|A)}
\epsilon_A^{x+R-1}h_{\eta_A}(C)\\
&\hspace{16mm}\cdot
\left(A_{\eta_A,\epsilon_A}(\tau)
      -A_{\eta_A,\epsilon_A}(\tau-x-1)\right).
\end{aligned}
\tag{NB.5}
\]
Indeed its two deficits become
\(3k-3-b-2c=\tau\) and \(\tau-x-1\), and its phase
\(\epsilon^{x+c+k-1}=\epsilon^{x+R-1}\).
The factor \(h_\eta(C)\) is \(C+1\) for \(\eta=111\),
the even-degree indicator for \(\eta=21\), and the periodic
sequence \(1,-1,0\) for \(\eta=3\). These follow directly
from its printed rational generating function.

Every term in (NB.5) is therefore the trace of the specified
normal Young and complementary-line Pieri maps, with its actual
orientation. The only remaining steps are exact rational
polynomial evaluation and positive finite differences.

## 2. The full three-row singleton simplex

LetV be the complementary standard module of dimension
three. The actual one-slot Pieri projection gives the

# A complete fixed positive formula in outer degree five

## G-036. Every Schur plethysm coefficient with outer size five

For every \(n\ge0\), every \(\mu\vdash5\), and every partition
\(\lambda\vdash5n\), the coefficient
\[
p_{\mu,(n)}^\lambda
=[S_\lambda V:S_\mu(\operatorname{Sym}^n V)]
\tag{CF.1}
\]
has an explicit positive formula using at most152 selected bounded
rational polytopes, each with at most eleven integer variables.
All matrices, constants, residue rules and branch maps are fixed
and specified by the constructions below. Their description sizes
are polynomial in the binary input length. The coefficient itself
is evaluated by a fixed number of arithmetic operations and
binomial coefficients of order at most six, hence in polynomial
bit complexity.

The statement applies in every ambient dimension at least the
length of \(\lambda\); the usual Schur dimension zeros apply in
smaller dimensions. It includes every outer label and every
determinant parity. The full support was already determined in
G031; the present theorem gives the positive value of every
coefficient, including the previously remaining interior regions.
No general elimination, character summation of input-dependent
length, or uncomputed cohomology rank occurs in its evaluator.

## 1. The actual balanced module and the length-zero cases

The exact Cauchy and tensor-word maps of G015 identify (CF.1)
with the multiplicity of the Specht module \([\mu]\) in
\[
B_{\lambda,n}=(S_\lambda\mathbb Q^5)_{(n,n,n,n,n)},
\tag{CF.2}
\]
with its actual action by permutation matrices. The rational
Young projector specifies the outer Schur summand. These are
the same maps used in G027/T049 and every formula below.

For \(\ell(\lambda)>5\) the coefficient is zero. Indeed the
actual idempotent image \(S_\mu(\operatorname{Sym}^n V)\)
is a summand of \((\operatorname{Sym}^nV)^{\otimes5}\).
Successive one-row Pieri inclusions add five horizontal strips.
Each strip can create at most one new row: two new rows would
both add a box in their first column, contrary to horizontality.
Thus no Young component with more than five rows occurs.
Its positive formula is the empty disjoint union.

For every other partition, pad by zeros to five rows. At
\(n=0\), (CF.2) is the trivial line; its multiplicity is one
for \(\mu=(5)\) and zero for the other six labels. This also
agrees with the formulas below.

## 2. Stable first-row removal through its exact section map

Initially put \(k_{\rm raw}=\lambda_2-n\). For
\(k_{\rm raw}\le0\), let
\[
e=n-\lambda_2,\qquad n^0=n-e=\lambda_2,\qquad
\lambda^0=(\lambda_1-5e,\lambda_2,\lambda_3,\lambda_4,\lambda_5).
\tag{CF.3}
\]
The first gap is
\[
\lambda^0_1-\lambda_2
=3\lambda_2-\lambda_3-\lambda_4-\lambda_5\ge0,
\]
so \(\lambda^0\) is a valid partition of \(5n^0\).
T032's stable-chart map is multiplication by \(u^e\), where
\(u\) is the product of the five first-column coordinates.
It is invariant under \(S_5\), adds \(5e\) to the first
right weight and \(e\) to each row weight, and identifies
\(B_{\lambda^0,n^0}\) with \(B_{\lambda,n}\).
The inverse is division by \(u^e\); T032's proved balanced
normal-order statement establishes its polynomial extension.
Thus this step retains the exact module and outer label.

The resulting order is zero and G021 applies. For positive
initial order, use the following complementary-column map when
needed, then apply (CF.3) to that partition only when its raw
order is negative. This requires at most one complement and
one stable removal.

## 3. The determinant complement and the normalized order

For a five-row partition put
\[
d=\lambda_5,\quad x=\lambda_4-\lambda_5,\quad
b=\lambda_3-\lambda_4,\quad c=\lambda_2-\lambda_3,
\quad k=\lambda_2-n.
\tag{CF.4}
\]
At \(k\ge0\), the weight sum gives exactly
\[
\begin{aligned}
n&=d+b+x+c-k,\\
\lambda&=(d+3b+2x+4c-5k,d+b+x+c,d+b+x,d+x,d),\\
g:=\lambda_1-\lambda_2&=2b+x+3c-5k\ge0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{CF.5}
\]

Take \(H=\lambda_1\) and
\[
\lambda^c=(H-\lambda_5,H-\lambda_4,H-\lambda_3,
H-\lambda_2,0),\qquad n^c=H-n.
\tag{CF.6}
\]
The exterior-column perfect pairing
\(\Lambda^jE\otimes\Lambda^{5-j}E\to\det E\),
followed by the rational Young projections, gives
\[
B_{\lambda^c,n^c}
\simeq (B_{\lambda,n})^*\otimes\operatorname{sgn}^H.
\tag{CF.7}
\]
Its maps and determinant sign are those proved in G015 and
used explicitly in G033/G034. To identify a rational finite
group module with its dual, average the positive rational
tensor dot product over \(S_5\) and use its nonsingular Gram
matrix and inverse. Thus duality in (CF.7) is an actual
equivariant isomorphism. Tensoring a Specht module with sign
is the column/row Young comparison \([\mu]\otimes\operatorname{sgn}
\simeq[\mu']\). Consequently the outer label is transposed
exactly when \(H\) is odd.

Direct substitution in (CF.4) gives the complete new dictionary:
\[
x^c=g,\quad b^c=c,\quad c^c=b,\quad d^c=0,
\qquad k^c_{\rm raw}=b+c-k.
\tag{CF.8}
\]
For positive initial \(k\), take the complement exactly when
\(b+c-k<k\). Its order after the proved stable removal is
\[
k^c=\max(0,b+c-k).
\]
For a negative complementary raw order the removed stable power
is \(e=k-b-c\). The complementary first-row gap after removal
is
\[
x-5e=g+3b+2c\ge0,
\]
which explicitly checks the endpoint partition. Its outer label
is the one already specified by (CF.7), with no additional sign.

After this single decision the retained parameters always satisfy
\[
k\ge0,\qquad b+c\ge2k,
\qquad2b+x+3c\ge5k.
\tag{CF.9}
\]
Without complement, the decision inequality is exactly
\(b+c\ge2k\). With complement and positive new order,
the old strict inequality gives
\(b+c>2(b+c-k)\). At new order zero the inequality is
automatic. All maps have been specified, so (CF.9) is a
normalization of the actual multiplicity through (CF.3) and
(CF.7), including all signs and boundary cases.

## 4. Three exhaustive positive-formula providers

On the domain (CF.9), use the following disjoint decisions:

| Parameter range | Exact provider | Maximum selected polytopes | Maximum variables |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| c≥2k | G021, with delta=c−2k | 122 | 11 |
| k≤c<2k | T059, HT1–12 | 151 | 11 |
| c<k | G035, NB1–15 | 152 | 11 |

These alternatives exhaust every nonnegative \(c,k\).
The first includes \(k=0\). The second has exactly the inverse
parameters
\[
(X,B,K,U)=(x,b-2k+c,2k-c-1,c-k),
\]
all nonnegative by (CF.9) and its stated range. The third is
precisely G035's domain. G035's explicit lower-cone, strip and
small-order inverses exhaust it; its \(c=0,1\) providers are
the completed whole-wall formulas G033/G034. Thus no additional
region or limiting case is left to evaluate.

Each provider proves an exact formula
\[
\sum_{\delta\in\mathcal D}
D_{\nu,r,\delta}\prod_i\binom{q_i}{\delta_i},
\qquad D_{\nu,r,\delta}\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0},
\tag{CF.10}
\]
with its residue rules, literal integer matrices and a bijection
between each summand and its selector/increasing-subset choices.
G021 also fixes every bounded coefficient explicitly. The
positive-order constants in T059/G035 follow from their complete
rational domination certificates; their zero-order constants
are multiplicities of the actual normal module. The entire
construction therefore has proved nonnegative constants.
The largest selected tag count is152 and the largest variable
count is eleven, as in the table.

The parameter changes (CF.3)–(CF.8) and all inverse branch maps
use affine integer expressions, parity, inequalities and maximum
with zero. Each parameter is bounded by a fixed multiple of
\(n+1\). Each Newton order is at most six in total, and all
fixed evaluation arguments are bounded constants. Arithmetic
on these expressions and binomial coefficients consequently
has polynomial bit complexity in the binary input length.
Every polytope witness has at most eleven integer coordinates
and a polynomial bit length, with fixed linear constraint data.
This proves both the positive-description assertion and the
stated exact evaluation bound.

## 5. Executable realization and independent checks

`outer_five_positive.py` accepts an original partition and outer
label. Its `partition_route` records the original degree, the
complement decision and height, the stable power, the normalized
partition, all six physical arguments, and the selected provider.
For a G035 branch it also returns its exact lower-region decision.
`coefficient_partition` evaluates the positive formula, and
`partition_polytopes` exports the corresponding literal matrices.
The same module exposes a physical-parameter entry point without
requiring the caller to normalize first.

The zero-length and degree-zero conventions are explicit. The
program validates partition order and nonnegativity, divisibility
of its size by five, and the outer label. It asserts the exact
shape identity (CF.5) and both inequalities in (CF.9) after the
actual transports. The finite provider computations use the
fixed rational data; they do not call a general plethysm oracle.

The separate checker `check_outer_five_positive.py` compares the
output against the original balanced cycle/Pieri calculation at
original partition inputs. Its cases cover all three top-level
providers, every G035 boundary, both lower cones, both entire
small-twist walls, determinant shifts, complementary partitions
and first-row extensions. It also checks exported provider
bounds, all seven overlength zeros and all seven degree-zero
values. The exact counts and outcomes are saved in
`OUTER_FIVE_POSITIVE_ROUTING_RECEIPT.json`. The whole-proof
readings and independent certificate reconstructions underlying
G021, G033–G035 and T058–T059 are recorded separately.

## 6. Grothendieck dictionary and the exact remaining uniform gate

The input is the Schur-operation class of
\(S_\mu(\operatorname{Sym}^n\mathcal V)\) on a locally free
sheaf. The integral tensor and Schur constructions define its
scheme-theoretic object over \(\mathbb Z\); the multiplicity
statement is taken on the characteristic-zero generic fiber.
The rational Young and Gram projectors have their explicit
finite matrices and denominators. They spread over the
corresponding localized integral base. No assertion about
constant multiplicity across unspecified residue characteristics
is used.

The tensor-word and weight maps identify its generic-fiber
representation class with (CF.2). Stable multiplication and the
perfect exterior-column pairing are the actual arrows (CF.3)
and (CF.7). G027/T049 then gives the exact coherent section
module, its oriented quotient complex and its normal Young
extraction. T058/G035/T059 specify every singleton, pair and
triple comparison and every finite coefficient reindexing.
The selector/subset maps in (CF.10) are literal finite-set
bijections with the displayed lattice points. Thus each stage
has its exact comparison, retaining the original Schur class.

The coordinate/Proj and section maps have the EGA II2.4.1–2.4.2
and2.5.2/2.5.4 locators; the frame and comodule maps are
SGA3 I4.5/4.7.2–4.7.3; the representation-to-associated-sheaf
K0 morphism is SGA6 VI3.3. The λ and Schur operations are
SGA6 V4.2,4.4,4.8–4.9. Cote133/028 is carried by A012's
explicit tensor-word, torus-weight and Young maps. These are
the same proved dictionaries used by the component formulas,
now joined by the complete determinant/stable routing.

The remaining positive-description gate is uniformity in a
varying outer degree. G009–G011 supply the actual finite
algebra maps and terminating positive counts there; the
polynomial bounds on their Hilbert bases, Reynolds lists and
elimination remain the stated gate. The present fixed-outer
theorem closes the full outer-five coefficient row and leaves
that exact varying-degree requirement explicitly recorded.


# Complete nonvanishing for outer degree five

## G-031. Every shape, every outer label and every inner degree

Let \(n\ge0\), \(\mu\vdash5\), and \(\lambda\vdash5n\).
The following fixed procedure decides exactly whether
\(p_{\mu,(n)}^\lambda\) is positive. It uses a fixed table of344
integer vectors, the explicit strict-chamber rule G028, and a
bounded number of integer operations. No plethysm coefficient
remains to be evaluated by this decision procedure.

For length greater than five the coefficient is zero: the actual
Young projector embeds \(S_\mu(\operatorname{Sym}^n V)\)
in \((\operatorname{Sym}^n V)^{\otimes5}\), and repeated Pieri
allows at most five rows. Otherwise pad to five entries and put
\[
d=\lambda_5,\qquad g_i=\lambda_i-\lambda_{i+1}\quad(1\le i\le4).
\tag{NW.1}
\]
Use the effective label \(\nu=\mu\) at even \(d\) and
\(\nu=\mu^t\) at odd \(d\).

For \(g=0\), the only nonzero effective label is \((5)\),
with multiplicity one. For all four gaps positive, G028 gives
the exact rule: the five middle labels always occur; both extreme
labels vanish on \(g=(L,1,1,1)\) and \(g=(1,1,1,L)\),
\(L\ge1\), \(L\equiv1\pmod5\); the effective trivial label
also vanishes at \(g=(1,2,2,1),(2,1,1,2)\). There are no
other strict-chamber zeros.

For every other gap vector use the following normal form. Write
\(g=(a,b,c,e)\), and first test the first line:
Set \(L_1=\max(1,3b+2c+e)\) and
\(L_4=\max(1,a+2b+3c)\). Then
\[
N(g)=
\begin{cases}
(L_1+(a-L_1)\bmod10,b,c,e),&a\ge L_1,\\
(a,b,c,L_4+(e-L_4)\bmod10),&e\ge L_4,\\
g,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\tag{NW.2}
\]
The first applicable line is used. The fixed catalog in §5
contains344 distinct vectors \(z\), each with its complete set
of zero effective labels. The exact decision is
\[
\boxed{\ p_{\mu,(n)}^\lambda=0
\ \Longleftrightarrow\
N(g)\text{ is a catalog vector and }\nu
\text{ is one of its listed zero labels}.\ }
\tag{NW.3}
\]
This formula applies to the proper nonempty gap supports; the two
other cases were explicitly settled above. The supplied JSON and
TSV also give all seven exact multiplicities at every catalog
vector. They remain those values on its stable rays and on their
normal-form preimages.

This completes the full outer-five nonvanishing question. The
positive coefficient formulas already proved remain available in
their full stated regions. The present finding supplies a support
decision for every remaining coefficient, with all comparison maps
and a finite proof of exhaustion.

## 1. Exact stable maps in both end directions

Determinant multiplication gives the actual sign conversion in
(NW.1). Its normalized shape is
\[
\lambda^0=(a+b+c+e,b+c+e,c+e,e,0),\qquad
n_0=(a+2b+3c+4e)/5.
\tag{NW.4}
\]
The weighted sum is divisible by five. The first stable region
\(a\ge3b+2c+e\) is precisely \(\lambda^0_2\le n_0\).
The actual G027 quotient-section chart identifies its balanced
module with
\[
\operatorname{sgn}^{\,b+c+e}
S_{(b+c+e,b+c,b)}\mathfrak h_5.
\tag{NW.5}
\]
Increasing \(a\) by five multiplies the balanced expression
by \(u=\prod_iX_{i1}\); the shared full section space gives its
inverse on the image. Hence it is an isomorphism and preserves
every multiplicity.

For the second stable region use the perfect exterior-column
pairing in width \(H=a+b+c+e\). It identifies the balanced
module with the dual module of the reversed gap vector
\((e,c,b,a)\), times \(\operatorname{sgn}^H\).
The first stable inequality of that reversed vector is precisely
\(e\ge a+2b+3c\). Increasing \(e\) by ten increases \(H\)
by ten and the first gap of the complementary shape by ten.
Thus the same actual chart isomorphism and the unchanged
determinant sign preserve every multiplicity. A step of five in
this last direction instead transposes the effective label; using
ten in (NW.2) retains its complete vector.

The lower bound one in (NW.2) preserves the positive support
coordinate on a one-axis face. All subtractions are nonnegative
multiples of ten. They retain both the congruence and every zero
gap, and the maps just proved establish equality of all
coefficients before and after normalization.

Both stable inequalities can hold together only when \(b=c=0\)
and \(a=e\). At such a point each individual end direction has
its stated stable ray. These two rays must both be retained; their
interaction is explicitly checked below.

## 2. Every seed and every allowed increment

Fix a nonempty proper support \(S\subset\{1,2,3,4\}\).
For \(i\in S\), write
\(g_i=1+p_i+2t_i\), with \(p_i\in\{0,1\}\) and
\(t_i\ge0\); outside \(S\) put zero. Select a componentwise
minimal \(u\le t\) for which the weighted sum of
\((1+p_i)+2u_i\) is divisible by five.

Every such minimal \(u\) has total at most four. A list of five
indexed weights has two equal partial sums among its six partial
sums modulo five. It therefore contains a nonempty zero-sum
subvector, whose removal from a vector of total at least five
would contradict minimality. Enumeration of the finitely many
parities and \(u\) with total at most four gives all the seeds
used here. There are172 seeds across the fourteen supports.

The difference \(t-u\) belongs to
\[
M_S=\{v\in\mathbf Z_{\ge0}^{S}:\ \sum_iiv_i\equiv0\pmod5\}.
\tag{NW.6}
\]
Every indecomposable nonzero element has total at most five:
a vector of greater total has a proper nonempty zero-sum
subvector of length at most five by the same partial-sum argument.
Thus enumerating total at most five and keeping the
componentwise minimal nonzero solutions gives the complete
generator list. Recursive subtraction proves generation.
Both these enumerations are literal fixed loops in
five_row_face_exploration.py, and all their outputs are retained.

For each generator \(h\), G024 gives an actual invariant-section
embedding from gap vector \(g\) to \(g+2h\), preserving
each outer label. To identify its highest weight explicitly,
put \(\eta_i=\sum_{j\ge i}h_j\), \(\eta_5=0\).
Then \(|\eta|=\sum_iih_i=5q\), so G024 multiplies by
the specified nonzero invariant section of weight \(2\eta\).
The tensor and chart degree increases are exactly the changes
in (NW.4). Every shape with all seven labels positive remains
fully positive after any later generator sequence.

## 3. Complete finite closure, including interacting rays

A catalog node is deficient: at least one of its seven
multiplicities is zero. Each node contributes its point. It
also contributes a ray \(z+10q\,e_j\), \(q\ge0\), for each
stable end axis \(j=1,4\) that it has. The union of these
points and rays will be denoted \(D_S\).

The algorithm starts from every deficient seed in support \(S\),
after normalization. For every retained node \(z\) and generator
\(h\), it evaluates \(N(z+2h)\). A fully positive value is an
exit. Every deficient value is retained and its transitions are
examined. In addition it makes the following finite checks for
each stable axis of every retained node.

Set \(w=z+2h\), and let
\[
L_1(w)=\max(1,3w_2+2w_3+w_4),\qquad
L_4(w)=\max(1,w_1+2w_2+3w_3).
\]
For the selected stable axis \(j\), put
\[
Q(z,h,j)=\max\left(0,\left\lceil
\frac{L_j(w)-w_j}{10}\right\rceil\right).
\tag{NW.7}
\]
The algorithm checks every \(q=0,\ldots,Q(z,h,j)\) in
\[
N(w+10q\,e_j).
\tag{NW.8}
\]
All are exits or retained deficient nodes.
Every generator has total at most five, and its largest
coefficient in either threshold is three. Since \(z\) was
already stable in direction \(j\), its threshold deficit
after adding \(2h\) is at most30. Hence \(Q\le3\).

For every \(q\ge Q\), \(w+10q e_j\) is stable in that same
axis. Its normal form is constant, because its other coordinates
are fixed and its varying coordinate has constant residue modulo
ten. At the possible equality of both stable inequalities,
\(w_2=w_3=0,w_1=w_4\), either normalization fixes the equality
point; the subsequent original-axis normalization has the same
value. This proves constancy also at that endpoint.
Thus (NW.8) exhausts the entire ray transition, including a
generator that raises its stability threshold or switches which
stable direction is selected. No commutation of normalization
with other increments is assumed.

The algorithm terminates with the following exact counts.
Support indices in this table refer to \(g_1,g_2,g_3,g_4\).
The ray-base count counts both directions at a node that has both.

| 2 | 2 | 6 | 6 | 0 | 6 | 0 |
| 3 | 2 | 6 | 6 | 0 | 6 | 0 |
| 4 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 0 | 2 |
| 1,2 | 8 | 52 | 208 | 160 | 32 | 20 |

Here is the full exhaustion proof. Every input starts at one
of the proved seeds and is obtained by a finite generator
sequence. A fully positive seed or intermediate exit stays
positive, by the explicit multiplication injection. A deficient
seed belongs to \(D_S\), by normalization. For a point in
\(D_S\), the recorded point transition classifies its next
increment. For a ray point, (NW.7)–(NW.8) classify every next
increment, including its unbounded tail. A deficient target
normalizes to a retained node and hence belongs to its point
or stable ray. Induction along the finite generator sequence
proves that every deficient input belongs to \(D_S\).

Conversely every retained point has its computed deficient
vector; every ray has the same vector by the actual stable
isomorphisms. Thus every point of \(D_S\) is deficient.
Every retained node is already normalized, and normalizing
any of its ray points returns that node. Conversely (NW.2)
identifies every normal-form preimage with that node.
Consequently deficiency is exactly membership of \(N(g)\)
in the fixed node table. Its individual zero entries prove
(NW.3), including the determinant-label conversion.

## 4. Reproducible certificate, evaluator and geometric meaning

The complete source, normalized targets, raw targets, all seven
cycle traces and all seven multiplicities of every seed and
transition are in ALL_WALL_SUPPORT_GRAPH.json. The executable
all_wall_support_graph.py specifies every finite test just proved.
It checks all1896 point transitions and all2084 ray cases.
There are2218 distinct normalized evaluated gap vectors; the
largest normalized inner degree in those transitions is67.
These are finite character evaluations using the exact balanced
cycle-alternant/Pieri algorithm of G025, with the infinite input
range exhausted by the preceding proof.

ALL_WALL_SUPPORT_NODES.tsv gives every full vector in the344-node
catalog. FIVE_ROW_SUPPORT_INDEX.json is the fixed small evaluator
index, and five_row_support.py implements exactly (NW.1)–(NW.3)
and G028's strict rule. Its arithmetic count is fixed independently
of the input sizes; its integer bit cost is polynomial in their
bit lengths. It does no input-size representation computation.
The initial evaluator verification compared3640 actual support
entries on all congruent gap vectors in \(\{0,\ldots,5\}^4\),
including both determinant parities. Every exact exceptional
vector returned there also agreed. The independent reconstruction
and whole-proof reviews are recorded separately as they finish.

Every edge of this support proof is a specified invariant-section
map, and each normalization is the specified quotient-section
isomorphism or its perfect complementary-column pairing. The
frame action is SGA3 I4.5,I4.7.2–4.7.3; the Schur operations
are SGA6 V4.2,4.4,4.8–4.9 and cote133/024–029 via A010.
The frame and its five linear ideals have models over
\(\mathbf Z[1/5]\); in each fixed degree the rational Young
projectors are defined after additionally inverting the relevant
factorials. The rank statements here concern their characteristic-zero
generic fibers. This specifies the integral construction and its
scalar extension, without asserting equal ranks in every residue
characteristic.

EGA II2.4.1–2.4.2 gives the actual Proj charts, and
II2.5.2,2.5.4 the exact associated-sheaf functor. G027§6's
finite equivariant free resolutions carry the coherent complexes
to locally free \(K_0\) in SGA6 VI3.3. Thus the table decides
nonzero Schur-component ranks of those exact section modules.
For the symmetric canonical map, R031 then determines the actual
image rank by its source at \(n\le4\), its target minus the
eight stated kernel copies at \(n=5\), and its full target at
\(n\ge6\). These use the EGA I9.5.2 graded coordinate-image
scheme of that same normalized map.

The axes column lists stable end directions; a dash means an
isolated point. Each listed axis permits every nonnegative
increment of ten in that one coordinate. At a node with both
axes, take the union of the two rays. The finite closure proof,
including the bounded transition checks, also covers sums of
increments in different axes. Labels are written compactly:
41 means \((4,1)\), 11111 means \((1^5)\), and so on.
The effective-label convention is (NW.1).

# Charged oscillators, the frame quotient, and an exact theta branching realization

## T-052. The complete charge and lowest-type dictionary

Work over \(\mathbf Q\) for the polynomial maps, and extend scalars
to \(\mathbf C\) for the unitary groups. Let \(m\ge3\),
\(n\ge0\), \(\mu\vdash m\), and \(\lambda\vdash mn\)
with at most \(m\) parts. Pad \(\lambda\) by zeros. Define
\[
\begin{gathered}
e=\max(0,n-\lambda_2),\qquad n_0=n-e,\qquad
\lambda^0=(\lambda_1-me,\lambda_2,\ldots,\lambda_m),\\
r=m-2,\quad F=\mathbf Q^r,\quad W=\mathbf Q^m,
\quad k=\lambda_2-n_0,\\
\alpha=(\lambda_2-\lambda_m,\lambda_2-\lambda_{m-1},
\ldots,\lambda_2-\lambda_3),\quad N=|\alpha|,\quad
b=N-mk=\lambda^0_1-\lambda_2.
\end{gathered}
\tag{OC.1}
\]
All these are nonnegative integers, \(\lambda^0\) is a partition,
and \(|\lambda^0|=mn_0\). Let
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal P&=\mathbf Q[X_{ai},Y_i:1\le a\le r,1\le i\le m],\\
R_a&=\sum_iX_{ai}Y_i,\qquad C_a=\sum_i\partial_{X_{ai}}\partial_{Y_i},\\
Q_i&=\sum_aX_{ai}\partial_{X_{ai}}-Y_i\partial_{Y_i}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{OC.2}
\]
The superscript \([k]\) below imposes \(Q_i=k\) for every
\(i\). Subscripts \((N,b)\) impose the total \(X\)-degree
\(N\) and \(Y\)-degree \(b\). Put
\[
\mathcal H^{[k]}_{N,b}
=\mathcal P^{[k]}_{N,b}\cap\bigcap_{a=1}^r\ker C_a,
\qquad
K_{\alpha,k}=\operatorname{Hom}_{GL(F)}
(S_\alpha F,\mathcal H^{[k]}_{N,b}).
\tag{OC.3}
\]
Here \(GL(F)\) acts on the \(X\) variables without a vacuum
twist. Column permutations act simultaneously on \(X_{ai}\)
and \(Y_i\). There is an actual rational \(S_m\)-module
isomorphism
\[
\boxed{(S_\lambda W)_{(n^m)}
\simeq\operatorname{sgn}^{\lambda_2}\otimes K_{\alpha,k}.}
\tag{OC.4}
\]
Its maps, including the dual comparison, are specified in §§3–5.
Consequently, writing \(\tau=\mu\) when \(\lambda_2\) is
even and \(\tau=\mu^t\) when it is odd,
\[
\boxed{p_{\mu,(n)}^\lambda
=\dim\operatorname{Hom}_{S_m}([\tau],K_{\alpha,k}).}
\tag{OC.5}
\]

The same space is a lowest-type multiplicity for the actual unitary
dual pair \(U(r,1),U(m)\). More precisely, let \(L_k\) be the
one-column charged oscillator of §6. Then (OC.5) is the multiplicity
in \(S_\tau(L_k)\) of the irreducible lowest-weight oscillator
module whose lowest \(U(r)\times U(1)\) type has weights
\[
(\alpha_1+m/2,\ldots,\alpha_r+m/2;\,-b-m/2).
\tag{OC.6}
\]
All half-integral weights here refer to the stated metaplectic
preimages, or to a common covering group. The rational finite
identity (OC.4) uses ordinary permutation matrices after the
explicit vacuum untwist. No historical novelty is claimed for
the oscillator correspondence; the new comparison here assembles
it with T-049's actual diagonal quotient and the flag chart.

## 1. Every commuting operator and its scalar shift

Use indices \(a,b,c\in\{1,\ldots,r\}\), and add an index
\(0\). Define
\[
\begin{gathered}
A_{ab}=\sum_iX_{ai}\partial_{X_{bi}}+\frac m2\delta_{ab},
\qquad A_{00}=-\sum_iY_i\partial_{Y_i}-\frac m2,\\
A_{a0}=-R_a,\qquad A_{0a}=C_a,\\
B_{ij}=\sum_aX_{ai}\partial_{X_{aj}}-Y_j\partial_{Y_i}
       +\frac{r-1}{2}\delta_{ij},\qquad
G_{ij}=B_{ij}-\frac{r-1}{2}\delta_{ij}.
\end{gathered}
\tag{OC.7}
\]
They satisfy
\[
[A_{uv},A_{st}]=\delta_{vs}A_{ut}-\delta_{ut}A_{sv},
\quad [B_{ij},B_{pq}]=\delta_{jp}B_{iq}-\delta_{iq}B_{pj},
\quad [A_{uv},B_{ij}]=0.
\tag{OC.8}
\]
The \(G_{ij}\) are the ordinary algebraic \(\mathfrak{gl}(W)\)
action on \(\operatorname{Sym}(F\otimes W\oplus W^*)\).
In particular \(G_{ii}=Q_i\), whereas the oscillator's compact
diagonal weight on the charged space is
\((k+(r-1)/2)^m\).

Here is a direct verification of the signs and constants. The
polynomial Weyl relations give
\[
\begin{split}
[C_a,R_b]
&=\sum_iX_{bi}\partial_{X_{ai}}
  +\delta_{ab}\left(\sum_iY_i\partial_{Y_i}+m\right)\\
&=A_{ba}-\delta_{ab}A_{00},\\
[A_{ab},R_c]&=\delta_{bc}R_a,
\qquad [A_{ab},C_c]=-\delta_{ac}C_b,\\
[A_{00},R_a]&=-R_a,
\qquad [A_{00},C_a]=C_a.
\end{split}
\tag{OC.9}
\]
These identities, \([R_a,R_b]=[C_a,C_b]=0\), and the usual
matrix-unit brackets for \(X\partial_X\) prove the first
identity in (OC.8). The two terms in \(G_{ij}\) each give a
\(\mathfrak{gl}_m\) representation. Their commutators with
\(R_a\) cancel as \(X_{ai}Y_j-X_{ai}Y_j\); their
commutators with \(C_a\) cancel as well. This proves every
mixed bracket. The centers agree literally:
\[
\sum_aA_{aa}+A_{00}=\sum_iB_{ii}
=N_X-N_Y+\frac{m(r-1)}2.
\tag{OC.10}
\]
Thus all \(A\)'s preserve each joint charge space.

Give monomials the Fischer inner product
\(\langle X^uY^v,X^{u'}Y^{v'}\rangle
=\delta_{u,u'}\delta_{v,v'}u!v!\). Then
\[
R_a^\dagger=C_a,\quad A_{ab}^\dagger=A_{ba},\quad
A_{00}^\dagger=A_{00},\quad
A_{a0}^\dagger=-A_{0a},\quad B_{ij}^\dagger=B_{ji}.
\tag{OC.11}
\]
For a matrix in \(\mathfrak u(r,1)\), the coefficients of
\(E_{a0}\) and \(E_{0a}\) are complex conjugates; (OC.11)
makes its action skew-adjoint. The compact
\(\mathfrak u(m)\) action is skew-adjoint by the last identity.
These are exactly the two real forms with the declared shifts.

## 2. The real symplectic embedding and the vacuum character

Let \(H=\mathbf C^{r,1}\), \(W=\mathbf C^m\) with their
Hermitian forms, conjugate-linear in the first entry. On the real
vector space underlying \(H\otimes W\), take
\(\omega=\operatorname{Im}(h_H\otimes h_W)\).
The tensor actions of \(U(r,1)\) and \(U(m)\) are mutual
centralizers in its real symplectic group.

Indeed, a real-linear map commuting with the first group commutes
with its scalar \(i\), so is complex-linear. Its complex
commutant is \(1_H\otimes\operatorname{End}_{\mathbf C}(W)\).
One can see this without a real-form assumption: diagonal phases
give the diagonal matrix units on \(H\), positive-coordinate
unitaries give the matrix units within the positive block, and a
boost between a positive and the negative coordinate gives the
remaining off-diagonal units. Preservation of \(\omega\),
together with complex linearity, implies preservation of the
Hermitian form, since
\(\operatorname{Re}h(v,w)=\omega(v,iw)\). The commutant
inside the symplectic group is therefore exactly \(U(m)\).
The reverse argument starts with the natural irreducible \(U(m)\)
action and yields \(U(r,1)\).

Choose the positive compatible complex structure equal to \(i\)
on the positive part and \(-i\) on the negative part. Its
holomorphic creation space is
\(F\otimes W\oplus W^*\). For
\((a,z,g)\in U(r)\times U(1)\times U(m)\), its action is
\(a\otimes g\) on \(X\) and \(z^{-1}g^{-t}\) on
\(Y\). With the positive-energy oscillator convention of T-001,
the polynomial Fock space is tensored with the vacuum character
\(\chi_0\) on the metaplectic preimage, where
\[
\chi_0^2=(\det a)^m z^{-m}(\det g)^{r-1}.
\tag{OC.12}
\]
The half derivative of this determinant is exactly the collection
of constants in (OC.7). Thus (OC.7) is the actual oscillator
restriction for this real dual pair.

The \(GL(F)\) action used in (OC.3) removes the
\((\det a)^{m/2}\) vacuum factor. The ordinary column action
\(G\) removes the compact vacuum character \(\chi_W\),
whose square is \((\det g)^{r-1}\). If \(r\) is odd,
the explicit section of this cover with
\(\chi_W(g)=(\det g)^{(r-1)/2}\) gives the finite factor
\(\operatorname{sgn}^{(r-1)/2}\) on permutation matrices.
If \(r\) is even, retain the pullback double cover and its
character \(\chi_W\), then tensor by \(\chi_W^{-1}\).
This cancels the central kernel and descends to the literal
\(S_m\) action. In particular no fractional power of the sign
character is being used as a character of \(S_m\).

The primary oscillator source used here is Basile–Joung–Mkrtchyan–
Mojaza, *Dual Pair Correspondence in Physics: Oscillator Realizations
and Representations*, arXiv:2006.07102v2, §5.2, equations
(5.21)–(5.30), printed pp.29–31, at
[the primary PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2006.07102).
Its parameters are \(M_+=r,M_-=1,N=m\). Equations
(5.21)–(5.22) give these operators and shifts; (5.27)–(5.30)
give the traceless lowest types. The complete cited passages were
read, including the dual tensor construction (A.25)–(A.28).
The source's double-cover convention is explicit in (1.16),
printed p.7, and its oscillator monodromy calculation is
(2.12)–(2.18), printed p.10.

## 3. The actual charge homogenization and quotient map

Put
\[
D_k=\bigotimes_{i=1}^m\operatorname{Sym}^{\ge k}F
\subset\mathbf Q[Z_{ai}],\qquad L_a=\sum_i Z_{ai}.
\tag{OC.13}
\]
On a polynomial \(f\) homogeneous of degree \(d_i\ge k\)
in each block, define
\[
\Phi_k(f)=f(X)\prod_iY_i^{d_i-k}.
\tag{OC.14}
\]
This is a rational \(GL(F)\times S_m\)-equivariant bijection
from \(D_k\) to \(\mathcal P^{[k]}\). Its inverse erases
the \(Y\)'s: a charge-\(k\) monomial has forced exponent
\(d_i-k\) on \(Y_i\). It preserves \(X\)-degree and
satisfies
\[
\Phi_k(Z_{ai}f)=X_{ai}Y_i\Phi_k(f),
\qquad \Phi_k(L_af)=R_a\Phi_k(f).
\tag{OC.15}
\]
For \(E=\mathfrak h_m\), write
\(I_i=(\ell_i\otimes F)\subset\operatorname{Sym}(E\otimes F)\)
with \(\ell_i=e_i-\mathbf1/m\). The complete all-degree
theorem T-049, including its actual substitution map, gives
\[
J_k=\bigcap_i I_i^k=\prod_iI_i^k
\simeq D_k/(L_1,\ldots,L_r)D_k.
\tag{OC.16}
\]
Therefore for \(b=N-mk\ge0\), (OC.14) induces
\[
(J_k)_N\simeq
\mathcal P^{[k]}_{N,b}\big/
\sum_aR_a\mathcal P^{[k]}_{N-1,b-1}.
\tag{OC.17}
\]
A space with negative degree is zero. Each arrow in (OC.17)
is induced by (OC.14) and the literal substitution
\(Z_{ai}\mapsto\ell_i\otimes f_a\).

The Fischer orthogonal complement of the denominator is exactly
\(\mathcal H^{[k]}_{N,b}\), by \(R_a^\dagger=C_a\).
Both the denominator and this kernel are stable under
\(GL(F)\times S_m\). Thus orthogonal projection gives an
equivariant isomorphism of the quotient with that kernel.
It is also rational and completely finite. On the indicated
finite-dimensional space set \(T=\sum_aR_aC_a\), and factor
its rational characteristic polynomial as
\(\det(t-T)=t^s q(t)\), \(q(0)\ne0\). Then
\[
\pi_{\mathrm{harm}}=q(T)/q(0).
\tag{OC.18}
\]
The operator \(T\) is positive semidefinite and self-adjoint;
its kernel is the common kernel of the \(C_a\)'s. It is
diagonalizable, so (OC.18) is one on its zero eigenspace and zero
on every other eigenspace. This includes an invertible \(T\),
when the result is zero, and \(T=0\), when it is the identity.
The zero-dimensional case has its unique zero map. The inverse
of the resulting map is inclusion of a harmonic vector followed
by the quotient in (OC.17).

For clarity, (OC.14) also transports lowering to the explicit
operator
\[
\Phi_k^{-1}C_a\Phi_k
=\sum_i(N_i-k+1)\partial_{Z_{ai}},
\qquad N_i=\sum_aZ_{ai}\partial_{Z_{ai}}.
\tag{OC.19}
\]
The rightmost derivative acts first; on block degree \(d_i\)
the coefficient is \(d_i-k\). At \(d_i=k\) it is zero,
so it preserves the truncated space. The induced monomial norm
is \(\prod_i u_i!(d_i-k)!\). With this norm (OC.19) is
the adjoint of multiplication by \(L_a\). This independently
checks the endpoint and every scalar in the charge map.

## 4. The finite harmonic member of theta correspondence

Let \(V_\gamma(W)\) denote the irreducible rational
\(GL(W)\)-module of highest weight \(\gamma\). The
traceless tensor form of the compact-member correspondence is
\[
\mathcal H_{N,b}
\simeq
\bigoplus_{\substack{\alpha\vdash N\\\ell(\alpha)\le r}}
S_\alpha F\otimes
V_{(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_r,0,-b)}(W).
\tag{OC.20}
\]
Here \(\mathcal H_{N,b}\) imposes the lowering equations but
does not yet impose charge. This is the specialization
\(M_-=1\) of the source's (5.27)–(5.30). Its exact tensor
map is polarization into \(F\)-slots and \(W\)-slots,
application of their Young idempotents, and contraction of a
\(W\) slot with a \(W^*\) slot. The equations \(C_a=0\)
say precisely that all such contractions vanish after the
\(F\)-Young projection. The source's Levi–Civita map
(A.25) turns each covector column into its complementary vector
column; its relation (A.27) is the resulting Young relation.
It identifies the surviving irreducible highest weight in
(OC.20). Our lengths satisfy \(\ell(\alpha)+1\le m-1\)
when \(b>0\), so this use is strictly within that tensor range.

There is also a useful normalization of every displayed embedding.
Let \(\Delta_j=\det(X_{ai})_{1\le a,i\le j}\), and
\(\alpha_{r+1}=0\). Send the product of the standard highest
vectors in (OC.20) to
\[
v_{\alpha,b}=Y_m^b\prod_{j=1}^r
\Delta_j^{\alpha_j-\alpha_{j+1}}.
\tag{OC.21}
\]
It is nonzero, has \(GL(F)\)-weight \(\alpha\) and
ordinary \(GL(W)\)-weight \((\alpha,0,-b)\), and is
annihilated by every \(C_a\): its \(Y\) derivative uses
column \(m\), while its \(X\)'s use columns at most \(r\).
The compact raising operators kill the first-column minors.
Applying the two enveloping-algebra actions to (OC.21) supplies
the unique normalized intertwiner in (OC.20). This describes
the actual summand map as well as its labels. In the oscillator
action the compact weight in (OC.20) is shifted by
\((r-1)/2\) in every coordinate, and its lowest noncompact
type is (OC.6), directly from (OC.7).

Taking the charge weight in (OC.20) gives an ordinary
\(S_m\)-module isomorphism
\[
K_{\alpha,k}\simeq
\left(V_{(\alpha,0,-b)}(W)\right)_{(k^m)}.
\tag{OC.22}
\]
It uses literal permutation matrices for the \(G\) action.
The full compact group preserves the harmonic space; its
equal-weight subspace is preserved by these permutations.

## 5. Every determinant, dual, and first-row map in (OC.4)

First suppose \(e=0\). A direct calculation from (OC.1) gives
\[
\gamma=(\alpha,0,-b)
=\lambda_2\mathbf1-(\lambda^0_m,\ldots,\lambda^0_1).
\tag{OC.23}
\]
The actual rational representation map is
\[
V_\gamma(W)\simeq
(\det W)^{\lambda_2}\otimes(S_{\lambda^0}W)^*.
\tag{OC.24}
\]
To fix it without suppressing the dual, put
\(H=\lambda^0_1=\lambda_2+b\) and
\(\beta=(H-\lambda_m^0,\ldots,H-\lambda_1^0)
=(\alpha_1+b,\ldots,\alpha_r+b,b,0)\).
Columnwise exterior multiplication in the \(m\)-by-\(H\)
rectangle, followed by the Schur projections, is the perfect pairing
\[
S_{\lambda^0}W\otimes S_\beta W
\longrightarrow(\det W)^H.
\tag{OC.25}
\]
It is nonzero on complementary highest and lowest column tensors;
the highest weights are contragredient with this determinant
twist, so the induced pairing is perfect. Tensoring its second
factor by \((\det W)^{-b}\) gives (OC.24), with its
normalization matched to (OC.21). This also works when \(b=0\).

On the charge weight, (OC.24) reads
\[
K_{\alpha,k}\simeq
\operatorname{sgn}^{\lambda_2}\otimes
\left((S_{\lambda^0}W)_{(n_0^m)}\right)^*,
\tag{OC.26}
\]
since \(k-\lambda_2=-n_0\). The sign is exactly the
determinant of the permutation matrix in (OC.25).

We now give the dual comparison actually used in (OC.4). Realize
\(S_{\lambda^0}W\) as the image of a rational Young
idempotent in \(W^{\otimes mn_0}\). Equip the standard rational
basis of \(W\) with its dot product and use the tensor product
form. Restriction to this image, and then to its balanced weight
space, is nondegenerate: after extension to \(\mathbf R\)
the form is positive definite. Permutation matrices preserve it
and commute with the Young idempotent. Hence
\[
v\longmapsto\bigl(w\longmapsto\langle v,w\rangle\bigr)
\tag{OC.27}
\]
is a rational \(S_m\)-equivariant isomorphism to that balanced
space's dual. This map concerns the specified finite group action;
no \(GL(W)\)-self-duality is being substituted for (OC.24).

Finally allow \(e>0\). In T-032's flag algebra let \(x_i\)
be the first-column variables and \(u=\prod_i x_i\). The
balanced chart gives the actual bijection
\[
\cdot u^e:
(S_{\lambda^0}W)_{(n_0^m)}
\longrightarrow (S_\lambda W)_{(n^m)}.
\tag{OC.28}
\]
Indeed its right highest weight increases by \((me,0,\ldots,0)\),
its left weight increases by \((e^m)\), and both sides are
the same tail flag module in that chart. The inverse divides
by \(u^e\), with polynomiality proved in T-032 by the exact
minor count. Also \(u\) is fixed by every slot permutation.
When \(n>\lambda_2\),
\(\lambda^0_1=\lambda_2+N\ge\lambda_2\), so all its
partition and degree conditions hold. Composing (OC.28),
(OC.27), (OC.26) and (OC.22) proves (OC.4). Combining this
with T-003's balanced-weight Schur–Weyl map proves (OC.5).
The empty partition at \(n=0\) gives \(k=N=b=0\) and a
single trivial harmonic vector, so it is included.

There is a second explicit route through the frame ideal:
T-032/G-027's flag map and relative Schur pairing identify the
balanced module with
\(\operatorname{sgn}^{\lambda_2}
\operatorname{Hom}_{GL(F)}(S_\alpha F,(J_k)_N)\).
Equations (OC.14)–(OC.18) identify this with (OC.4).
Thus the charged oscillator and the frame-ideal model are related
by the actual homogenization, quotient and harmonic projection,
in addition to their compact highest-weight comparison.

## 6. A Schur functor of one charged lowest-weight module

For one column, the same homogenization identifies the charge-\(k\)
space with
\(L_k=\bigoplus_{d\ge k}\operatorname{Sym}^dF\).
Write \(z_a\) for its variables and \(N_z\) for their degree.
The \(\mathfrak{gl}_{r+1}\) action is
\[
\begin{gathered}
A^{(1)}_{ab}=z_a\partial_{z_b}+\tfrac12\delta_{ab},
\quad A^{(1)}_{00}=-N_z+k-\tfrac12,\\
A^{(1)}_{a0}=-z_a,
\qquad A^{(1)}_{0a}=(N_z-k+1)\partial_{z_a}.
\end{gathered}
\tag{OC.29}
\]
The last operator acts by \((d-k)\partial_{z_a}\) in
degree \(d\). Its lowest compact type is
\(\operatorname{Sym}^kF\otimes(\det F)^{1/2}\)
with negative \(U(1)\) weight \(-1/2\).

This algebraic lowest-weight module is irreducible. A nonzero
submodule contains a nonzero homogeneous element: the degree
operator is diagonal and a polynomial in it isolates any of the
finitely many degree components of a vector. Choose the least
degree occurring in the submodule. At degree \(d>k\) some
derivative is nonzero, and (OC.29) lowers that degree, a
contradiction. At degree \(k\) the irreducible compact
\(\operatorname{Sym}^k F\) is therefore present. Multiplication
by the \(z_a\)'s generates every higher symmetric power, so
the submodule is all of \(L_k\). The transported Fischer form
supplies its unitary oscillator realization on the corresponding
cover. This argument also covers \(k=0\).

Tensoring (OC.29) over the \(m\) columns gives exactly
(OC.7) on \(\mathcal P^{[k]}\), by (OC.14). Thus
\[
L_k^{\otimes m}\simeq\mathcal P^{[k]}
\tag{OC.30}
\]
as an actual module for the noncompact oscillator algebra and
the literal tensor-permutation \(S_m\). All group statements
can be read on a common cover of \(U(r,1)\); the tensor
vacuum exponents sum to \(m/2\), as required by (OC.7).

The compact-member theta decomposition, with its summands generated
by (OC.21), gives
\[
S_\tau(L_k)\simeq
\bigoplus_{\substack{\alpha,b\ge0\\|\alpha|-b=mk}}
\mathcal D^{(m)}_{\alpha,b}\otimes
\operatorname{Hom}_{S_m}
\left([\tau],(V_{(\alpha,0,-b)}W)_{(k^m)}\right).
\tag{OC.31}
\]
Here \(\ell(\alpha)\le r\), and
\(\mathcal D^{(m)}_{\alpha,b}\) is the irreducible oscillator
module with the lowest compact type (OC.6). The algebraic direct
sum in (OC.31) consists of finite polynomial vectors. The
displayed map is the known theta summand inclusion generated
from (OC.21), followed by taking the \(S_m\) Hom space in
(OC.30). Distinct labels have distinct lowest compact types.
Equations (OC.22), (OC.26) and (OC.27) therefore make its
specified multiplicity exactly (OC.5).

The irreducibility and direct sum in this application can also
be checked directly from (OC.20). In every finite total degree,
Fischer decomposition writes
\(\mathcal P_D=\mathcal H_D+\sum_aR_a\mathcal P_{D-2}\).
The \(R_a\)'s commute with the compact column action, so
iteration generates each column isotypic component from its
harmonics. For a given \(\gamma=(\alpha,0,-b)\),
(OC.20) gives exactly one harmonic bidegree and the irreducible
lowest \(GL(F)\) type \(S_\alpha F\). A nonzero submodule
of its column multiplicity space contains a homogeneous vector:
a polynomial in the energy
\(\sum_aA_{aa}-A_{00}=N_X+N_Y+m(r+1)/2\)
isolates a degree component. Its least occurring degree is killed
by every lowering operator. It therefore meets that unique
lowest type, contains the whole type by compact irreducibility,
and generates the full multiplicity space by the preceding
Fischer recursion. This proves irreducibility. The ordinary
isotypic direct sum for the compact group then gives (OC.31)
with the actual summand inclusions already specified.

The relevant lowest vectors can be obtained entirely in a finite
space: impose (OC.3), row degrees \(\alpha_a\), and
\(\sum_iX_{ai}\partial_{X_{bi}}=0\) for \(a<b\),
then apply the Specht Hom projector. All these rational operators
are explicit and commute with the slot action. The positive
lowest-type decomposition does not remove that last projector;
the general positive counts G-009–G-011 and the direct families
already proved evaluate it by their separately established maps.

## 7. Endpoints and proof status

At \(b=0\), every charged monomial has each block degree
exactly \(k\), so no lowering or quotient relation occurs:
\(\mathcal H^{[k]}_{mk,0}=(\operatorname{Sym}^kF)^{\otimes m}\).
Equation (OC.5) becomes the complementary-partition plethysm
identity with shape \(\alpha\), inner degree \(k\), and
the sign \(\operatorname{sgn}^{\lambda_2}\). Its actual
map is precisely the column pairing (OC.25). At \(k=0\),
(OC.16) is the polynomial quotient by the diagonal subspace,
\(J_0=\operatorname{Sym}(\mathfrak h_m\otimes F)\);
this recovers the stable flag chart through (OC.14)–(OC.18).
For \(\ell(\lambda)>m\), T-002's Cauchy decomposition
gives zero, and no oscillator label is needed.

The exact script `oscillator_charge_checks.py` verified 1895
normal-ordered Weyl-algebra commutator identities in ranks
\((r,m)=(1,3),(2,4),(3,5)\), together with the adjoints and
center identities. It constructed 42 literal rational joint
lowering/compact-raising nullspaces and their permutation traces.
After both determinant parities and the allowed first-row shifts,
all 663 plethysm coefficients and 663 class traces agreed with
the independent cycle-index/Murnaghan--Nakayama implementation.
Six exact characteristic-polynomial projectors passed idempotence,
lowering-kernel and rank checks. The largest tested polynomial
domain had dimension 200. The receipt is
`OSCILLATOR_CHARGE_RECEIPT.json`; these finite computations support
the all-parameter proofs and do not replace them.

The root, rectangular and archive agents independently read and checked the complete proof
(OC.1)–(OC.31), including the real centralizers, every scalar

The rectangular and archive agents also independently read the
