# The charged incidence algebra and the actual frame Rees algebra

## T-053. Multiplication, a quadratic degeneration, and its exact finite-group obstruction

Let \(m\ge3\), \(1\le r\le m-2\), \(F=\mathbf Q^r\),
and \(E=\mathfrak h_m\). Retain T-049's frame ideals
\(I_i=(\ell_i\otimes F)\) and
\(J_k=\bigcap_i I_i^k=(J_1)^k\subset
S=\operatorname{Sym}(E\otimes F)\). Define
\[
\mathcal P=\mathbf Q[X_{ai},Y_i],\qquad
R_a=\sum_{i=1}^m X_{ai}Y_i,\qquad
\mathcal B=\mathcal P/(R_1,\ldots,R_r).
\tag{IR.1}
\]
Give \(X_{ai}\) column charge \(e_i\), \(Y_i\) column
charge \(-e_i\), and give \(X_{ai}\) row weight
\(\varepsilon_a\), \(Y_i\) row weight zero. The relations
have charge zero and row weights \(\varepsilon_a\).
There is an actual \(GL(F)\times S_m\)-equivariant graded
algebra isomorphism
\[
\boxed{\mathcal R(J_1)=\bigoplus_{k\ge0}J_kt^k
\simeq\bigoplus_{k\ge0}\mathcal B_{(k^m)}.}
\tag{IR.2}
\]
The degree \(k\) on the right is the equal nonnegative charge;
polynomial degree in \(S\) corresponds to \(X\)-degree.
Every row-weight component has the explicit positive count in
(IR.8), using at most \(2^r\) bounded integer polytopes of
\(rm+m\) variables. These count the entire indicated torus
weight space. The highest-type and Specht projectors that give
individual plethysms remain the explicit ones of T-052.

In the displayed coordinates, no monomial initial ideal of
\((R_1,\ldots,R_r)\) is preserved by the literal column
permutation action of \(S_m\). The proof in §4 is a
degree-two orbit calculation for this specified action.

## 1. The algebra map and every grading

In \(\mathbf Q[Z_{ai}]\), put
\(D_k=\bigotimes_i\operatorname{Sym}^{\ge k}F\) and
\(L_a=\sum_i Z_{ai}\). On a polynomial with block degrees
\(d_i\ge k\), use the charge map of T-052,
\[
\Phi_k(f)=f(X)\prod_iY_i^{d_i-k}.
\tag{IR.3}
\]
It is linear on the direct sum of block-homogeneous pieces.
Since each \(R_a\) has charge zero,
\[
\mathcal B_{(k^m)}
=\mathcal P_{(k^m)}/\sum_aR_a\mathcal P_{(k^m)}.
\]
The equations \(\Phi_k(L_af)=R_a\Phi_k(f)\) therefore
give the component isomorphism
\(D_k/LD_k\simeq\mathcal B_{(k^m)}\).
T-049 identifies its left side with \(J_k\) by literal
substitution \(Z_{ai}\mapsto\ell_i\otimes f_a\).

For \(f\in D_k\) and \(g\in D_l\), first take them
block-homogeneous with degrees \(d_i\), \(d'_i\).
Then \(fg\in D_{k+l}\) and
\[
\Phi_k(f)\Phi_l(g)
=f(X)g(X)\prod_iY_i^{d_i+d'_i-k-l}
=\Phi_{k+l}(fg).
\tag{IR.4}
\]
Bilinearity proves the same identity for all \(f,g\).
The multiplication in \(D_k/LD_k\) maps to multiplication
of their substituted polynomials in \(J_k\). Hence (IR.4)
proves multiplication compatibility across every pair of degrees,
and proves (IR.2), including its unit at \(k=0\).

In particular the degree-zero coefficient algebra map sends
\(\ell_i\otimes f_a\) to \([X_{ai}Y_i]\); the relations
\(\sum_i\ell_i=0\) map to \(R_a=0\). A generating
degree-one element of the Rees algebra has the concrete image
\[
t\prod_{i=1}^m(\ell_i\otimes f_{a_i})
\longmapsto\prod_{i=1}^m X_{a_i i}.
\]
These formulas specify the algebra map on generators; their
well-definedness and bijectivity are exactly (IR.3)–(IR.4) and
the proved component quotient.

The maps preserve row weights, \(X\)-degree and slot
permutations. At equal charge \(k\), the \(Y\)-degree
is forced to be \(N-mk\) for \(X\)-degree \(N\).
The full \(GL(F)\) action is also preserved: the \(R_a\)'s
transform as \(F\), and both homogenization and substitution
commute with row changes of basis. Thus the torus gradings and
the larger equivariance have distinct, specified roles in (IR.2).

For a scheme description, let \(T=(\mathbf G_m)^m\) act
with the stated charges, and introduce a variable \(z\) of
charge \((-1,\ldots,-1)\). Then
\[
\mathcal R(J_1)\simeq(\mathcal B[z])^T,
\qquad f\in\mathcal B_{(k^m)}\longmapsto fz^k.
\tag{IR.5}
\]
Indeed an invariant polynomial has exactly these charge-homogeneous
terms, with \(k\ge0\) because its \(z\)-exponent is
nonnegative. Formula (IR.4) makes this identification an algebra
map. The inclusion of invariant rings defines the actual affine
quotient morphism from the incidence scheme \(XY=0\), with
this extra affine coordinate, to \(\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal R(J_1)\).
Slot permutations fix \(z\) and normalize \(T\), so this
morphism retains their action. T-049's explicit Rees charts and
relative Proj construction therefore apply to this same algebra.

## 2. A complete quadratic Gröbner calculation

Use a graded monomial order: compare total degree first, then
the weight assigning one to \(X_{aa}\), \(1\le a\le r\),
and zero to every other variable, then a fixed lexicographic
order. It gives
\[
\operatorname{in}(R_a)=X_{aa}Y_a,
\qquad
\operatorname{in}(R_1,\ldots,R_r)
=(X_{11}Y_1,\ldots,X_{rr}Y_r).
\tag{IR.6}
\]
Here is a direct normal-form proof of the second equality.
Write \(M_a=X_{aa}Y_a\) and
\(T_a=-\sum_{i\ne a}X_{ai}Y_i\), and replace every
factor \(M_a\) by \(T_a\). Each replacement strictly
decreases the total degree in the diagonal variables
\(X_{11},\ldots,X_{rr}\), since no \(T_a\) contains
any of these variables. Thus rewriting terminates. The leading
monomials are pairwise coprime. If two different rules apply to
a monomial \(qM_aM_b\), applying them in either order gives
\(qT_aT_b\). The case of two occurrences of the same rule
has the identical replacement. Induction on diagonal-variable
degree therefore proves that every sequence of reductions has
the same linear normal form: after either first rule, apply the
other, and use the induction hypothesis for every lower-degree
term. This argument extends linearly to polynomials.

The normal form kills every multiple of \(M_a-T_a=R_a\),
and every reduction preserves its residue modulo the relation
ideal. Hence the standard monomials give a basis of the quotient.
Moreover every rewriting step lowers the chosen monomial order.
A relation with a standard leading monomial could not reduce to
zero, since lower monomials never create that leading monomial.
This proves (IR.6), including the asserted Gröbner-basis property.
Every reduction preserves row weight, column charge and the two
degrees in \(X\) and \(Y\).

This also proves that \(R_1,\ldots,R_r\) is a regular
sequence, without a dimension inference. Suppose \(f\) is a
nonzero standard representative modulo the first \(a-1\)
relations. The leading monomial of \(R_af\) is
\(M_a\operatorname{in}(f)\). Since \(M_a\) uses no
variable in the previous leading monomials, that product is not
divisible by any of them. Thus \(R_af\) is nonzero modulo
the preceding relations. This is the required injectivity at
each step.

The degeneration itself is explicit. Set
\[
\mathscr B=\mathbf Q[s,X,Y]\big/
\left(X_{aa}Y_a+s\sum_{i\ne a}X_{ai}Y_i:1\le a\le r\right).
\tag{IR.7}
\]
The same proof works over \(\mathbf Q[s]\), replacing
\(M_a\) by \(sT_a\): the two possible reductions of
\(M_aM_b\) both give \(s^2T_aT_b\), and termination
uses the same diagonal-variable degree. The standard monomials
therefore form a free \(\mathbf Q[s]\)-basis. In particular
this is a flat family. Its fiber at \(s=0\) is the monomial
quotient in (IR.6), and its fiber at \(s=1\) is \(\mathcal B\).
Over \(s\ne0\), the map from (IR.7) to
\(\mathcal B[s,s^{-1}]\) sends its \(X_{aa}\) to
\(sX_{aa}\), and fixes all other \(X\)'s and \(Y\)'s;
the inverse sends the original \(X_{aa}\) to
\(s^{-1}X_{aa}\). It sends each relation to \(sR_a\).
These are the exact general-fiber isomorphisms.

Every row-weight and charge piece is free with its indicated
standard basis. Selecting the equal nonnegative charge pieces
therefore gives a flat algebra family whose general fiber is
the Rees algebra in (IR.2). These maps retain the stated torus
gradings; their behavior under the full permutation action is
settled separately in §4.

## 3. The literal bounded polytopes

Fix \(k\ge0\) and a row weight
\(\eta=(\eta_1,\ldots,\eta_r)\in\mathbf Z_{\ge0}^r\).
For each \(A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}\), use integer
variables \(u_{ai}\) and \(v_i\), with constraints
\[
\begin{gathered}
u_{ai}\ge0,\quad v_i\ge0,\qquad
\sum_i u_{ai}=\eta_a,\qquad
\sum_a u_{ai}-v_i=k,\\
a\in A:\quad u_{aa}=0,\ v_a\ge1,\qquad
a\notin A:\quad v_a=0.
\end{gathered}
\tag{IR.8}
\]
Call this rational polytope \(\mathscr P_{A}(\eta,k)\).
It is bounded: each \(u_{ai}\le\eta_a\), and the column
equations give \(0\le v_i\le|\eta|\). Its point
\((u,v)\) gives the monomial \(X^uY^v\). The row and
charge equations give exactly the required weight, and the last
conditions guarantee that no \(X_{aa}Y_a\) divides it.
Conversely every standard monomial has the unique tag
\(A=\{a\le r:v_a>0\}\), and gives exactly one point of
(IR.8). Thus there is a proved bijection and
\[
\boxed{\dim(\mathcal B_{(k^m)})_\eta
=\dim(J_k)_\eta
=\sum_{A\subseteq[r]}
\#\bigl(\mathscr P_A(\eta,k)\cap\mathbf Z^{rm+m}\bigr).}
\tag{IR.9}
\]
If \(|\eta|<mk\), summing the column equations forces
\(\sum_i v_i<0\), so every polytope is empty. The zero
weight at \(k=0\) has its single point in the empty tag.

This also identifies precisely which representation-theoretic
sum the count evaluates. Put \(N=|\eta|\), \(b=N-mk\).
When \(b<0\), all the spaces and counts are zero by the
summed charge equation. For \(b\ge0\),
write \(K_{\alpha,k}\) for T-052's ordinary multiplicity
space for the current row dimension. When \(r<m-2\), pad
\(\alpha\) by zeros and add zero-degree \(X\) rows.
Inclusion of polynomials independent of those rows identifies
the highest multiplicity spaces literally: the new lowering
and compact raising equations vanish, and their zero row weights
force every polynomial in the enlarged space to be independent
of those rows. Thus this is the space of T-052 with the padded
partition. The actual \(GL(F)\times S_m\) decomposition gives
\[
\dim(J_k)_\eta
=\sum_{\substack{\alpha\vdash N\\\ell(\alpha)\le r}}
\dim(S_\alpha F)_\eta\;\dim K_{\alpha,k}
=\sum_{\alpha,\tau}
K_{\alpha,\eta}\,\dim[\tau]\,
\dim\operatorname{Hom}_{S_m}([\tau],K_{\alpha,k}).
\tag{IR.10}
\]
To specify every last factor, set
\[
\gamma=(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_r,0^{m-r-1},-b),
\quad t=\alpha_1,\quad n=t-k,\quad
\lambda=t\mathbf1-\operatorname{reverse}(\gamma).
\]
For a nonzero component, \(N\ge mk\), whence
\(t\ge N/r\ge k\). Thus \(n\ge0\), and
\(\lambda\) is a partition of \(mn\), with
\(\lambda_2=t\). The zero partition has \(t=k=n=0\).
The actual zero-row inclusion just given, followed by T-052's
column pairing and rational balanced dual map, yields
\[
\dim\operatorname{Hom}_{S_m}([\tau],K_{\alpha,k})
=p_{\tau^{(t)},(t-k)}^\lambda,
\qquad
\tau^{(t)}=\begin{cases}\tau&t\text{ even},\\
\tau'&t\text{ odd},\end{cases}
\]
where \(\tau'\) is the conjugate partition. The finite twist
is exactly \(\operatorname{sgn}^t\).
Equation (IR.10) therefore specifies both positive weights and
every plethysm label in the sum. The individual factors are
obtained by the highest-type and Specht maps in T-052;
(IR.9) counts their displayed weighted sum.

## 4. The narrowly stated permutation obstruction

Let \(\prec\) be any monomial order in the fixed coordinates
of (IR.1), and set \(I=(R_1,\ldots,R_r)\). Its degree-two
space is exactly the \(r\)-dimensional span of the \(R_a\)'s.
Consequently \(\operatorname{in}_\prec(I)_2\) is an
\(r\)-dimensional monomial space. Every one of its monomials
is \(X_{ai}Y_i\) for some \(a,i\): these are all the
monomials that occur in the degree-two relations. There are no
relations in smaller degree.

The column-permutation orbit of any such monomial is
\(\{X_{aj}Y_j:1\le j\le m\}\), a set of exactly
\(m\) distinct monomials. A permutation-stable monomial
space containing one must contain all of them. This would force
\(r\ge m\), contrary to \(r\le m-2\). Hence
\[
\boxed{\operatorname{in}_\prec(I)
\text{ is not stable under the literal }S_m
\text{ column action for any such monomial order}.}
\tag{IR.11}
\]
This disproves the particular proposal that standard monomials
from a monomial degeneration in these coordinates inherit that
same slot-permutation action. It makes no claim about a change
of coordinates, other equivariant filtrations, or the already
proved positive formulas. The original quotient and the Rees
algebra retain their actual \(S_m\) actions through (IR.2).

## 5. Exact resolution and Grothendieck transport

The regular sequence proved in §2 gives the actual finite
\(GL(F)\times GL(W)\)-equivariant free resolution
\[
0\longrightarrow\mathcal P\otimes\Lambda^rF
\longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow
\mathcal P\otimes F\longrightarrow\mathcal P
\longrightarrow\mathcal B\longrightarrow0,
\tag{IR.12}
\]
where the \(j\)-th term is shifted by \((j,j)\) in
\((X,Y)\)-degree. The differential is
\[
f\otimes(f_{a_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge f_{a_j})
\longmapsto\sum_{h=1}^j(-1)^{h-1}R_{a_h}f
\otimes f_{a_1}\wedge\cdots\widehat{f_{a_h}}
\cdots\wedge f_{a_j}.
\tag{IR.13}
\]
Its charge is zero, \(GL(W)\) fixes each \(R_a\), and
\(GL(F)\) acts on their span as \(F\). These facts prove
equivariance of every differential. Selecting a torus weight is
exact because a rational torus representation is the direct sum
of its weight spaces. Thus each finite bidegree and equal-charge
piece gives, in the representation Grothendieck group of
\(GL(F)\times S_m\),
\[
[(J_k)_N]=[\mathcal H^{[k]}_{N,b}]
=\sum_{j=0}^r(-1)^j
[\Lambda^jF\otimes\mathcal P^{[k]}_{N-j,b-j}].
\tag{IR.14}
\]
The first equality is the actual rational projection of T-052,
and the second is the Euler relation of (IR.12), rather than
an equality inferred from dimension. Under (IR.3), the cyclic
trace of its tensor factors is T-049's factored character.

On \(\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal P\), (IR.12) is a finite
equivariant vector-bundle resolution of the coherent module
defined by the closed incidence immersion. The action is given
by the polynomial coactions specified in (IR.1). Sheafifying
the graded resolution on \(\operatorname{Proj}\mathcal P\)
uses the exact graded sheafification map; T-049 §7 records its
verified EGA and SGA locators. The Rees identification (IR.2)
is a separate algebra isomorphism, so it also induces literal
isomorphisms on its affine scheme and relative Proj charts.
This states the base of each resolution and each geometric map.

## 6. Proof status

The full argument above proves every multiplication and grading,
the specified quadratic Gröbner basis, the flat-family maps,
the standard-monomial/polytope bijection, the degree-two
permutation obstruction and the exact equivariant resolution.
The standalone `charged_incidence_polytopes.py` exports all
integer matrices in (IR.8), and optionally enumerates their
standard monomials. Its reproduction script
`check_charged_incidence.py` passed 151 row-weight/charge cases,
with 4653 literal standard witnesses and unique membership in
the complete tagged constraint systems. The counts matched the
alternating Koszul formula in every case and 104 independently
constructed lowering-matrix nullities. Six exact symbolic
Gröbner calculations checked both the original and parameter
families in three ranks. The receipt is
`CHARGED_INCIDENCE_RECEIPT.json`.

The root and archive agents read the whole proof and passed its
algebra, flat family, polytopes and obstruction. The archive
agent also completed its review of every added lower-rank label
and the direct diamond proof, recorded as A-062. Its separate
literal row-composition/polytope enumeration matched the
exterior-Koszul truncated counts in 418 cases, with 15042
standard monomial points and 220 forced-empty endpoints, in
ranks \((r,m)=(1,3),(1,4),(2,4),(2,5),(3,5)\).
The independent receipt is
`work/archive/CHARGED_INCIDENCE_POLYTOPE_RECEIPT.json`.
Those executed comparisons are distinguished from the complete
mathematical readings.


# A varying-outer-degree first-hook formula and its actual kernel module

## T-060. Stable first-hook tails, positive polytopes and exact support

Let \(m\ge4\), \(a\ge1\), \(t\ge0\), \(n\ge a+t\), and
\(\mu\vdash m\). Put
\[
\begin{gathered}
\lambda=(A,a+t,t+1,t^{m-3}),\\
A=mn-a-(m-1)t-1,\qquad D=a+1.
\end{gathered}
\tag{FH.1}
\]
Set \(\nu=\mu\) for even \(t\), and \(\nu=\mu'\) for odd
\(t\). For a cell \(z=(i,j)\), write \(c(z)=j-i\), and define
\[
\mathcal C_\nu=\nu\setminus\{(1,1),(2,1)\}
\quad\text{when }\nu\ne(m).
\]
Let
\[
f_\nu(q)=\sum_{T\in\operatorname{SYT}(\nu)}q^{\operatorname{comaj}(T)}
=q^{n(\nu)}\frac{\prod_{i=1}^m(1-q^i)}
 {\prod_{z\in\nu}(1-q^{h(z)})},
\qquad n(\nu)=\sum_i(i-1)\nu_i.
\tag{FH.2}
\]
The comajor convention and its complete standardization bijection are
T027/S.3 and S.13–S.16. The hook specialization is Macdonald,
*Symmetric Functions and Hall Polynomials*, second edition,
I§3 Example2, printed p45.

For \(\nu\ne(m)\), put
\[
N_\nu(q)=f_\nu(q)\sum_{z\in\mathcal C_\nu}q^{c(z)+1}
=\sum_{s=0}^{\binom m2+1}N_{\nu,s}q^s.
\tag{FH.3}
\]
All its coefficients are nonnegative integers. The exact positive formula is
\[
\boxed{
p_{\mu,(n)}^\lambda
=\sum_sN_{\nu,s}\,
\#\{(u_2,\ldots,u_m)\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^{m-1}:
\textstyle\sum_{i=2}^m i u_i=D-s\}.}
\tag{FH.4}
\]
For the trivial effective label \(\nu=(m)\), it is
\[
\boxed{
p_{\mu,(n)}^\lambda
=\sum_{2\le i<j\le m}
\#\{(u_i,\ldots,u_m)\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^{m-i+1}:
\textstyle\sum_{l=i}^m l u_l=D-i-j\}.}
\tag{FH.5}
\]
Negative right sides give empty polytopes. Formula (FH.4) uses at most
\(\binom m2+2\) selected bounded polytopes with at most \(m\)
variables; (FH.5) uses \(\binom{m-1}{2}\) with at most \(m-1\)
variables. Every matrix is explicit in §5.

There is also a closed nonvanishing test. For \(\nu\ne(m)\), let
\[
L_\nu=n(\nu)+\min_{z\in\mathcal C_\nu}(c(z)+1).
\tag{FH.6}
\]
Then
\[
\boxed{
p_{\mu,(n)}^\lambda>0
\iff
\begin{cases}
D\ge L_\nu,&\nu\ne(m),\\
D\ge5,&\nu=(m).
\end{cases}}
\tag{FH.7}
\]
The result concerns the stated varying-\(m\) family. It is an explicit
coinvariant/kernel realization, with its classical ingredients cited
below; no assertion of global priority is made.

## 1. Exact stable-chart and hook maps

Write \(E=\mathfrak h_m=\mathbb Q^m/\mathbb Q(1,\ldots,1)\),
with its permutation action. The first gap in (FH.1) is
\[
A-(a+t)=mn-2a-mt-1\ge(m-2)a-1\ge0.
\]
Thus the output is a partition of \(mn\). Since \(n\ge\lambda_2\),
the exact flag-chart map T032 gives
\[
(S_\lambda\mathbb Q^m)_{(n^m)}
\simeq S_{(a+t,t+1,t^{m-3})}E
\simeq\operatorname{sgn}^{t}\otimes S_{(a,1)}E.
\tag{FH.8}
\]
The first map uses the balanced flag generators and multiplication by
\(u^{n-\lambda_2}\), with the polynomial inverse proved in T032.
The second removes \(t\) full exterior columns through the perfect
determinant pairing. The actual determinant of the permutation quotient
\(E\) is the permutation sign. Together with the Cauchy/Young map of
T003, this proves that the desired multiplicity is
\([\,[\nu]:S_{(a,1)}E\,]\), including its exact sign.

Let \(P=\operatorname{Sym}E\), grade \(P\otimes E\) by polynomial
degree plus one, and let
\[
\delta:P\otimes E\longrightarrow P,
\qquad \delta(f\otimes v)=fv,\qquad K=\ker\delta.
\tag{FH.9}
\]
This is an actual \(S_m\)-equivariant module map with image \(P_+\).
Its degree-\(D=a+1\) kernel is \(S_{(a,1)}E\). More explicitly,
the map
\[
q\otimes(u\wedge v)\longmapsto qu\otimes v-qv\otimes u
\]
from \(\operatorname{Sym}^{a-1}E\otimes\Lambda^2E\) has this
image. The one-box Pieri decomposition and the nonzero hook highest
vector identify its image with the hook Young summand. A concrete
projection onto that image is
\[
1-\frac1D\nabla\delta,
\qquad \nabla p=\sum_j\frac{\partial p}{\partial z_j}\otimes z_j;
\quad\delta\nabla p=Dp
\tag{FH.10}
\]
on degree \(D\). The expression is independent of the basis used
to write the natural polarization map. This proves the comparison with
the actual kernel, including its rational inverse on the complementary
symmetric summand.

## 2. Coinvariants, a free nontrivial multiplicity module and its numerator

Let \(e_i\) be the elementary symmetric functions on the centered
coordinates of \(E\), and put
\[
I=P^{S_m}=\mathbb Q[e_2,\ldots,e_m],\qquad
H=P/(e_2,\ldots,e_m),\qquad M=\binom m2.
\]
The usual coinvariant freeness gives a graded equivariant isomorphism
\(I\otimes H\to P\): choose a homogeneous section of the quotient,
average it over \(S_m\), and multiply. The homogeneous-basis criterion
that this is an isomorphism is Stanley, *Invariants of finite groups
and their applications to combinatorics*, Proposition3.1, p482, and
Theorem3.10, p485. The invariant-polynomial assertion is its §4,
pp486–489. The quotient is concentrated in degrees \(0,\ldots,M\).
These statements hold over \(\mathbb Q\); the section and every
matrix just specified have rational coefficients.

For a nontrivial irreducible \([\nu]\), every element in its
isotypic component of \(P\) has positive degree. Taking
\(\operatorname{Hom}_{S_m}([\nu],-)\) in (FH.9) therefore gives
a surjection onto the free \(I\)-module \(P_\nu\). Choose its
homogeneous \(I\)-basis from \(H_\nu\); lift each basis map of
degree \(D\) by \(\nabla/D\), and extend \(I\)-linearly. This
is an explicit rational \(I\)-linear section. Hence \(K_\nu\)
is a graded direct summand of a finite free \(I\)-module.

For completeness, its graded freeness needs no unspecified basis
theorem. Choose homogeneous lifts of a vector-space basis of
\(K_\nu/I_+K_\nu\); multiplication gives a map from the corresponding
graded free module. Graded Nakayama proves surjectivity. Projectivity
splits the map, and its kernel has zero quotient by \(I_+\), so graded
Nakayama again proves that kernel zero. These steps specify the free
isomorphism: in finite degree the lifts can be chosen by rational row
reduction of the actual kernels and invariant multiples. The resulting
free generators have degrees at most \(M+1\), by (FH.11) below.
The coefficient formula does not require this basis computation.

The finite numerator is
\[
\operatorname{Hilb}(K_\nu;q)
=\frac{q f_{\nu\otimes E}(q)-f_\nu(q)}
 {\prod_{i=2}^m(1-q^i)}.
\tag{FH.11}
\]
The degree of its numerator is at most \(M+1\), since both
fake-degree polynomials refer to \(H\). Here the denominator refers
to the displayed algebra \(I\), so it retains its actual free-module
meaning.

We compute the numerator explicitly. On a cycle of length \(l\),
the polynomial/exterior trace on the permutation representation is
\((1-(-z)^l)/(1-q^l)\). Removing its trivial line and applying the
Frobenius formula gives
\[
\sum_{j\ge0}\operatorname{Hilb}((P\otimes\Lambda^jE)_\nu;q)z^j
=\frac{1-q}{1+z}\,
s_\nu\left[\frac{1-(-z)}{1-q}\right].
\tag{FH.12}
\]
Macdonald I§3 Example3, p45, evaluates the right side. Multiplying
by \(\prod_{i=2}^m(1-q^i)\) gives exactly
\[
\sum_j f_{\nu\otimes\Lambda^jE}(q)z^j
=f_\nu(q)\prod_{v\in\nu\setminus\{(1,1)\}}
(1+zq^{c(v)}).
\tag{FH.13}
\]
The one removed factor is the literal \(1+z\) at cell \((1,1)\).
For non-row \(\nu\), cell \((2,1)\) contributes \(q^{-1}\)
to the coefficient of \(z\). Thus
\(qf_{\nu\otimes E}-f_\nu\) is exactly (FH.3): its subtraction
cancels this one specified term. Every remaining summand is a
nonnegative shifted fake-degree polynomial. The shifts may be
negative, but the resulting exponents are nonnegative: the lowest
possible exponent is at least
\(n(\nu)+2-\ell(\nu)\ge1\). This proves (FH.3)–(FH.4)
with no positivity inferred from a virtual expression alone.

## 3. Trivial multiplicity: actual differential forms and positive cells

The missing trivial component in the surjection onto \(P_+\)
matters. Its exact replacement is Solomon's invariant-form theorem:
*Invariants of finite reflection groups*, Nagoya Math.J.22(1963),
§3 unnumbered Theorem, p59, complete proof pp59–61. In degree one
it identifies
\[
(P\otimes E)^{S_m}=\bigoplus_{i=2}^m I\xi_i,
\qquad \xi_i=\frac1i\,de_i,\qquad\delta\xi_i=e_i.
\tag{FH.14}
\]
The invariant dot form identifies \(E\) with its dual so that these
are the same polynomial differential forms as (FH.9). Euler's formula
proves the last equality, including its scalar. Thus \(K^{S_m}\)
is the actual first cycle module of the sequence \((e_2,\ldots,e_m)\).

Fix a nonconstant monomial \(e^\beta\) in \(I\), let
\(J=\{l:\beta_l>0\}\), and put \(i=\min J\). In multidegree
\(\beta\), the domain of (FH.14) has basis
\(e^\beta\xi_l/e_l\), \(l\in J\), all of which map to
\(e^\beta\). Consequently its kernel has the exact basis
\[
e^\beta\left(\frac{\xi_j}{e_j}-\frac{\xi_i}{e_i}\right),
\qquad j\in J\setminus\{i\}.
\tag{FH.15}
\]
Both denominators cancel because \(\beta_i,\beta_j\ge1\).
Grouping these basis vectors by \((i,j)\) gives
\[
\operatorname{Hilb}(K^{S_m};q)
=\sum_{2\le i<j\le m}
\frac{q^{i+j}}{\prod_{l=i}^m(1-q^l)}.
\tag{FH.16}
\]
This is an actual disjoint basis decomposition: a monomial and its
least support index are unique, and the displayed differences are a
basis in each multidegree. It proves (FH.5).

The nontrivial-label freeness cannot be extended to the trivial label.
Already for \(m=4\), multiplying (FH.16) by
\((1-q^2)(1-q^3)(1-q^4)\) gives
\[
q^5+q^6+q^7-q^9.
\tag{FH.17}
\]
A finite graded free module over this specific invariant algebra has
a numerator with nonnegative coefficients, namely its basis degrees.
The coefficient \(-1\) therefore proves that this trivial cycle module
is not graded free over \(I\). The positive cells (FH.15) retain the
actual module in this case.

## 4. Exact nonvanishing thresholds

The hook product in (FH.2) has lowest coefficient one, in degree
\(n(\nu)\). The coefficient one degree later is the number of
removable corners minus one: each hook of length one contributes
\(1+q+O(q^2)\), while \(\prod_{i=1}^m(1-q^i)=1-q+O(q^2)\).
Therefore (FH.3) has a positive coefficient at degree \(L_\nu\).

It also has a positive coefficient at \(L_\nu+1\) for every
non-row \(\nu\vdash m\) with \(m\ge4\). For a nonrectangle,
there are at least two corners, so the preceding fake-degree
coefficient supplies it. For a rectangle with at least two rows,
the retained cell weights \(c(v)+1\) contain their minimum and
the next integer. For a column these are \(2-m,3-m\). For width
at least two and height two they are \(1,2\). For width at least
two and height at least three they are \(2-\ell,3-\ell\), given
by the bottom first and second cells or the adjacent first-column
cell. The two retained cells exist since \(m\ge4\).

The coin weights include two and three, which generate exactly zero
and every integer at least two. Hence the coefficients at
\(L_\nu\) and \(L_\nu+1\), followed by these coin increments,
prove positivity in every degree at least \(L_\nu\). All smaller
degrees are absent by minimality. For (FH.16), the smallest degree
is five, from \((i,j)=(2,3)\), and degree six occurs from \((2,4)\).
The former cell again supplies every increment generated by two and
three. This proves (FH.7), including every endpoint.

## 5. Literal polytopes, effective computation and encoding

For each nonzero \(N_{\nu,s}\), use variables
\(u_2,\ldots,u_m,y\) and constraints
\[
u_i\ge0,\qquad0\le y\le N_{\nu,s}-1,\qquad
\sum_{i=2}^m i u_i=D-s.
\tag{FH.18}
\]
The selector can be deleted when \(N_{\nu,s}=1\). The integer
points are in bijection with a coin solution and one basis label of
that numerator degree. For (FH.5), omit the selector and use exactly
the displayed weighted equality. All these polytopes are bounded
because every coin weight is positive. The program
`first_hook_positive.py` exports their integer equality and inequality
matrices and the precise tag of each selected piece.

The numerator is computed without a character table: truncate the
hook product at degree \(M\), expand each factor
\((1-q^h)^{-1}\) by the coefficient recurrence, multiply by
\(\prod_{i=1}^m(1-q^i)\), shift by \(n(\nu)\), and add the
\(m-2\) content shifts. This uses polynomially many integer
operations in \(m\). The intermediate coefficient bit lengths are
\(O(m\log(m+1))\): the truncated denominator coefficients count
at most \((M+1)^m\) tuples, and the numerator has at most \(2^m\)
signed terms. Thus (FH.18) has a polynomial-size effective description.

The coefficient itself can also be evaluated in polynomial bit
complexity in \(m+\log(a+1)\). For \(P(q)/Q(q)\), with
\(Q(0)=1\), multiply numerator and denominator by \(Q(-q)\).
The denominator is even. To extract degree \(D\), retain the parity
\(D\bmod2\) of the new numerator, replace \(q^2\) by \(q\),
and replace \(D\) by \(\lfloor D/2\rfloor\). Repeating gives
the constant coefficient. This is Bostan–Mori's Algorithm1
(OneCoeff), §2.1, in *A simple and fast algorithm for computing the
N-th term of a linearly recurrent sequence*, SOSA2021, pp121–122
(author PDF pp4–5). The displayed identity records its exact
coefficient comparison in the present ring.
All denominator degrees are \(O(m^2)\). Their roots remain roots
of unity after squaring, so their coefficients have bit length
\(O(m^2)\). The numerator coefficients are bounded by a fixed
degree-\(O(m)\) polynomial in the accessed coefficient index times
\(2^{O(m^2)}m!\), using (FH.4) or (FH.5); hence their bit lengths
are polynomial in \(m+\log(a+1)\). There are only
\(O(\log(a+1))\) iterations, and naive polynomial multiplication
already gives the stated complexity. The script implements this exact
integer parity reduction, not an input-degree dynamic program.

The encoding statement is explicit. The bounds are polynomial in
\(m\) plus the binary lengths of the parameters. For \(t\ge1\),
the original output has \(m\) positive parts, so this is also
polynomial in its usual explicitly listed binary-part encoding.
For \(t=0\), a binary outer partition can encode large \(m\) in
few parts; the same ordinary-input assertion is made only when
\(m\) is explicitly/unarily encoded. No compressed-encoding claim
is made. Complementary outputs inherit the exact formula through
the exterior-column pairing and sign rule of T004/G015.

## 6. Grothendieck dictionary and checked sources

The original Schur-operation class is transported by the exact
balanced Cauchy, Young and stable-flag maps in (FH.8). The kernel
(FH.9) is an equivariant coherent module on the affine scheme
\(\operatorname{Spec}P\); over \(\operatorname{Spec}I\), its
nontrivial multiplicity components have the specified free
isomorphisms, while the trivial component has the exact cycle
presentation and basis (FH.14)–(FH.15). The gradient and Euler maps
are algebraic morphisms of these modules. Their associated sheaf
and representation-\(K_0\) classes are carried by the same
SGA3 I4.5/4.7.2–4.7.3 and SGA6 VI3.3 dictionaries already verified
in G015/T032. The Schur and \(\lambda\) operations use SGA6
V4.2,4.4,4.8–4.9 and the exact archive-cote133 tensor/Young maps
recorded in A012. The rational finite matrices spread over a
localization of \(\mathbb Z\) clearing their denominators; the
coefficient theorem is on the characteristic-zero generic fiber.

Primary sources read for the steps newly used here:

* Macdonald, second edition, I§3 Examples2–3, p45: ordinary and
  super principal specialization, including the full interpolation
  proof. PDF: <https://math.berkeley.edu/~corteel/MATH249/macdonald.pdf>.
* Stanley, *Invariants of finite groups and their applications to
  combinatorics*, Bull.AMS1(1979), Proposition3.1 p482,
  Theorem3.10 p485, and §4 pp486–490: homogeneous-basis freeness,
  invariant polynomials and the coinvariant representation.
  PDF: <https://sites.math.washington.edu/~billey/classes/reflection.groups/presentations/archive/stanley.1979.pdf>.
* Solomon, *Invariants of finite reflection groups*, Nagoya
  Math.J.22(1963), §3 Theorem p59, complete proof pp59–61,
  formula(4)p62: actual invariant differential-form basis.
  DOI: <https://doi.org/10.1017/S0027763000011028>.
* Bostan–Mori, SOSA2021, §2.1, proof of Theorem1 and Algorithm1,
  pp121–122 (author PDF pp4–5): parity reduction of a rational series.
  PDF: <https://specfun.inria.fr/bostan/BoMo21.pdf>.

# A uniform positive formula for every stable hook tail

## G-037. Varying outer degree, hook length and outer Schur label

Let \(m\ge3\), \(a\ge1\), \(0\le r\le m-2\), \(t\ge0\),
and \(n\ge a+t\) be integers. Put
\[
\begin{gathered}
A=mn-a-(m-1)t-r,\qquad D=a+r,\\
\lambda=(A,a+t,(t+1)^r,t^{m-2-r}).
\end{gathered}
\tag{HK.1}
\]
For every \(\mu\vdash m\), the coefficient
\(p_{\mu,(n)}^\lambda\) equals the number of integer points
in one explicitly constructed bounded rational polytope.
It has at most \(m^2+3m-4\) variables and polynomially many
integer constraints. Its matrices are constructed directly below.
An exact rational-series evaluator computes the coefficient in
time polynomial in \(m\) and the binary parameter lengths.

The encoding assertion is precise. With \(m\) explicitly sized,
these are uniform polynomial bounds. For \(t\ge1\), all \(m\)
parts of \(\lambda\) are positive, so its ordinary explicit list
contains \(m\) entries. The bounds are polynomial in that binary-part
input length and give a \(\#P\) lattice verifier. At \(t=0\), a
compressed list can have far fewer than \(m\) entries; the bound
in \(m\) is retained without asserting a bound polynomial in
\(\log m\). The formulas and support include \(t=0\).

There is a complete support test. Put
\(\nu=\mu\) for even \(t\), and \(\nu=\mu'\) for odd \(t\).
For \(\nu\ne(m)\), let \(C_\nu\) be its cells except
\((1,1),(2,1)\), and put \(w(i,j)=j-i+1\).
Let \(L\) be \(b(\nu)=\sum_i(i-1)\nu_i\) plus the sum of
the \(r\) smallest weights in this multiset. Then
\[
\boxed{\begin{aligned}
p_{\mu,(n)}^\lambda>0\iff{}&D\ge L\ \text{and}\\
&\neg\bigl(D=L+1,\ \nu\text{ rectangular},\ r\in\{0,m-2\}\bigr).
\end{aligned}}
\tag{HK.2}
\]
For \(\nu=(m)\), put \(L_0=(r+2)(r+3)/2-1\). Then
\[
\boxed{\begin{aligned}
p_{\mu,(n)}^\lambda>0\iff{}&D\ge L_0\ \text{and}\\
&\neg\bigl(r=m-2,\ D=L_0+1\bigr).
\end{aligned}}
\tag{HK.3}
\]
The reflection-group identities used below are cited as known results.
The actual plethysm comparison, uniform polytope, support and
evaluation algorithm are specified in full.

## 1. The balanced chart and the actual hook module

The first gap is
\[
A-a-t=m(n-a-t)+(m-2)a-r\ge0.
\]
The remaining parts are ordered and sum to \(mn\). Thus every
declared parameter gives a partition, including
\(a=1,r=m-2,n=a+t\).

Let \(W=\mathfrak h_m\) be the sum-zero standard permutation
module. T032/C4–C8 gives the actual equivariant isomorphism
\[
(S_\lambda\mathbb Q^m)_{(n^m)}
\simeq S_{(a+t,(t+1)^r,t^{m-2-r})}W
\simeq\operatorname{sgn}^t\otimes S_{(a,1^r)}W.
\tag{HK.4}
\]
The first map substitutes the balanced flag minors and multiplies
by \(u^{n-a-t}\), with the proved inverse chart. The second
uses the exterior-volume tensor and rational Young projectors;
\(\det W=\operatorname{sgn}\). The Specht column/row Young
comparison identifies \([\mu]\otimes\operatorname{sgn}\)
with \([\mu']\). Thus the requested coefficient is the
\([\nu]\)-multiplicity in the displayed hook module.

Put \(P=\operatorname{Sym}W\). Define the Koszul differential
\[
\partial(f\otimes v_1\wedge\cdots\wedge v_j)
=\sum_{s=1}^j(-1)^{s-1}fv_s\otimes
v_1\wedge\cdots\widehat v_s\cdots\wedge v_j.
\tag{HK.5}
\]
Give polynomial degree \(d\) tensored with exterior degree \(j\)
total degree \(d+j\). These equivariant maps preserve total degree.
The exterior derivative \(d_P\) satisfies
\(\partial d_P+d_P\partial=D\,\mathrm{id}\) on total degree \(D\):
the product and exterior rules prove this on each monomial wedge.
Hence \(D^{-1}d_P\) is an explicit contracting homotopy for \(D>0\).

Write \(Z_j=\ker\partial_j\) for \(j\ge1\), and \(Z_0=P_+\).
The actual Young inclusion identifies
\[
(Z_r)_D\simeq S_{(D-r,1^r)}W\qquad(D-r\ge1).
\tag{HK.6}
\]
Indeed exterior Pieri decomposes
\(\operatorname{Sym}^{D-r}W\otimes\Lambda^rW\) into the two
Young-projector images of shapes \((D-r+1,1^{r-1})\) and
\((D-r,1^r)\). The target of \(\partial\) contains the first
and no second shape. On the first highest vector
\(x_1^{D-r}\otimes e_1\wedge\cdots\wedge e_r\), the differential
has the nonzero term
\(x_1^{D-r+1}\otimes e_2\wedge\cdots\wedge e_r\).
Thus its kernel is exactly the second Young image. At \(r=0\)
this is the identity in positive degree. This specifies the
comparison map, including the one-column endpoint.

## 2. The exact bivariate character and its positive cancellation

For a cycle type \(\rho\vdash m\), the polynomial/exterior trace is
\[
\frac{\det(1+u\rho\mid W)}{\det(1-q\rho\mid W)}
=\frac{1-q}{1+u}
\prod_{j\in\rho}\frac{1-(-u)^j}{1-q^j}.
\tag{HK.7}
\]
Multiply the eigenvalues of each literal permutation cycle and
remove the fixed trivial line to obtain this identity.
Taking its Frobenius inner product with \([\nu]\) computes the
actual multiplicity series of \(P\otimes\Lambda W\).

Macdonald, *Symmetric Functions and Hall Polynomials*, second
edition, I§3 Examples2–3, printed p.45, gives
\[
s_\nu\left[\frac{1-z}{1-q}\right]
=q^{b(\nu)}\prod_{c\in\nu}
\frac{1-zq^{\operatorname{ct}(c)}}{1-q^{h(c)}}.
\tag{HK.8}
\]
Its substitution is \(z=-u\), with exactly the power sums in
(HK.7). The source's polynomial interpolation proof from finite
principal specialization applies to this formal exterior variable.
T027/S13–S15 gives the complete standardization bijection
\[
f_\nu(q):=\sum_{T\in\operatorname{SYT}(\nu)}
q^{\operatorname{comaj}(T)}
=q^{b(\nu)}
\frac{\prod_{i=1}^m(1-q^i)}
{\prod_{c\in\nu}(1-q^{h(c)})}.
\tag{HK.9}
\]
Here \(\operatorname{comaj}(T)=\sum_{j\in\operatorname{Des}(T)}(m-j)\),
and a descent places \(j+1\) in a lower row.

Put \(Q_m(q)=\prod_{i=2}^m(1-q^i)\). Cancelling the factor
for the specified cell \((1,1)\) gives
\[
\operatorname{Hilb}_\nu(P\otimes\Lambda W;q,u)
=\frac{f_\nu(q)}{Q_m(q)}
\prod_{c\ne(1,1)}(1+u q^{\operatorname{ct}(c)}).
\tag{HK.10}
\]
The total-degree convention replaces \(u\) by \(qu\).
The actual short exact sequences from §1, with \(P/Z_0=\mathbb Q\),
give
\[
(1+u)\sum_{j\ge0}\operatorname{Hilb}_\nu(Z_j;q)u^j
=\operatorname{Hilb}_\nu(P\otimes\Lambda W;q,qu)
-\mathbf1_{\nu=(m)}.
\tag{HK.11}
\]
For \(\nu\ne(m)\), the cell \((2,1)\) exists and has content
\(-1\). Its factor on the right is exactly \(1+u\).
Consequently
\[
\boxed{
p_{\mu,(n)}^\lambda
=[q^D]\frac{f_\nu(q)\,
e_r(q^{w(c)}:c\in C_\nu)}{Q_m(q)}.}
\tag{HK.12}
\]
The elementary polynomial sums over \(r\)-element subsets of
the specified cells; repeated equal weights retain distinct choices.
Its product with \(f_\nu\) has nonnegative coefficients and
nonnegative exponents. For any chosen set \(J\),
\[
b(\nu)+\sum_{(i,j)\in J}(j-i+1)
=\sum_{(i,j)\notin J}(i-1)+\sum_{(i,j)\in J}j\ge0.
\]
Every fake-degree exponent is at least \(b(\nu)\). Thus negative
cell weights cause no negative exponent in the numerator.
The exact sequences and Young maps above establish the original
module comparison; (HK.9) and literal subset expansion give the
subsequent finite-set count.

## 3. The invariant branch and an actual monomial basis

For \(\nu=(m)\), the invariant polynomial ring on \(W\) is
\(I=\mathbb Q[e_2,\ldots,e_m]\). Solomon, *Invariants of finite
reflection groups*, Nagoya Math. J.22 (1963), §3, unnumbered
Theorem p.59, proof pp.59–61, identifies invariant differential
forms as the exterior algebra over \(I\) on \(de_2,\ldots,de_m\).
The actual map sends each generator to that differential; its
inverse is the unique invariant coefficient expansion.
Use the invariant rational dot product on \(W\) and its inverse
to identify these forms with \(P\otimes\Lambda W\).

Euler contraction gives \(\partial(de_j)=j e_j\).
The scaled generators \(\xi_j=de_j/j\) therefore give the
actual weighted Koszul complex
\[
I\otimes\Lambda(\xi_2,\ldots,\xi_m),\qquad
\partial\xi_j=e_j,\qquad
\deg e_j=\deg\xi_j=j.
\tag{HK.13}
\]
Rational averaging makes invariant projection exact, so its cycles
are precisely the required invariant cycles.

Give both \(e_j\) and \(\xi_j\) the \(j\)-th unit multidegree.
For \(\beta=(\beta_2,\ldots,\beta_m)\), let
\(J=\{j:\beta_j>0\}\) and \(i=\min J\).
The monomials \(e^{\beta-\mathbf1_S}\xi_S\), \(S\subseteq J\),
identify this multigraded complex with the exterior algebra on
basis \(v_j\), whose differential contracts \(v_j\mapsto1\).
Its degree-\(r\) kernel has the explicit basis
\[
e^\beta\bigwedge_{j\in T}
\left(\frac{\xi_j}{e_j}-\frac{\xi_i}{e_i}\right),
\qquad T\subseteq J\setminus\{i\},\quad |T|=r.
\tag{HK.14}
\]
Each expression is polynomial: in a nonzero wedge term each
denominator occurs at most once and has positive exponent in
\(\beta\). In the basis \(v_i,v_j-v_i\), contraction kills exactly
the exterior algebra in the latter vectors. This proves spanning
and independence. In exterior degree zero retain positive total
degree, giving \(Z_0=I_+\).

The unique least support index, the chosen subset and the remaining
monomial exponents give the positive series
\[
\boxed{
p_{\mu,(n)}^\lambda
=[q^D]\sum_{i=2}^m
\frac{q^i e_r(q^{i+1},\ldots,q^m)}
{\prod_{j=i}^m(1-q^j)}.}
\tag{HK.15}
\]
This counts the actual basis (HK.14).

## 4. The literal integer polytopes

For the nontrivial branch, use \(X_{c,j}\) for each cell
\(c\in\nu\) and label \(1\le j\le m\), descent bits
\(\delta_j\) for \(j<m\), subset bits \(Y_c\) for \(c\in C_\nu\),
and coin variables \(b_i\) for \(2\le i\le m\).
All \(X,\delta,Y\) lie in \([0,1]\) and all \(b_i\ge0\).
Impose
\[
\sum_jX_{c,j}=1,\qquad
\sum_cX_{c,j}=1,\qquad
\sum_{c\in C_\nu}Y_c=r.
\tag{HK.16}
\]
Put \(\ell_c=\sum_jjX_{c,j}\) and
\(R_j=\sum_c\operatorname{row}(c)X_{c,j}\).
For an adjacent right or lower cell \(c'\), impose
\(\ell_c+1\le\ell_{c'}\). Also impose
\[
1-m(1-\delta_j)\le R_{j+1}-R_j\le m\delta_j
\qquad(1\le j<m)
\tag{HK.17}
\]
and the degree equation
\[
\sum_{i=2}^m i b_i+
\sum_{j=1}^{m-1}(m-j)\delta_j+
\sum_{c\in C_\nu}w(c)Y_c=D.
\tag{HK.18}
\]
Include \(b_i\le\lfloor(D+m^2)/i\rfloor\).
These bounds follow from (HK.18), since all negative contributions
are bounded cell weights. At an integer point (HK.16) assigns
every label exactly once. The adjacency conditions give a standard
tableau. Equation (HK.17) uniquely fixes its descents, and the
\(Y\)'s choose its cell subset. Equation (HK.18) counts exactly
(HK.12). The converse fixes every variable, so this is a bijection.
The number of variables is \(m^2+3m-4\).

For the trivial branch use \(z_j,y_j,\beta_j\), \(2\le j\le m\),
with \(0\le z_j,y_j\le1\) and
\(0\le\beta_j\le\lfloor D/j\rfloor\). Impose
\[
\begin{gathered}
\sum_jz_j=1,\quad \sum_jy_j=r,\qquad
y_j\le\sum_{i<j}z_i,\\
\beta_j\ge z_j+y_j,\qquad
\beta_j\le D\sum_{i\le j}z_i,\qquad
\sum_{j=2}^m j\beta_j=D.
\end{gathered}
\tag{HK.19}
\]
The single nonzero \(z_i\) is the least positive exponent index:
lower exponents are zero and \(\beta_i\ge1\).
The \(y\)-indices lie above it and have positive exponents.
Thus each integer point is precisely one basis element (HK.14),
and conversely each such element fixes every variable.
This branch has \(3m-3\) variables.

All matrices are integer linear matrices of polynomial size.
The bit lengths of the coefficients and bounded integer witnesses
are polynomial in the declared encoding. Matrix multiplication
checks a witness in polynomial time. Both polytopes are bounded,
including when their lattice counts are zero.

## 5. Proof of the exact support test

T028/S23–S25 proves by semistandard tableaux that the lowest
coefficient of \(f_\nu\) is one in degree \(b(\nu)\), and its
next coefficient is the number of removable corners minus one.
The lowest elementary-subset degree in (HK.12) is the sum of
the \(r\) smallest weights. No degree below \(L\) occurs,
and degree \(L\) occurs. Since \(m\ge3\), coin weights two and
three occur in the denominator. Every integer at least two is
their nonnegative sum. Thus every degree at least \(L+2\)
occurs; only the next degree needs analysis.

A nonrectangular partition has at least two removable corners,
so its next fake-degree coefficient is positive.
For a rectangular non-row partition, the retained weights form
a consecutive integer interval. For a column these are
\(2-i\), \(3\le i\le m\). For a height-two rectangle of width
at least two, they range from one to the width.
For height at least three and width at least two, adjacent
row intervals overlap; removing the two specified cells removes
no weight value, since their values one and zero also occur
at \((2,2)\) and \((3,2)\).

Every nonempty proper minimum-cardinality subset of a nonconstant
consecutive multiset admits an increase of its sum by one.
At a strict sorted cut replace the largest selected value by
the next. At an equal cut value, replace a selected cut value
by a value one higher. At a cut at the maximum value, replace
a selected value one lower by an unselected maximum.
Consecutiveness and nonconstancy ensure the required values.
Thus \(0<r<m-2\) gives a positive next elementary coefficient.
At \(r=0,m-2\) the elementary polynomial has a single exponent.
The cases with at most one retained cell have no nonempty proper
subset. This proves exactly (HK.2).

For (HK.15), the minimum is
\(i=2,T=\{3,\ldots,r+2\}\), of degree
\(2+3+\cdots+(r+2)=L_0\). When \(r<m-2\), increasing the
largest selected index by one gives degree \(L_0+1\);
for \(r=0\), use \(i=3\).
At \(r=m-2\) the minimum tag is the only tag, and the
coins cannot add one. Its denominator includes weights two
and three, so all increments at least two occur.
This proves (HK.3).

## 6. Exact evaluation at binary-sized degrees

Compute (HK.9) to degree \(\binom m2\) by polynomial multiplication
and division by \(1-q^{h(c)}\). Its finite tableau expression
proves that degree bound and positivity. Compute each elementary
polynomial by cardinality-indexed dynamic multiplication.
The numerator in (HK.12) has degree \(O(m^2)\), nonnegative
exponents, and coefficient bit length \(O(m\log m)\).
Equation (HK.15) has at most \(m-1\) positive rational terms
with numerator and denominator degrees \(O(m^2)\).

Use Bostan–Mori, *A Simple and Fast Algorithm for Computing the N-th Term of a Linearly Recurrent Sequence*, SOSA2021, §2.1, proof of Theorem1 and Algorithm1 (OneCoeff), printed pp121–122, author PDF pp4–5, <https://specfun.inria.fr/bostan/BoMo21.pdf>. The following specialization records its exact parity map and the bit bound for these particular denominators.

For any one of these fractions \(P(q)/Q(q)\), put
\(S(q)=P(q)Q(-q)\) and \(T(q)=Q(q)Q(-q)\).
The latter has only even powers. Retain in \(S\) the powers
of the desired parity and halve their indices; in \(T\)
retain the even powers and halve their indices. These new
polynomials give the coefficient in degree \(\lfloor D/2\rfloor\).
Indeed expanding \(S/T\) and taking its even or odd part gives
exactly this identity. Iterate to degree zero and divide the
constant terms. This proves the exact parity algorithm used
by the evaluator.

There are \(O(\log(D+1))\) iterations with degree \(O(m^2)\).
Denominator roots remain roots of unity: the step squares
each root while retaining its multiplicity. The constant term
is one, so coefficients have magnitudes at most \(2^{O(m^2)}\).
Each numerator step increases its coefficient bit length by
only \(O(m^2)\). Thus the arithmetic has polynomial bit
complexity in \(m\) and \(\log(D+1)\). This proves the claimed
evaluation bound as well as the independent polytope construction.

## 7. Geometric dictionary and verification

The balanced flag chart (HK.4) is T032's actual coordinate and
section map. Its frame and Proj constructions use SGA3
I4.5/4.7.2–4.7.3 and EGA II2.4.1–2.4.2,2.5.2/2.5.4.
The hook is the coherent Koszul kernel on the affine space
associated to \(W\), with explicit Euler contraction and
homogeneous contracting homotopy. The invariant differential
map (HK.13), its scalar division and the basis (HK.14)
give the same cycle module through actual arrows.
Young projection, determinant volume and Specht sign retain
the original representation and its associated bundle.
Its class lies in SGA6 VI3.3; Schur/λ operations use SGA6
V4.2,4.4,4.8–4.9. Cote133/028 is carried by A012's
tensor-word, torus-weight and Young maps.
Rational maps spread over the base obtained by inverting their
finite denominators; multiplicities are on the characteristic-zero
generic fiber.

The final matrices count the literal tableaux, cell subsets
and monomial-cycle basis through the proved inverse encodings.
They give effective section multiplicities throughout this
stable-hook family with varying outer degree and hook length.
The general varying-shape positive-description gate is recorded
separately.

The file `stable_hook_positive.py` exports the sparse integer
matrices, validation function, exact support test and binary-degree
evaluator. The separate checker computes actual permutation-cycle
Schur traces through hook Jacobi–Trudi and literal
Murnaghan–Nakayama character inner products. It also checks
original plethysms through power-sum composition and every
generated small matrix witness. Its executed counts and outcome
are in `STABLE_HOOK_POSITIVE_RECEIPT.json`. Whole-proof and
source readings have separate dated events.



# The first unstable hook order in every outer degree

## T-061. An exact evaluation kernel and a positive deleted-point formula

Let \(m\ge4\), \(a\ge2\), \(0\le r\le m-2\), \(t\ge0\), and
\(\mu\vdash m\), with
\[
(m-2)a\ge m+r.
\]
Put
\[
\begin{aligned}
n&=a+t-1,\\
\lambda&=((m-1)a+t-m-r,a+t,(t+1)^r,t^{m-2-r}),\\
D&=a+r,\qquad
\nu=\begin{cases}\mu,&t\text{ even},\\\mu',&t\text{ odd}.
\end{cases}
\end{aligned}
\tag{UH.1}
\]
These are precisely the valid hook-tail parameters of ideal order one:
\(\lambda_2-n=1\). Set \(q=m-1-r\), and let
\[
\mathcal T_{m,r}=
\{(q+1,1^r),(q,1^{r+1})\}
\ \cup\ \{(q,2,1^{r-1}):r\ge1,\ q\ge2\}.
\tag{UH.2}
\]
The displayed partitions are distinct; the last term is included only
under its stated conditions. Let \(c_{m,a,r}(\nu)\) be the complete
stable-hook coefficient of G037, namely
\([\,[\nu]:S_{(a,1^r)}\mathfrak h_m\,]\).

Then the exact formula is
\[
\boxed{
p_{\mu,(n)}^\lambda
=c_{m,a,r}(\nu)-\mathbf1_{\nu\in\mathcal T_{m,r}}.}
\tag{UH.3}
\]
The subtraction has an explicit positive realization. At \(a=2\),
the coefficient is one for
\(\nu=(m-r-2,2,1^r)\) and zero otherwise. At \(a\ge3\), an
unaffected label uses G037's single polytope. For an affected label,
§4 specifies one actual lattice point of that polytope and §5 partitions
its complement into disjoint bounded polytopes. There are at most
\(2(m^2+3m-4)\) selected pieces, with at most \(m^2+3m-4\)
variables each. All matrices and the removed point are constructed
in polynomial time in \(m\) and the binary parameter lengths.
The exact coefficient and its nonvanishing are computed in the same
polynomial bit bound by G037 and (UH.3).

As in G037, ordinary binary-part input bounds follow when \(t\ge1\),
because the output then has \(m\) positive parts. At \(t=0\),
the polynomial bound in \(m\) is asserted for explicit/unary outer
degree, without a bound polynomial in a compressed \(\log m\) input.

## 1. The actual first-order section module

Let \(E=\mathfrak h_m\), of dimension \(m-1\), with its rational
invariant dot form. Let \(v_i=e_i-m^{-1}\mathbf1\), and
\(Z=\{[v_1],\ldots,[v_m]\}\subset\mathbb P(E)\).
Every \(m-1\) of these vectors form a basis and their sole relation
is \(\sum_i v_i=0\). Write \(Q\) for the tautological quotient
on \(\mathbb P(E)\).

The exact flag vanishing model G015 gives, after the full determinant
factor is removed,
\[
(S_\lambda\mathbb Q^m)_{(n^m)}
\simeq\operatorname{sgn}^{t}\otimes
H^0\bigl(\mathbb P(E),\mathcal I_Z\otimes
\mathcal O(a)\otimes\Lambda^rQ^*\bigr).
\tag{UH.4}
\]
Here \(\mathcal O(a)\Lambda^rQ^*=\Omega^r(a+r)\).
To specify the pushforward from the full flag, trivialize \(Q\)
on an affine base chart. The remaining flag factor has the exterior
Young line of weight \((1^r)\), whose sections are \(\Lambda^rQ^*\)
by the exact Borel–Weil/Plücker map used in G015. The Čech maps
on this product chart are scalar maps over \(\mathbb Q\); tensoring
them with the base ideal module is exact over that field. Their
degree-zero kernel therefore gives precisely the sheaf in (UH.4).
These local comparisons glue. No flatness of the point ideal is assumed.

The Euler inclusion of \(\Omega^r(a+r)\) into
\(\mathcal O(a)\otimes\Lambda^rE^*\) identifies its sections
with G037's actual Koszul kernel \((Z_r)_D\). Its point evaluation is
\[
\operatorname{ev}_a:S_{(a,1^r)}E^*\longrightarrow
\bigoplus_{i=1}^m\Lambda^r\operatorname{ann}(v_i),
\qquad F\longmapsto(F(v_i))_i.
\tag{UH.5}
\]
The values lie in the displayed annihilator because the Euler
contraction of \(F\) is zero. The fiber line is trivialized by the
specified affine vector \(v_i\), so literal permutations introduce
no additional scalar. The form identifies all duals equivariantly.
Consequently the right side is
\[
T_{m,r}=\operatorname{Ind}_{S_{m-1}}^{S_m}
\Lambda^r\mathfrak h_{m-1},
\tag{UH.6}
\]
and (UH.4) is exactly \(\operatorname{sgn}^t\otimes\ker\operatorname{ev}_a\).

## 2. Surjectivity, including the smallest degree

First let \(a\ge3\). Write \(z_i\) for the centered coordinate
function and \(s_2=\sum_jz_j^2\). Define
\[
p_i=\frac{m}{m-2}z_i^2-
\frac{s_2}{(m-2)(m-1)},\qquad
\ell_i=\frac{m}{m-1}z_i.
\tag{UH.7}
\]
Direct substitution gives \(p_i(v_j)=\delta_{ij}\) and
\(\ell_i(v_i)=1\). For
\(\phi_i\in\Lambda^r\operatorname{ann}(v_i)\), put
\[
s_i(\phi_i)=p_i\ell_i^{a-3}\,
\iota_z(\ell_i\wedge\phi_i).
\tag{UH.8}
\]
This is a polynomial horizontal \(r\)-form of coefficient degree
\(2+(a-3)+1=a\), since \(\iota_z^2=0\). Its value is
\(\phi_i\) at \(v_i\) and zero at every other point.
The sum of these maps is an actual rational equivariant right inverse
to (UH.5): the coordinate formulas and affine frame are permuted
literally. This proves surjectivity for every \(r\) at \(a\ge3\).

At \(a=2\), consider the map into the same evaluation target from
\(E^*\otimes\Lambda^{r+1}E^*\), sending
\(l\otimes\theta\) to the values of \(l\iota_z\theta\).
Its adjoint under the natural perfect pairings is
\[
(\psi_i)_i\longmapsto
\sum_{i=1}^m v_i\otimes(v_i\wedge\psi_i),
\qquad\psi_i\in\Lambda^r(E/\mathbb Qv_i).
\tag{UH.9}
\]
The wedge is well defined and injective on each quotient exterior
power. Because the kernel of \(\mathbb Q^m\to E\),
\(e_i\mapsto v_i\), is the constant line, a tuple in (UH.9)'s
kernel has \(v_i\wedge\psi_i=\eta\) independent of \(i\).
Thus
\[
\eta\in\bigcap_i\bigl(v_i\wedge\Lambda^rE\bigr)
\subseteq\Lambda^{r+1}E.
\]
Choose any \(m-1\) frame vectors as a basis. A wedge lying in every
one of their principal exterior ideals must contain every basis
vector. It is zero when \(r+1<m-1\). Therefore (UH.9) is injective
for \(r\le m-3\), and evaluation is surjective in that range.
The validity inequality at \(a=2\) gives \(r\le m-4\), so this
includes every declared degree-two parameter.

For precision, at the excluded endpoint \(a=2,r=m-2\), the
intersection is \(\det E\), and the cokernel has the sign character
and dimension one. Thus the surjectivity bound was not extended
past the proved degree range. At \(a=1\) no parameter satisfies
the first-gap inequality in (UH.1).

The adjoint proof also specifies a rational splitting at \(a=2\):
if \(B\) is the map just used, take invariant positive dot forms and
use \(B^*(BB^*)^{-1}\), followed by \(l\otimes\theta\mapsto
l\iota_z\theta\). The surjectivity proof makes the Gram inverse
well defined. Together with (UH.8), this supplies actual splittings
at every valid parameter, not only a character comparison.

## 3. The at-most-three correction labels and the degree-two value

The exterior representation in (UH.6) is the hook
\([(m-1-r,1^r)]\) of \(S_{m-1}\). Inducing one box gives exactly
the addable-box partitions in (UH.2), each once. This is the usual
Frobenius induction product followed by the one-box Pieri identity:
Macdonald I§7(7.1)–(7.3), pp112–113, and I§5(5.16), p73.
The coset map and rational Young projections give the corresponding
actual module decomposition. The exact surjection (UH.5) consequently
proves (UH.3), including every outer determinant twist.

At \(a=2\), first remove the determinant shift \(t\) through
the perfect exterior-column map of T005. The inner degree becomes
one and the output becomes
\[
\lambda^0=(m-r-2,2,1^r,0^{m-r-2}).
\]
Its nonzero entries form a partition precisely because \(r\le m-4\).
The actual tensor-word/Young construction gives
\(S_\mu(\operatorname{Sym}^1V)=S_\mu V\); the determinant
shift has already changed the effective outer label to \(\nu\).
Thus the coefficient is exactly the indicator stated after (UH.3).
Equivalently, the evaluation kernel is the single Specht type
\([(m-r-2,2,1^r)]\), with its rational Young inclusion. This
also agrees with the degree-two evaluation splitting just proved.

## 4. A specified stable-hook lattice point to remove

Assume \(a\ge3\) and \(\nu\in\mathcal T_{m,r}\). We construct
one point of G037's actual polytope. The construction is polynomial
in \(m\) and the binary degree, and includes its smallest cases.

For a non-row \(\nu\), let \(T_0\) be the row-superstandard
tableau, with consecutive labels in successive rows. Its comajor
degree is \(b(\nu)\). Choose the \(r\) smallest retained cell
weights \(w(i,j)=j-i+1\), breaking ties lexicographically.
This gives the minimum degree \(L\) from G037. For the two hook
labels in (UH.2) the minima are respectively \(r+2\) and
\(r+1\); for the third label the minimum is \(r+2\).
The row label occurs only at \(r=0\) and is treated below.

If \(D-L\ne1\), it is nonnegative and, in these parameters,
at least two. Represent it by coins two and three: take one coin
three when it is odd, and fill the remainder with coins two.
The tableau, subset and coins give the required point.

The remaining case is \(a=3\) for a label with \(L=r+2\).
The following changes increase the numerator degree by exactly one:

| Effective label | Change from the minimum tableau/subset |
|---|---|
| \((q+1,1^r)\), \(r\ge1\) | Swap the entries at \((1,q+1)\) and \((2,1)\). |
| \((q,2,1^{r-1})\), \(r\ge2\) | Swap the entries at \((2,2)\) and \((3,1)\). |
| \((q,2)\), \(q\ge3\) | Use first row \(1,\ldots,q-1,q+2\), second row \(q,q+1\). |
| \((2,2)\) | Keep \(T_0\) and choose retained cell \((1,2)\) instead of \((2,2)\). |

Each displayed tableau remains standard. In the first two rows of
the table, the affected descent moves one step earlier and the
remaining descents are unchanged, increasing comajor by one. In
the third row the sole descent moves from \(q\) to \(q-1\).
In the last row the chosen weight increases from one to two.
Thus the total degree becomes exactly \(D\), with no coins needed.

For the row label \(\nu=(m)\), one has \(r=0\) and \(D=a\ge3\).
Represent \(D\) using coins two and three as above, set the single
least-support bit to the first positive exponent, and set every
subset bit to zero. This gives exactly one point of (HK.19).

Finally fill every assignment bit, descent bit, subset bit and coin
coordinate with the values just specified. The construction fixes
every variable. These formulas give the function
`canonical_removed_point` in the executable; its result is checked
against the literal G037 matrices.

## 5. Positive disjoint cells and the executable formula

Let \(P\) be the relevant stable-hook polytope in its given order of
\(N\le m^2+3m-4\) coordinates, and let \(v\in P\cap\mathbb Z^N\)
be the point just constructed. For each \(j=1,\ldots,N\), use two
copies of the original constraints, adding
\[
x_i=v_i\quad(i<j),\qquad
x_j\le v_j-1
\quad\text{or}\quad x_j\ge v_j+1.
\tag{UH.10}
\]
These are bounded rational polytopes. Their lattice sets are disjoint:
the tag records the first coordinate at which a point differs from
\(v\), and the sign of that difference. Conversely every integer
point of \(P\setminus\{v\}\) has exactly this tag. Thus their
total lattice count is the original stable coefficient minus one.
Together with the actual evaluation splitting, this proves the
positive formula for its kernel. No rank calculation remains.

An unaffected label uses \(P\) itself. The degree-two indicator is
the zero-dimensional one-point polytope or the empty union. The
program `first_unstable_hook_positive.py` exports every literal matrix,
the original parameters, its effective label, and the removed point.
Its exact coefficient routine calls G037's proved binary-degree
evaluator and removes the specified target multiplicity. This is
polynomial bit computation, and (UH.10) is a positive polynomial-size
description of the same value.

## 6. Scheme and K0 transport, endpoints and scope

The original comparison is G015's coordinate map and polynomial
extension criterion with \(k=1\), retaining the determinant line.
The projective pushforward in (UH.4), the Euler inclusion and the
point restriction are actual maps of coherent sheaves. The rational
right inverses (UH.8)–(UH.9) induce the finite-group module splitting
whose covariant rank is computed by (UH.3). The kernels and images
therefore carry the same Schur-operation class through the established
SGA3 I4.5/4.7.2–4.7.3, SGA6 VI3.3 and SGA6 V4.2,4.4,4.8–4.9
dictionaries, with the archive-cote133 tensor/Young comparison A012.
The explicit affine/projective constructions use the EGA locators
already checked for G015. All maps are rational and spread after
their finite denominators are inverted; the multiplicity statement
is on the characteristic-zero generic fiber.

The valid small parameters are exhausted: \(a=1\) is impossible;
\(a=2\) is exactly \(r\le m-4\); every \(a\ge3\) is valid
for every \(r\le m-2\). The last assertion follows from
\((m-2)3-m-r\ge m-4\ge0\). Thus the first unstable hook order
has a complete positive formula in varying outer degree, hook length
and outer label. Higher ideal orders remain a separate explicit
section problem.
