# Stable tails with second part two in every outer degree

## G-038. Positive free and Koszul formulas for all stable tails \((a,2)\)

Let \(m\ge3\), \(a\ge2\), \(t\ge0\), \(n\ge a+t\), and
\(\mu\vdash m\). Define
\[
\begin{gathered}
\lambda=(mn-a-2-(m-1)t,a+t,t+2,t^{m-3}),\qquad D=a+2,\\
\nu=\mu\quad(t\text{ even}),\qquad
\nu=\mu'\quad(t\text{ odd}),\qquad N=\binom m2.
\end{gathered}
\tag{SR2.1}
\]
The displayed tuple is a partition: its first gap is at least
\(a-2\), and its second gap is \(a-2\). The coefficient
\(p_{\mu,(n)}^\lambda\) has a positive description by at most
\(N+4\) explicitly constructed bounded polytopes, each with at
most \(3m-3\) variables. Their matrices and an exact coefficient
and support evaluator have bit complexity polynomial in \(m\)
and the binary parameter lengths. At \(t\ge1\), the ordinary
binary-part output lists \(m\) positive parts. At \(t=0\), the
bound is stated in \(m\) and the binary parameters; no bound
polynomial in the compressed \(\log m\) encoding is asserted.

Here is the full formula. Put \(W=\mathfrak h_m\),
\(P=\operatorname{Sym}W\), and
\(I=P^{S_m}=\mathbb Q[e_2,\ldots,e_m]\), with
\(\deg e_i=i\). Let \(f_\alpha(q)\) be the actual graded
coinvariant multiplicity polynomial of \([\alpha]\), as in
G037/HK8–11. For a representation \(T\), write
\(f_T=\sum_\alpha[T:[\alpha]]f_\alpha\). Define
\[
A_\nu(q)=q^2f_{[\nu]\otimes\operatorname{Sym}^2W}(q),
\qquad B_\nu(q)=qf_{[\nu]\otimes W}(q).
\tag{SR2.2}
\]
There are two specified exceptional labels:
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
\nu&d_\nu\\\hline
(m-1,1)&1\\
(m-2,1,1)&2
\end{array}
\]
They are distinct for every \(m\ge3\). Let \(\epsilon_\nu=1\)
on these two labels and zero on all others; terms containing
\(d_\nu\) below occur only for these two labels. Set
\[
F_\nu(q)=A_\nu(q)-B_\nu(q)
+\epsilon_\nu q^{d_\nu}
 \left(1-\sum_{i=2}^m q^i\right)
=\sum_{j=0}^{N+2}c_{\nu,j}q^j.
\tag{SR2.3}
\]
Every \(c_{\nu,j}\) is a nonnegative integer. The exact positive
coefficient is
\[
\boxed{\begin{aligned}
p_{\mu,(n)}^\lambda
={}&\sum_{j=0}^{N+2}c_{\nu,j}
 \#\{(b_2,\ldots,b_m)\ge0:\ \sum_{i=2}^m ib_i=D-j\}\\
&+\epsilon_\nu [q^{D-d_\nu}]
 \sum_{2\le i<k\le m}
 \frac{q^{i+k}}{\prod_{l=i}^m(1-q^l)}.
\end{aligned}}
\tag{SR2.4}
\]
All counts with a negative right side are zero. Sections3–5 give
the actual module decomposition proving positivity of (SR2.3),
and sections6–7 give a polynomial algorithm for its coefficients
and every polytope matrix.

## 1. Exact transport to the stable Schur module

Use the stable flag coordinate map T032/C4–8, or the balanced
highest-space model G015 with ideal order zero. Removing the
displayed determinant line by its perfect exterior-column pairing
gives the actual \(S_m\)-module isomorphism
\[
(S_\lambda\mathbb Q^m)_{(n^m)}
\simeq\operatorname{sgn}^t\otimes S_{(a,2)}W.
\tag{SR2.5}
\]
The condition \(\lambda_2\le n\) is precisely \(a+t\le n\).
The same coordinate map multiplies the stable first-row generator
when \(n\) increases, and its inverse divides on the specified
stable chart; polynomial extension was proved in T032. Thus
(SR2.5) identifies the original coefficient with
\([S_{(a,2)}W:[\nu]]\), including the sign twist. All subsequent
maps are on this actual Schur module.

## 2. Quadratic polarization, its kernel and its whole cokernel

Give the two free \(P\)-modules
\[
\mathcal A=P\otimes\operatorname{Sym}^2W,
\qquad \mathcal B=P\otimes W
\]
the total grading in which their tensor factors have degrees two
and one. The \(P\)-linear, \(GL(W)\)-equivariant morphism is
\[
\phi(f\otimes uv)=fu\otimes v+fv\otimes u.
\tag{SR2.6}
\]
Put \(K=\ker\phi\). In total degree \(D\ge4\), Pieri gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal A_D&=S_{(D)}W\oplus S_{(D-1,1)}W
                         \oplus S_{(D-2,2)}W,\\
\mathcal B_D&=S_{(D)}W\oplus S_{(D-1,1)}W.
\end{aligned}
\tag{SR2.7}
\]
The Young inclusions are the rational tensor symmetrizers; use
Macdonald I§5(5.16), p73, for the Pieri decomposition. The map
on the first summand is nonzero, since
\(x^{D-2}\otimes x^2\) maps to
\(2x^{D-1}\otimes x\). On the second summand its highest vector
\[
x^{D-2}\otimes xy-x^{D-3}y\otimes x^2
\]
maps to
\(x^{D-1}\otimes y-x^{D-2}y\otimes x\), which is nonzero.
Both vectors are killed by the raising operator sending \(y\)
to \(x\), so this specifies the asserted highest summands.
The highest vector
\[
x^{D-2}\otimes y^2-2x^{D-3}y\otimes xy
                       +x^{D-4}y^2\otimes x^2
\]
is killed by \(\phi\) and by that raising operator. Its weight is
\((D-2,2)\). The rational Young inclusion and complete
reducibility now give the exact kernel
\[
K_D=S_{(D-2,2)}W\quad(D\ge4).
\tag{SR2.8}
\]
These calculations remain valid in dimension two; unavailable
Schur summands vanish by their column antisymmetrizers.

The small degrees determine the entire cokernel. At degree one,
\(\mathcal A_1=0\) and \(\mathcal B_1=W\). At degree two,
the map is the nonzero symmetric inclusion
\(\operatorname{Sym}^2W\to W\otimes W\), whose cokernel
is \(\Lambda^2W\). At degree three the two summands displayed
for \(\mathcal B_D\) occur once in \(\mathcal A_D\), and the
same two nonzero vectors prove surjectivity. All degrees at least
four were already covered. Consequently
\[
\operatorname{coker}\phi=W\text{ in degree1}
                 \ \oplus\ \Lambda^2W\text{ in degree2}.
\tag{SR2.9}
\]
Every positive-degree element of \(I\) kills this cokernel,
because its degree is at least two and all cokernel degrees at
least three are zero. The exterior hook Young map identifies
\(W=[m-1,1]\) and \(\Lambda^2W=[m-2,1,1]\).
This proves the two exact exceptional labels, with multiplicity
one and their specified degrees.

## 3. Actual free modules away from those two labels

Apply \(\operatorname{Hom}_{S_m}([\nu],-)\) to (SR2.6).
Rational averaging makes this functor exact. The homogeneous
coinvariant section, averaged over \(S_m\), gives the actual
graded multiplication isomorphism \(I\otimes H\simeq P\)
used in A088§1, with \(H=P/(I_+)\). Thus
\(\mathcal A_\nu\) and \(\mathcal B_\nu\) are finite graded
free over \(I\); their basis polynomials are exactly
\(A_\nu(q)\) and \(B_\nu(q)\). The rational invariant perfect
forms identify dual Specht modules and justify the tensor
multiplicity notation in (SR2.2).

For every label outside the two in (SR2.9), the actual map
\(\mathcal A_\nu\to\mathcal B_\nu\) is surjective. Lift each
chosen homogeneous free basis vector of the target and extend
\(I\)-linearly. This is a graded section of the displayed map,
so its kernel is finite graded projective. Choose homogeneous
lifts of a basis modulo \(I_+\). Graded Nakayama gives a
surjective map from the associated graded free module. Its
kernel is a graded direct summand, because the target is
projective. Reducing modulo \(I_+\) leaves zero kernel, and a
second graded Nakayama application gives zero kernel itself.
This proves a free isomorphism. Its basis degrees have
polynomial \(A_\nu-B_\nu=F_\nu\), establishing positivity
for every such label through an actual module decomposition.

## 4. The two exceptional modules and the exact Koszul summand

Fix either of the two listed labels and write \(d=d_\nu\).
The cokernel is one copy of \(I/I_+\) in degree \(d\).
Choose a homogeneous free basis of \(\mathcal B_\nu\)
adapted to its quotient: one basis vector \(e_0\) of degree
\(d\) maps to1, and every other basis vector maps to0.
Such a basis is obtained by rational row reduction among the
degree-\(d\) basis vectors; all other degrees already map to0.
It follows exactly that
\[
\operatorname{im}\phi_\nu=I_+e_0\oplus\mathcal B',
\tag{SR2.10}
\]
where \(\mathcal B'\) is the free span of the remaining vectors.

Lift the basis of \(\mathcal B'\) through the actual map.
Projection to \(\mathcal B'\) gives a split surjection, and
its kernel \(\mathcal A_0\) is graded free by the same
projective/Nakayama proof. The remaining map is the actual
surjection
\(\mathcal A_0\to I_+e_0\).
For each \(i=2,\ldots,m\), choose a homogeneous lift \(x_i\)
of \(e_ie_0\), in degree \(d+i\).
Their residues in \(\mathcal A_0/I_+\mathcal A_0\) are
linearly independent: a relation would map to a relation among
the independent minimal generators \(e_i\) in
\(I_+/I_+^2\). Choose a homogeneous complementary residue
basis in the kernel of this residue map and lift it to vectors
\(y_j\). The \(x_i,y_j\) form a homogeneous free basis;
the graded Nakayama argument just given proves this directly.

Every image of \(y_j\) is in \(I_+^2e_0\). Express it as
\(\sum_i g_{ji}e_ie_0\), where each \(g_{ji}\in I_+\)
is homogeneous, and replace \(y_j\) by
\(y_j-\sum_i g_{ji}x_i\). This is an invertible triangular
basis change and makes every such image zero. We have proved
the actual graded decomposition
\[
\begin{gathered}
K_\nu\simeq\mathcal F_\nu\oplus Z_1(I)[d],\\
Z_1(I)=\ker\left(\bigoplus_{i=2}^m I\xi_i
 \longrightarrow I\right),\quad
\deg\xi_i=i,\quad\xi_i\longmapsto e_i.
\end{gathered}
\tag{SR2.11}
\]
Here \([d]\) denotes addition of \(d\) to the degrees, and
\(\mathcal F_\nu\) is the free span of the adjusted \(y_j\).
Every map and basis choice can be implemented by rational
homogeneous row reduction in the indicated finite degrees.

The basis polynomial of \(\mathcal A_0\) is
\(A_\nu-B_\nu+q^d\). Removing the displayed free basis
vectors \(x_i\) subtracts \(q^d\sum_{i=2}^m q^i\).
The remaining free polynomial is exactly (SR2.3). Its
coefficients are therefore nonnegative integers for both
exceptional labels as well. Since the coinvariant degrees
are at most \(N\), every free generator degree is at most
\(N+2\). The same bound covers the correction terms because
\(m\le N\) for \(m\ge3\).

## 5. A polynomial basis for the weighted Koszul cycle

For a monomial \(e^\beta\), let
\(J=\{i:\beta_i>0\}\) and \(i=\min J\).
For each \(k\in J\setminus\{i\}\), the polynomial vector
\[
e^\beta\left(\frac{\xi_k}{e_k}
                         -\frac{\xi_i}{e_i}\right)
\tag{SR2.12}
\]
is in \(Z_1(I)\). The notation has no poles: both denominators
divide the displayed monomial. In this multidegree the map to
\(I\) sends every basis vector \(e^\beta\xi_j/e_j\)
to \(e^\beta\). Its kernel has precisely the differences
in (SR2.12) as a basis. This is a complete direct proof over
every multidegree, and agrees with G037/HK13–14 and A088§2.

The index \(i\) is the first positive exponent; choosing
\(k>i\) forces both exponents to be positive. Other exponents
with index at least \(i\) are arbitrary. Consequently the
Hilbert series of this actual basis is
\[
\operatorname{Hilb}Z_1(I)
=\sum_{2\le i<k\le m}
  \frac{q^{i+k}}{\prod_{l=i}^m(1-q^l)}.
\tag{SR2.13}
\]
Combining (SR2.8), the free decompositions and (SR2.13) gives
(SR2.4) in every parameter of (SR2.1).

## 6. Computing the free numerator in polynomial time

No enumeration of all partitions of \(m\) is needed. Write
\(\alpha\nearrow\beta\) for addition of one corner box.
The permutation module \(E=\mathbb Q^m\) has \(E=\mathbf1\oplus W\).
The actual coset tensor map and restriction/induction give
\[
[\nu]\otimes E\simeq
 \operatorname{Ind}_{S_{m-1}}^{S_m}
 \operatorname{Res}_{S_{m-1}}^{S_m}[\nu].
\]
For definiteness, the coset tensor isomorphism sends
\(v\otimes gH\) to \(g\otimes g^{-1}v\), with inverse
\(g\otimes w\mapsto gw\otimes gH\).
Therefore the multiplicity of \([\alpha]\) in
\([\nu]\otimes W\) is the number of two-step paths
\(\nu\searrow\beta\nearrow\alpha\), minus
\(\mathbf1_{\alpha=\nu}\). This yields at most \(O(m^2)\)
candidate labels by literal corner operations.

There is also an actual isomorphism
\[
\mathbb Q\{\{i,j\}:i<j\}
 \longrightarrow\operatorname{Sym}^2W,
\qquad \{i,j\}\longmapsto(P_me_i)(P_me_j).
\tag{SR2.14}
\]
To prove injectivity, pair with the hyperplane \(\sum x_i=0\).
A kernel element gives a quadratic polynomial
\(\sum_{i<j}a_{ij}x_ix_j\) vanishing on that hyperplane.
It is divisible by \(\sum x_i\), and hence equals
\((\sum x_i)(\sum b_ix_i)\). Its square coefficients are
zero, forcing every \(b_i=0\), and then every \(a_{ij}=0\).
Both spaces have dimension \(\binom m2\), proving the stated
equivariant isomorphism, with a rational inverse.

The left side of (SR2.14) is the coset module for
\(S_{m-2}\times S_2\). The same tensor-coset map identifies
\([\nu]\otimes\operatorname{Sym}^2W\) with induction of
its restriction to that subgroup. One removes a two-box
horizontal strip or a two-box vertical strip from \(\nu\)
and adds a strip of the same kind. Each branch has multiplicity
one by the two Pieri identities, and different branches are
counted separately. Thus
\[
\begin{aligned}
M_{\nu,\alpha}={}&
 \#\{\beta:\nu/\beta,\alpha/\beta
                         \text{ horizontal strips of size2}\}\\
&+\#\{\beta:\nu/\beta,\alpha/\beta
                         \text{ vertical strips of size2}\}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{SR2.15}
\]
This formula follows from Frobenius reciprocity and the actual
rational Young branching maps; use Macdonald I§7(7.1)–(7.3),
pp112–113, and I§5(5.16) and its conjugate, p73. Two corner
removals followed by two additions give \(O(m^4)\) candidate
paths. The strip tests are the displayed interlacing inequalities
for horizontal strips and row differences at most one for
vertical strips. No unspecified tensor-product coefficient is
left in (SR2.2).

For each encountered \(\alpha\), use the proved fake-degree
formula from G037/HK8–11:
\[
f_\alpha(q)=q^{b(\alpha)}
 \frac{\prod_{i=1}^m(1-q^i)}
      {\prod_{c\in\alpha}(1-q^{h(c)})}.
\tag{SR2.16}
\]
Truncate the formal product division at degree \(N\); this
recovers the whole polynomial, whose degree is at most \(N\).
The coefficients count standard tableaux with the proved comajor
statistic and have size at most \(m!\). The path multiplicities
are polynomial in \(m\), so every computed coefficient has
\(O(m\log m)\) bits. Equations (SR2.2)–(SR2.3) now compute
all \(c_{\nu,j}\) in polynomial bit complexity. Positivity
was proved by the exact free decomposition and is also checked
as an executable assertion.

## 7. Literal polytopes, support and binary-degree evaluation

For each \(j\) with \(c_{\nu,j}>0\) and \(j\le D\), take
the following bounded polytope in \(m\) variables:
\[
\begin{gathered}
0\le u\le c_{\nu,j}-1,\qquad
0\le b_i\le\left\lfloor\frac{D-j}{i}\right\rfloor
\quad(2\le i\le m),\\
\sum_{i=2}^m ib_i=D-j.
\end{gathered}
\tag{SR2.17}
\]
The integer coordinate \(u\) indexes the homogeneous free
basis vectors in degree \(j\); \(b\) indexes their invariant
monomial multiples. Fixing a basis by the homogeneous rational
row reductions above gives an actual bijection. The matrices
are computed from (SR2.3) and need no construction of the full
possibly large basis.

On an exceptional label, append the single polytope
G037/HK19 with \(r=1\), trivial label, and total degree
\(D-d_\nu\). It uses the \(3(m-1)\) variables recording
least support, one chosen further support index, and exponents.
Its already proved inverse is exactly (SR2.12). Here the hook
parameter passed to G037 is \(D-d_\nu-1\ge1\), so every
declared input lies in its domain. There are at most \(N+3\)
free-degree polytopes and one cycle polytope, giving the bound
\(N+4\) and maximum dimension \(3m-3\).

The support test is explicit. A free-degree term contributes
precisely when \(c_{\nu,j}>0\) and
\(D-j\in\{0,2,3,4,\ldots\}\), because the available
coin sizes contain2 and3 and have no1. The cycle term uses
G037's proved trivial-hook support: for \(m\ge4\), every
degree at least5 occurs; for \(m=3\), degrees at least5
occur except6. Applying this to \(D-d_\nu\), and taking
the union with the free-degree test, decides every zero.

For exact coefficient evaluation, apply G037/HK18's proved
Bostan–Mori parity extraction to
\(F_\nu(q)/\prod_{i=2}^m(1-q^i)\), and append the same
G037 trivial-hook evaluator at the shifted degree. Numerator
and denominator degrees are \(O(m^2)\); the denominator
roots are roots of unity, and the bit bound proved there
applies verbatim to these exact polynomials. This supplies
polynomial bit complexity in \(m\) and \(\log(D+1)\).
The executable `stable_second_row_positive.py` contains the
corner and strip paths, every finite polynomial, support test,
literal matrix and coefficient procedure.

## 8. Geometric dictionary and check scope

Equation (SR2.5) is the actual balanced frame/flag comparison
of G015 and T032, with its determinant line. Equations
(SR2.6), (SR2.10) and (SR2.11) define morphisms and coherent
kernel sheaves over \(\operatorname{Spec}I\). The free
summands and weighted Koszul cycle are actual sheaves with
the exhibited presentations and basis morphisms. The
coset/Young maps in (SR2.14)–(SR2.15) transport the invariant
character calculation to this same kernel. These comparisons
use SGA3 I4.5/4.7.2–4.7.3 for frames and associated bundles,
EGA II2.4.1–2.4.2 and2.5.2/2.5.4 for the projective and
coherent constructions, SGA6 VI3.3 and V4.2,4.4,4.8–4.9
for the exact Schur and K0 operations. Archive cote133/028
is carried by A012's actual tensor-word, torus-weight and
Young maps. All maps are rational and spread after their
displayed finite denominators are inverted; the coefficient
theorem concerns the characteristic-zero fiber.

Whole-proof readings and independent computations are recorded
as separate dated events. The finite checks exercise the
proved maps and formulas; their numerical ranges do not replace
the unbounded module argument in sections2–5.


# Stable tails with second part three in every outer degree

## G-039. Cubic polarization and an explicit positive formula

Let \(m\ge3\), \(a\ge3\), \(t\ge0\), \(n\ge a+t\), and
\(\mu\vdash m\). Put
\[
\begin{gathered}
\lambda=(mn-a-3-(m-1)t,a+t,t+3,t^{m-3}),\quad D=a+3,\\
\nu=\mu\ (t\text{ even}),\qquad\nu=\mu'\ (t\text{ odd}),
\qquad N=\binom m2.
\end{gathered}
\tag{SR3.1}
\]
The original Schur plethysm coefficient has an explicit positive
formula using at most \(N+7\) bounded polytopes, each with at
most \(3m-1\) variables. Their matrices, the complete support
test and an exact coefficient evaluator are computable in bit
complexity polynomial in \(m\) and the binary parameters.
As in G037–G038, \(t\ge1\) gives \(m\) explicitly listed
positive output parts. At \(t=0\), the bound is in \(m\),
without a claim polynomial in the compressed \(\log m\) input.

For \(m\ge4\), the formula below has three types of positive
terms: an explicitly computed free numerator, ordinary weighted
Koszul cycles, and weighted cycles for the regular sequence
\(e_2^2,e_3,\ldots,e_m\). Its proof computes the actual
cubic polarization cokernel, including the action of \(I\).
The rank-two case \(m=3\) is given by its exact determinant
pairing in §7.

Write \(W=\mathfrak h_m\), \(P=\operatorname{Sym}W\), and
\(I=\mathbb Q[e_2,\ldots,e_m]\), \(\deg e_i=i\).
Use the actual coinvariant multiplicity polynomial \(f_T(q)\)
from G038/SR2.2. Define
\[
A_\nu=q^3f_{[\nu]\otimes\operatorname{Sym}^3W},
\qquad B_\nu=q^2f_{[\nu]\otimes\operatorname{Sym}^2W}.
\tag{SR3.2}
\]
There is a specified equivariant injection
\(\operatorname{Sym}^2W\to S_{(2,2)}W\), proved in §2.
Let \(\mathcal R\) be its Ricci-kernel complement and put
\[
c_2=[\operatorname{Sym}^2W:[\nu]],\quad
c_{21}=[S_{(2,1)}W:[\nu]],\quad c_R=[\mathcal R:[\nu]].
\tag{SR3.3}
\]
These are nonnegative integers. Set
\[
\begin{aligned}
C_0(q)&=c_2q^2+c_{21}q^3+c_Rq^4,\\
C_1(q)&=c_2q^2\left(q^4+\sum_{i=3}^m q^i\right)
             +(c_{21}q^3+c_Rq^4)\sum_{i=2}^m q^i,\\
F_\nu(q)&=A_\nu(q)-B_\nu(q)+C_0(q)-C_1(q)
              =\sum_{j=0}^{N+3}f_{\nu,j}q^j.
\end{aligned}
\tag{SR3.4}
\]
Every \(f_{\nu,j}\) is nonnegative. For an ordered positive
weight list \(\mathbf w=(w_1,\ldots,w_k)\), define the
explicit positive series
\[
Z_{\mathbf w}(q)=\sum_{1\le i<j\le k}
                  \frac{q^{w_i+w_j}}{\prod_{l=i}^k(1-q^{w_l})}.
\tag{SR3.5}
\]
Let \(\mathbf u=(2,3,\ldots,m)\) and
\(\mathbf v=(4,3,4,5,\ldots,m)\). The two entries4 in
\(\mathbf v\) refer respectively to \(e_2^2\) and \(e_4\),
so they label distinct generators. The exact formula is
\[
\boxed{\begin{aligned}
p_{\mu,(n)}^\lambda=[q^D]\Bigg(&
 \frac{F_\nu(q)}{\prod_{i=2}^m(1-q^i)}
 +(c_{21}q^3+c_Rq^4)Z_{\mathbf u}(q)\\
 &+c_2q^2(1+q^2)Z_{\mathbf v}(q)\Bigg).
\end{aligned}}
\tag{SR3.6}
\]
Section6 gives the literal bounded polytopes and all finite
polynomial calculations; no unknown multiplicity remains in
the formula.

## 1. Actual cubic polarization and every cokernel degree

The stable balanced flag map G015 and T032/C4–8 gives
\[
(S_\lambda\mathbb Q^m)_{(n^m)}
 \simeq\operatorname{sgn}^t\otimes S_{(a,3)}W.
\tag{SR3.7}
\]
Its hypotheses hold because \(\lambda_2=a+t\le n\), and
the first two gaps are respectively at least \(a-3\) and
equal to \(a-3\). This is the same actual determinant and
stable-first-row comparison used in G038/SR2.5.

Take the two graded free \(P\)-modules
\[
\mathcal A=P\otimes\operatorname{Sym}^3W,
\qquad\mathcal B=P\otimes\operatorname{Sym}^2W,
\]
with total degrees three and two for their tensor factors.
The \(P\)-linear, \(GL(W)\)-equivariant transfer is
\[
\phi(f\otimes uvw)
=fu\otimes vw+fv\otimes uw+fw\otimes uv.
\tag{SR3.8}
\]
For a completely specified highest-vector check, use variables
\(x,y\) in the first factor and \(X,Y\) in the second.
At first-factor degree \(b\ge0\), the Pieri highest vectors are
\[
H_i=x^{b-i}X^{3-i}(xY-yX)^i,
\qquad0\le i\le\min(b,3).
\]
Their weights are \((b+3-i,i)\). The transfer is
\(x\partial_X+y\partial_Y\), so it sends them to
\[
(3-i)x^{b-i+1}X^{2-i}(xY-yX)^i
\quad(0\le i\le2),
\]
and kills \(H_3\). These are the rational Young/Pieri
inclusions of Macdonald I§5(5.16), p73; the displayed vectors
are annihilated by the simultaneous raising operator.
Thus the map is nonzero on every target summand and its
kernel in total degree \(D=b+3\ge6\) is exactly
\[
K_D=S_{(D-3,3)}W.
\tag{SR3.9}
\]

The same finite summands give the whole cokernel:
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
\text{total degree}&\operatorname{coker}\phi\\\hline
2&\operatorname{Sym}^2W\\
3&S_{(2,1)}W\\
4&S_{(2,2)}W.
\end{array}
\tag{SR3.10}
\]
At degree five the summands \((5),(4,1),(3,2)\) occur on
both sides and have nonzero scalars3,2,1. All larger degrees
are surjective by the same argument, and smaller omitted
degrees have zero target. Hence (SR3.10) exhausts the
cokernel, with no infinite-degree remainder.

## 2. The exact quadratic invariant action and Ricci splitting

For this section \(m\ge4\), so \(d=\dim W=m-1\ge3\).
Let \(g\) be the rational invariant dot form on the sum-zero
space. Use its inverse to identify tensors and quadratic
forms. Since \(\sum z_i=0\), the elementary invariant is
\(e_2=-\frac12\sum z_i^2\). Every invariant of degree
at least three kills the cokernel in (SR3.10), by its stated
degree support. The only remaining action is multiplication
by \(e_2\) from degree two to degree four.

Here is the actual quotient map identifying that action.
For symmetric tensors \(A,B\), define
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal K(A,B)_{ijkl}={}&A_{ik}B_{jl}+A_{jl}B_{ik}\\
&-A_{il}B_{jk}-A_{jk}B_{il}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{SR3.11}
\]
Its image has the alternating pairs, pair interchange and
first Bianchi identity of the Young summand \(S_{(2,2)}W\).
It is symmetric in \(A,B\), killing the \((3,1)\) summand
of \(\operatorname{Sym}^2W\otimes\operatorname{Sym}^2W\).
Its full four-slot symmetrization is zero, killing \((4)\).
It is nonzero, for example on \(x^2\otimes y^2\).
Pieri has exactly these three summands, each once. Therefore
(SR3.11) induces an isomorphism from the actual degree-four
cokernel to this tensor realization of \(S_{(2,2)}W\).
It is the specified Young quotient, not a comparison of
dimensions alone. Multiplication by \(e_2\) is, in this
realization, the nonzero scalar \(-1/2\) times
\(B\mapsto\mathcal K(g,B)\).

Contract the first and third slots using \(g^{-1}\). Direct
summation in (SR3.11) gives
\[
\operatorname{Ric}\mathcal K(g,B)
  =(d-2)B+(\operatorname{tr}B)g.
\tag{SR3.12}
\]
The trace of this expression is \(2(d-1)\operatorname{tr}B\).
Consequently the inverse on the image is the explicit map
\[
B=\frac1{d-2}\left(
 \operatorname{Ric}R-
 \frac{\operatorname{tr}\operatorname{Ric}R}{2(d-1)}g\right).
\tag{SR3.13}
\]
All denominators are nonzero for every declared \(m\ge4\).
This proves injectivity of the actual \(e_2\) map. The same
formula gives a right inverse to Ricci on all symmetric
tensors. Subtracting \(\mathcal K(g,B)\) with \(B\) from
(SR3.13) defines the equivariant projector onto
\(\mathcal R=\ker\operatorname{Ric}\). Thus the degree-four
module is the actual direct sum of the quadratic image and
\(\mathcal R\). Every map is \(O(W,g)\)-equivariant and
hence \(S_m\)-equivariant.

With degree shifts written explicitly, the entire cokernel
is therefore the following actual graded \(I,S_m\)-module:
\[
\begin{aligned}
C\simeq{}&
\bigl(I/(e_2^2,e_3,\ldots,e_m)\bigr)[2]
                          \otimes\operatorname{Sym}^2W\\
&\oplus (I/I_+)[3]\otimes S_{(2,1)}W
 \oplus (I/I_+)[4]\otimes\mathcal R.
\end{aligned}
\tag{SR3.14}
\]
For the first summand, send its degree-two generator to the
given class and its multiple by \(e_2\) to the actual image
under multiplication. The injection just proved makes this
a chain of length exactly two. All other positive invariant
actions vanish by degree. The other two summands use the
displayed Young and Ricci projectors. This proves (SR3.14)
as a module isomorphism, including all invariant actions.

## 3. Cancelling free covers by explicit homogeneous basis changes

Apply \(\operatorname{Hom}_{S_m}([\nu],-)\). Rational
averaging is exact. The actual invariant/coinvariant
multiplication \(I\otimes H\simeq P\) of A088§1 makes
\(\mathcal A_\nu\) and \(\mathcal B_\nu\) finite graded
free, with basis polynomials \(A_\nu,B_\nu\).
Equation (SR3.14) gives \(c_2,c_{21},c_R\) copies of its
three displayed cyclic modules. Their minimal generator
and relation free modules are \(M_0,M_1\), with basis
polynomials \(C_0,C_1\) in (SR3.4). The relations are
the literal generators \(e_2^2,e_3,\ldots,e_m\) or
\(e_2,\ldots,e_m\), in the indicated component and degree.

We now compare these covers with the actual map. In the
quotient \(\mathcal B_\nu/I_+\mathcal B_\nu\), select
homogeneous vectors mapping to the displayed basis of
\(C_\nu/I_+C_\nu\). Lift them so that their images in
\(C_\nu\) are the specified cyclic generators, subtracting
positive-invariant multiples of already chosen lifts as
needed. Choose a complementary residue basis in the kernel.
Each complementary image is an invariant-polynomial
combination of the specified cyclic generators with zero
constant coefficients. Subtract these same combinations
of their lifts. The complementary images become zero.
These operations preserve the residue basis and hence give
an invertible homogeneous basis change by graded Nakayama.
The quotient map is now the literal direct sum of
\(M_0\to C_\nu\) and a free summand mapping to zero.

The latter free summand lies in the image of \(\phi_\nu\).
Lift its basis through \(\phi_\nu\), extend \(I\)-linearly,
and cancel this actual split summand on both sides. The
remaining domain \(\mathcal A_0\) is graded free: it is
projective, and the two graded Nakayama steps in G038§3
give a free basis. Its map is onto
\(L_1=\ker(M_0\to C_\nu)\).

Lift the specified minimal generators of \(L_1\), namely
the relation basis of \(M_1\), to homogeneous vectors of
\(\mathcal A_0\). Their residues are independent because
their images form a basis of \(L_1/I_+L_1\). Choose a
complement in the kernel of this residue map and lift it.
Its images lie in \(I_+L_1\), so they are combinations of
the minimal relation generators with coefficients in
\(I_+\). Subtracting those combinations of the chosen
lifts makes these images zero. This invertible triangular
basis change proves the actual decomposition
\[
K_\nu\simeq\mathcal F_\nu\oplus
                  \ker(M_1\longrightarrow M_0).
\tag{SR3.15}
\]
The free basis polynomial of \(\mathcal F_\nu\) is exactly
\(A_\nu-B_\nu+C_0-C_1=F_\nu\). This proves all the
nonnegative coefficients asserted in (SR3.4). It also
proves the degree bound \(N+3\): the free domain has
degrees at most \(N+3\), and every correction has degree
at most \(m+4\le N+3\) for \(m\ge4\).
All choices above are fixed by homogeneous rational row
reduction; the claimed kernel is the kernel of the original
map through the displayed invertible changes of bases.

## 4. Positive bases for both types of relation cycles

For a polynomial ring \(J=\mathbb Q[z_1,\ldots,z_k]\)
with positive weights \(w_i\), the kernel of
\(\bigoplus J\xi_i\to J\), \(\xi_i\mapsto z_i\),
has the following complete vector-space basis. For every
nonzero exponent vector \(\beta\), let \(i\) be its first
positive index; for each further positive index \(j>i\), use
\[
z^\beta\left(\frac{\xi_j}{z_j}-\frac{\xi_i}{z_i}\right).
\tag{SR3.16}
\]
The denominators cancel. In that multidegree the differential
sends each available coordinate vector to \(z^\beta\),
so exactly these differences form a basis of its kernel.
This proves (SR3.5) for arbitrary specified positive weights
by a direct coefficientwise bijection.

For the ordinary relation sequence, take
\(J=I\), \(z=(e_2,\ldots,e_m)\) and weights \(\mathbf u\).
For the other sequence take
\[
J=\mathbb Q[e_2^2,e_3,\ldots,e_m],\qquad
z=(e_2^2,e_3,e_4,\ldots,e_m).
\]
These are algebraically independent, and \(I=J\oplus e_2J\)
as an actual graded free \(J\)-module. Tensoring the kernel
map with this free module preserves its kernel. Its basis
is (SR3.16) and \(e_2\) times that same basis. Its Hilbert
series is therefore \((1+q^2)Z_{\mathbf v}\), with the
two degree-four generators still separately indexed.
The decompositions (SR3.14)–(SR3.15) now prove precisely
(SR3.6), after using the exact highest-space map (SR3.7).

## 5. Polynomial computation of every finite numerator and multiplicity

G038/SR2.14–16 already compute the tensor operators
\(T\mapsto T\otimes W\) and
\(T\mapsto T\otimes\operatorname{Sym}^2W\) through corner
and two-strip paths. Here is a finite path formula for the
remaining symmetric cube. The actual monomial orbit
decomposition of \(\operatorname{Sym}^3E\), \(E=\mathbb Q^m\),
has orbits of types3,21,111. They give respectively the
point, ordered-pair and unordered-triple permutation modules.
Since \(E=\mathbf1\oplus W\), the direct symmetric-power
decompositions give in the representation ring
\[
[\operatorname{Sym}^3W]
=[\mathbb Q\{(i,j):i\ne j\}]
+[\mathbb Q\{\{i,j,k\}:i,j,k\text{ distinct}\}]
-[\mathbb Q\{\{i,j\}:i\ne j\}].
\tag{SR3.17}
\]
This follows by subtracting the actual decompositions of
\(\operatorname{Sym}^3E\) and \(\operatorname{Sym}^2E\);
it computes characters of the stated actual symmetric cube.
The final positive numerator was already proved by modules
in §3, independently of this subtraction used in its algorithm.

Tensoring with the ordered-pair module is restriction to
\(S_{m-2}\) followed by induction: remove two boxes in
order, then add two in order, counting every path.
Tensoring with the unordered-triple module is restriction
to \(S_{m-3}\times S_3\) and induction. For each removed
three-box shape \(\beta\subset\nu\), its three restriction
multiplicities are
\[
\begin{aligned}
u_3(\nu/\beta)&=\mathbf1_{\nu/\beta\text{ horizontal}},\\
u_{111}(\nu/\beta)&=\mathbf1_{\nu/\beta\text{ vertical}},\\
u_{21}(\nu/\beta)&=
 \#\{\gamma:\nu/\gamma\text{ one box},
               \gamma/\beta\text{ horizontal two-strip}\}
 -u_3(\nu/\beta).
\end{aligned}
\tag{SR3.18}
\]
Pieri proves the first two identities; the third follows from
the actual induction decomposition \(s_2s_1=s_3+s_{21}\).
Thus the tensor multiplicity of \([\alpha]\) is
\(\sum_\beta\sum_{\tau=3,21,111}
u_\tau(\nu/\beta)u_\tau(\alpha/\beta)\).
These are the rational coset and Young maps already specified
in G038§6. At most three corner removals and three additions
are used, so this has polynomial size \(O(m^6)\).

The other fixed Schur modules in (SR3.3) are computed from
the two displayed Jacobi–Trudi/Pieri identities
\[
\begin{aligned}
[S_{(2,1)}W]&=[\operatorname{Sym}^2W\otimes W]
                                      -[\operatorname{Sym}^3W],\\
[S_{(2,2)}W]&=[\operatorname{Sym}^2W\otimes\operatorname{Sym}^2W]
                                      -[\operatorname{Sym}^3W\otimes W].
\end{aligned}
\tag{SR3.19}
\]
For the second identity, the summands \((4),(3,1)\) cancel
from the two actual Pieri decompositions, leaving precisely
\((2,2)\). Compose the already specified tensor operators;
only a fixed number of corner steps is involved. The
coefficient of the trivial label in \([\nu]\otimes T\)
gives \([T:[\nu]]\), using the actual invariant perfect
Specht pairing. Finally subtract the quadratic image
multiplicity from \([S_{(2,2)}W:[\nu]]\) to obtain \(c_R\),
justified by the Ricci splitting (SR3.12)–(SR3.13).

For every encountered label use the exact fake-degree
polynomial G038/SR2.16, with its finite hook product
division through degree \(N\). The number of corner paths
is polynomial in \(m\), their length is fixed, and every
coefficient has \(O(m\log m)\) bits by the standard-tableau
bound. This computes (SR3.2)–(SR3.4) in polynomial bit
complexity. No partition enumeration or uncomputed tensor
multiplicity is used by the formula executable.

## 6. Literal polytopes, exact support and evaluation

Each nonzero coefficient \(f_{\nu,j}\), \(j\le D\), gives
the free-degree polytope G038/SR2.17 with multiplicity
\(f_{\nu,j}\) and target degree \(D-j\). It has \(m\)
variables. For each of the three possible cycle terms, use
one least-support polytope as follows. For its weight list
\((w_1,\ldots,w_k)\), multiplicity \(c>0\), and shifted
degree \(L\), take integer variables
\(z_i,y_i\in[0,1]\), exponents
\(0\le b_i\le\lfloor L/w_i\rfloor\), and
\(0\le u\le c-1\). Impose
\[
\begin{gathered}
\sum_i z_i=1,\quad\sum_i y_i=1,\quad
y_j\le\sum_{i<j}z_i,\\
b_j\ge z_j+y_j,\qquad
b_j\le L\sum_{i\le j}z_i.
\end{gathered}
\tag{SR3.20}
\]
For the ordinary cycle term impose \(\sum_i w_ib_i=L\).
For the quadratic-sequence term append
\(\eta\in[0,1]\) and impose
\(\sum_i w_ib_i+2\eta=L\).
These are exactly the monomial-cycle labels in (SR3.16),
with \(\eta\) recording the free \(J\)-basis \(1,e_2\).
The bit \(z\) records the first positive exponent and
\(y\) the chosen later positive index; their inverse is
unique. There are \(3(m-1)+1\) ordinary variables and
one additional quadratic remainder bit, giving maximum
\(3m-1\). There are at most \(N+4\) free-degree pieces
and three cycle pieces, giving \(N+7\).

The free terms have the exact support test
\(f_{\nu,j}>0\) and \(D-j\in\{0,2,3,\ldots\}\).
For \(m\ge4\), ordinary cycles have every degree at least5,
as proved in G037/HK17. The quadratic-sequence cycles after
extension to \(I\) have every degree at least7 and no
smaller degree. To verify this last assertion directly,
the three generator weights4,3,4 give basis degrees7 and8,
and multiplication by the remainder basis element \(e_2\)
adds2. The least-support branch with first index1 permits
every further monomial in weights3 and4. Degrees7,8,9,10,
11,12 are all reached, and adding3 reaches every larger
degree. Every basis vector uses two distinct generator
indices of total weight at least7. Hence the complete
support test is the union of the free test and
\[
(c_{21}>0\text{ and }D\ge8)
\quad\text{or}\quad
((c_2+c_R)>0\text{ and }D\ge9).
\tag{SR3.21}
\]

Exact evaluation uses G037's Bostan–Mori parity operation
on each rational series in (SR3.6). There are \(O(m^2)\)
cycle pairs, each with degree \(O(m^2)\) denominator,
all roots of unity. The same explicit polynomial bit
bound proved in G037§6 applies to their specified weights
and the finite numerator from (SR3.4). Summing the terms
remains polynomial in \(m\) and \(\log(D+1)\).
The executable `stable_third_row_positive.py` supplies the
literal path counts, polynomials, support and matrix data.

## 7. The complete \(m=3\) endpoint

Here \(\dim W=2\). Complementary column wedge pairing
gives the actual equivariant isomorphism
\[
S_{(a,3)}W\simeq(\det W)^3\otimes\operatorname{Sym}^{a-3}W.
\tag{SR3.22}
\]
The three two-box columns supply the determinant factor,
and the remaining row is the symmetric power. The
determinant of \(W\) is the sign character, so the
effective label becomes \(\nu'\). The three fake-degree
polynomials for \(S_3\) are respectively
\(1,q+q^2,q^3\) for \((3),(2,1),(1,1,1)\), obtained
from the same hook formula. Thus the coefficient is
\[
[q^{a-3}]\frac{f_{\nu'}(q)}{(1-q^2)(1-q^3)}.
\tag{SR3.23}
\]
Its at-most-two free-degree polytopes have at most three
variables, and include \(a=3\) without a missing endpoint.
Its support is the same finite coin test. These bounds
are within the global \(N+7\), \(3m-1\) bounds.

## 8. Geometric transport and verification scope

The stable flag/frame map (SR3.7), its determinant pairing
and every Young/coset morphism are the literal maps already
identified in G015, T032 and G038. Cubic transfer defines
a coherent kernel over \(\operatorname{Spec}I\). The
Ricci contraction is a rational associated-bundle morphism
on the orthogonal frame reduction, with exact inverse
(SR3.13) on its specified image. The finite cyclic
presentations in (SR3.14) and actual homogeneous changes
of bases in (SR3.15) identify the same kernel sheaf with
its free and Koszul summands. Flat extension from
\(\operatorname{Spec}J\) uses the exhibited two-element
free basis \(1,e_2\). Thus the positive counts are basis
counts for those actual coherent modules.

The locators are SGA3 I4.5 and4.7.2–4.7.3 for frames
and associated bundles; EGA II2.4.1–2.4.2 and2.5.2/2.5.4
for the projective/coherent constructions; SGA6 VI3.3
and V4.2,4.4,4.8–4.9 for the exact Schur and K0 operations.
Archive cote133/028 is transported by A012's tensor-word,
weight and Young maps. The coefficients are in
characteristic zero; the maps spread after their actual
finite denominators, including \(d-2\) and \(2(d-1)\),
are inverted. No unspecified integral rank comparison is
asserted.

Full-proof readings and executed finite checks are separate
dated events. The complete unbounded formula is proved by
the exact cokernel action and module decomposition above.


# All stable two-row tails with a fixed second part

## G-040. A positive algorithm with an explicit fixed-parameter bound

For every integer \(b\ge2\), the following whole parameter family
has a positive bounded-polytope formula of polynomial description
size in \(m\) and the binary parameter lengths:
\[
\begin{gathered}
m\ge3,\quad a\ge b,\quad t\ge0,\quad n\ge a+t,
\quad\mu\vdash m,\\
\lambda=(mn-a-b-(m-1)t,a+t,b+t,t^{m-3}).
\end{gathered}
\tag{FS.1}
\]
Here \(b\) is the fixed parameter. The algorithm below supplies
computable functions \(f,g\) and a bound
\[
f(b)\bigl(m+\operatorname{bits}(a,t,n,\mu)+1\bigr)^{g(b)}
\tag{FS.2}
\]
for construction, exact coefficient evaluation and support decision.
It gives polynomial bounds for each fixed \(b\); it makes no
polynomial claim when \(b\) varies unrestrictedly. The positive
polytopes have at most \(3m+2b\) variables. For \(t\ge1\), the
ordinary binary-part output contains \(m\) positive parts. The
explicit-\(m\) convention at \(t=0\) is retained as in G037–G039.

The construction uses a finite actual cokernel, minimal homogeneous
covers, an explicit decomposition by the exponents of the high-degree
invariants, and a bounded Gröbner calculation in at most \(b-2\)
variables. G038 and G039 give the much smaller displayed formulas
at \(b=2,3\). The present construction applies to every \(b\).

## 1. The actual transfer and its finite cokernel

Put \(W=\mathfrak h_m\), \(P=\operatorname{Sym}W\),
\(I=\mathbb Q[e_2,\ldots,e_m]\), and \(D=a+b\).
The flag and determinant map T032/C4–8 identifies the original
balanced module with
\(\operatorname{sgn}^t\otimes S_{(a,b)}W\).
The effective label is \(\nu=\mu\) for even \(t\), and
\(\nu=\mu'\) for odd \(t\). The first two partition gaps are
nonnegative because \(a\ge b\) and \(n\ge a+t\).

Use the graded free \(P\)-modules with tensor degrees \(b,b-1\),
and the literal derivative transfer
\[
\phi_b:P\otimes\operatorname{Sym}^bW
 \longrightarrow P\otimes\operatorname{Sym}^{b-1}W,
\qquad
f\otimes v_1\cdots v_b\longmapsto
 \sum_{i=1}^b fv_i\otimes\prod_{j\ne i}v_j.
\tag{FS.3}
\]
For first-factor degree \(u\), its Pieri highest vectors are
\(x^{u-i}X^{b-i}(xY-yX)^i\),
\(0\le i\le\min(u,b)\). The operator
\(x\partial_X+y\partial_Y\) has coefficient \(b-i\)
on each such vector. Thus its only kernel summand, at \(u\ge b\),
is \(S_{(u,b)}W\), and it is surjective at total degrees
at least \(2b-1\). At the remaining degrees its entire cokernel is
\[
C_{b-1+j}=S_{(b-1,j)}W,
\qquad0\le j\le b-1,
\quad C_e=0\text{ in all other degrees}.
\tag{FS.4}
\]
For \(j=0\), this denotes \(\operatorname{Sym}^{b-1}W\).
The nonzero coefficients \(b-i\), the rational Young inclusions
and the same two-row Pieri calculation as G039§1 prove all these
claims, including \(\dim W=2\). There is no asymptotic cokernel.

Let \(L=2b-2\), \(B=\min(m,b-1)\),
\[
J=\mathbb Q[e_2,\ldots,e_B],\qquad
Y=(e_{B+1},\ldots,e_m),\qquad I=J[Y].
\tag{FS.5}
\]
Every variable in \(Y\) kills \(C\): its degree is at least
\(b\), whereas \(C\) is supported in degrees \(b-1\) through
\(2b-2\), so its image has degree at least \(2b-1\).
The action of the variables of \(J\) is the actual
multiplication induced from the first factor of (FS.3). It is
computed by the finite matrices of (FS.3) in degrees at most \(L\).
No decomposition of this finite \(J\)-module is assumed.

## 2. Constructing the covariant cokernel in polynomial size

Each vector space used in degrees at most \(L\) has dimension
at most \(f(b)(m+1)^L\): use the monomial bases of the two
symmetric factors in (FS.3). Choose the rational basis
\(e_i-e_m\) of \(W\). Adjacent permutations have explicit
integer matrices, and symmetric powers of degree at most \(L\)
have polynomial-size rational matrices for fixed \(b\).
Exact row reduction gives the quotient spaces in (FS.4), the
adjacent-permutation matrices on them, and the multiplication
maps by every \(e_i\), \(2\le i\le B\).
The elementary invariant is obtained from the actual centered
vectors \(P_me_i\); its sum over \(i\)-subsets has at most
\(m^i\) terms. All degrees here are bounded by \(L\).

Only labels satisfying
\[
\nu_1\ge m-L
\tag{FS.6}
\]
can occur in \(C\). Indeed every degree-\(e\) summand embeds,
by its rational Young map, in \(W^{\otimes e}\subset E^{\otimes e}\),
where \(E=\mathbb Q^m\) and \(e\le L\). The literal word orbits
in \(E^{\otimes e}\) have stabilizer \(S_{m-l}\), \(l\le e\).
Successive one-box induction from the row \((m-l)\) gives only
partitions containing that row. This proves (FS.6) through the
actual word, coset and Young maps.

For a label violating (FS.6), put \(C_\nu=0\) immediately.
For every remaining label construct its rational Specht module
using row tabloids and the column antisymmetrizer. There are
at most \(f(b)(m+1)^L\) tabloids: choose the at most \(L\)
letters outside the first row, then place them in the remaining
rows. The column group has size bounded only by \(L\), because
all nonsingleton columns contain one of these at most \(L\)
lower boxes. The orbit span of one column polytabloid under
adjacent permutations is the actual Young module \([\nu]\).
It is obtained by at most the number of tabloids many independent
row-reduction additions. This is the same Young-group-algebra
realization underlying A012, with the explicit quotient from
row-symmetric tensor words to row tabloids.

Solve the intertwining equations
\(T\rho_\nu(s_i)=\rho_C(s_i)T\), \(i=1,\ldots,m-1\),
degree by degree. They give exactly
\(C_\nu=\operatorname{Hom}_{S_m}([\nu],C)\), since the
adjacent transpositions generate the group. The multiplication
matrices commute with these actions and induce the actual
\(J\)-module structure on the resulting solution spaces.
Their dimensions, matrix sizes and coefficient bit lengths are
polynomial in \(m\) for each fixed \(b\). Rational Gaussian
elimination has polynomial bit bounds from its determinant
minors. This construction never sums over all \(m!\) permutations.
For \(m\le L\), all these bounds remain within a function of \(b\).

## 3. Minimal finite covers and the actual free remainder

Choose a homogeneous basis of \(C_\nu/J_+C_\nu\) and fixed lifts.
It gives the minimal graded cover
\(F_0\to C_\nu\) over \(J\), with a basis polynomial
\(c_0(q)\) supported in degrees at most \(L\).
Its kernel \(R\) is generated in weighted degrees at most
\(L+B\le2L\). Here is an explicit proof and algorithm for
this bound. Order homogeneous free monomials in \(F_0\) by
a fixed term order and greedily retain independent images in
\(C_\nu\). The retained monomials are the normal monomials
of the kernel: multiplying a dependent relation by a variable
preserves its leading-term relation. They all have weight at
most \(L\). Every minimal leading monomial outside this
order ideal is a variable times a normal monomial, and hence
has weight at most \(L+B\). Its image is a linear combination
of earlier retained monomials of the same weight. These
relations form a Gröbner basis by their exact leading ideal,
and in particular generate \(R\) in the asserted degree range.

In degrees through \(L+B\), compute the relation spaces and
divide by the multiples of lower-degree relations. Fixed
homogeneous lifts of their quotient bases give the minimal
free cover
\[
F_1\xrightarrow{d_J}F_0\longrightarrow C_\nu\longrightarrow0,
\qquad K_J=\ker d_J.
\tag{FS.7}
\]
Write \(c_1(q)\) for the basis polynomial of \(F_1\).
Both ranks and all these finite matrices have the polynomial
bounds from §2; the number of \(J\)-monomials in weight
at most \(2L\) depends only on \(b\).

Over \(I=J[Y]\), the minimal first two covers of the same
module \(C_\nu\) are
\[
M_0=I\otimes_JF_0,\qquad
M_1=(I\otimes_JF_1)\oplus
       \bigoplus_{y_i\in Y}(I\otimes_JF_0)\xi_i,
\tag{FS.8}
\]
where \(\xi_i\) has degree \(\deg y_i\) and maps by
multiplication by \(y_i\). The first summand maps by \(d_J\).
These generators are minimal: in \(Y\)-degree zero they are
the minimal \(J\)-relations, and in each single-variable
\(Y\)-degree they are the free generator residues of \(F_0\).
Higher \(Y\)-degrees are their multiples. This also proves
directly that the image is the full kernel of \(M_0\to C_\nu\).

The covariants of the actual domain and target of (FS.3) are
graded free over \(I\), by the averaged coinvariant section.
Their basis polynomials are
\[
A_\nu(q)=q^b f_{[\nu]\otimes\operatorname{Sym}^bW}(q),
\qquad B_\nu(q)=q^{b-1} f_{[\nu]\otimes\operatorname{Sym}^{b-1}W}(q).
\tag{FS.9}
\]
Apply the two actual homogeneous cover cancellations of
G039§3 to (FS.8): adapt the target basis to the minimal
cokernel generators, lift and cancel its free zero-image
complement, then adapt the remaining domain basis to the
minimal relations and kill its complementary images by a
triangular basis change. This gives an isomorphism on the
actual transfer kernel
\[
K_\nu\simeq\mathcal F_\nu\oplus\ker(M_1\to M_0),
\tag{FS.10}
\]
where \(\mathcal F_\nu\) is graded free, with nonnegative
basis polynomial
\[
F_\nu(q)=A_\nu(q)-B_\nu(q)+c_0(q)-c_1(q)
                   -c_0(q)\sum_{i=B+1}^m q^i.
\tag{FS.11}
\]
All choices and inverse basis changes are those explicitly
proved in G039§3. This proves coefficientwise positivity
of (FS.11) for every label, including \(C_\nu=0\).
Its degree is at most
\(\max\{\binom m2+b,m+L,2L\}\).

## 4. A positive decomposition by the high-variable multidegree

Write \(y^\beta\) for a monomial in \(Y\). At
\(\beta=0\), the kernel in (FS.10) is exactly \(K_J\).
At \(\beta\ne0\), let \(i\) be the first positive index
and let \(S=\{j:\beta_j>0\}\). The degree-\(\beta\)
domain consists of one copy of \(F_1\) and one copy of
\(F_0\) for each \(j\in S\). Its map is
\[
(u,(v_j)_{j\in S})\longmapsto d_Ju+\sum_{j\in S}v_j.
\tag{FS.12}
\]
Thus its kernel has the explicit inverse pair of maps
\[
\begin{aligned}
F_1\oplus\bigoplus_{j\in S\setminus\{i\}}F_0
 &\longrightarrow\ker(\text{FS.12}),\\
(u,(v_j)_{j\ne i})&\longmapsto
 \left(u,\ v_i=-d_Ju-\sum_{j\ne i}v_j,\ (v_j)_{j\ne i}\right).
\end{aligned}
\tag{FS.13}
\]
The inverse reads \(u\) and all nondistinguished \(v_j\).
The omitted monomial factors are exactly
\(y^\beta\) in the first summand and
\(y^{\beta-e_j}\xi_j\) in the second. They are polynomial
because \(\beta_j>0\). This proves a genuine vector-space
basis decomposition in every multidegree.

Consequently its Hilbert series has the positive form
\[
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Hilb}\ker(M_1\to M_0)
={}&\operatorname{Hilb}K_J\\
&+\operatorname{Hilb}F_1\,
       \sum_{\beta\ne0}q^{\sum_{i>B}i\beta_i}\\
&+\operatorname{Hilb}F_0\,
       Z_{(B+1,B+2,\ldots,m)}(q).
\end{aligned}
\tag{FS.14}
\]
The last series is the explicit star-cycle series (SR3.5).
An empty high-variable list makes both latter terms zero;
a one-variable list makes the last term zero. Thus this
also covers every small \(m\).

## 5. Polynomial Gröbner bounds for the remaining fixed-variable kernel

There are \(\ell=B-1\le b-2\) variables in \(J\).
At \(b=2\), the ring is \(J=\mathbb Q\), so
\(F_0=C_\nu\), \(F_1=K_J=0\); the high-variable formula
already gives the complete kernel. More generally zero-variable
matrices are handled directly by rational linear algebra.
Let \(r_0,r_1\) be the ranks of \(F_0,F_1\), and set
\(\delta=\max(1,2L)\). Regard (FS.7) temporarily as an
ordinary polynomial matrix with degree-zero basis vectors;
its entries have ordinary degree at most \(\delta\).
The original positive weighted degrees and shifts are
retained separately in every monomial and matrix.

The Hermann–Seidenberg bound, in Aschenbrenner,
*Ideal membership in polynomial rings over the integers*,
§3, Theorem3.2, PDFp16, bounds kernel generators by
\[
H=(2\max(1,r_0)\delta)^{2^\ell}.
\tag{FS.15}
\]
The primary text is
https://www.mat.univie.ac.at/~maschenbrenner/pdf/ideal2.pdf.
The statement and the complete §3 proof through Theorem3.2
were read; it applies over \(\mathbb Q\) to this exact matrix.

Liang, *Degree bounds for Gröbner bases of modules*,
arXiv:1905.07517v3, Corollary42, PDFp19, gives the
ordinary-degree bound
\[
G=2\bigl(H\max(1,r_1)\bigr)^{2^\ell}
\tag{FS.16}
\]
for a reduced module Gröbner basis generated in degrees
at most \(H\), for any term order. Use the primary
https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.07517; Corollaries38/42 and the
Theorem40–41 passage were read. The non-graded version
is used, so no equality of ordinary and weighted gradings
is assumed. Zero or full kernels are handled directly.

For each fixed \(b\), both bounds are polynomial in
\(r_0,r_1\), hence in \(m\). They also give an explicit
polynomial bit algorithm: enumerate all vector polynomials
of ordinary degree at most \(G\), solve (FS.7) by rational
linear algebra, and row-reduce their coefficients in the
chosen term order. Every reduced Gröbner basis element
occurs in this finite solution space by (FS.15)–(FS.16).
Select the minimal leading monomials under divisibility
and their reduced lifts. They generate the whole leading
module and hence give a Gröbner basis. Weighted-homogeneous
components can be processed separately, since (FS.7) is
weighted homogeneous; extracting them never increases
the ordinary degree. The unique reduced basis can also
be taken weighted homogeneous.

The number of monomials used is at most
\(r_1\binom{G+\ell}{\ell}\). All output coefficients are
ratios of minors of the finite linear system, giving
polynomial bit length and bit time in these sizes and
the input coefficient height. Thus the computation has
the bound (FS.2), without a search through unbounded degrees.

## 6. Positive lattice sets for every kernel term

The weighted-homogeneous initial module of \(K_J\) is a
direct sum of monomial ideals, one for each basis vector
of \(F_1\). In each component, partition every exponent
axis at all exponents appearing in its leading generators.
Use disjoint integer intervals between consecutive cut
values, including the last infinite interval. Divisibility
by each generator is constant on every resulting grid box.
Retain exactly the boxes belonging to the initial module.
There are polynomially many boxes for fixed \(\ell\):
at most \((s+1)^\ell\) per component with \(s\) leading
generators. Every retained box is a product of integer
intervals. Intersect it with
\[
\sum_{i=2}^{B} i\alpha_i+\deg(\text{component})=D.
\tag{FS.17}
\]
Every infinite upper endpoint is replaced by
\(\lfloor D/i\rfloor\). This gives bounded polytopes.
Their lattice points index an actual basis of \(K_{J,D}\):
for each initial monomial use the first Gröbner element
whose leading monomial divides it and take the corresponding
monomial multiple. Distinct leading monomials give linear
independence, and Gröbner reduction gives spanning in
each finite weighted degree. This specifies the triangular
bijection back to the actual kernel.

Each coefficient of the nonnegative polynomial (FS.11)
gives the free-degree polytope (SR2.17), now with degree
shift and multiplicity from that polynomial. The middle
term of (FS.14) uses a homogeneous free basis of \(F_1\),
arbitrary \(J\)-monomials and a nonempty \(Y\)-monomial.
Partition the last set by its first positive index: all
earlier exponents are zero, that exponent is at least one,
and all later exponents are nonnegative. Append the
weighted degree equation and a bounded index for the
number of free generators in the chosen degree. This
gives at most \(m-B\) polytopes per occurring free degree.

For the last term of (FS.14), use the single least-support
cycle polytope (SR3.20) on \(Y\), append the arbitrary
\(J\)-exponents, the degree shift and a bounded generator
index for \(F_0\). It is exactly the inverse basis
construction (FS.13). The total variable count is below
\(3m+2b\), and the number of pieces and constraints obeys
(FS.2). Distinct components, degrees and least-support
indices are retained as disjoint tags.

## 7. Computing the two free input characters and exact values

The finite polynomial (FS.9) is computable for arbitrary
\(\nu\), without constructing its potentially large
Specht module. The actual identity
\(\operatorname{Sym}^jW=\operatorname{Sym}^jE-
\operatorname{Sym}^{j-1}E\) in the representation ring
comes from \(E=\mathbf1\oplus W\). The monomial orbits
of \(\operatorname{Sym}^jE\) are indexed by partitions
\(\rho\vdash j\). With \(l=\ell(\rho)\le m\), their
stabilizer is
\[
S_{m-l}\times\prod_{d\ge1}S_{m_d(\rho)}.
\tag{FS.18}
\]
The tensor-coset isomorphism of G038§6 identifies tensoring
with that orbit module with restriction and induction
through this very subgroup. Enumerate each distinct partition
\(\eta\subseteq\nu\) of size \(m-l\) exactly once. For each
tuple of small-factor labels \(\sigma_d\vdash m_d(\rho)\),
compute the iterated Littlewood–Richardson multiplicity
\(c^\nu_{\eta,\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\ldots}\). For each distinct
output partition \(\kappa\supseteq\eta\) of size \(m\), the
contribution is the product
\[
c^\nu_{\eta,\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\ldots}\,
c^\kappa_{\eta,\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\ldots}.
\]
Sum these products over the displayed distinct shapes and labels.
The iterated LR coefficients count the intermediate shapes for
the ordered small subgroup factors; an ordering of the removed
corner boxes supplies no additional multiplicity. These are
finite tableaux on at most \(b\)
boxes; the complete LR map and proof are Macdonald I§9,
pp142–147, as freshly read for T064. The identical tensor
coset and rational Young maps prove this use for arbitrary
\(\nu\). At most \(f(b)(m+1)^{2b}\) candidates occur.
Apply the exact finite fake-degree hook formula (SR2.16)
to each resulting label. This computes (FS.9), (FS.11)
and every free coefficient within (FS.2).

For exact values, the free and high-variable terms have
rational series with denominator factors \(1-q^i\),
\(2\le i\le m\), and polynomially many shifts.
For every grid box of §6, multiply its finite interval
series and unbounded geometric series. At most
\(2^\ell\) numerator terms arise by expanding its finite
interval factors; this is a function of \(b\). Its shifts
are polynomially bounded by (FS.16). Bostan–Mori parity
extraction from G037§6 evaluates these exact root-of-unity
denominators in time polynomial in their degrees and
\(\log(D+1)\), with the proved coefficient-height bound.
The high-variable star series has only \(O(m^2)\) pairs.
The exact sum therefore obeys (FS.2). Testing whether
that nonnegative integer is zero gives the full support
decision in the same bound.

## 8. Geometric comparison and precise implementation scope

The original coefficient is transported by the actual
balanced flag map and determinant pairing in §1. Transfer
(FS.3), its finite cokernel and both minimal covers are
equivariant coherent-module maps over \(\operatorname{Spec}I\).
The free cancellation (FS.10) and the explicit multidegree
inverse (FS.13) are isomorphisms of the specified graded
modules or vector-space fibers, as indicated. The initial
module in §6 is related by its leading-term filtration
and the displayed triangular basis lift; weighted degree
is preserved throughout. Thus each positive count is
carried to the same original highest multiplicity space.

The fixed transport locators are SGA3 I4.5 and4.7.2–4.7.3;
EGA II2.4.1–2.4.2 and2.5.2/2.5.4; SGA6 VI3.3 and
V4.2,4.4,4.8–4.9. The archive comparison is A012's
tensor-word, row-symmetry and Young maps for cote133/028.
All scalar calculations are over \(\mathbb Q\), and
the stated multiplicities extend to characteristic-zero
fields by the rational maps. No characteristic-p rank
assertion is inferred from those maps.

This report proves and specifies the complete finite
algorithm. The small closed formulas at \(b=2,3\) have
their own executable implementations and receipts in
G038–G039. General-purpose execution and any additional
finite tests of the present construction are recorded
separately, with their actual scope. Whole-proof readings
must be recorded before this finding is marked completed.


# Hook jets on a projective frame in varying outer degree

## T-062. An explicit surjective jet map in every ideal order

Let \(m\ge4\), \(k\ge1\), \(a\ge2k+1\), \(0\le r\le m-2\),
\(t\ge0\), and \(\mu\vdash m\). Set
\[
\begin{aligned}
n&=a+t-k,\\
\lambda&=((m-1)a+t-mk-r,a+t,(t+1)^r,t^{m-2-r}),\\
\nu&=\mu\quad(t\text{ even}),\qquad
\nu=\mu'\quad(t\text{ odd}).
\end{aligned}
\tag{HJ.1}
\]
The first gap is nonnegative: its minimum is
\((m-2)(2k+1)-mk-(m-2)=(m-4)k\). Thus these parameters
always define a partition of \(mn\).

Write \(E=\mathfrak h_m\), \(v_i=e_i-m^{-1}\mathbf1\), and
\(Z=\{[v_i]\}\subset\mathbb P(E)\). Let \(Q\) be the tautological
quotient. There is an actual split exact sequence of rational
\(S_m\)-modules
\[
\begin{split}
0\longrightarrow
H^0\bigl(\mathcal I_Z^k\otimes\Omega^r(a+r)\bigr)
\longrightarrow S_{(a,1^r)}E^*
\xrightarrow{\operatorname{jet}_k}
\operatorname{Ind}_{S_{m-1}}^{S_m}
\left(\bigoplus_{j=0}^{k-1}
\operatorname{Sym}^j\mathfrak h_{m-1}
\otimes\Lambda^r\mathfrak h_{m-1}\right)
\longrightarrow0.
\end{split}
\tag{HJ.2}
\]
The duals in the target are identified by the specified rational dot
forms. G015's actual flag map, with T061's exterior pushforward, gives
\[
(S_\lambda\mathbb Q^m)_{(n^m)}
\simeq\operatorname{sgn}^t\otimes\ker\operatorname{jet}_k.
\tag{HJ.3}
\]
Consequently the plethysm coefficient is the stable-hook multiplicity
of \([\nu]\) minus its multiplicity in the explicit induced module.
All maps and the splitting are given below. The positive polytope
conversion in T063 is proved for \(k=2\); (HJ.2) itself holds for
every displayed \(k\).

### 1. Quadratic coordinates for all normal directions

Let \(U=H^0(\mathcal I_Z(2))\). At every point, differentiation on
the affine chart \(\ell_i=1\), where \(\ell_i=mz_i/(m-1)\), gives
a surjection
\[
\partial_i:U\longrightarrow W_i^*,\qquad W_i=\ker\ell_i.
\tag{HJ.4}
\]
Here is an explicit rank proof. Use \(s=m-1\ge3\) frame vectors as
a basis. The projective points are the coordinate points and
\([1:\cdots:1]\). Their quadratic ideal is spanned by
\(x_jx_l-x_1x_2\), with \(j<l\), omitting the zero member.
This is the actual ideal presentation proved in G016; its degree-two
part also follows by evaluating a general quadratic. At a coordinate
point \(e_h\), \(h\notin\{1,2\}\), the pairs \((h,j)\) give every
transverse derivative \(dx_j\). At \(e_1\), the pairs \((1,j)\)
and \((2,j)\), \(j\ge3\), give \(dx_j-dx_2\) and \(-dx_2\);
the argument at \(e_2\) is identical. At the all-ones point the
derivatives are \(dx_j+dx_l-dx_1-dx_2\). Taking a third index
shows that these span every coordinate difference, the full
projective cotangent space. This proves (HJ.4).

Give \(U\) the invariant positive rational form inherited from
\(\operatorname{Sym}^2E^*\). The explicit rational map
\[
\sigma_i=\partial_i^*(\partial_i\partial_i^*)^{-1}:
W_i^*\longrightarrow U
\tag{HJ.5}
\]
is a derivative right inverse. It commutes with the stabilizer of
\(v_i\), and all \(\sigma_i\) are related by literal permutations.
The inverse exists by the proved surjectivity and positivity, so
no unspecified generic rank is used.

Use the quadratic separators
\[
p_i=\frac m{m-2}z_i^2-
\frac{\sum_jz_j^2}{(m-2)(m-1)}.
\tag{HJ.6}
\]
They satisfy \(p_i(v_j)=\delta_{ij}\), as computed in T061.
Choose a basis \(u_1,\ldots,u_{m-2}\) of \(W_i^*\), and write
\(f_h=\sigma_i(u_h)\). At \(v_i\), the functions \(y_h=f_h/p_i\)
have zero constant term and independent linear terms \(u_h\).
Thus substitution induces an isomorphism of finite jet algebras
\[
\mathbb Q[y_1,\ldots,y_{m-2}]/(y)^k
\xrightarrow{\sim}
\mathcal O_{\mathbb P(E),[v_i]}/\mathfrak m_i^k.
\tag{HJ.7}
\]
An exact inverse is obtained by successively removing homogeneous
terms of orders \(1,\ldots,k-1\). This finite triangular construction
proves the isomorphism and specifies its rational map.

The homogeneous polynomials
\[
p_i^{\,k-|\beta|}f_1^{\beta_1}\cdots f_{m-2}^{\beta_{m-2}},
\qquad |\beta|<k,
\tag{HJ.8}
\]
all have degree \(2k\). Their jets at \([v_i]\) form a basis,
because (HJ.8) is \(p_i^k y^\beta\), with \(p_i^k\) a unit there.
At every other point each \(p_i\) and \(f_h\) belongs to the
maximal ideal; the total number of factors is \(k\). They therefore
vanish to order at least \(k\) at all other points. This is the exact
simultaneous scalar interpolation map.

### 2. The horizontal lift and the equivariant jet splitting

For \(\phi\in\Lambda^r\operatorname{ann}(v_i)\), put
\[
H_i(\phi)=\iota_z(\ell_i\wedge\phi).
\tag{HJ.9}
\]
This is a horizontal form of coefficient degree one. On the affine
chart \(\ell_i=1\), it gives a bundle isomorphism from the constant
space \(\Lambda^rW_i^*\) to horizontal forms: restriction to \(W_i\)
is its inverse. The Euler contraction squares to zero, proving
horizontality directly.

Multiply (HJ.8) times (HJ.9) times \(\ell_i^{a-2k-1}\). The
exponent is nonnegative, and the coefficient degree is exactly \(a\).
The resulting horizontal forms are global sections of
\(\Omega^r(a+r)\). Their jets at point \(i\) form a basis of all
form-valued jets, and their jets at all other points vanish.
The finite inverse in (HJ.7), with the unit factor \(p_i^k\)
removed, constructs an actual right inverse at that point.
Expressed through the symmetric powers of (HJ.5), this construction
is independent of the chosen basis and stabilizer-equivariant.
Summing over the points gives an \(S_m\)-equivariant rational
right inverse to \(\operatorname{jet}_k\).

On \(\ell_i=1\), the stabilizer fixes \(v_i\) and acts linearly
on \(W_i\cong\mathfrak h_{m-1}\). Its action on the order-\(<k\)
Taylor algebra is exactly \(\bigoplus_{j<k}\operatorname{Sym}^jW_i^*\).
The specified affine vector trivializes the homogeneous line without
a further character. The horizontal basis contributes
\(\Lambda^rW_i^*\). This proves the precise target and every twist.

The ideal power in (HJ.2) is the ordinary power as a sheaf. At each
of the disjoint reduced points it is the maximal ideal power, so
its kernel is exactly order-\(k\) jet vanishing. G015's actual flag
extension criterion uses this same sheaf. T061's exterior pushforward
and tensor-with-ideal comparison apply on each product chart, giving
(HJ.3).

## T-063. A polynomial-size positive formula at second ideal order

Take \(k=2\) in (HJ.1), so \(a\ge5\). Let
\(c_{m,a,r}(\nu)=[\,[\nu]:S_{(a,1^r)}\mathfrak h_m\,]\)
be G037's stable hook coefficient. Define \(d_{m,r}(\nu)\) by
the following finite Young-graph rule. Put \(q=m-1-r\).
Start with
\[
(q-1,1^r)\quad(q\ge2),\qquad
(q,1^{r-1})\quad(r\ge1).
\tag{HJ.10}
\]
From each displayed partition of \(m-2\), add two boxes in successive
partition-preserving steps. Count the paths ending at \(\nu\). Then
\[
\boxed{
p_{\mu,(a+t-2)}^\lambda
=c_{m,a,r}(\nu)-d_{m,r}(\nu),\qquad
0\le d_{m,r}(\nu)\le4.}
\tag{HJ.11}
\]
Every such coefficient is the lattice count of at most
\(8(m^2+3m-4)-3\) bounded rational polytopes in at most
\(m^2+3m-4\) variables. Complete matrices are constructed in time
polynomial in \(m\) and the binary input lengths; the exact coefficient
and nonvanishing have the same polynomial bit bound. For ordinary
binary-part encoding this gives the corresponding polynomial and
counting bounds when \(t\ge1\). At \(t=0\), the assertion retains
an explicit/unary \(m\) parameter, as in G037 and T061.

### 3. The actual two-step branching map

For \(k=2\), the fiber in (HJ.2) is
\((\mathbb Q\oplus\mathfrak h_{m-1})\otimes
\Lambda^r\mathfrak h_{m-1}\). Its first factor is the literal
permutation module on \(m-1\) coordinates. If \(G=S_m\),
\(K=S_{m-1}\), \(L=S_{m-2}\), and
\(H=\Lambda^r\mathfrak h_{m-1}\), the tensor-induction isomorphism is
\[
g\otimes(hL\otimes v)\longmapsto gh\otimes h^{-1}v:
\operatorname{Ind}_K^G(\mathbb Q[K/L]\otimes H)
\xrightarrow{\sim}
\operatorname{Ind}_L^G\operatorname{Res}_L^K H.
\tag{HJ.12}
\]
Representative changes and the defining induced-module relations give
the same image, and the displayed formula has its inverse on the coset
summands. Under \(L\), the standard module splits as
\(\mathfrak h_{m-2}\oplus\mathbb Q\): the second line is spanned
by the vector with its first \(m-2\) coordinates equal to one and
its last equal to \(-(m-2)\). Taking exterior powers gives the two
hooks in (HJ.10), with out-of-range exterior powers zero. Two
applications of one-box Pieri through rational Young projections
give exactly the path rule.

For each starting hook and final label there are at most two orders
for adding the specified pair of boxes. There are at most two starting
hooks, proving \(d\le4\). Every resulting diagram is a hook plus
two boxes, so it has at most two boxes on any diagonal. The row
label \((m)\) has \(d=1\) exactly for \(r=0,1\), and otherwise
has \(d=0\). These observations include all short-row and maximal-leg
endpoints. Equation (HJ.11) follows from the actual split sequence
(HJ.2), including its determinant twist.

### 4. Polynomially many candidates for the points to delete

Suppose \(d=d_{m,r}(\nu)>0\), first with \(\nu\ne(m)\).
G037's single polytope records a standard tableau \(T\), an
\(r\)-subset \(S\) of
\(C_\nu=\nu\setminus\{(1,1),(2,1)\}\), and coins of weights
\(2,\ldots,m\), with total
\[
\operatorname{comaj}(T)+
\sum_{(i,j)\in S}(j-i+1)+\sum_{h=2}^m h\beta_h=a+r.
\tag{HJ.13}
\]
Write \(b(\nu)=\sum(i-1)\nu_i\), and let \(L\) be \(b(\nu)\)
plus the sum of the \(r\) smallest retained weights. G037's positive
numerator has smallest exponent exactly \(L\). The Koszul cycle space
has no total degree \(D\le r\): for \(r>0\), a constant exterior
form killed by every coordinate contraction is zero; for \(r=0\)
the cycle convention is \(P_+\). The positive numerator and
constant-one denominator therefore prove
\[
L\ge r+1.
\tag{HJ.14}
\]

Choose \(a_0=5\) when \(a\) is odd and \(a_0=6\) when \(a\)
is even. The surjective jet map at \(a_0\) proves that the stable
polytope has at least \(d\) lattice points. Every such point has
numerator excess at most \(a_0+r-L\le5\). The following enumeration
finds \(d\) explicit distinct points among polynomially many candidates.

Enumerate semistandard fillings \(u(i,j)\) satisfying
\[
u(i,j)\ge i-1,\qquad
\sum_{(i,j)\in\nu}(u(i,j)-(i-1))\le5.
\tag{HJ.15}
\]
There are at most \(\binom{m+5}{5}\) nonnegative increment arrays.
Retain the weak-row, strict-column fillings. Standardize by increasing
entry, with equal entries ordered from left to right, and remove
duplicates. This finds every standard tableau with
\(\operatorname{comaj}(T)-b(\nu)\le5\): its minimal semistandard
filling puts at label \(j\) the number of descents at indices less
than \(j\). Its entry sum is comajor, every entry is at least the
row index minus one, and the indicated standardization recovers \(T\).
These are the actual standardization maps of T028/G037.

For the subset, sort the retained weights and let \(w_0\) be the
\(r\)-th smallest. In a subset with excess at most five, every cell
of weight below \(w_0-5\) is forced in, and every cell of weight
above \(w_0+5\) is forced out. Otherwise replacing the missing
smallest cell or the oversized chosen cell already costs more than
five. The intervening eleven weight levels contain at most 22 cells
by the diagonal bound after (HJ.12). Enumerate their subsets of the
required size. The cases \(r=0\) and \(r=|C_\nu|\) have a unique
subset. After the tableau and subset are fixed, the remaining coin
degree is at most five, so enumerate those partitions directly.
Check (HJ.13) and take the first \(d\) distinct complete points
in the fixed enumeration order. The proved surjection ensures
termination.

For general \(a\) of the same parity, increase each point's
weight-two coin by \((a-a_0)/2\). This injective map of complete
tableau/subset/coin data produces exactly \(d\) distinct specified
points of the stable polytope for \(a\).

For the row label there is one point to delete and \(r=0,1\).
Use HK.19's invariant-form polytope, always with least-support index
two. For \(r=0\), represent \(a\ge5\) by twos and threes, with a
single three precisely when \(a\) is odd. For \(r=1\), put
\(D=a+1\). When \(D\) is even, choose one four, subset \(\{4\}\),
and fill the remainder with twos. When \(D\) is odd, use one three,
subset \(\{3\}\), and fill the remainder with twos. The exponent
of two is always positive and every HK.19 inequality holds.

### 5. At most four successive point deletions

Start with G037's bounded polytope in \(N\) ordered variables.
For each of the at most four specified points, locate its unique
current cell by checking the literal inequalities. Replace only
that cell by the \(2N\) first-difference cells of T061 UH.10.
All other cells remain. Distinctness and disjointness ensure that
the owner exists and is unique. Induction gives a disjoint
bounded-polytope decomposition of the original lattice set minus
exactly the \(d\) points, with
\[
1+d(2N-1)\le8N-3
\tag{HJ.16}
\]
cells when \(d>0\); when \(d=0\), retain the original cell.
The copied constraints are complete matrices, so this includes
every tag and added row. No character calculation or elimination
is hidden in point selection.

The exact coefficient is G037's proved rational-series coefficient
minus the two-box path count. Its bit bound is polynomial in \(m\)
and the parameter lengths, as is (HJ.15), the constant-size subset
search, the explicit coin shift, and every polytope matrix operation.
The actual jet splitting proves that this positive count is the
requested multiplicity. This does not identify the deleted monomial
vectors with the image of that splitting: the dimension identity is
proved by (HJ.2)/(HJ.12), and its lattice-set bijection is the stated
cell partition.

The executable is second_unstable_hook_positive.py. It returns the
exact coefficient or all literal matrices and deleted points. The
two one-box steps use Macdonald I§7(7.1)–(7.3), pp112–113, and
I§5(5.16), p73, freshly checked for T061; the actual hook/Koszul
and single-polytope maps are G037. Scheme transport is G015's exact
flag map and T061's local ideal pushforward, with the same checked
EGA/SGA tensor, Schur, and rational-spreading conventions.
