# Every multiplicity in the image of the outer-five canonical map

## R-031. Exact rank law, all degrees and all output partitions

Work over a field of characteristic zero. Write

\[
h_{d,e}:\operatorname{Sym}^{d}(\operatorname{Sym}^{e}V)
\longrightarrow\operatorname{Sym}^{e}(\operatorname{Sym}^{d}V)
\tag{OF.1}
\]

for symmetric-tensor inclusion, transpose of the \(d\times e\)
tensor grid, and symmetric projection, using averaging inclusions.
Let \(a_{d,e}^{\lambda}\) be the multiplicity of \(S_\lambda V\)
in its source. Define the actual image multiplicity

\[
\rho_n^\lambda=
\dim\operatorname{Hom}_{GL(V)}
  (S_\lambda V,\operatorname{im}h_{n,5}).
\tag{OF.2}
\]

For every integer \(n\ge1\), every partition \(\lambda\vdash5n\),
and every \(V\) with \(\dim V\ge\ell(\lambda)\),

\[
\boxed{
\rho_n^\lambda=
\begin{cases}
a_{n,5}^{\lambda},&1\le n\le4,\\
a_{5,5}^{\lambda}-\mathbf1_{\lambda\in\mathcal E},&n=5,\\
a_{5,n}^{\lambda},&n\ge6,
\end{cases}}
\tag{OF.3}
\]

where the finite set is exactly

\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal E=\{&
(14,7,2,2),\ (13,7,2,2,1),\ (12,7,3,2,1),\\
& (12,6,3,2,2),\ (12,5,4,3,1),\ (11,5,4,4,1),\\
& (10,8,4,2,1),\ (9,7,6,3)\}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{OF.4}
\]

The corresponding cokernel multiplicity is
\(a_{5,n}^{\lambda}-\rho_n^\lambda\). Thus its values are,
respectively, \(a_{5,n}^{\lambda}-a_{n,5}^{\lambda}\),
\(\mathbf1_{\lambda\in\mathcal E}\), and zero in the three
ranges of (OF.3). The rank on the full \(\lambda\)-isotypic space
is \(\rho_n^\lambda\dim S_\lambda V\).

These assertions assemble established results for the specified
canonical maps. The finite strict-partition table below and the exact
normalization check are given to make their application directly
reviewable. No historical novelty is claimed for the rank law.

## 1. The transpose map, including its scalar

Equip \(V^{\otimes N}\) and \((V^*)^{\otimes N}\) with their
ordinary tensor evaluation pairing. On every symmetric power use the
pairing induced by its averaged tensor inclusion. For example,

\[
\langle v_1\cdots v_e,\phi_1\cdots\phi_e\rangle
=\frac1{e!}\sum_{\sigma\in S_e}
  \prod_{i=1}^e\phi_i(v_{\sigma(i)}).
\tag{OF.5}
\]

Nested symmetric powers use the corresponding nested averaging. Let
\(i_{d,e}\) be their inclusion into \(V^{\otimes de}\), and
\(q_{d,e}\) the quotient that multiplies within rows and then among
rows. Their composite \(i_{d,e}q_{d,e}\) is the orthogonal averaging
idempotent for the row wreath group. Consequently
\(i_{d,e}^*=q_{d,e}\) and \(q_{d,e}^*=i_{d,e}\).
For the grid permutation \(\tau_{d,e}\), its transpose is its
inverse, which is \(\tau_{e,d}\). The exact identity is therefore

\[
h_{d,e}=q_{e,d}\tau_{d,e}i_{d,e},\qquad
h_{d,e}(V)^*=h_{e,d}(V^*).
\tag{OF.6}
\]

There is no additional scalar in (OF.6). It identifies the kernels,
cokernels and ranks used in the proof of (OF.3).

## 2. The fourth square base and its exact primary certificate

The original source is Juby Jacob, *Representation Theory of
Association Schemes*, RWTH Aachen dissertation (2004), **Definition
4.1.1, printed p.92; §4.2, printed pp.95–99; Table 4.4, printed
pp.104–106**. The source is

<https://publications.rwth-aachen.de/record/51990/files/Jacob_Juby.pdf>.

The final paragraph of §4 before §5 in Müller–Neunhöffer,
*Some computations regarding Foulkes’ conjecture* (2005), explicitly
attributes the fourth-square calculation to Jacob §4.2. The authors’
primary preprint is

<https://www.math.rwth-aachen.de/homes/Max.Neunhoeffer/Publications/pdf/foulkes.pdf>.

Here is the actual map between Jacob's matrix and (OF.1).
Take \(N=uv\), let \(e_1,\ldots,e_N\) be distinct basis vectors,
and consider the multilinear weight \((1^N)\). A basis of
\(\operatorname{Sym}^{v}\operatorname{Sym}^{u}\) at that weight
is indexed by partitions \(L=\{L_1,\ldots,L_v\}\) of
\(\{1,\ldots,N\}\) into \(v\) unordered blocks of size \(u\):

\[
q_L=\prod_{i=1}^{v}\left(\prod_{k\in L_i}e_k\right).
\tag{OF.7}
\]

The target basis has analogous vectors \(q_W\), where \(W\)
has \(u\) blocks of size \(v\). Jacob's matrix \(M_{u,v}\)
has entry one exactly when every intersection \(L_i\cap W_j\)
has one element. In the averaged inclusion of \(q_L\), every
ordered row arrangement has coefficient
\(1/[v!(u!)^v]\). For a fixed transverse \(W\), exactly
\(v!u!\) arrangements project to \(q_W\): choose the row
ordering and the column ordering, after which every cell is fixed.
All other \(W\) receive zero. Hence

\[
h_{v,u}(q_L)=(u!)^{1-v}\sum_W(M_{u,v})_{W,L}q_W.
\tag{OF.8}
\]

In particular, the multilinear matrix of \(h_{4,4}\) is precisely
\(24^{-3}M_{4,4}\).

Jacob computes the adjacency algebra for the permutation action of
\(S_{16}\) on these block partitions. Its orbital matrices
\(A_0,\ldots,A_{42}\) form a basis of the commutant, and
\(A_{42}=M_{4,4}\). They obey

\[
A_iA_j=\sum_k p_{ij}^{k}A_k.
\tag{OF.9}
\]

Jacob's **Definition 1.1.11, printed p.9**, defines the displayed
collapsed matrix to have row \(j\), column \(k\) equal to
\(p_{j,42}^{k}\). Thus the matrix of right multiplication
by \(A_{42}\), in the basis \(A_j\) and column coordinates,
is its transpose. On
printed p.99 Jacob records

\[
\det B_{42}=2^{223}3^{67}\ne0.
\tag{OF.10}
\]

This gives an inverse in the finite-dimensional unital adjacency
algebra: solve \(BA_{42}=A_0\). In its faithful matrix
representation that equation makes \(A_{42}\) invertible. It
therefore proves injectivity of the multilinear map in (OF.8).

For completeness, passage from multilinear weight to every vector
space retains the actual map. Schur–Weyl decomposition of
\(V^{\otimes N}\), followed by the row averaging idempotents,
writes (OF.1) as \(\bigoplus_\lambda
\operatorname{id}_{S_\lambda V}\otimes H_\lambda\).
For \(V=\mathbb Q^N\), the weight \((1^N)\) in its tensor
power has basis \(e_{\sigma(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes
e_{\sigma(N)}\), a regular symmetric-group module. Applying
a primitive Young idempotent gives the nonzero Specht module of
shape \(\lambda\), exactly the multilinear weight in
\(S_\lambda\mathbb Q^N\). Every \(H_\lambda\) is therefore
injective when the multilinear map is injective. The same matrices
\(H_\lambda\) occur in every dimension, so \(h_{4,4}\) is
injective in every dimension.

The independent arithmetic receipt in this run extracts all 1,849
entries of Table 4.4, reconstructs its three column blocks, and
recomputes (OF.10) by fraction-free Bareiss elimination. Every exact
division is checked. Separate modular Gaussian eliminations give
determinants 82, 15 and 6627 modulo 101, 1009 and 10007. The matrix
and executable are `JACOB_2004_TABLE_4_4.tsv` and
`verify_jacob_fourth_base.py`; the receipt is
`JACOB_FOURTH_BASE_DETERMINANT_CHECK.txt`. The source's orbital
enumeration itself was not rerun. Its construction and the exact
matrix-to-map relation above were read and checked.

## 3. The remaining established canonical inputs

**Degree four.** Apply McKay's propagation proof to the established
injectivity of \(h_{4,4}\). The conclusion needed here is the
actual injectivity of \(h_{4,5}\). A full primary proof of the
propagation is Christian Ikenmeyer, *On McKay's propagation theorem
for the Foulkes conjecture*, **Theorem 1.3, printed p.2; proof in
§§2–6, printed pp.3–8**:

<https://arxiv.org/pdf/1509.04957>.

That paper's map definition on p.2 is (OF.1). Its full proof was
read in this run; R-024 §6 records the auxiliary raising-operator
normalizations and the retained spectator tensor factor. Those
corrections multiply only auxiliary injectivity maps by nonzero
scalars and retain the canonical grid map itself. This gives
\(\rho_4^\lambda=a_{4,5}^{\lambda}\).

**Degrees one, two and three.** At \(n=1\), \(h_{1,5}\)
is the identity on \(\operatorname{Sym}^5V\). For \(n=2,3\),
Sra's **Theorem 1.3, printed p.2**, in *The q-Foulkes problem III:
On Foulkes’ conjecture with a graded inner factor*, v1, states
surjectivity of \(h_{b,a}\) for every \(b\ge(a-1)^2\).
The exact two substitutions \((b,a)=(5,2),(5,3)\) satisfy this
bound. The full polarization/annihilator proof was read and audited
in R-021–R-024. Its primary text is

<https://suvrit.github.io/papers/qfoulkes3/qfoulkes3-v1.pdf>.

By (OF.6), these surjections transpose to injectivity of
\(h_{2,5}\) and \(h_{3,5}\). This proves the first line of
(OF.3) at every remaining positive degree. At degree zero the
canonical scalar map \(\mathbb Q\to\mathbb Q\) is also the
identity; it can be added separately with the empty partition.

**Degree five and every larger degree.** Cheung–Ikenmeyer–Mkrtchyan,
*Symmetrizing tableaux and the 5th case of the Foulkes conjecture*,
**Theorem 6(a),(b), printed p.3**, supplies injectivity of
\(h_{5,6}\) and the exact kernel

\[
\ker h_{5,5}=\bigoplus_{\lambda\in\mathcal E}S_\lambda V,
\tag{OF.11}
\]

with each listed summand once. The primary text is

<https://arxiv.org/pdf/1509.03944>.

Its p.2 definition again is (OF.1). The source proves its
computations using exact integer evaluation and representation
matrices. Its large original matrices were not recomputed in this
run. The stated maps, multiplicities and parameter range were
checked against the primary text and are used with their stated
scope. McKay propagation applied to the \((5,6)\) base gives
injectivity of \(h_{5,n}\) for every \(n\ge6\); (OF.6)
then gives surjectivity of \(h_{n,5}\) for every such degree.
This proves the remaining two lines of (OF.3).

The literature computations in sufficiently large dimension imply
the conclusions in every smaller dimension by the actual inclusion
\(V\hookrightarrow V\oplus W\), which commutes with all tensor
permutations and symmetric-power maps. The uniform Schur–Weyl
multiplicity matrices above give the same conclusion and show that
the kernel summands in (OF.11) are simply absent when their lengths
exceed the dimension. All maps and their ranks are defined over
\(\mathbb Q\); extension to any characteristic-zero field
preserves the ranks. This completes the proof of (OF.3).

## 4. Complete finite strict-chamber gate

Strict means \(\lambda_1>\lambda_2>\lambda_3>\lambda_4>
\lambda_5\ge0\), padding partitions to five entries. There are no
strict partitions of size below ten. At \(n=2\) there is one,
at \(n=3\) seven, and at \(n=4\) thirty. Every strict partition
has at least four nonzero rows. The actual averaging inclusion
\(\operatorname{Sym}^{n}\operatorname{Sym}^{5}V
\hookrightarrow(\operatorname{Sym}^{5}V)^{\otimes n}\), followed
by the usual successive Pieri decompositions, shows that its source
contains only shapes of length at most \(n\). Thus every strict
actual image is zero at \(n=2,3\), including the three nonzero
target multiplicities at \(n=3\).

The accompanying executable checks **every** partition of \(5n\)
of length at most five for \(1\le n\le4\): 313 partitions in
total. For both source and target it compares two exact calculations:

1. Expand the plethysm in power sums by its symmetric-group cycle
   index, and evaluate every irreducible character by literal
   rim-hook Murnaghan–Nakayama recursion.
2. Expand the monomial-multiset character
   \([t^d]\prod_{|\alpha|=e}(1-tx^\alpha)^{-1}\) in five
   variables; multiply by the Weyl alternant and extract each
   highest-weight coefficient. The total monomial character
   dimension is checked against
   \(\binom{\binom{e+4}{4}+d-1}{d}\).

All 626 coefficient comparisons agree. All 192 degree-four source
coefficients also agree with T-037's fixed positive polytope
evaluator, used with outer label \((4)\), inner degree five.
Partitions of greater length have zero source and target in these
degrees by the same averaging inclusion and Pieri argument.
These computations evaluate multiplicities; the map ranks follow
from the proved injectivity, not from numerical comparison alone.

The complete receipts are
`OUTER5_CANONICAL_LOW_DEGREE_CHECK.tsv` and
`OUTER5_CANONICAL_STRICT_LOW_DEGREES.tsv`, generated by
`verify_outer5_canonical_low_degrees.py`. The table below contains
all 38 strict cases. At degree four, 16 image multiplicities are one
and the other 14 are zero. Exactly four nonzero target components
are reached in full: \((13,4,2,1)\), \((9,8,2,1)\),
\((8,6,5,1)\) and \((7,6,4,3)\).

At degree five the four strict shapes in (OF.4) are
\((12,7,3,2,1)\), \((12,5,4,3,1)\),
\((10,8,4,2,1)\) and \((9,7,6,3,0)\); their image
multiplicities are exactly their target multiplicities minus one.
Every other strict degree-five target is reached in full. Every
strict target at degree at least six is reached in full. Together
with G-028's complete coefficient support, this resolves the actual
symmetric canonical-map gate on the entire strict five-row chamber.

# Canonical surjectivity from the complete finite degree-five kernels

## R-032. Five explicit families below the full degree-five base

Let \(a\ge6\), put \(C_a=\binom a2-10\), and use the
normalized canonical map

\[
h_{b,a}:\operatorname{Sym}^b(\operatorname{Sym}^aV)
\longrightarrow\operatorname{Sym}^a(\operatorname{Sym}^bV)
\tag{FK.1}
\]

over a characteristic-zero field. For a partition \(\lambda\),
write \(\lambda'_2=\#\{i:\lambda_i\ge2\}\), with missing
parts zero. Every target \(\lambda\)-isotypic component is reached
in each of the following unconditional parameter families:

\[
\boxed{
\begin{gathered}
1\le t\le4,\qquad b=C_a+t,\qquad\lambda\vdash ab,\\
\lambda_2\le t,\qquad \lambda_2+\lambda'_2\le t+2;
\end{gathered}}
\tag{FK.2}
\]

and

\[
\boxed{
\begin{gathered}
b=C_a+5=\binom a2-5,\qquad\lambda\vdash ab,\qquad\lambda_2\le5,\\
\lambda_2\le4\quad\text{or}\quad\lambda_3\le3
\quad\text{or}\quad\lambda_4\le2\quad\text{or}\quad\lambda_5=0.
\end{gathered}}
\tag{FK.3}
\]

These assertions retain every target multiplicity and every
dimension. A target shape with more than \(a\) rows is zero by
the symmetric-power inclusion and Pieri rule, so it causes no
exception. The full degree-five base in R-024 starts at
\(b=C_a+6\); (FK.2)–(FK.3) use its five preceding integer
degrees, with their complete finite lower kernels. At the fifth
degree, (FK.3) contains the earlier \(\lambda_2\le4\) result
and adds the displayed parts of the \(\lambda_2=5\) band.

The proof gives an actual injection of the remaining annihilator
into a finite sum of explicit Pieri modules, stated in (FK.10).
It also gives the positive lattice-point upper bound (FK.11) for
every remaining cokernel in these second-row bands. No historical
novelty is asserted for these consequences.

## 1. Exact lower kernels and their minimal tails

Put

\[
\mathcal K_{s,d}(W)=\ker h_{s,d}(W),\qquad
\mathcal K_{s,d}^{\le t}=
\bigoplus_{\eta_2\le t}(\mathcal K_{s,d})_\eta.
\tag{FK.4}
\]

The exact tensor-pairing identity \(h_{d,s}(V)^*=h_{s,d}(V^*)\)
in R-024 (P.6), also proved with scalar one in R-031 (OF.6),
identifies this kernel with the image annihilator of (FK.1).
The polynomial isotypic notation in (FK.4) includes complete
multiplicity spaces.

R-031 gives the complete multiplicities of
\(\mathcal K_{5,t}\) at \(1\le t\le5\). For \(t\le4\)
they are \(a_{5,t}^\mu-a_{t,5}^\mu\), from actual injectivity
of the transpose canonical map. At \(t=5\) they are the eight
published Cheung–Ikenmeyer–Mkrtchyan kernel summands, each once.
Restricting to \(\mu_2\le t\) yields respectively
\(0,3,4,19,2\) distinct summands. The complete 28-row table is
included at the end of this report; the sole multiplicity two is
\(\mu=(10,4,4,2)\) at \(t=4\).

For each surviving \(\mu\), remove its first row and pad the
tail to four coordinates. The componentwise minimal tails are

\[
\begin{array}{c|l}
t&\text{minimal tails}\\\hline
1&\varnothing\\
2&(2,2,0,0)\\
3&(3,2,0,0),\ (2,2,2,0)\\
4&(4,2,0,0),\ (3,2,2,0),\ (2,2,2,2)\\
5&(5,4,3,1).
\end{array}
\tag{FK.5}
\]

The finite arithmetic input here is exhaustive: R-031 independently
computed both characters for every partition of size \(5t\) and
length at most five at \(1\le t\le4\), using both literal
Murnaghan–Nakayama and a monomial-multiset/Weyl-alternant extraction.
The archive agent independently reconstructed every coefficient by
the G-027 restriction complex. The executable
`verify_finite_base_tail_ranges.py` extracts exactly the nonzero
differences in the stated second-row bands, verifies their minimal
tail antichains, and checks the explicit tail conditions in all
251 sorted bounded four-tuples. The general inequalities below
are proved directly and do not depend on sampling an unbounded
parameter. The exact input and receipt are
`FINITE_BASE_KERNELS.tsv` and `FINITE_BASE_TAIL_CHECK.tsv`.

## 2. The actual iterated annihilator injection

For \(r\ge5\), set \(C_5=0\), \(C_{r+1}=C_r+r\),
and \(b_s=C_s+t\). Thus \(b_{r+1}-r=b_r\ge t\ge1\).
For the symmetric \((r+1)\)-slot space, let

\[
\delta(w_0\cdots w_r)=\frac1{r+1}
\sum_i\left(\prod_{j\ne i}w_j\right)\otimes w_i,
\qquad
T_{r,r,b}f=[z_1^r\cdots z_r^r]
 f(v_1+z_1x,\ldots,v_r+z_rx).
\tag{FK.6}
\]

Multiplication is a left inverse of \(\delta\). The normalized
map \(\Theta_{r+1,b}=(T_{r,r,b}\otimes1)\delta\) has the
following actual restriction, proved in R-024 (P.11)–(P.16):

\[
\Theta_{r+1,b}:\mathcal K_{r+1,b}(W)
\longrightarrow
\operatorname{Sym}^{r^2}W\otimes
\mathcal K_{r,b-r}(W)\otimes\operatorname{Sym}^{b}W.
\tag{FK.7}
\]

Here is the exact kernel-membership argument. Represent \(F\)
by its symmetric \((r+1)\)-linear form \(\mathcal A_F\) on
\(\operatorname{Sym}^b V\). For a product \(Q\) of \(b-r\)
linear factors, the form \((x^r+c y^r)Q\) splits into \(b\)
linear factors over \(\mathbb C\). The coefficient of \(c\)
in the defining diagonal vanishing, divided by \(r+1\), is
\(\mathcal A_F(x^rQ,\ldots,x^rQ,y^rQ)=0\).
Apply the \(b-r\) ordinary directional derivatives corresponding
to the factors of \(Q\) to
\(\mathcal A_F(x^rQ,\ldots,x^rQ,y^b)\). The result is
\(b!/r!\) times that zero expression. Before the \(i\)-th
derivative the degrees in its two exchanged vector variables are
\(b-i+1,r\), whose difference is \(b-r-i+1\ge1\).
The one-step \(GL_2\) string calculation in R-024 (P.14)
makes each such derivative injective. Removing them successively
shows \(\mathcal A_F(x^rQ,\ldots,x^rQ,y^b)=0\).
Thus the middle \(r\)-linear form lies in the stated lower
canonical kernel. Its actual coefficient is

\[
\Theta F(v_1,\ldots,v_r;x,y)=
\binom br^r\mathcal A_F
 (x^rv_1^{b-r},\ldots,x^rv_r^{b-r},y^b).
\tag{FK.8}
\]

Evaluation at every \(x,y\) separates the outer symmetric
factors and proves (FK.7) as a tensor identity. The construction
and its coefficients are rational.

Now apply (FK.7) with \(b=b_{r+1}\), restricting to
\(\lambda_2\le t\). Every first-factor type \(\nu\)
occurring after \(\delta\) has \(\lambda/\nu\) a horizontal
strip by Pieri; in particular \(\nu_2\le\lambda_2\le t\).
R-018 proves injectivity of \(T_{r,r,b}\) on every entire
type with \(\nu_2\le b-r\). Since \(t\le b-r=b_r\),
the restriction of \(\Theta\) to the entire second-row band
is injective. Different isotypic components remain distinct
under this equivariant map.

In the codomain of (FK.7), every lower type \(\eta\)
contributing to a type \(\lambda\) is contained in it:
two applications of Pieri add the horizontal strips of sizes
\(r^2\) and \(b\). In particular \(\eta_2\le t\).
Consequently the actual injective restriction is

\[
\mathcal K_{r+1,b_{r+1}}^{\le t}
\hookrightarrow
\operatorname{Sym}^{r^2}W\otimes
\mathcal K_{r,b_r}^{\le t}\otimes
\operatorname{Sym}^{b_{r+1}}W.
\tag{FK.9}
\]

Iterate (FK.9) on its middle factor, retaining the other factors
and using only ordinary tensor-factor permutations. Tensoring an
injective linear map preserves injectivity. This gives the fully
specified composite injection

\[
\boxed{
\mathcal K_{a,b_a}^{\le t}(W)
\hookrightarrow\mathcal K_{5,t}^{\le t}(W)\otimes
\bigotimes_{r=5}^{a-1}
 \left(\operatorname{Sym}^{r^2}W\otimes
       \operatorname{Sym}^{b_{r+1}}W\right).}
\tag{FK.10}
\]

Its total degree is correct at every step:
\((r+1)b_{r+1}-r b_r=r^2+b_{r+1}\).
This proves (FK.10) in every dimension and, by extension from
its rational matrices, over every characteristic-zero field.

## 3. Explicit support exclusion and proof of the families

Every type in the codomain of (FK.10) contains at least one of
its base shapes \(\mu\), because each successive factor adds
a horizontal strip. For a nonzero target in (FK.2) or (FK.3),
\(\ell(\lambda)\le a\), so

\[
\lambda_1\ge ab_a-(a-1)t=aC_a+t\ge30+t>5t\ge\mu_1.
\]

Thus \(\mu\subseteq\lambda\) depends only on their tails.
The tail containment conditions are exactly the upward closures
of (FK.5).

For \(2\le t\le4\), write \(p=\lambda_2\le t\)
and \(q=\lambda'_2\). For \(p\le1\), none of the tails
in (FK.5) is contained and \(p+q\le t+2\) holds. For
\(2\le p\le t\), the tails in question are
\((t-j,2^{j+1})\), \(0\le j\le t-2\). The first
coordinate permits precisely \(j\ge t-p\); the remaining
coordinates require \(q\ge j+3\). Some such tail is
contained exactly at \(q\ge t-p+3\). Its exclusion is
therefore exactly \(p+q\le t+2\). At \(t=1\), the base
kernel is zero and the same displayed inequality holds
automatically on \(\lambda_2\le1\). This proves that the
codomain in (FK.10) has zero \(\lambda\)-isotypic component
for every parameter in (FK.2).

At \(t=5\), the unique minimal tail is \((5,4,3,1)\).
Its exclusion on \(\lambda_2\le5\) is exactly the
disjunction in (FK.3). Again the codomain has zero component.
Injectivity of (FK.10) then forces the actual annihilator
component to vanish. The perfect pairing (FK.4) proves the
surjectivity assertions (FK.2)–(FK.3), including all
multiplicities.

## 4. A positive explicit upper bound for the remaining cokernel

The same injection gives a further unconditional quantitative
statement. Let \(1\le t\le5\), \(a\ge6\),
\(b=C_a+t\), and \(\lambda\vdash ab\) with
\(\lambda_2\le t\). Let \(m_t(\mu)\) be the base
multiplicities in the complete table. Set \(N_{\mu,\lambda}\)
equal to the number of partition chains starting at \(\mu\),
ending at \(\lambda\), and successively adding horizontal
strips of sizes
\(25,b_6,36,b_7,\ldots,(a-1)^2,b_a\).
Then

\[
\boxed{
0\le\operatorname{mult}_\lambda\operatorname{coker}h_{b,a}
\le\sum_{\mu}m_t(\mu)N_{\mu,\lambda}.}
\tag{FK.11}
\]

For explicit polytopes, pad every intermediate partition to
\(\max\{a,\ell(\lambda)\}\) rows. Thus the same codomain
count is retained even when the actual target is zero because
\(\ell(\lambda)>a\). For each adjacent pair \(\eta,\theta\)
impose
\(\theta_i\ge\eta_i\ge\theta_{i+1}\), nonnegativity,
and \(\sum_i\theta_i-\sum_i\eta_i\) equal to its
specified strip size. Fix the endpoints. These are bounded
integer polytopes whose lattice points are precisely the chains;
the inequalities themselves prove the horizontal-strip
bijection. A label of multiplicity two is counted with two
separate tags. Pieri identifies this positive count with the
codomain multiplicity in (FK.10), proving (FK.11) for the
actual cokernel.

For a concrete nonzero value in (FK.3), every \(a\ge6\),
\(b=\binom a2-5\) has

\[
\rho_{b,a}^{(ab-5,5)}=a_{a,b}^{(ab-5,5)}=2.
\tag{FK.12}
\]

Indeed the target's binary weight \((ab-j,j)\), for
\(j=4,5\), has a monomial basis indexed by partitions of
\(j\) with at most \(a\) parts, each at most \(b\).
Here \(a\ge6\) and \(b\ge10\), so these counts are the
unrestricted partition numbers \(p(4)=5\), \(p(5)=7\).
Each binary Schur module with second row at most \(j\)
contributes once to this weight, giving the multiplicity
\(p(5)-p(4)=2\). Schur–Weyl functoriality preserves this
two-row multiplicity in every dimension at least two.
Surjectivity (FK.3) then gives the exact actual image value.
This calculation is included as a concrete consequence, without
a novelty claim for the two-row coefficient.

# A unit-multiplicity family with an explicit invariant and canonical image

## R-033. The full two-column tail family

For every pair of integers \(a\ge2,n\ge2\) and every
\(1\le j\le a-1\), put

\[
\lambda=(an-2j,2^j).
\]

It is a partition: \(an-2j\ge2a-2j\ge2\). Its exact
symmetric plethysm multiplicity is

\[
\boxed{a_{a,n}^{(an-2j,2^j)}=1.}
\tag{UT.1}
\]

The proof below gives its actual invariant tensor, its exact
balanced flag morphism, and the exterior-power map determining
the invariant line. It also proves the following actual canonical
image families for
\(h_{n,a}:\operatorname{Sym}^n\operatorname{Sym}^aV
\to\operatorname{Sym}^a\operatorname{Sym}^nV\):

\[
\boxed{
\begin{array}{ll}
a\ge2,\quad n\ge2(a-1),\quad1\le j\le a-1,&
\operatorname{mult}_{\lambda}\operatorname{im}h_{n,a}=1,\\
a\ge6,\quad n\ge2a-5,\quad1\le j\le a-1,&
\operatorname{mult}_{\lambda}\operatorname{im}h_{n,a}=1.
\end{array}}
\tag{UT.2}
\]

All multiplicities are taken in dimension at least \(j+1\).
In a smaller dimension the Schur functor is zero. No historical
novelty claim is made for (UT.1) or for the literature inequality
used below.

## 1. An exact exterior transfer sequence

For any characteristic-zero vector space \(W\), define

\[
\begin{aligned}
D_j:\Lambda^jW\otimes\Lambda^jW
&\longrightarrow\Lambda^{j+1}W\otimes\Lambda^{j-1}W,\\
D_j((u_1\wedge\cdots\wedge u_j)\otimes
      (v_1\wedge\cdots\wedge v_j))
&=\sum_{\ell=1}^j(-1)^{\ell-1}
 (u_1\wedge\cdots\wedge u_j\wedge v_\ell)
 \otimes(v_1\wedge\cdots\widehat v_\ell\cdots\wedge v_j).
\end{aligned}
\tag{UT.3}
\]

Both alternating multilinear expressions show that this is
well-defined and natural in \(W\). Embed these two spaces as
the weights \((j,j)\) and \((j+1,j-1)\) in
\(\Lambda^{2j}(W\otimes\mathbb Q^2)\), writing all first-copy
factors before all second-copy factors. The Lie operator
\(E_{12}\) replaces one second-copy vector by its first-copy
vector. Moving the replaced vector past its \(\ell-1\)
preceding second-copy vectors gives exactly (UT.3), including
its sign and scalar.

The commuting Young projectors give the skew Cauchy decomposition

\[
\Lambda^{2j}(W\otimes\mathbb Q^2)
=\bigoplus_{k=0}^j
 S_{(2^k,1^{2j-2k})}W\otimes S_{(2j-k,k)}\mathbb Q^2.
\tag{UT.4}
\]

Terms with too many rows in \(W\) vanish. In its two-dimensional
factor write
\(S_{(2j-k,k)}\mathbb Q^2=\det^k\operatorname{Sym}^{2j-2k}\mathbb Q^2\).
The source line has vector
\(\det^k e_1^{j-k}e_2^{j-k}\), and its image is

\[
(j-k)\det^k e_1^{j-k+1}e_2^{j-k-1}.
\tag{UT.5}
\]

Every target line has \(k<j\), so the map is onto each
target summand. Exactly \(k=j\) is killed. Consequently
the actual maps form the short exact sequence

\[
0\longrightarrow S_{(2^j)}W
\longrightarrow\Lambda^jW\otimes\Lambda^jW
\xrightarrow{D_j}\Lambda^{j+1}W\otimes\Lambda^{j-1}W
\longrightarrow0.
\tag{UT.6}
\]

The first map is its column-antisymmetrized Young component
in the tensor space, with the usual rational Young projector.
Equations (UT.4)–(UT.5) identify its image with the literal
kernel, and fix the second map without a dimension-only
identification.

## 2. The invariant line for the standard permutation representation

Let \(E=\mathbb Q^a\), with its permutation basis \(e_i\),
let \(\mathbf1=\sum_i e_i\), and let

\[
W=\mathfrak h_a=\{(z_1,\ldots,z_a):\textstyle\sum_i z_i=0\},
\qquad P(e_i)=e_i-a^{-1}\mathbf1.
\tag{UT.7}
\]

For \(0\le q\le a-1\), the exact hook identification is

\[
[a-q,1^q]\simeq\Lambda^q\mathfrak h_a.
\tag{UT.8}
\]

Here is the explicit map and normalization. Send a tabloid of
shape \((a-q,1^q)\), with entries \(i_1,\ldots,i_q\) in
its ordered singleton rows, to
\(e_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge e_{i_q}\). This is an
\(S_a\)-equivariant map on the tabloid permutation module.
For a polytabloid whose first column is
\((i_0,i_1,\ldots,i_q)\), column antisymmetrization gives

\[
q!\,(e_{i_1}-e_{i_0})\wedge\cdots\wedge(e_{i_q}-e_{i_0}).
\tag{UT.9}
\]

To check the factor, fix the entry omitted from the wedge.
The remaining \(q!\) column permutations give that same
ordered wedge after their two signs cancel. Expanding the
right side gives exactly these \(q+1\) possible omissions.
Taking \(i_0=a\) gives a spanning wedge basis. The hook
Specht dimension is \(\binom{a-1}{q}\): a standard hook
tableau is specified by its \(q\) first-column entries below
1. Thus the map restricts to the isomorphism (UT.8).
The characteristic-zero irreducibility of the Specht modules
then gives distinct irreducible representations for distinct
\(q\). This is also the precise hook/exterior identification
in Giannelli's Lemma 2.3.3 used and source-checked in R-003.

The ordinary dot product on \(E\) restricts nondegenerately
to \(\mathfrak h_a\), and its determinant form restricts
nondegenerately to each exterior power. These invariant forms
give the actual self-duality maps. Therefore

\[
\begin{aligned}
\dim(\Lambda^jW\otimes\Lambda^jW)^{S_a}&=1,\\
(\Lambda^{j+1}W\otimes\Lambda^{j-1}W)^{S_a}&=0
\qquad(1\le j\le a-2).
\end{aligned}
\tag{UT.10}
\]

The first equality is the endomorphism space of the irreducible
hook; the second is the homomorphism space between two distinct
hooks, under the specified dualities. At \(j=a-1\), the
first exterior power is the one-dimensional sign representation
and the target of (UT.6) is zero, yielding the same invariant
conclusion. The Reynolds operator \(a!^{-1}\sum_{g\in S_a}g\)
makes taking invariants exact. Applying it to (UT.6) proves

\[
\dim(S_{(2^j)}\mathfrak h_a)^{S_a}=1
\qquad(1\le j\le a-1).
\tag{UT.11}
\]

There is an explicit nonzero invariant in this kernel. Set
\(f_i=e_i-e_a\), \(1\le i<a\). In the wedge basis
\(f_I\), let \(G_j\) be the matrix of the induced determinant
form. Then

\[
\Omega_j=\sum_{I,J}(G_j^{-1})_{I,J}f_I\otimes f_J
\tag{UT.12}
\]

is its coevaluation tensor. It corresponds to the identity on
\(\Lambda^jW\), so it is nonzero and invariant.
Equation (UT.10) proves \(D_j\Omega_j=0\), including the
endpoint \(j=a-1\). The inverse of the first arrow in
(UT.6) on its kernel therefore supplies a specified generator
of the line in (UT.11).

## 3. Exact projected matching and flag morphisms

The invariant just constructed has a literal matching-tensor
description. In \(W\otimes W\), put

\[
J=(P\otimes P)\sum_{i=1}^a e_i\otimes e_i
=\sum_{i=1}^a P(e_i)\otimes P(e_i).
\tag{UT.13}
\]

Since \(P\) is the orthogonal projection onto \(W\),
this is exactly its coevaluation tensor. Place the \(j\)
copies of \(J\) in tensor positions \((1,j+1),\ldots,(j,2j)\).
Apply the exterior quotient in the first and last \(j\)
positions. The result is

\[
\sum_{i_1,\ldots,i_j}
 P(e_{i_1})\wedge\cdots\wedge P(e_{i_j})
 \otimes P(e_{i_1})\wedge\cdots\wedge P(e_{i_j})
=j!\,\Omega_j.
\tag{UT.14}
\]

Indeed the induced map \(\Lambda^jP\) is again an orthogonal
projection. Summing over increasing \(j\)-subsets gives
its coevaluation on its image, and summing over ordered
distinct indices contributes exactly \(j!\). Thus projection
of a fixed perfect matching, followed by the two exterior
quotients and division by \(j!\), gives precisely (UT.12).
This proves the matching-to-Schur morphism in every stated
rank; it does not require independence of all matching tensors.

To obtain the plethysm line, use an \(a\times a\) matrix
\(X\), put \(x_i=X_{i1}\), \(u=\prod_i x_i\), and define
for \(|I|=j+1\)

\[
v_{j+1,I}=\left(\prod_{i\notin I}x_i\right)
\det X_{I,\{1,\ldots,j+1\}}.
\tag{UT.15}
\]

The exact T-032 map identifies \(\Lambda^j\mathfrak h_a\)
with \(\mathbf1\wedge\Lambda^j\mathfrak h_a\) by
\(w\mapsto\mathbf1\wedge w\). On the open set \(u\ne0\),
its coordinates are
\(v_{j+1}=u\,\mathbf1\wedge\bar w_2\wedge\cdots\wedge\bar w_{j+1}\),
where \((w_k)_i=X_{ik}/x_i\) and \(\bar w_k\) subtracts
the mean coordinate. Substitution of these minors defines the
algebra morphism on the smaller flag algebra; it respects its
relations because these are actual minors of the matrix
\((u\bar w_2,\bar w_3,\ldots)\).

For the degree \((2^j)\) Schur component, its balanced
component map is exactly

\[
f\longmapsto u^{n-2}f(v_{j+1}).
\tag{UT.16}
\]

It has row weight \((n^a)\) and right weight
\((an-2j,2^j)\). For clarity its inverse on the dense chart
is also explicit: prescribe nonzero \(u_0\) and centered
columns \(F_1,\ldots,F_{a-1}\); choose \(\prod_i x_i=u_0\)
and set \(X_{i2}=x_i(F_1)_i/u_0\),
\(X_{ik}=x_i(F_{k-1})_i\) for \(k\ge3\). The prescribed
minor matrix is recovered exactly. Thus (UT.16) is injective.
For surjectivity, expand a balanced flag polynomial as flag
monomials and replace each higher minor by
\(u^{-1}(\prod_{i\in I}x_i)v_{|I|,I}\). Its right weight
has exactly two higher-minor factors; balance leaves precisely
\(u^{n-2}\) times smaller flag degree \((2^j)\). This
proves surjectivity. The exponent is nonnegative because
\(n\ge2\), so every element maps to a polynomial.

The row permutation action fixes \(u\) and commutes with
centering, so (UT.16) is \(S_a\)-equivariant with the
ordinary standard action on \(\mathfrak h_a\).
The exact Cauchy/Schur–Weyl balanced multiplicity map gives

\[
a_{a,n}^{(an-2j,2^j)}
=\dim(S_{(an-2j,2^j)}\mathbb Q^a)_{(n^a)}^{S_a}
=\dim(S_{(2^j)}\mathfrak h_a)^{S_a}=1.
\tag{UT.17}
\]

Its invariant generator is the polynomial image under (UT.16)
of the vector (UT.12) in the kernel component (UT.6).
This proves (UT.1) with its actual morphisms.

## 4. Actual canonical image and a rectangular-Kronecker consequence

Every partition in (UT.1) has second row two. Apply R-034
(LP.2), respectively (LP.4), at \(t=2\). The entire
target component is in the image for the two ranges (UT.2).
Its target multiplicity is exactly one by (UT.17), proving
the stated actual image multiplicity. This uses the annihilator
injections (LP.12) and (LP.20) and their scalar-one transpose
pairing; no dimension comparison is substituted for the map.

There is also the unconditional rectangular family

\[
\boxed{
a\ge2,\quad1\le j\le a-1,\quad n\ge2j:
\qquad g\bigl((an-2j,2^j),(a^n),(a^n)\bigr)\ge1.}
\tag{UT.18}
\]

Use the tail \(\rho=(2^j)\), of size \(2j\), in
Ikenmeyer–Panova Proposition 2.8, “Inequality of
Multiplicities,” p.7. Its stable range is \(n\ge|\rho|\),
and its plethysm term is exactly the one in (UT.17).
The source statement and full proof apply also at \(a=2\).
For the exact finite coordinate-ring maps, set
\(M=n\binom{n+n^2-1}{n}\) and
\(\lambda_M=(aM-2j,2^j)\). Proposition 2.6(b)'s padding
lift, Lemma 2.7's determinant realization, and coordinate
restriction give the finite chain

\[
1=a_{a,n}^{\lambda}
\le\operatorname{mult}_{\lambda_M}\mathbb C[\Gamma_n^M]_a
\le\operatorname{mult}_{\lambda_M}\mathbb C[\mathrm{Det}_M]_a
\le g(\lambda_M,(a^M),(a^M)).
\tag{UT.19}
\]

Here the middle inequality is the actual restriction from
\(\Gamma_n^M\subseteq\mathrm{Det}_M\); the last is the
determinant orbit Peter–Weyl comparison in Proposition 2.5.
Their Theorem 2.1's rectangular stability identifies the last
term with the one in (UT.18), since \(M,n\ge2j\).
The complete source-map chain was already written and checked
in R-014 and is specialized here without changing its maps.
The primary source is Ikenmeyer–Panova, *Rectangular Kronecker
coefficients and plethysms in geometric complexity theory*,
arXiv:1512.03798v2, <https://arxiv.org/pdf/1512.03798>.

All maps and all averaging and factorial scalars in this report
are rational. Scalar extension proves the same statements over
every characteristic-zero field.


# Canonical-map ranges linear in the outer degree at fixed second row

## R-034. The actual annihilator injection and unconditional ranges

All vector spaces are over a characteristic-zero field. For
\(a,b\ge1\), use the normalized grid map

\[
h_{b,a}:\operatorname{Sym}^{b}(\operatorname{Sym}^{a}V)
\longrightarrow\operatorname{Sym}^{a}(\operatorname{Sym}^{b}V).
\tag{LP.1}
\]

Every whole target \(\lambda\)-isotypic component is reached in
the following two families, with all its multiplicities:

\[
\boxed{a\ge2,\quad t\ge1,\quad b\ge t(a-1),\quad
\lambda\vdash ab,\quad\lambda_2\le t.}
\tag{LP.2}
\]

For the stronger degree-five profile, put

\[
B_t=
\begin{cases}
1,&t=1,\\
5,&2\le t\le4,\\
6,&t=5,\\
t,&t\ge6,
\end{cases}
\qquad
C_{a,t}=\sum_{r=5}^{a-1}\min\{r,t\}.
\tag{LP.3}
\]

Then the second family is

\[
\boxed{a\ge6,\quad t\ge1,\quad b\ge C_{a,t}+B_t,\quad
\lambda\vdash ab,\quad\lambda_2\le t.}
\tag{LP.4}
\]

In particular, the following are explicit uniform subfamilies of
(LP.4):

| Second-row bound | Every outer degree | Inner-degree range |
|---|---|---|
| \(\lambda_2\le1\) | \(a\ge6\) | \(b\ge a-4\) |
| \(\lambda_2\le2\) | \(a\ge6\) | \(b\ge2a-5\) |
| \(\lambda_2\le3\) | \(a\ge6\) | \(b\ge3a-10\) |
| \(\lambda_2\le4\) | \(a\ge6\) | \(b\ge4a-15\) |
| \(\lambda_2\le5\) | \(a\ge6\) | \(b\ge5a-19\) |
| \(\lambda_2\le t,\ t\ge6\) | \(a\ge6\) | \(b\ge t(a-4)\) |

For \(t\ge6\) the capped sum in (LP.3) improves the last
displayed sufficient bound and has the exact closed form

\[
C_{a,t}+t=
\begin{cases}
\binom a2-10+t,&6\le a\le t+1,\\
ta-\binom t2-10,&a\ge t+1.
\end{cases}
\tag{LP.5}
\]

The two expressions agree at \(a=t+1\). Thus for fixed
\(t\), the asserted threshold grows linearly with \(a\).
For example \(t=6\) gives \(b\ge6a-25\) for every
\(a\ge7\), together with \(b\ge11\) at \(a=6\).

The proof below establishes an exact common-polarization morphism
on the prescribed second-row band. It uses the already proved
arbitrary-power theorem R-018 and the actual canonical bases
checked in R-031; it does not infer map ranks from a comparison of
source and target dimensions. No historical novelty claim is made.

## 1. Exact kernels of one directional derivative

Let \(W\) be the space of polynomial generators for vector
variables \(y,z\), and put

\[
D_{z,y}=\sum_i z_i\frac{\partial}{\partial y_i}.
\]

On bidegree \((p,q)\), this is an actual equivariant map

\[
D_{z,y}:\operatorname{Sym}^{p}W\otimes\operatorname{Sym}^{q}W
\longrightarrow\operatorname{Sym}^{p-1}W
                  \otimes\operatorname{Sym}^{q+1}W.
\tag{LP.6}
\]

For \(p\ge1\), its exact kernel is

\[
\boxed{
\ker D_{z,y}=
\begin{cases}
0,&p>q,\\
S_{(q,p)}W,&1\le p\le q.
\end{cases}}
\tag{LP.7}
\]

Here the last space is its Cauchy summand inside the source.
To verify both the summand and the map, realize the source as the
weight \((p,q)\) part of
\(\operatorname{Sym}^{p+q}(W\otimes\mathbb Q^2)\).
The Cauchy decomposition, obtained by the commuting Young
projectors on the tensor factors, is

\[
\bigoplus_{j=0}^{\min(p,q)}
S_{(p+q-j,j)}W\otimes
 \left(\det^j\otimes
       \operatorname{Sym}^{p+q-2j}\mathbb Q^2\right)_{(p,q)}.
\tag{LP.8}
\]

The indicated weight line is the determinant factor times
\(e_y^{p-j}e_z^{q-j}\). The operator in (LP.6) is exactly
the Lie-algebra operator \(e_z\partial_{e_y}\) on that
factor, and sends this vector to

\[
(p-j)\det^j e_y^{p-j-1}e_z^{q-j+1}.
\tag{LP.9}
\]

It is nonzero for every \(j<p\); the only vanished line is
\(j=p\le q\), giving precisely (LP.7). This proves the
kernel including all multiplicities and all small dimensions;
an overly long Schur functor is simply zero.

Now tensor (LP.6) with the polynomial spaces in any other vector
variables, at their actual fixed multidegrees. Such a spectator
space is a tensor product of symmetric powers of \(W\).
The kernel tensors with that same space, since the operator is
\(D_{z,y}\otimes1\). Successive Pieri decompositions show
that every constituent of
\(S_{(q,p)}W\) tensored with the spectator space contains the
diagram \((q,p)\), and therefore has second row at least
\(p\). In particular, for every fixed band \(\eta_2\le t\),
all such maps with \(p>t\) are injective on the entire band,
even when \(p\le q\). This is a consequence of the exact
kernel (LP.7) and the literal tensoring map, with no discarded
spectator factors.

## 2. Freeing one argument with an arbitrary whole power

Let \(r,t\ge1\), put

\[
L\ge\min\{r,t\},\qquad b\ge L+t,\qquad m=b-L\ge t\ge1.
\tag{LP.10}
\]

Write \(\mathcal K_{s,d}(W)=\ker h_{s,d}(W)\), and use a
superscript \(\le t\) for its entire second-row band.
These are the actual image annihilators, by the scalar-one
pairing identity in R-031 (OF.6).

Define the same normalized contraction as before,

\[
\delta(w_0\cdots w_r)=\frac1{r+1}\sum_i
  \left(\prod_{j\ne i}w_j\right)\otimes w_i,
\]

and use the arbitrary-power common polarization

\[
T_{r,L,b}f(v_1,\ldots,v_r;x)
=[z_1^L\cdots z_r^L]
  f(v_1+z_1x,\ldots,v_r+z_rx).
\tag{LP.11}
\]

The following is an actual injective restriction of their
composite:

\[
\boxed{
\Theta^{(L)}_{r+1,b}:=(T_{r,L,b}\otimes1)\delta:
\mathcal K_{r+1,b}^{\le t}(W)
\hookrightarrow
\operatorname{Sym}^{rL}W\otimes
\mathcal K_{r,m}^{\le t}(W)\otimes\operatorname{Sym}^{b}W.}
\tag{LP.12}
\]

First prove membership in the lower kernel. Let \(F\) be a
vector in a complete \(\lambda\)-isotypic component of
\(\mathcal K_{r+1,b}\), with \(\lambda_2\le t\), and
let \(\mathcal A_F\) be its corresponding symmetric
\((r+1)\)-linear form on \(\operatorname{Sym}^bV\).
For \(Q=y_1\cdots y_m\), the form
\((x^L+c z^L)Q\) splits into \(b\) linear factors over
\(\mathbb C\). Coefficient extraction in its diagonal
vanishing gives

\[
\mathcal A_F(x^LQ,\ldots,x^LQ,z^LQ)=0,
\tag{LP.13}
\]

with \(r\) copies of the first argument; the extracted
coefficient is \(r+1\) times this expression.
Set

\[
G_F(x,y_1,\ldots,y_m,z)
=\mathcal A_F(x^LQ,\ldots,x^LQ,z^b).
\tag{LP.14}
\]

This construction is a \(GL(V)\)-equivariant polynomial map
of \(F\), so its image belongs to the same whole
\(\lambda\)-isotypic component. All variables in (LP.14)
remain independent while taking derivatives. The exact identity
is

\[
D_{y_m,z}\cdots D_{y_1,z}G_F
=\frac{b!}{L!}
\mathcal A_F(x^LQ,\ldots,x^LQ,z^LQ)=0.
\tag{LP.15}
\]

Before the \(i\)-th derivative, the exchanged bidegrees in
\((z,y_i)\) are \((p,q)=(b-i+1,r)\).
The other variables have nonnegative fixed polynomial degrees:
\(rL\) in \(x\), \(r+1\) in previously used \(y\)'s,
and \(r\) in unused \(y\)'s. In particular they are exactly
the spectator factors of §1. Also \(p\ge L+1\).

There are two exhaustive parameter cases. For \(L\ge r\),
\(p\ge L+1>q\), so (LP.7) gives full injectivity.
For \(t\le L<r\), \(p\ge L+1\ge t+1\); (LP.7) and the spectator
Pieri argument give injectivity on the whole
\(\lambda_2\le t\) band. These operators are equivariant,
so every intermediate image remains in that band. Starting with
the last derivative in (LP.15) and successively using these
injective restrictions proves \(G_F=0\).

For every fixed \(x,z\), the symmetric \(r\)-linear form
\(\mathcal A_F(x^LQ_1,\ldots,x^LQ_r,z^b)\) therefore has
zero diagonal on every product of \(m\) linear factors.
This is exactly the defining lower-kernel condition
\(\mathcal K_{r,m}\), without replacing the specified
canonical map. In vector slots the normalized composite is

\[
\Theta^{(L)}F(v_1,\ldots,v_r;x,z)
=\binom bL^r\mathcal A_F
 (x^Lv_1^m,\ldots,x^Lv_r^m,z^b).
\tag{LP.16}
\]

Evaluation at all \(x,z\) separates its symmetric-power
factors, proving tensor membership in
\(\operatorname{Sym}^{rL}W\otimes\mathcal K_{r,m}W
\otimes\operatorname{Sym}^bW\). Any lower type \(\eta\)
contributing to a type \(\lambda\) in this tensor product
is contained in \(\lambda\), by two Pieri steps. Thus
\(\eta_2\le\lambda_2\le t\), proving precisely the
codomain band in (LP.12).

## 3. Injectivity of the arbitrary-power common polarization

The needed statement of R-018 is its full arbitrary-power
formula, not a specialization to \(L=r\): for
\(b\ge L\ge0\), the map (LP.11) is injective on every
whole \(\nu\)-isotypic component with
\(\nu_2\le b-L\). We recall its actual inverse argument
to verify this dependence on \(L\).

Use coordinates \(X_{ji}\) on the \(r\) slots and put
\(x_i=X_{1i}\). Every highest polynomial of row weight
\(\nu\) is a linear combination of products of initial-row
flag minors. There are exactly \(\nu_2\) factors of
height at least two in each homogeneous product. Each minor
uses a slot at most once. Hence, after setting \(x_i=1\),
the highest polynomial \(P\) has degree at most
\(\nu_2\) in each remaining slot block. Separate
homogenization of degree \(b\) in each slot is the inverse
of this evaluation.

At common vector \(e_1\), (LP.11) sends a monomial of
block degrees \(d_i\) to the same monomial, homogenized to
degree \(b-L\), times exactly

\[
\prod_{i=1}^r\binom{b-d_i}{L}.
\tag{LP.17}
\]

For \(d_i\le\nu_2\le b-L\), these are nonzero integers,
and division by their product is an explicit inverse on this
polynomial subspace. Thus no nonzero highest vector in the
specified component can be killed. Equivariance then proves
injectivity on its entire multiplicity space. The flag-minor
generation and separate homogenization proof are given in full
in R-018 (R018.5)–(R018.13); their displayed formulas allow
every \(L\), including the boundary \(b-L=\nu_2\).

After \(\delta\), each first-factor type \(\nu\) for
a source type \(\lambda\) satisfies \(\nu_2\le
\lambda_2\le t\), by Pieri. By (LP.10), \(t\le m=b-L\),
so (LP.17) makes \(T_{r,L,b}\) injective on all these
components. Multiplication is a left inverse of \(\delta\).
Consequently their composite is injective on the complete
second-row band. Together with §2 this proves (LP.12).

## 4. Iteration from the two exact bases

For (LP.2), use \(L=t\) at every step, including steps
with \(t>r\). The membership proof in §2 still applies:
\(L=t\ge r\) gives \(p\ge L+1>r\) and full derivative
injectivity. All other formulas are unchanged. Starting at
outer degree \(a\) and inner degree \(b\), the lower
inner degree at outer degree \(s\) is

\[
b_s=b-t(a-s),\qquad b_2\ge t.
\tag{LP.18}
\]

At each step \(s\ge3\), \(b_s-t=b_{s-1}\ge t\ge1\).
Thus every restriction (LP.12) is injective. The actual
degree-two canonical map \(h_{b_2,2}\) is surjective for
every \(b_2\ge1\), by Sra's Theorem 1.3 at \(a=2\),
whose bound is \((2-1)^2=1\). Its transpose has zero
kernel \(\mathcal K_{2,b_2}\). Iterating the actual
injections therefore gives \(\mathcal K_{a,b}^{\le t}=0\),
proving (LP.2) through the scalar-one adjoint pairing.

For (LP.4), write \(s=b-C_{a,t}\ge B_t\ge t\), and
set

\[
b_q=s+\sum_{r=5}^{q-1}\min\{r,t\}
\qquad(5\le q\le a).
\tag{LP.19}
\]

At the step from \(q=r+1\) to \(r\), take
\(L=\min\{r,t\}\). Then \(b_{r+1}-L=b_r\ge s\ge t\ge1\),
so all the maps (LP.12) are defined and injective. They compose,
with only tensor-factor permutations, to

\[
\mathcal K_{a,b}^{\le t}(W)\hookrightarrow
\mathcal K_{5,s}^{\le t}(W)\otimes
\bigotimes_{r=5}^{a-1}
 \left(\operatorname{Sym}^{r\min(r,t)}W
       \otimes\operatorname{Sym}^{b_{r+1}}W\right).
\tag{LP.20}
\]

The total degree is correct since
\((r+1)b_{r+1}-r b_r=r\min(r,t)+b_{r+1}\).
The precise base vanishing is

\[
\mathcal K_{5,s}^{\le t}=0\qquad(s\ge B_t).
\tag{LP.21}
\]

For \(t=1\), this follows from the identity at \(s=1\),
the complete exact R-031 tables at \(s=2,3,4\), the
eight degree-five kernel labels (all having second row at
least five), and full injectivity for \(s\ge6\).
For \(2\le t\le4\), the same eight labels give the base
at \(s=5\), and every larger degree is injective.
For \(t=5\), use full injectivity at every \(s\ge6\).
For \(t\ge6\), every \(s\ge B_t=t\) lies in that same
full-injectivity range. These are precisely the established
canonical results and primary locators proved and checked in
R-031, including Cheung–Ikenmeyer–Mkrtchyan Theorem 6 and
the complete McKay propagation proof. Thus the codomain in
(LP.20) is zero, proving (LP.4).

All operators are rational and all nonzero scalars are
explicit in (LP.9), (LP.15), (LP.16) and (LP.17). The
arguments over \(\mathbb C\) therefore prove the same
rank statements over every characteristic-zero field.
Zero-dimensional spaces have zero positive-degree targets;
in dimension one the map sends its pure-power basis to the
corresponding pure-power basis, with scalar one. This also
checks the low-dimensional endpoints directly.

## 5. A literal boundary check for the injectivity requirement

The bound \(b-L\ge t\) in (LP.10) is used by the
explicit inverse (LP.17). The following actual example
checks that it cannot simply be deleted from (LP.12).
Take four slots in a four-dimensional space, let
\(D=\det(v_1,v_2,v_3,v_4)\), let \(x_i\) be their first
coordinates, and set

\[
F=D^2x_1x_2x_3x_4.
\tag{LP.22}
\]

It is a nonzero slot-symmetric highest polynomial of
separate degree three and weight \((6,2,2,2)\).
The target of \(h_{4,3}\) has at most three rows by
its inclusion in \((\operatorname{Sym}^4W)^{\otimes3}\)
and Pieri, so this vector belongs to \(\mathcal K_{4,3}\).
For \(r=3,L=t=2,b=3\), substitute
\(v_i\mapsto v_i+z_i x\) in the first three slots.
The determinant is linear in \(z_1,z_2,z_3\) jointly,
because any term using the same common column twice
vanishes. Its square has total \(z\)-degree at most two,
and the first-coordinate product contributes at most three.
Thus the coefficient of \(z_1^2z_2^2z_3^2\) is zero.
The composite kills the nonzero vector (LP.22) here,
where \(b-L=1<t\). This validates the role of the stated
range and does not assert a classification outside it.

## Primary inputs and proof scope

The annihilator diagonal and normalized tensor transpose
are written in R-024 and R-031. The directional-kernel
calculation (LP.6)–(LP.9) and its spectator restriction are
proved here. The common-polarization input is the complete
arbitrary-power R-018 (R018.1)–(R018.13), reread for this
proof. The external degree-two input is Suvrit Sra,
*The q-Foulkes problem III: On Foulkes’ conjecture with a
graded inner factor*, v1, Theorem 1.3, p.2 and proof §2.2:
<https://suvrit.github.io/papers/qfoulkes3/qfoulkes3-v1.pdf>.
The degree-five inputs and their exact source maps are
Cheung–Ikenmeyer–Mkrtchyan, Theorem 6,
<https://arxiv.org/pdf/1509.03944>, and Ikenmeyer,
Theorem 1.3 and full §§2–6 propagation proof,
<https://arxiv.org/pdf/1509.04957>.
Their computational and source-review scopes are recorded
separately in R-031 and the check ledger.


# The complete second-row-two canonical rank law

## R-035. An exact determinant-square scalar

Work in characteristic zero. All canonical grid maps use normalized
tensor symmetrization, so the transpose identity is the scalar-one
identity of R-031 (OF.6). Let \(a,n\ge2\), \(1\le j\le a-1\),
and put \(\lambda_j=(an-2j,2^j)\). The exact target and image
multiplicities are

\[
\boxed{
a_{a,n}^{\lambda_j}=1,\qquad
\operatorname{mult}_{\lambda_j}\operatorname{im}h_{n,a}
=\begin{cases}1,&j<n,\\0,&j\ge n.\end{cases}}
\tag{SR.1}
\]

The first assertion is R-033. Below we prove the second by an
explicit nonzero scalar for the actual map, and prove that these
are all the nonzero components with second row two. In particular,

\[
\boxed{
a\ge2,\quad n\ge a:\quad h_{n,a}\text{ reaches the entire
target second-row band }\lambda_2\le2.}
\tag{SR.2}
\]

For \(2\le n<a\), the cokernel in this band is exactly

\[
\boxed{
\bigoplus_{j=n}^{a-1} S_{(an-2j,2^j)}V,}
\tag{SR.3}
\]

each summand once. All statements include the natural convention
that an overly long Schur functor vanishes in the given dimension.
Thus (SR.2) holds in every dimension. The missing summands in
(SR.3) are present whenever their lengths fit. No historical
novelty claim is made.

## 1. The actual invariant polynomial and normalized Chow evaluation

Use \(a\) vector slots with first \(j+1\) coordinates
\((x_i,y_{i1},\ldots,y_{ij})\). Write \(u=\prod_{i=1}^a x_i\),
and let \(X_I\) be the \((j+1)\times(j+1)\) matrix in the
slots \(I\), with these columns in that order. Define

\[
F_{a,n,j}
=u^{n-2}\sum_{\substack{I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,a\}\\|I|=j+1}}
 \left(\prod_{i\notin I}x_i\right)^2\det(X_I)^2.
\tag{SR.4}
\]

Every slot has degree \(n\). The polynomial is slot-symmetric,
because determinants are squared. Its coordinate weight is
\((an-2j,2^j)\): the lower \(j\) coordinates each have
degree two and total degree is \(an\). The initial-column
determinants and first coordinates are fixed by the relevant
highest-weight unipotent group, so this is a highest polynomial.
It is nonzero: take all \(x_i=1\), and take the lower
coordinate vectors in the slots to include \(0,e_1,\ldots,e_j\),
with all remaining lower vectors zero. At least one determinant
in (SR.4) is nonzero, and the sum of real squares is positive.
Thus (SR.4) spans the highest multiplicity line proved in R-033.

Let \(\mathcal A_F\) be the symmetric \(a\)-linear form on
\(\operatorname{Sym}^nV\) determined by
\(\mathcal A_F(v_1^n,\ldots,v_a^n)=F(v_1,\ldots,v_a)\).
For \(n\) vectors \(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_n\), set
\(Q=\ell_1\cdots\ell_n\). The normalized canonical map
satisfies exactly

\[
(h_{a,n}F)(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_n)
=\mathcal A_F(Q,\ldots,Q).
\tag{SR.5}
\]

To verify the normalization, represent the evaluation tensor as
the normalized symmetric product of
\(\ell_1^a,\ldots,\ell_n^a\). After transposing the grid,
every one of its \(a\) rows contains
\(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_n\). Normalized inner symmetrization
turns each row into \(Q\), and all rows are identical, so the
outer symmetrization leaves \(Q^a\). Thus the opposite grid
map sends this evaluation tensor exactly to \(Q^a\).
The perfect normalized tensor pairing and its scalar-one adjoint
identity give (SR.5), without any additional factorial.

For a monomial in one slot, the corresponding pairing is

\[
\left\langle x^{n-|\beta|}y^\beta,
e_0^{n-|\beta|}e^\beta\right\rangle
=\frac{(n-|\beta|)!\prod_p\beta_p!}{n!}.
\tag{SR.6}
\]

This follows by counting the permutations matching the letters
in normalized symmetric tensors. We retain this normalization
in the next calculation.

## 2. Evaluation by the exact quadratic pairing matrix

First take \(\ell_k=(1,v_k)\), \(v_k\in\mathbb Q^j\),
and write

\[
s=\sum_{k=1}^n v_k,\qquad
T=\sum_{k=1}^n v_kv_k^t,\qquad
\mu=\frac{s}{n},\qquad
M=\frac{ss^t-T}{n(n-1)}.
\tag{SR.7}
\]

Define the linear functional on quadratics
\(L_Q(q)=\langle x^{n-2}q,Q\rangle\). Expanding
\(Q=\prod_k(e_0+\sum_p(v_k)_pe_p)\) and using (SR.6)
gives exactly

\[
L_Q(x^2)=1,\qquad L_Q(xy_p)=\mu_p,\qquad
L_Q(y_py_q)=M_{pq}.
\tag{SR.8}
\]

For \(p\ne q\), the numerator of the last expression is
\(\sum_{k\ne l}(v_k)_p(v_l)_q\) and its normalization is
\(1/(n(n-1))\). For \(p=q\), the polynomial coefficient
sums over \(k<l\), and the pairing factor is
\(2/(n(n-1))\), giving the identical matrix formula. Thus
both repeated and distinct coordinate indices are accounted for.
The matrix of this quadratic functional is

\[
B=\begin{pmatrix}1&\mu^t\\\mu&M\end{pmatrix},\qquad
\det B=\det(M-\mu\mu^t).
\tag{SR.9}
\]

For one subset \(I\) in (SR.4), expand the determinant
square into its two permutation sums. Applying the independent
slot functionals \(L_Q\) gives

\[
\sum_{\sigma,\tau\in S_{j+1}}
 \operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\operatorname{sgn}(\tau)
 \prod_{i=1}^{j+1}B_{\sigma(i),\tau(i)}
=(j+1)!\det B.
\tag{SR.10}
\]

For each fixed \(\sigma\), reindexing the product converts
the sum over \(\tau\) into the determinant of \(B\).
Every outside slot in (SR.4) contributes \(L_Q(x^2)=1\).
There are \(\binom a{j+1}\) subsets. Consequently

\[
\mathcal A_{F_{a,n,j}}(Q,\ldots,Q)
=\frac{a!}{(a-j-1)!}\det(M-\mu\mu^t).
\tag{SR.11}
\]

No probabilistic interpretation is needed: (SR.8)–(SR.11)
are identities of rational polynomial functionals on the stated
tensor powers.

The exact matrix simplification is

\[
M-\mu\mu^t
=-\frac1{n(n-1)}\left(T-\frac{ss^t}{n}\right).
\tag{SR.12}
\]

It follows by putting the coefficients of \(ss^t\) over the
denominator \(n^2(n-1)\): their difference is \(1\).
The coefficient of \(T\) is \(-1/(n(n-1))\).
This verifies both the sign and the complete denominator.

## 3. The exact canonical-map scalar

For the \(n\) rows \((1,v_k)\), let \(Z\) denote their
\(n\times(j+1)\) matrix. Cauchy–Binet and its block Gram
matrix give

\[
\begin{aligned}
F_{n,a,j}(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_n)
&=\sum_{|I|=j+1}\det(Z_I)^2
=\det(Z^tZ)\\
&=\det\begin{pmatrix}n&s^t\\s&T\end{pmatrix}
=n\det\left(T-\frac{ss^t}{n}\right).
\end{aligned}
\tag{SR.13}
\]

For \(j+1>n\), the sum is empty and the Gram determinant
is zero, so the same identity holds with both sides zero.
For \(j+1\le n\), this is exactly the polynomial (SR.4)
with \(a,n\) exchanged, evaluated at first coordinates one.
Combining (SR.5), (SR.11), (SR.12) and (SR.13) proves

\[
\boxed{
h_{a,n}F_{a,n,j}
=(-1)^j\frac{a!}{(a-j-1)!\,n^{j+1}(n-1)^j}
 F_{n,a,j}.}
\tag{SR.14}
\]

Here \(F_{n,a,j}=0\) for \(j\ge n\). The calculation
was on first coordinates one. Every vector with nonzero first
coordinate is a scalar multiple of such a vector. Both sides
have degree \(a\) in each of their \(n\) slots, so homogeneity
proves equality on the dense open set with all first coordinates
nonzero. Both sides are polynomials, proving (SR.14) everywhere.
Thus the equality is an actual morphism identity, including its
normalization, rather than a comparison of multiplicities.

For \(j<n\), the right-hand polynomial is nonzero, by the
same explicit specialization used after (SR.4). One numerical
specialization making the scalar visible takes
\(v_1=e_1,\ldots,v_j=e_j\) and all remaining \(v_k=0\).
Then \(T-ss^t/n=I-\mathbf1\mathbf1^t/n\), whose determinant
is \((n-j)/n\), by its eigenspaces \(\mathbf1\) and
\(\mathbf1^\perp\). Equation (SR.11) becomes the nonzero
rational number

\[
(-1)^j\frac{a!}{(a-j-1)!}
\frac{n-j}{n^{j+1}(n-1)^j}.
\tag{SR.15}
\]

For \(j\ge n\), the target of \(h_{a,n}\) has at most
\(n\) rows, by its inclusion in
\((\operatorname{Sym}^aV)^{\otimes n}\) and successive
Pieri. Thus its entire \(\lambda_j\)-component is zero,
also verified literally in (SR.14). Scalar-one transposition
preserves the rank on each highest multiplicity space. Since
R-033 proves that the target line of \(h_{n,a}\) has
multiplicity one, this proves the full rank assertion (SR.1).

## 4. The full second-row band, including all one-box tails

Let \(\lambda\vdash an\), \(\lambda_2\le2\), and
\(\ell(\lambda)\le a\). The exact stable flag chart applies
because \(n\ge2\). Write its tail as
\(\nu=(2^j,1^k)\), where \(j+k\le a-1\). The chart
and its ordinary permutation action give the actual equality

\[
a_{a,n}^{\lambda}=\dim(S_\nu\mathfrak h_a)^{S_a}.
\tag{SR.16}
\]

For \(k>0\), put \(p=j+k\), \(q=j\). The weight
\((p,q)\) version of the same skew Cauchy construction used
in (UT.4) gives the actual Young-component embedding

\[
S_{(2^j,1^k)}\mathfrak h_a
\hookrightarrow\Lambda^{j+k}\mathfrak h_a
                    \otimes\Lambda^j\mathfrak h_a.
\tag{SR.17}
\]

Indeed the skew Cauchy summand with two-dimensional factor
\(S_{(j+k,j)}\mathbb Q^2\) has the required weight line
\((p,q)\); the other factor is its transposed shape
\((2^j,1^k)\). The inclusion is obtained by the same
column-antisymmetrized rational Young projector, so it is
\(S_a\)-equivariant. By (UT.8) and its explicit invariant
self-dualities, the right-hand invariant space is
\(\operatorname{Hom}_{S_a}([a-j-k,1^{j+k}],[a-j,1^j])\).
These are distinct irreducible hooks, including \(j=0\).
The homomorphism space is zero. The injective map (SR.17)
therefore proves zero invariants in (SR.16).

For \(k=0,j>0\), (UT.11) gives one invariant. For
\(j=k=0\), the tail is empty and the top-row component is
one-dimensional in multiplicity; the canonical map sends its
pure-power generator to itself with scalar one. Finally,
\(\ell(\lambda)>a\) gives zero target by the same
successive-Pieri bound. These exhaust every partition in the
stated second-row band. Together with (SR.1), they prove
(SR.2) and (SR.3).

The case \(n=1\), excluded only to keep the denominators in
(SR.7) uniform, is the actual identity
\(\operatorname{Sym}^aV\to\operatorname{Sym}^aV\).
The case \(a=1\) is the corresponding identity. Thus all
degree-one endpoints are also determined explicitly.

## Scope and exact transport

The normalized grid/pairing identities are R-031 (OF.6), the
unit multiplicity and hook maps are R-033, and the flag map is
T-032 with its explicit substitution and dense inverse. Every
operator, invariant, pairing scalar and polynomial identity in
(SR.4)–(SR.17) is over \(\mathbb Q\). Base change therefore
gives the same maps and ranks in characteristic zero. For an
associated vector bundle, applying its principal \(GL\)-bundle
functor to these natural tensor maps gives the corresponding
bundle maps; all displayed identities hold in each local
trivialization and hence glue. No identification of a canonical
image with an auxiliary product ideal is used in this proof.


# The complete second-row-three canonical rank law

## R-036. Exact unit components and their actual cubic-minor scalar

Let \(a,n\ge2\). In the whole band \(\lambda\vdash an\),
\(\lambda_2\le3\), the only nonzero target multiplicities in
\(\operatorname{Sym}^a\operatorname{Sym}^nV\) are the following,
each with multiplicity one:

\[
\begin{array}{ll}
(an),&\\
(an-2j,2^j),&1\le j\le a-1,\\
(an-2j-3,3,2^j),&n\ge3,\quad0\le j\le a-3.
\end{array}
\tag{CT.1}
\]

As usual, summands longer than \(\dim V\) vanish. The first
component is reached by \(h_{n,a}\) with scalar one. The second
is reached exactly for \(j<n\), by R-035. The third has the
actual image multiplicity

\[
\boxed{
\operatorname{mult}_{(an-2j-3,3,2^j)}\operatorname{im}h_{n,a}
=\begin{cases}1,&j\le n-3,\\0,&j\ge n-2,
\end{cases}
\quad a,n\ge3,\quad0\le j\le a-3.}
\tag{CT.2}
\]

Consequently \(h_{n,a}\) is surjective on the entire second-row
band \(\lambda_2\le3\) for all \(n\ge a\ge2\). For
\(a,n\ge3\), its cokernel in that band is exactly

\[
\boxed{
\bigoplus_{j=n}^{a-1}S_{(an-2j,2^j)}V
\ \oplus\
\bigoplus_{j=n-2}^{a-3}S_{(an-2j-3,3,2^j)}V.}
\tag{CT.3}
\]

Every summand occurs once; a range with lower endpoint above its
upper endpoint is empty. At \(n=2\), the second sum is absent,
and the first sum is precisely R-035's cokernel. These assertions
come from the explicit morphisms proved below. No historical
novelty claim is made.

## 1. An exact invariant-algebra map excluding all other tails

Let \(E=\mathbb Q^a\), \(W=\mathfrak h_a\), and let
\(P:E\to W\) be the rational orthogonal projection (UT.7).
Take a three-dimensional auxiliary space \(T\). We claim the
following actual surjective graded algebra map:

\[
\operatorname{Sym}(\Lambda^2T)\otimes\Lambda(\Lambda^3T)
\twoheadrightarrow\bigl(\Lambda(W\otimes T)\bigr)^{S_a}.
\tag{CT.4}
\]

Here the degree-two generator sends \(t\wedge t'\) to
\(\sum_i(Pe_i\otimes t)\wedge(Pe_i\otimes t')\), and the
degree-three generator is the corresponding sum of three factors
in the same row. The first generators are even and the last is
odd, so these formulas define the displayed graded-commutative
algebra morphism. It is \(GL(T)\)-equivariant.

To prove surjectivity, first work in \(\Lambda(E\otimes T)\),
using a basis of three Grassmann letters per row. For a nonempty
subset \(S\subseteq\{1,2,3\}\), define the row power sum
\(p_S\) by summing the product of its letters over all rows.
For an ordered list \(S_1,\ldots,S_l\), let
\(A(S_1,\ldots,S_l)\) be the sum of their products over
injective assignments to rows, retaining the displayed factor
order. Every nonzero invariant monomial-orbit sum is a nonzero
rational multiple of one of these \(A\)'s. An orbit with two
identical odd row types has zero average, since swapping those
rows changes its sign. All other stabilizer factors are positive
factorials after fixing the displayed ordering.

Expand \(p_{S_1}\cdots p_{S_l}\) and group its row assignments
by their equality partition \(\pi\) of \(\{1,\ldots,l\}\).
The discrete partition contributes exactly \(A(S_1,\ldots,S_l)\).
Every other partition contributes a signed \(A\) with fewer
occupied rows: merge the subsets inside each block, use zero when
a Grassmann letter repeats, and use the literal exterior-product
sign when ordering the remaining letters and blocks. This is an
exact expansion, because equality partitions partition all row
assignments. Induction on \(l\) proves that the \(p_S\)'s
generate every invariant. Thus this argument supplies the algebra
maps and their spanning proof, including every finite row count.

The exterior map induced by \(P\) is an equivariant surjection.
Its restriction on invariants is onto: the equivariant inclusion
\(W\hookrightarrow E\) supplies a lift, or equivalently one
can apply the rational Reynolds projector. After projection,
the singleton sums vanish because \(\sum_iPe_i=0\).
The remaining sums are exactly the generators of (CT.4), proving
that assertion.

In dimension three,
\(\Lambda^2T\simeq(\det T)\otimes T^*\) by exterior
contraction. Therefore the domain of (CT.4) has precisely the
irreducible \(GL(T)\)-summands

\[
S_{(p,p,0)}T\quad\text{and}\quad S_{(p+1,p+1,1)}T,
\qquad p\ge0,
\tag{CT.5}
\]

each once. This follows from the actual determinant-contraction
map and the symmetric power of the standard dual representation.
The rational skew Cauchy Young projectors identify the target of
(CT.4) with

\[
\bigoplus_{\nu_1\le3}
(S_\nu W)^{S_a}\otimes S_{\nu^t}T.
\tag{CT.6}
\]

Thus every invariant here has multiplicity at most one, and the
only possible nonempty tails are \((2^j)\) and \((3,2^j)\).
This conclusion is a consequence of the explicit surjection and
the commuting Young decompositions. R-033 determines the first
family. For the second, length gives zero at \(j\ge a-1\).
At \(j=a-2\), \(\dim W=a-1=j+1\), and exterior-column
multiplication gives the actual isomorphism

\[
S_{(3,2^{a-2})}W\simeq(\det W)^2\otimes W.
\tag{CT.7}
\]

The determinant-square character is trivial on \(S_a\), while
\(W\) has no invariants. This proves zero also at this endpoint.
The following explicit polynomial proves nonvanishing for all
remaining \(j\).

## 2. The centered cubic-minor polynomial

Put \(s=j+1\), so \(a\ge s+2\). For \(a\) vectors
\(w_i\in\mathbb Q^s\), set

\[
\bar w=\frac1a\sum_iw_i,\quad z_i=w_i-\bar w,\quad
S=\sum_i z_i z_i^t,\qquad
f_a(w)=\sum_i(z_i)_1\,z_i^t\operatorname{adj}(S)z_i.
\tag{CT.8}
\]

This is slot-symmetric and translation invariant. Under
\(w_i\mapsto g w_i\), its vector-valued version transforms
by \((\det g)^2g\), because
\(\operatorname{adj}(gSg^t)=(\det g)^2g^{-t}\operatorname{adj}(S)g^{-1}\).
This identity follows first for invertible \(S\) and then as
a polynomial identity. The first component is consequently the
highest vector of weight \((3,2^{s-1})\) in its lower
coordinates. Equivalently, the raising operators
\(\sum_i(w_i)_p\partial_{(w_i)_q}\), \(p<q\), kill
this component, and its diagonal degrees are \(3,2,\ldots,2\).

We need its exact degree in each slot. Let \(R\) be the matrix
whose rows are \(r_i=(1,w_i^t)\). For a subset \(I\) of
size \(s+1\), write \(R_I\) for its square row minor. The
following polynomial identity provides that degree bound:

\[
\boxed{
H_a(w):=a^2f_a(w)=
\sum_{|I|=s+1}
\left((a-s-1)\sum_{i\in I}(w_i)_1
      -(s+1)\sum_{i\notin I}(w_i)_1\right)\det(R_I)^2.}
\tag{CT.9}
\]

For a direct verification, center the last \(s\) columns by
a determinant-one column matrix. It sends \(R^tR\) to
\(\operatorname{diag}(a,S)\). The adjugate congruence then
gives
\(r_i\operatorname{adj}(R^tR)r_i^t=\det S+a z_i^t\operatorname{adj}(S)z_i\).
Use the weighted Gram matrix
\(R^t\operatorname{diag}(t_1,\ldots,t_a)R\), differentiate
Cauchy–Binet with respect to \(t_i\), and set all \(t_l=1\).
This same adjugate expression equals
\(\sum_{I\ni i}\det(R_I)^2\), since exactly those minors
carry that row weight. Multiply by \((z_i)_1\), sum over
\(i\), and use \(\sum_i z_i=0\). The result is
\(a f_a=\sum_I(\sum_{i\in I}(z_i)_1)\det(R_I)^2\).
Substitute \(z_i=w_i-\bar w\) and multiply by \(a\)
to obtain (CT.9), with both coefficients as displayed.
The argument is polynomial and remains valid at singular Gram
matrices. Formula (CT.9) has degree at most three in each slot.

The polynomial is nonzero for every \(a\ge s+2\). Take
the centered vectors

\[
e_1,e_1,e_2,\ldots,e_s,
-2e_1-e_2-\cdots-e_s,
\quad\text{and }a-s-2\text{ zero vectors}.
\tag{CT.10}
\]

Put \(D=\operatorname{diag}(2,1,\ldots,1)\) and
\(v=(2,1,\ldots,1)^t\). Then \(S=D+vv^t\),
\(\det S=2(s+2)\), and
\(S^{-1}=D^{-1}-D^{-1}vv^tD^{-1}/(s+2)\), as verified
by multiplication. The adjugate quadratic values on \(e_1\),
on each other \(e_i\), and on \(v\) are respectively
\(s,2(s+1),2(s+1)\). Hence

\[
f_a=-2(s+2)\ne0.
\tag{CT.11}
\]

For \(n\ge3\), use slots \((x_i,y_i)\), put
\(u=\prod_i x_i\), and define the highest polynomial

\[
G_{a,n,s}=u^nH_a(y_1/x_1,\ldots,y_a/x_a).
\tag{CT.12}
\]

This expression is polynomial. Its fully polynomial formula,
with \(X_I\) the minor of rows \((x_i,y_i)\), is

\[
\begin{split}
G_{a,n,s}=u^{n-3}\sum_{|I|=s+1}
\left(\prod_{i\notin I}x_i\right)^2\det(X_I)^2
\biggl(& (a-s-1)\sum_{i\in I}(y_i)_1\prod_{l\ne i}x_l\\
&-(s+1)\sum_{i\notin I}(y_i)_1\prod_{l\ne i}x_l\biggr).
\end{split}
\tag{CT.13}
\]

Each slot has degree \(n\), and the weight is
\((an-2s-1,3,2^{s-1})\). The translations in (CT.8)
are exactly the raising substitutions from the first coordinate;
the other raising operators were checked above. Thus this is a
nonzero slot-symmetric highest polynomial. It proves the invariant
line for every \(j=s-1\le a-3\).

The ordinary Cauchy highest-column construction identifies
\(H_a\) with the indicated vector of \(S_{(3,2^{s-1})}W\).
In T-032 (C.11), scaling the first centered column by \(u\)
multiplies it by \(u^3\); multiplication by the chart's
\(u^{n-3}\) is therefore exactly (CT.12). This fixes its
actual flag-component map. T-032's stable chart now proves every multiplicity in
(CT.1) for \(n\ge3\): its balanced module is
\(S_{(\lambda_2,\ldots,\lambda_a)}W\), with the ordinary
permutation action, and (CT.4)–(CT.13) exhaust its invariant
lines. A partition with more than \(a\) rows has zero target,
by inclusion in \((\operatorname{Sym}^nV)^{\otimes a}\)
and successive Pieri.

## 3. The exact inner-degree-two endpoint

At \(n=2\), T-032 still embeds the balanced space in its
tail module, with inverse given by its explicit polynomial
extension criterion. The tail classification (CT.4) therefore
still excludes every other family. For a cubic tail the possible
invariant line would have chart polynomial \(u^{-1}G_{a,3,s}\).
It is not polynomial, as the following actual specialization
proves.

Set \(x_1=0\), \(y_1=e_1\), and set every other \(x_i=1\).
Among the other lower vectors use \(0,e_2,\ldots,e_s\),
with the remaining vectors zero. In (CT.13), a minor subset not
containing row one contributes zero because of its outside
\(x_1^2\). In a subset containing row one, only the linear
summand with \(i=1\) survives. Its coefficient is
\(a-s-1>0\). The surviving sum is a positive multiple of a
sum of real determinant squares, with at least one square
nonzero. Thus \(x_1\) does not divide \(G_{a,3,s}\),
so \(u\) does not divide it. The exact chart criterion proves
that this entire possible invariant line is absent at \(n=2\).
R-035 determines the remaining two-column tails and top row,
which proves (CT.1) also at this endpoint.

## 4. The complete normalized third-moment calculation

We now compute the actual canonical map on (CT.12). Take
\(a\ge s+2\), \(n\ge3\), and \(n\) vectors
\(\ell_k=(1,v_k)\). Set \(Q=\prod_k\ell_k\).
The scalar-one Chow pairing (SR.5) gives

\[
(h_{a,n}G_{a,n,s})(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_n)
=\mathcal A_{G_{a,n,s}}(Q,\ldots,Q).
\tag{CT.14}
\]

The one-slot functional
\(L_Q(q)=\langle x^{n-3}q,Q\rangle\) on cubics is also
applied to a lower-coordinate polynomial of degree \(d\le3\)
by multiplying it by \(x^{3-d}\). It has
degree-\(d\) lower-coordinate tensor, for \(0\le d\le3\),

\[
\frac1{n(n-1)\cdots(n-d+1)}
\sum_{k_1,\ldots,k_d\text{ distinct}}
v_{k_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{k_d}.
\tag{CT.15}
\]

The expression is symmetric. Its evaluation on coordinate
monomials follows from the exact multinomial pairing (SR.6);
in particular it includes all repeated coordinate factors.
Translation invariance of (CT.9) allows all \(v_k\) to be
replaced by \(v_k-\frac1n\sum_l v_l\). We therefore carry
out the calculation with \(\sum_kv_k=0\). Then the first
moment is zero and the next two moments are

\[
C_2=-\frac{S_2}{n(n-1)},\qquad
C_3=\frac{2S_3}{n(n-1)(n-2)},\qquad
S_2=\sum_kv_kv_k^t,\quad S_3=\sum_kv_k^{\otimes3}.
\tag{CT.16}
\]

The first identity subtracts the repeated indices from
\((\sum v_k)^{\otimes2}=0\). For the second, the three
patterns with exactly two equal indices each sum to \(-S_3\);
the all-equal pattern is \(S_3\). Subtracting them from
the zero full tensor gives the distinct-index sum \(2S_3\).
This proves every coefficient in (CT.16).

We compute the formal independent-slot evaluation of (CT.9)
with these moments. The outside linear terms have zero evaluation.
For one minor subset of size \(s+1\), the quadratic matrix
is \(B=\operatorname{diag}(1,C_2)\). Put
\(B_1=L_Q(w_1\,r r^t)\), with \(r=(1,w^t)\).
The lower block of \(B_1\) is the slice \((C_3)_{1pq}\),
and its upper left entry is zero. Differentiating the exact
two-permutation identity (SR.10) gives

\[
L_Q^{\otimes(s+1)}
\left(\sum_{i=1}^{s+1}(w_i)_1\det(R_I)^2\right)
=(s+1)!\operatorname{tr}(\operatorname{adj}(B)B_1)
=(s+1)!\sum_{p,q}(\operatorname{adj}C_2)_{pq}(C_3)_{1pq}.
\tag{CT.17}
\]

The differentiation merely chooses the one row with the extra
linear factor in each determinant-product monomial. The block
adjugate calculation is polynomial, so no nonsingularity
assumption on the moments is used. There are
\(\binom a{s+1}\) minor subsets, and their inside coefficient
is \(a-s-1\). Hence

\[
\mathcal A_{G_{a,n,s}}(Q,\ldots,Q)
=\frac{a!}{(a-s-2)!}
\sum_{p,q}(\operatorname{adj}C_2)_{pq}(C_3)_{1pq}.
\tag{CT.18}
\]

Adjugation has degree \(s-1\). Inserting (CT.16) converts
the last contraction into

\[
\frac{2(-1)^{s-1}}{n^s(n-1)^s(n-2)}
\sum_k(v_k)_1v_k^t\operatorname{adj}(S_2)v_k
=\frac{2(-1)^{s-1}}{n^s(n-1)^s(n-2)}f_n(v).
\tag{CT.19}
\]

By (CT.9), \(H_n=n^2f_n\), also when the minor sum is
identically zero. Combining the actual maps proves the exact
scalar identity

\[
\boxed{
h_{a,n}G_{a,n,s}
=\frac{2(-1)^{s-1}a!}
{(a-s-2)!\,n^{s+2}(n-1)^s(n-2)}\,G_{n,a,s}.}
\tag{CT.20}
\]

For \(n\le s+1\), define the right-hand generator by the
same formula (CT.13). It is identically zero: for \(n<s+1\)
the subset sum is empty, while at \(n=s+1\) its inside
coefficient and its outside sum both vanish. At \(n\ge s+2\),
(CT.10)–(CT.11) prove it is nonzero. The scalar in (CT.20)
is always nonzero in its stated domain.

The calculation allowed an arbitrary mean to be removed by the
literal translation symmetry, so it proves equality for all
vectors with first coordinate one. Homogeneity in the \(n\)
slots extends it to the dense open set of nonzero first
coordinates, and polynomiality extends it everywhere. Thus
(CT.20) is an identity of the actual canonical morphisms.

## 5. Rank, endpoints, and exact transport

The multiplicity line of the source in (CT.20) is unique by
(CT.1). The target generator is nonzero exactly when
\(n\ge s+2\). Transposing the normalized grid map preserves
rank on each multiplicity space, so (CT.20) proves (CT.2) with
\(j=s-1\). For \(n\le s+1\), (CT.4)–(CT.7) also
give zero multiplicity on the opposite side; the literal zero
in (CT.20) retains the exact map at that endpoint.

Together with the determinant-square scalar of R-035 and the
complete exclusions in (CT.4), this proves every term of
(CT.3) and full surjectivity in the stated \(n\ge a\) band.
At degree one the canonical map is the actual symmetric-power
identity, as in R-035. At \(a=2\), there are no cubic-tail
components; R-035 handles the full band. Thus no endpoint is
obtained by substituting into a zero denominator.

All constructions use rational tensor maps, Reynolds and Young
projectors, exterior multiplication, coefficient extraction and
polynomial identities. Their exact associated-bundle transport
is the frame-torsor construction recorded for R-033–R-035; the
weight extraction is the diagonal coaction projector and the
canonical maps are the same normalized tensor morphisms in
every trivialization. The finite checks are recorded separately
from this full parameter proof. No input-dependent numerical
rank assumption occurs in the argument.

The precise representation-to-bundle map is
\(M\mapsto\mathscr F(E)\times_{GL(V)}M\), where
\(\mathscr F(E)\) is the frame torsor of a finite locally
free module \(E\) on a \(\mathbb Q\)-scheme. The same
formula sends every equivariant arrow in this proof to its
associated-bundle arrow. The rational Young and Reynolds
idempotents give actual direct-summand subbundles; hence their
kernels, images and rank statements are the local constant
matrices proved above and glue on overlaps. On exact
Grothendieck groups this is the frame-torsor morphism in
**SGA 6, Exposé VI, Theorem 3.3**, with its stated category
of bounded-rank locally free modules on a commutatively ringed
topos. **SGA 6 V, Proposition 4.2 and Definition 4.4** give
the evaluation of the free \(\lambda\)-ring, and
**V, Proposition 4.8 and Corollary 4.9** give its finite-rank
quotient. These exact statements and the frame proof were read
in the saved French mathematical transcription; this does not
claim inspection of an original SGA scan.

The coaction and exact diagonal weight projectors are those of
**SGA 3 I, §4.5 and Propositions 4.7.2–4.7.3**. The
T-032 chart uses the literal localization at \(u\). In its
projective flag presentation, the affine degree-zero localization
charts are **EGA II 2.4.1–2.4.2, p.28**; its graded-module
sheafification and exactness are **II 2.5.2 and 2.5.4, p.31**.
These EGA/SGA3 locators and their scope were independently checked
by the archive agent and are recorded in its source notes.
For the supplied archive **cote 133/028**, the actual map from
tensor words to Young cosets, followed by the torus-weight
extraction and Schur filtration, is the complete integral
construction A-012 (A12.2)–(A12.4). Applying its rational
projector splittings gives precisely the tensor/Schur classes
used here. This specifies the archive and Grothendieck transport
through actual morphisms.

## 6. Executed independent finite checks

The script `verify_second_row_three_rank_law.py` expands the
product of the input linear forms and both determinant permutation
sums, and pairs every monomial using its exact multinomial
denominator. Its 40 cases cover \(3\le a,n\le6\) and every
\(1\le s\le a-2\). The first coordinates are nonunit integers.
Every literal pairing agrees with (CT.20), including the sampled
zero endpoints \(n\le s+1\), and every asserted nonzero case
is nonzero. This calculation does not call the moment formulas
or a canonical-rank routine. The complete receipt is
`SECOND_ROW_THREE_CANONICAL_SCALAR_CHECK.tsv`.

The same script independently expands the plethysms in power sums
and uses the Murnaghan–Nakayama rule for all valid second-row-at-most-
three shapes at \(2\le a\le6,\ 2\le n\le4\). All 340
target coefficients and all 340 source coefficients agree with
the unit/zero classification, including the inner-degree-two
extension endpoint. The receipt is
`SECOND_ROW_THREE_BAND_MN_CHECK.tsv`. These finite comparisons
are checks of the full proof, and the actual canonical ranks
are established by the literal scalar identity (CT.20).


# Explicit canonical preimages for every even tail

## R-037. A uniform actual nonvanishing family

Let \(a\ge2\), let \(\rho\ne\varnothing\) be a partition
with \(\ell(\rho)\le a-1\), and put
\(d=|\rho|\), \(q=\rho_1\). For every integer
\(n\ge d+q\), and every vector space with
\(\dim V\ge\ell(\rho)+1\), set

\[
\lambda=(an-2d,2\rho_1,2\rho_2,\ldots).
\tag{EP.1}
\]

Then

\[
\boxed{\operatorname{mult}_{\lambda}\operatorname{im}h_{n,a}\ge1.}
\tag{EP.2}
\]

The maps below construct both a nonzero highest image vector and
its explicit preimage. This is a nonvanishing assertion; no
equality with the whole target multiplicity is asserted. No
historical novelty claim is made.

## 1. The exact graded multiplication morphism

For a vector space \(V\), the product map

\[
m_a:V^a\longrightarrow\operatorname{Sym}^aV,
\qquad(v_1,\ldots,v_a)\longmapsto v_1\cdots v_a
\tag{EP.3}
\]

is polynomial and invariant under slot permutations. Pullback
of polynomial functions gives the actual algebra homomorphism

\[
\Phi_a=m_a^*:
