## 4. Exact finite-row relations

At \(a=m+2=k+1\), every subset is \(I=[a]\setminus\{i\}\).
Centering gives
\(T_{I,p}=-z_{ip}\) and \(U_{I,pq}=S_{pq}-z_{ip}z_{iq}\).
The weight in (ME.8) becomes
\(-(S_{11}z_{i2}-S_{12}z_{i1})\).
The right side of (ME.7), divided by \(a\), uses exactly
\(1/a\) times that weight. Hence
\[
\Phi_2=(a-1)\Phi_1/a.
\tag{ME.14}
\]
The first row of (ME.10) is nonzero at \(l=1\), and the
formal \(F_1,F_2\) are independent, so \(\Phi_1\ne0\).
The invariant dimension is one.

At \(a=m+1\), the only subset is the full set and its
centered first sums are zero. Equations (ME.6)–(ME.8)
give both \(\Phi_j=0\).
At \(a\le m\), their subset sums are empty and again
both vanish. Their proved spanning gives zero dimension.
The invariant dimension at every row count is therefore
exactly \(s_a\). Since all vectors extend for \(n\ge4\),
dehomogenization and (ME.9) prove the target formula in (ME.2).

## 5. The split-form matrix and actual ranks

Let
\[
u_n=\frac{n(n-1)}{(n-2)(n-3)},\qquad
\mathcal H_{n,m}=
\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\(m+1)u_n&-6u_n\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The exact centered split-form moments give
\[
\begin{pmatrix}F_1\\F_2\end{pmatrix}
=\frac{2(-1)^m}{n^{m+1}(n-1)^{m+1}(n-2)}
\mathcal H_{n,m}
\begin{pmatrix}\Phi_{1;n}\\\Phi_{2;n}\end{pmatrix}.
\tag{ME.15}
\]
For the first row, each term has \(m\) second moments and
one third moment. For the second row, use the fourth-moment
numerators
\[
D_{11}^0:\ S_{11}S+2(Se_1)(Se_1)^t-6D_{11},
\]
\[
D_{12}^0:\ S_{12}S+(Se_1)(Se_2)^t+(Se_2)(Se_1)^t-6D_{12}.
\]
The mixed determinant satisfies
\(\mathcal B_S(S,C_p)=(m-1)f_p\).
The two rank-one parts add \(2(S_{11}f_2-S_{12}f_1)\);
their \(-2\det(S)C_{112}\) terms cancel.
The resulting numerator is
\((m+1)\Phi_1-6\Phi_2\).
Its denominator ratio to the first row is
\(N_2^2/N_4=u_n\).
This verifies every coefficient and sign in (ME.15).

The actual normalized canonical identities are
\[
\boxed{
\begin{pmatrix}
h_{a,n}\widehat\Phi_{1;a,n,m}\\
h_{a,n}\widehat\Phi_{2;a,n,m}
\end{pmatrix}
=c_{a,n,m}\mathcal E_{a,m}\mathcal H_{n,m}
\begin{pmatrix}
\widehat\Phi_{1;n,a,m}\\
\widehat\Phi_{2;n,a,m}
\end{pmatrix},\quad
c_{a,n,m}=
\frac{2(-1)^m(a)_{m+1}}
{n^{m+1}(n-1)^{m+1}(n-2)}.}
\tag{ME.16}
\]
This is the scalar-one pairing SR.5–SR.6.
First-coordinate homogeneity extends it from the affine chart
to the polynomial identity everywhere.

For \(a,n\ge m+3\), both bases have size two, and
\(\det\mathcal E\ne0\), \(\det\mathcal H=-6u_n\ne0\).
In column coordinates its matrix is
\(c_{a,n,m}(\mathcal E_{a,m}\mathcal H_{n,m})^t\).
Under \(h_{n,a}\), an actual preimage of target coordinate
column \(v\) has source coordinates
\[
c_{n,a,m}^{-1}
(\mathcal E_{n,m}^{-1})^t(\mathcal H_{a,m}^{-1})^t v.
\tag{ME.17}
\]
All entries are explicit rational functions, or adjugate over
the displayed nonzero determinants.

For mixed one- and two-dimensional blocks, the matrix with
the larger source row count is invertible before restriction
to the finite target span. In the reverse direction, the
nonzero first row of \(\mathcal E\), followed by invertible
\(\mathcal H\), remains nonzero in the two-dimensional target.
Thus their rank is one.
The last unit square is \(a=n=m+2\).
After substituting (ME.14), the scalar of
\(\mathcal E_{a,m}\mathcal H_{n,m}\), omitting the
nonzero common factor \(c\), is
\[
\frac{m^2-3m-2}{(m+2)m(m-1)}.
\tag{ME.18}
\]
Direct substitution gives this fraction.
Its numerator is \(-4,-2,2\) at \(m=2,3,4\), and its
increment from \(m\) to \(m+1\) is \(2m-2>0\).
It is therefore nonzero for every integer \(m\ge2\).
For \(n\le m+1\), both target generators vanish by §4.
This proves rank \(\min(s_a,s_n)\) for \(h_{a,n}\);
scalar-one transposition proves (ME.2).

## 6. The whole cubic extension and its zero canonical image

There is a particularly simple degree-three combination:
\[
\Psi=a\Phi_2-(a-1)\Phi_1.
\]
For a subset \(J\), put
\(J_J(z)=U_{J,11}T_{J,2}-U_{J,12}T_{J,1}\).
Equations (ME.7)–(ME.8) and the zero total centered first sums
give the exact identity
\[
\boxed{\Psi=\sum_{|I|=m+1}J_{I^c}(z)\,f_I.}
\tag{ME.19}
\]
Indeed (ME.8) minus \(a\Phi_1\) replaces the inside second
sums by minus the outside second sums, and
\(T_{I,p}=-T_{I^c,p}\) supplies the remaining sign.

The weight \(J_J\) depends only linearly on a common translation.
Explicitly, translating by \((M_1,M_2)\) gives
\[
J_J(w-M)=J_J(w)
-|J|(M_2U_{J,11}-M_1U_{J,12})
-M_1T_{J,1}T_{J,2}+M_2T_{J,1}^2.
\]
For a row in \(I\), its occurrence in \(J_{I^c}(z)\)
is only through this common mean, hence is linear.
The minor square adds degree at most two.
For a row outside \(I\), the determinant is independent
of that row and the weight has degree at most three.
Thus \(\Psi\) has row degree at most three.

For \(a\ge m+3\), \(\Psi\ne0\) because the two \(\Phi_j\)'s
are independent. The other direction really has degree four:
the first row of (ME.10) has nonzero coefficient
\((a)_k l/a^2\) on \(F_2\), which has genuine fourth-moment
dependence at fixed second and third moments.
A row-degree-three polynomial has no such dependence under
independent-row evaluation. Therefore \(\Phi_1\) cannot extend
to slot degree three. The full cubic extension is exactly
the line spanned by \(\Psi\).
At \(a=m+2\), (ME.14) makes \(\Psi=0\), and the same
fourth-moment argument excludes the sole invariant line.
At smaller \(a\) there are no invariants.

The actual cubic map is zero. Combining the two rows of
(ME.10) gives
\[
L^{\otimes a}\Psi=-(a)_{m+1}\frac{l(l-1)}a F_1.
\tag{ME.20}
\]
The fourth moments cancel before specialization.
For three split factors, \(F_1\) is a scalar multiple of
\(\Phi_{1;3}\), and this polynomial is zero because
\(3\le m+1\), by §4.
Consequently \(h_{a,3}\widehat\Psi=0\), and transposition
gives the asserted zero rank of \(h_{3,a}\).

For inner degree two, every polynomial highest weight in
\(\operatorname{Sym}^a(\operatorname{Sym}^2V)\) has even
parts: the exact symmetric-matrix LDL chart of QD.11–QD.12
restricts a highest polynomial to a monomial in diagonal
entries, each of torus weight twice a coordinate.
The present weight has a part equal to three, so its
highest space is zero. This proves the remaining target
statement without relying on a candidate polynomial's vanishing.

All these maps are rational and have the same multiplicity
matrices in every declared rank.
Their coordinate-ring and frame-torsor transports are the
actual morphisms R-037 EP.3–EP.5 and R-036 §5.

## 7. Executed checks

The script `verify_four_three_even_tail_block.py` expands the

(ME.11)–(ME.12), and pairs monomials against the actual split
form with exact multinomial denominators. It groups only
literal equal determinant monomials and uses a finite
nilpotent-variable product to sum the row assignments.
It does not call the proposed moment matrix on that side.
An independent fifth-moment extension check confirms the
degree-four cancellation at the smallest endpoint.

Population configurations have the full separately computed
generator rank \(s_n\), with nonunit first coordinates.
The exact matrix checks cover \(m=2,3\), \(n=4,5,6\),
and \((m,n)=(4,5),(4,6),(4,7)\), with three source row
counts beginning at \(m+2\).
The receipt is `FOUR_THREE_EVEN_TAIL_CANONICAL_CHECK.tsv`.
All 78 literal generator pairings pass.

A separate cycle-index/Murnaghan–Nakayama calculation verifies

The receipt is `FOUR_THREE_EVEN_TAIL_MN_CHECK.tsv`.
All 59 target coefficients and all 59 source coefficients pass.

# The complete single-four tail band of the canonical map

## R-044. Full multiplicities for \(\lambda_2\le4,\lambda_3\le3\)

Let \(n\ge a\ge2\), let \(\lambda\vdash an\), and pad its
parts by zeros. Over every field of characteristic zero, the
actual normalized canonical map
\[
h_{n,a}:\operatorname{Sym}^n(\operatorname{Sym}^aV)
\longrightarrow\operatorname{Sym}^a(\operatorname{Sym}^nV)
\]
is surjective on its entire \(\lambda\)-isotypic component whenever
\[
\boxed{\lambda_2\le4,\qquad\lambda_3\le3.}
\tag{SF.1}
\]
This includes every multiplicity in that component.
The assertion is literal for \(\dim V\ge\ell(\lambda)\);
for smaller dimension the component is zero on both sides,
by the column antisymmetrizer defining \(S_\lambda V\).

Here and below the normalized map is the rational tensor
grid permutation followed by the two block symmetrizers.
Its transpose is \(h_{a,n}\) under the exact pure-power
pairings SR.5–SR.6. Every map used in the proof is this map.

The proof joins the previously established moment blocks by
an actual invariant-algebra surjection that exhausts their
support. No historical novelty claim is made. The binary
subcase is the known actual Hermite map, with primary locator
Landsberg, arXiv:1305.7387v3, Theorem 7.21, §7.7, printed p.24;
§7.2 and Proposition 7.6 specify the same regrouping map and
transpose pairing. The explicit fourth-moment matrix R-038
refines that known binary rank statement.

## 1. Exact reduction to the four tail families

The case \(\lambda_2\le3\) is the full statement R-036 CT.1–CT.20,
with the quadratic family supplied by R-035. It remains to
treat \(\lambda_2=4,\lambda_3\le3\). Its tail has the form
\[
\nu=(4,3^p,2^q,1^s),\qquad p,q,s\ge0.
\tag{SF.2}
\]
Let \(E=\mathbb Q^a\), \(W=\mathfrak h_a\), and \(P:E\to W\)
be the sum-zero orthogonal projection.

There is an injective map from the highest space of weight
\((an-|\nu|,\nu)\) to \((S_\nu W)^{S_a}\).
Here is its actual coordinate construction. Write the \(a\)
vector slots as \((x_i,y_i)\), set \(u=\prod_i x_i\), and
dehomogenize a highest polynomial \(F\) by
\[
F(x_i,y_i)=u^n\,f(y_i/x_i).
\tag{SF.3}
\]
On this dense chart the highest equations in the first
coordinate say exactly that \(f\) is invariant under a
common translation of the rows. Hence \(f\) factors through
the linear map \((w_i)\mapsto(w_i-\bar w)\in W\otimes V'\).
The remaining highest equations and torus weight select
the rational Young-projector summand \(S_\nu W\); slot
symmetry selects its \(S_a\)-fixed space. Equality on the
dense chart proves injectivity. Conversely a vector in this
fixed space whose separate row degrees are at most \(n\)
homogenizes by (SF.3) to a polynomial highest vector.
These are the explicit maps used in CT.4 and QE.8–QE.9;
no equality of abstract dimensions is substituted for them.

For \(T=\mathbb Q^4\), the row power sums give the surjective
\(GL(T)\)-equivariant algebra morphism
\[
\mathcal A:=
\operatorname{Sym}(\Lambda^2T\oplus\Lambda^4T)
\otimes\Lambda(\Lambda^3T)
\twoheadrightarrow
\bigl(\Lambda(W\otimes T)\bigr)^{S_a}.
\tag{SF.4}
\]
The degree-\(d\) map sends \(t_1\wedge\cdots\wedge t_d\) to
\(\sum_i(Pe_i\otimes t_1)\wedge\cdots\wedge(Pe_i\otimes t_d)\).
HO.3 proves surjectivity by expanding injective row assignments
in power sums and descending on their equality partitions;
equal odd row types have zero invariant average, and every
remaining stabilizer contributes its explicit nonzero factorial.
Projection \(E\to W\) kills the singleton power sums. Thus
(SF.4) is a finite-row map for every \(a\), including the
small row counts.

The actual skew-Cauchy Young decomposition identifies the
\(S_{\nu^t}T\)-multiplicity of the target of (SF.4) with
\((S_\nu W)^{S_a}\), and
\[
\gamma:=\nu^t=(1+p+q+s,\ 1+p+q,\ 1+p,\ 1).
\tag{SF.5}
\]
The symmetric exterior-square algebra has the proved
Pfaffian/standard-minor decomposition
\[
\operatorname{Sym}(\Lambda^2T)
=\bigoplus_{P\ge Q\ge0}S_{(P,P,Q,Q)}T,
\tag{SF.6}
\]
with each summand once. This is HO.5, retaining its explicit
highest-minor maps and determinant character.

The exterior factors are, by complementary-column contraction,
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
e&\Lambda^e(\Lambda^3T)\\ \hline
0&\mathbb Q\\
1&\Lambda^3T\\
2&(\det T)\otimes\Lambda^2T\\
3&(\det T)^2\otimes T\\
4&(\det T)^3 .
\end{array}
\tag{SF.7}
\]
Because \(\gamma_4=1\), the last two rows of (SF.7) cannot
occur: their factors already contain at least two determinant
columns, and tensoring a polynomial Schur module cannot
remove a column. This last assertion follows directly by
writing \((\det T)^2\otimes S_\eta T=S_{\eta+(2^4)}T\).

We now enumerate the first three rows, with every allowed
Pieri map a column antisymmetrizer followed by the rational
Young projector.

For \(e=0\), equality of the first two and last two parts in
(SF.6), even after a determinant shift, forces \(s=p=0\).
This gives \((4,2^q)\).

For \(e=1\), put the paired shape after the determinant
shift equal to \((P,P,Q,Q)\). A vertical three-strip adds
indicators \(\epsilon_i\in\{0,1\}\), with
\(\sum\epsilon_i=3\). The fourth part gives
\(Q+\epsilon_4=1\).
If \(Q=0,\epsilon_4=1\), partition order forces
\(\epsilon_3=1\), and the remaining indicator is
\(\epsilon_1=1,\epsilon_2=0\). Thus \(p=0,s=1\).
If \(Q=1,\epsilon_4=0\), the other three indicators are all
one. Thus \(p=1,s=0\). These give respectively
\((4,2^q,1)\) and \((4,3,2^q)\).

For \(e=2\), the determinant in (SF.7) and \(\gamma_4=1\)
force the additional determinant exponent and the bottom
paired part to be zero, and the fourth indicator to be
zero. The vertical two-strip either uses rows \(1,2\),
giving \(p=s=0\), or rows \(1,3\), giving \(p=s=1\).
These give \((4,2^q)\), with \(q\ge1\), and
\((4,3,2^q,1)\).

Consequently (SF.4)–(SF.7), followed by the injective map
(SF.3), prove
\[
\boxed{
a_{a,n}^{(an-|\nu|,\nu)}=0
\quad\text{for every single-four tail outside }
\begin{cases}
(4,2^q),\\
(4,3,2^q),\\
(4,2^q,1),\\
(4,3,2^q,1).
\end{cases}}
\tag{SF.8}
\]
This is a proved vanishing statement for all finite \(a,n\)
and all valid partitions. It does not presuppose stable
row counts or a polynomial-extension assertion.

## 2. Exact multiplicity table in the ordered range

For \(n\ge a\ge2\) and \(n\ge4\), the complete target table
for the four tails is
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
\nu&\text{parameter}&a_{a,n}^{(an-|\nu|,\nu)}\\ \hline
(4)&q=0&1+\mathbf1_{a\ge4}\\
(4,2^q)&q\ge1&\min(3,\max(0,a-q-1))\\
(4,3,2^q)&q\ge0&\min(2,\max(0,a-q-3))\\
(4,2^q,1)&q\ge0&\mathbf1_{a\ge q+3}\\
(4,3,2^q,1)&q\ge0&\mathbf1_{a\ge q+5}.
\end{array}
\tag{SF.9}
\]
Rows are retained only when the displayed weight is a
partition. Lengths exceeding \(a\) give zero, also directly
from the tensor-slot Young projection.

The first row is R-038 FM.1–FM.17: at row counts two and
three the two quartics have one relation; at row counts at
least four they are independent. Both extend for \(n\ge4\).
Its actual map is the binary canonical isomorphism.

The second row is R-041 with \(m=q+1\). Its three explicit
Gram/weighted-minor polynomials span the invariant space,
have row degree at most four, and have finite dimension
\(r_a=\min(3,\max(0,a-m))\). The exact canonical rank is
\(\min(r_a,r_n)\), by QE.16–QE.20.
For \(n\ge a\) this equals \(r_a\).
The proof includes the one- and two-dimensional endpoints,
rather than applying the three-dimensional determinant
where it vanishes.

The third row is R-043 with \(m=q+2\). Its two explicit
polynomials have row degree at most four and dimension
\(s_a=\min(2,\max(0,a-m-1))\). Equations ME.10 and ME.15
give the full matrix
\[
c_{a,n,m}\mathcal E_{a,m}\mathcal H_{n,m},
\quad
\det\mathcal E_{a,m}
=\frac{(a-m-1)^2(a-m-2)}{a^4},
\quad
\det\mathcal H_{n,m}
=-\frac{6n(n-1)}{(n-2)(n-3)}.
\tag{SF.10}
\]
Its one-dimensional square has the nonzero scalar in
ME.18, and its mixed endpoints are proved by actual
restriction to the finite span. Thus its rank is
\(\min(s_a,s_n)=s_a\) for \(n\ge a\).
The column-coordinate inverse in ME.17 gives a rational
preimage of every vector in the full two-dimensional target.

For the fourth row, R-039 applies with \(m=q+2\).
Its polynomial \(A_{a,m}\) has row degree at most three,
and the normalized map has the exact identity
\[
h_{a,n}\widehat A_{a,n,m}
=
\frac{2(-1)^{m-1}(a)_{m+1}}
{n^{m+1}(n-1)^m(n-2)}
\,\widehat A_{n,a,m}.
\tag{SF.11}
\]
The nonzero range is \(a,n\ge m+1\), and all smaller
finite-row invariant spaces vanish. In the ordered range,
the target is reached whenever it exists.

For the fifth row, R-040 applies with \(m=q+3\).
Its polynomial \(D_{a,m}\) also has row degree at most
three, and the normalized identity is
\[
h_{a,n}\widehat D_{a,n,m}
=
\frac{4(-1)^{m-2}(a)_{m+2}}
{n^{m+2}(n-1)^m(n-2)^2}
\,\widehat D_{n,a,m}.
\tag{SF.12}
\]
The nonzero range is \(a,n\ge m+2\). The intervening
row count \(a=m+1\) vanishes by the explicit complementary
column pairing in HC.3–HC.4. Again \(n\ge a\) reaches
every nonzero target line.

For (SF.11)–(SF.12), exchanging \(a,n\) and taking the
displayed scalar reciprocal gives an actual preimage under
\(h_{n,a}\), with precisely the same highest polynomial.
For the larger blocks the inverse matrices and their
finite-span restrictions provide the preimages. Equivariance
then gives every vector in the corresponding Schur component:
a highest vector generates its irreducible Schur summand,
and the displayed highest-space maps have full multiplicity
rank. Complete reducibility separates the different copies.

## 3. All small ordered endpoints

For \(n=2\) with \(2\le a\le n\), the total degree is four,
so no partition has second part four. For \(n=3\), only
\(a=3\) can yield such a partition. There are exactly two:
\[
(5,4),\qquad(4,4,1).
\tag{SF.13}
\]
The first has target multiplicity zero: the binary weight
difference counts three partitions of four inside the
three-by-three rectangle and three partitions of three,
giving \(3-3=0\). Equivalently this is the exact quartic
extension relation in FM.5–FM.8.
The second is (SF.11) with \(a=n=3,m=2\); its scalar is
\[
\frac{2(-1)(3)_3}{3^3\,2^2\,1}=-\frac19\ne0.
\tag{SF.14}
\]
Thus it is reached in its entire one-dimensional highest
space. These are all remaining endpoints.

Equations (SF.8)–(SF.14), joined with R-036 for the
second-row-three band, prove (SF.1).

## 4. Polynomial-functor and geometric transport

Every generator, row-centering map, Young projector,
homogenization, grid symmetrizer and inverse used above
is defined over \(\mathbb Q\). The inverse scalars are
nonzero rational numbers in the asserted integer ranges.
Extension of scalars therefore preserves each statement.
The tensor maps are natural in \(V\); their Schur multiplicity
matrices are the displayed matrices in every rank
\(\dim V\ge\ell(\lambda)\).

For coordinate rings, the actual algebra morphism is the
graded Chow pullback in R-037 EP.3–EP.5, whose degree-\(n\)
piece is \(h_{n,a}\) with scalar one by EP.4.
For vector bundles it is the associated-bundle map formed
from these same rational \(GL(V)\)-morphisms on the frame
torsor. R-036 §5 records the exact SGA 6 VI Theorem 3.3,
SGA 6 V §4, SGA 3 I §4 and EGA II §§2.4–2.5 locators and
the representation-to-associated-bundle construction.
No equality in representation \(K_0\) is used to infer
surjectivity: the polynomial maps and inverses above supply it.

## 5. Independent finite verification

The script verify_single_four_tail_band.py enumerates every
single-four tail of length at most \(a-1\) and every valid
first part for \(2\le a\le n\le6\). It computes the target and
source coefficients by literal cycle-index expansion followed
by Murnaghan–Nakayama, without calling the invariant-algebra
decomposition or any canonical moment matrix.
Every target agrees with (SF.8)–(SF.9) and the small endpoint
(SF.13); every source dimension is at least that target
dimension. The receipt is SINGLE_FOUR_TAIL_BAND_MN_CHECK.tsv.
All 122 target coefficients and all 122 source coefficients pass.
This finite coefficient check does not replace the actual
canonical-map proof in §§2–3.



# The first repeated-four canonical block

## R-045. The complete \((4,4)\) tail, with all inner-degree endpoints

Let \(a\ge3\), \(n\ge4\), and \(\dim V\ge3\). Put
\[
\lambda=(an-8,4,4),\qquad r_t=\min(4,\max(0,t-2)).
\]
All these displayed weights are partitions. The exact
target and actual canonical-image multiplicities are
\[
\boxed{
a_{a,n}^{\lambda}=r_a,\qquad
\operatorname{mult}_\lambda\operatorname{im}h_{n,a}
=\min(r_a,r_n).}
\tag{DF.1}
\]
In particular the actual map is surjective in every
\(\lambda\)-multiplicity for all \(n\ge a\ge3\) for which
this weight is a partition.

For inner degree three the valid parameters are \(a\ge4\),
and the complete answer is
\[
\boxed{
a_{a,3}^{(3a-8,4,4)}=1+\mathbf1_{a\ge6},\qquad
\operatorname{mult}_{(3a-8,4,4)}
\operatorname{im}h_{3,a}=1.}
\tag{DF.2}
\]
For inner degree two, \(a\ge6\), the target multiplicity
of \((2a-8,4,4)\) is one and its canonical-image
multiplicity is zero.

The proof supplies the entire four-by-four matrix,
its exact determinant and inverse, all finite-dimensional
relations and endpoint minors, and the complete cubic
extension space. Its maps use the scalar-one tensor
pairing SR.5–SR.6 throughout. No historical novelty
claim is made.

## 1. Four highest polynomials and an invariant upper bound

Write the centered rows as \(z_i=(z_{i1},z_{i2})\), put
\([z_i,z_j]=z_{i1}z_{j2}-z_{i2}z_{j1}\), and define
\[
M_{pq}=\sum_i z_{i1}^p z_{i2}^q,\qquad
S=\begin{pmatrix}M_{20}&M_{11}\\M_{11}&M_{02}\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Use the following ordered generators:
\[
\begin{aligned}
Q_0&=(\det S)^2,\\
Q_1&=\sum_i(z_i^t\operatorname{adj}(S)z_i)^2,\\
Q_2&=\sum_{i,j}[z_i,z_j]^2
                  z_i^t\operatorname{adj}(S)z_j,\\
Q_3&=\sum_{i,j}[z_i,z_j]^4.
\end{aligned}
\tag{DF.3}
\]
Every index sum in the last two lines is ordered.

The determinant identity
\(\det S=\sum_{i<j}[z_i,z_j]^2\) and the exact equality
\[
z_i^t\operatorname{adj}(S)z_j
=\sum_k[z_i,z_k][z_j,z_k]
\]
express each \(Q_j\) as a sum of products of four brackets.
They are consequently \(GL_2\) highest tensors of weight
\((4,4)\), with determinant character \((\det)^4\), and
are invariant under row permutations and common translations.

Set \(z_i=w_i-\bar w\). For any fixed original row \(w_r\),
the leading terms of \(z_i,z_j\) in that row are scalar
multiples of the same vector. Their quadratic bracket
term is zero. Thus each bracket is separately linear
in every original row, and every \(Q_j\) has separate
row degree at most four. Hence
\[
\widehat Q_{j;a,n}
=\left(\prod_i x_i\right)^n Q_j(y_i/x_i)
\tag{DF.4}
\]
is a polynomial highest vector of weight \(\lambda\)
for every \(n\ge4\).

The transpose tail is \((2,2,2,2)\). Apply the exact
surjection (SF.4), whose finite-row proof is HO.3.
In its even exterior-degree part, exterior degree zero
gives three copies: the additional determinant exponents
are \(0,1,2\), with paired shapes respectively
\((2,2,2,2),(1,1,1,1),(0,0,0,0)\).
Exterior degree two is
\((\det T)\otimes\Lambda^2T\); it gives exactly one
additional copy, from \(\Lambda^2T\) and the vertical
strip in rows three and four after the determinant shift.
The strip in rows one and two violates the paired
partition inequality. Exterior degree four has a
determinant-cube factor and cannot have fourth part two.
Odd exterior degrees have odd total degree. The actual
Pieri Young projections therefore prove
\[
\dim(S_{(4,4)}\mathfrak h_a)^{S_a}\le4.
\tag{DF.5}
\]

The moment expressions of (DF.3), useful for checking
every normalization, are
\[
\begin{aligned}
Q_0={}&(M_{20}M_{02}-M_{11}^2)^2,\\
Q_1={}&M_{02}^2M_{40}-4M_{02}M_{11}M_{31}
 +(2M_{20}M_{02}+4M_{11}^2)M_{22}\\
 &-4M_{20}M_{11}M_{13}+M_{20}^2M_{04},\\
Q_2={}&2\{M_{02}(M_{30}M_{12}-M_{21}^2)
 -M_{11}(M_{30}M_{03}-M_{21}M_{12})\\
 &\hspace{20mm}+M_{20}(M_{21}M_{03}-M_{12}^2)\},\\
Q_3={}&2(M_{40}M_{04}-4M_{31}M_{13}+3M_{22}^2).
\end{aligned}
\tag{DF.6}
\]
These follow by expanding the two-by-two bracket, so
they are exact polynomial identities, including factors
two and the ordered-pair convention.

## 2. The injective independent-row map

Let \(A_D=\mathbb Q[w_1,w_2]_{\le D}\), and identify
row-symmetric polynomials in \(a\) rows of separate
degree at most \(D\) with \(\operatorname{Sym}^a A_D\).
The diagonal evaluation morphism is
\[
\mathcal E_a(f)(L)=L^{\otimes a}(f),
\qquad L\in A_D^*.
\tag{DF.7}
\]
It is injective: the rational polarization identity
recovers every symmetric multilinear evaluation from
the diagonal polynomial. Equivalently, its monomial
coefficients are the nonzero multinomial multiples
of the row-orbit coefficients of \(f\).

On the subspace of common-translation-invariant polynomials,
restriction of (DF.7) to
\[
L(1)=1,\qquad L(w_1)=L(w_2)=0
\tag{DF.8}
\]
remains injective. Indeed, for an arbitrary normalized \(L\)
let \(v=(L(w_1),L(w_2))\) and define
\(L_0(p)=L(p(w-v))\). Then \(L_0\) satisfies (DF.8), and
translation invariance gives
\(L^{\otimes a}f=L_0^{\otimes a}f\).
For \(L(1)\ne0\), normalize \(L\) first and multiply by
\(L(1)^a\). This proves vanishing on a dense open set
of all functionals, hence everywhere; polarization then
gives \(f=0\).

The same argument proves the exact filtration identity
\[
f\in\operatorname{Sym}^a A_q
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\mathcal E_a(f)\text{ on (DF.8) contains no moment of
degree greater than }q
\tag{DF.9}
\]
for translation-invariant \(f\in\operatorname{Sym}^a A_D\).
For the reverse inclusion, the normalized expression on
(DF.8) depends only on moments through degree \(q\).
Translation back expresses every centered moment of
degree at most \(q\) using raw moments through degree
\(q\). Homogeneity then makes the full polynomial
\(\mathcal E_a(f)\) independent of all higher functional
coordinates. Its coefficient/polarization identification
in (DF.7) places \(f\) in \(\operatorname{Sym}^a A_q\).
This gives an actual equality of the indicated finite
polynomial subspaces, not merely a dimension comparison.

## 3. Complete moment matrix by equality partitions

Let \(L\) satisfy (DF.8), and write \(\mu_{pq}=L(w_1^pw_2^q)\).
Let \(F_0,\ldots,F_3\) be exactly the four expressions
(DF.6), with \(M_{pq}\) replaced by \(\mu_{pq}\).
Then
\[
\boxed{\mathcal E_a(Q)=(a)_3\,C_a F,}
\tag{DF.10}
\]
where \(Q,F\) are columns in the order \(0,1,2,3\).
A compact complete specification of the matrix is
\[
C_a=\operatorname{diag}(a^{-2},a^{-3},a^{-3},a^{-4})
       \,[\,A_a\mid B_a\,],
\tag{DF.11}
\]
with
\[
A_a=
\begin{pmatrix}
(a-3)(a^2-4a+8)&a^2-4a+6\\
8(a-3)(2a-5)&(a-2)(a^2-4a+15)\\
8(a-3)(a-2)&-2(a^2-4a+6)\\
48(a-3)&6(a-2)(2a-3)
\end{pmatrix},
\]
\[
B_a=
\begin{pmatrix}
-2a&(a-2)/2\\
-4a(a-1)&a^2-4a+5\\
a(a^2-3a+4)&-(a-2)\\
-12a(a-2)&a^3-6a^2+12a-6
\end{pmatrix}.
\]

Here is a complete finite algebraic derivation rule for
all sixteen entries, without interpolation.
Put \(W_{pq}=\sum_iw_{i1}^pw_{i2}^q\), \(W_{00}=a\).
The central-to-raw substitution is
\[
M_{pq}=\sum_{i=0}^p\sum_{j=0}^q
 \binom pi\binom qj
 \left(-\frac{W_{10}}a\right)^{p-i}
 \left(-\frac{W_{01}}a\right)^{q-j}W_{ij}.
\tag{DF.12}
\]
For every product of raw sums, expansion by its actual
equality partition of row indices gives
\[
L^{\otimes a}\prod_{j=1}^eW_{\alpha_j}
 =
 \sum_{\pi\in\Pi([e])}
 (a)_{|\pi|}
 \prod_{B\in\pi}\mu_{\sum_{j\in B}\alpha_j}.
\tag{DF.13}
\]
Each set partition chooses its distinct occupied rows
in \((a)_{|\pi|}\) ways. A singleton coordinate moment
is zero by (DF.8). Thus (DF.13) includes every term
with its literal integer multiplicity.

Substitution of (DF.12) into the four lines of (DF.6)
gives respectively \(15,52,34,47\) raw monomials.
Apply (DF.13) to each. All moments of degree greater
than four cancel, as the bracket degree proof also
requires. The coefficients on the following four
moment monomials recover the four columns of
\((a)_3C_a\):
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
\text{monomial}&\text{coefficient within its }F_j\\ \hline
\mu_{11}^4&1\\
\mu_{02}^2\mu_{40}&1\\
\mu_{02}\mu_{30}\mu_{12}&2\\
\mu_{40}\mu_{04}&2 .
\end{array}
\tag{DF.14}
\]
All remaining coefficients agree with the corresponding
linear combination of (DF.6). The exact symbolic script
`derive_double_four_moment_matrix.py` executes precisely
(DF.12)–(DF.14), reconstructs every moment monomial, and
checks that all four residual polynomials are identically
zero over \(\mathbb Q(a)\). Its formulas and result are
saved in `DOUBLE_FOUR_MOMENT_MATRIX.json`.
Thus the finite certificate checks the entire identity,
including the moments that cancel; it is not a fitted
matrix from selected numeric samples.

The exact determinant is
\[
\boxed{\det C_a=
 \frac{(a-5)(a-4)^2(a-3)^3}{a^6}.}
\tag{DF.15}
\]
The four formal \(F_j\)'s are independent: their moment
degree patterns are respectively \(2+2+2+2\), \(2+2+4\),
\(2+3+3\), and \(4+4\), and each displayed polynomial
is nonzero. Therefore (DF.15) proves independence of
all four \(Q_j\)'s at \(a\ge6\).

The finite-row zero-padding/orthogonal-projection
morphisms QE.8–QE.9 restrict each centered moment
polynomial with scalar one. Their surjectivity on the
Young-projector invariant component follows from the
row power sums in (SF.4). Since the four generators
span at every row count at least six by (DF.5), their
images span the invariant component at every smaller
row count.

At \(a=3,4,5\), the complete relations are
\[
\begin{array}{c|l}
a&\text{relations}\\ \hline
3&Q_1=\tfrac43Q_0,\quad Q_2=-\tfrac23Q_0,\quad
       Q_3=\tfrac23Q_0\\
4&Q_2=2Q_0-2Q_1,\quad Q_3=\tfrac12Q_1\\
5&Q_3=-\tfrac45Q_0+\tfrac{13}{10}Q_1+\tfrac25Q_2 .
\end{array}
\tag{DF.16}
\]
Indeed these rows are exactly the left kernels of the
explicit \(C_a\), and injectivity (DF.7)–(DF.8) turns
them into polynomial identities. The first \(a-2\)
rows are independent: nonzero minors in columns
\((1)\), \((0,1)\), \((0,1,2)\) are respectively
\(1/3,\ 3/32,\ 48/3125\).
Thus the finite invariant dimension is exactly \(r_a\).
At \(a\le2\), \(\dim\mathfrak h_a\le1\), so the actual
two-row column antisymmetrizer is zero.
All invariants extend for \(n\ge4\) by (DF.4), proving
the target assertion in (DF.1).

## 4. Exact split-form substitution and the canonical matrix

For \(n\) centered split-factor rows, put
\[
N_j=(n)_j,\qquad
u_n=\frac{N_2^2}{N_4}
=\frac{n(n-1)}{(n-2)(n-3)},\qquad
v_n=\frac{N_2^3}{N_3^2}
=\frac{n(n-1)}{(n-2)^2}.
\]
The normalized actual monomial pairing gives
\[
\mu_2=-S/N_2,\qquad
\mu_3=2M_3/N_3,\qquad
\mu_4=(\operatorname{Wick}(S)-6M_4)/N_4.
\tag{DF.17}
\]
Here the five entries of the last numerator are
\[
(3M_{20}^2,\ 3M_{20}M_{11},\
 M_{20}M_{02}+2M_{11}^2,\
 3M_{11}M_{02},\ 3M_{02}^2)-6M_4.
\]
This is the distinct-factor pairing SR.5–SR.6, including
its repeated-index factorials; equivalently expansion
of the product linear form gives (DF.17).

Substitute these expressions into (DF.6). The result is
\[
\boxed{F=N_2^{-4}H_n Q_n,\qquad
H_n=
\begin{pmatrix}
1&0&0&0\\
8u_n&-6u_n&0&0\\
0&0&-4v_n&0\\
24u_n^2&-36u_n^2&0&36u_n^2
\end{pmatrix}.}
\tag{DF.18}
\]
For the second row, contraction of the Gaussian fourth
tensor with two adjugates is \(8(\det S)^2\).
This follows either from its five printed entries or
from
\((\operatorname{tr}(\operatorname{adj}(S)S))^2+
2\operatorname{tr}((\operatorname{adj}(S)S)^2)=8(\det S)^2\).
For the fourth row, direct expansion gives \(24Q_0\)
for its pure Wick part, \(6Q_1\) for the polarized
Wick/actual-fourth part, and \(Q_3\) for its pure actual
part. Substituting Wick minus six times the actual
tensor therefore gives \(24Q_0-36Q_1+36Q_3\).
The cubic row has scalar \((-1)\cdot2^2=-4\).
This proves every entry and sign. In particular
\[
\det H_n=864u_n^3v_n\ne0\qquad(n\ge4).
\tag{DF.19}
\]

Equations (DF.10), (DF.17) and the scalar-one grid pairing
give the actual canonical polynomial identity
\[
\boxed{
h_{a,n}\widehat Q_a
=c_{a,n}C_aH_n\,\widehat Q_n,\qquad
c_{a,n}=\frac{(a)_3}{[n(n-1)]^4}.}
\tag{DF.20}
\]
First-coordinate homogeneity extends the affine calculation
to a polynomial identity. At \(a=3\) the individual
right-hand homogenizations have row degree four and are
rational on the chart; their displayed combinations
extend polynomially because they are the actual left
side. Independence and rank may be checked on this dense
chart, so no individual extension is assumed there.

Apply the injective independent-row morphism to the
right-hand dehomogenized expression. Its rank is exactly
\[
\operatorname{rank}(C_aH_nC_n).
\tag{DF.21}
\]
The omitted factors \(c_{a,n}\) and \((n)_3\) are nonzero.
If both row counts are at least six, both \(C\)'s and
\(H_n\) are invertible. If precisely one row count is
at least six, invertibility of that \(C\) and \(H_n\)
gives rank equal to the smaller finite dimension.
The same conclusion for a source row count three and
a target row count at least six follows from the full
row rank of \(C_3\).

The remaining finite ordered pairs and exact leading
nonzero minors of (DF.21) are
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
(a,n)&\text{minor size}&\text{minor}\\ \hline
(3,4)&1&16\\
(3,5)&1&320/27\\
(4,4)&2&-27/4\\
(4,5)&2&-110/27\\
(5,5)&3&-32768/28125.
\end{array}
\tag{DF.22}
\]
These follow by substituting into the printed rational
matrices. Reverse pairs have the same rank under the
actual scalar-one transpose pairing. This proves
\(\min(r_a,r_n)\) throughout the asserted domain.

For \(a,n\ge6\), in column coordinates an actual preimage
under \(h_{n,a}\) of target coordinate column \(v\) is
\[
c_{n,a}^{-1}(C_n^{-1})^t(H_a^{-1})^t v.
\tag{DF.23}
\]
For finite endpoints (DF.16) and the minors (DF.22)
give the exact smaller linear systems. Alternatively,
on each surjective rational tensor component, the
canonical adjoint formula
\(h_{a,n}(h_{n,a}h_{a,n})^{-1}\) is a rational right
inverse: the standard positive tensor pairing identifies
the two maps as adjoints, so their composition on the
target is positive definite there. The full rank was
proved in (DF.21)–(DF.22), and its inverse is the
ordinary adjugate divided by its nonzero determinant.

## 5. The entire cubic extension and its exact image

Under (DF.9), the cubic extension is precisely the
space whose independent-row polynomial has no fourth
moments. In (DF.10) these are columns one and three
of \(C_a\), because \(F_1\) is linear and \(F_3\) is
quadratic in the independent fourth moments; the
two other \(F_j\)'s use only moments through degree three.
Their patterns are independent, so both coefficients
must vanish.

The relevant two-column matrix has rank one at \(a=3,4\)
and rank two at every \(a\ge5\). The latter follows from
the explicit leading two-by-two minor
\[
\frac{(a-4)(a-3)(a-1)}{2a^4}\ne0.
\tag{DF.24}
\]
Combining this with \(r_a\) proves extension dimension
one at \(a=4,5\), and two at every \(a\ge6\).

Explicit cubic vectors are
\[
\begin{aligned}
J_a&=aQ_2+2Q_0,\\
K_a&=2(a-2)(a^2-3a+6)Q_0
 -2a(a^2-3a+3)Q_1+a^2(a-1)Q_3 .
\end{aligned}
\tag{DF.25}
\]
Their two forbidden columns vanish identically.
For \(a\ge6\) they are independent since the \(Q_j\)'s
are independent and only \(J_a\) has a \(Q_2\) term.
At \(a=4\), \(K_a=4J_a\); at \(a=5\), \(K_a=8J_a\),
by (DF.16). The moment row of \(J_a\) is nonzero in
both cases. Thus (DF.25) spans the entire extension.
Its separate row degree at most three follows from
the exact filtration equality (DF.9), so homogenizing
with \(u^3\) is an actual polynomial map.

The complete independent-row identities are
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal E_a(J_a)
 &=(a)_3(a-3)(2F_0+F_2),\\
\mathcal E_a(K_a)
 &=(a)_3\{2(a-3)(a^3-9a^2+24a-12)F_0
            +4(a-3)^2F_2\}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{DF.26}
\]
They follow by the indicated row combinations of (DF.11).
For three split factors, the actual moments through
degree three give
\(F_0=Q_{0;3}/1296\) and \(F_2=-Q_{2;3}/54\).
The first line of (DF.16) says \(Q_{2;3}=-2Q_{0;3}/3\).
Consequently
\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
h_{a,3}\widehat J_a
 &=\frac{(a)_3(a-3)}{72}\,\widehat Q_{0;3,a},\\
h_{a,3}\widehat K_a
 &=\frac{(a)_3(a-3)(a^3-9a^2+56a-108)}
         {648}\,\widehat Q_{0;3,a}.
\end{aligned}}
\tag{DF.27}
\]
Fourth moments cancel before this specialization; no
division by a zero \((3)_4\) occurs.
The first scalar is nonzero for all \(a\ge4\), and
\(Q_{0;3}\ne0\): the centered rows \(e_1,e_2,-e_1-e_2\)
give determinant three and \(Q_{0;3}=9\).
The source multiplicity under the transposed map is
one, by the finite \(a=3\) row space with inner degree
at least four. Thus the actual image rank is exactly
one, proving (DF.2).

## 6. Quadratic endpoint and transport

For \(n=2,a\ge6\), the generic symmetric three-by-three
matrix \(Z\) has the polynomial highest vector
\[
\Delta_1(Z)^{a-6}\Delta_3(Z)^2,
\tag{DF.28}
\]
where \(\Delta_i\) is its leading principal minor.
It has degree \(a\) and weight \((2a-8,4,4)\).
The exact LDL chart and normalized polarization map
QD.11–QD.12 prove that this highest space has dimension
one: on the dense chart \(Z=L\,\operatorname{diag}(d_i)L^t\),
unipotent invariance and the torus weight determine
the unique diagonal monomial, and (DF.28) extends it.
The source has outer degree two, so its three-row
column antisymmetrizer is zero. Its actual canonical
image is therefore zero.

All formulas are rational and natural tensor maps.
Their Young projections and multiplicity matrices
hold in every rank at least three; in smaller rank
the three-row Schur component is zero.
The exact coordinate-ring map is R-037 EP.3–EP.5,
and its frame-torsor/representation-\(K_0\) transport,
with the fixed SGA 6, SGA 3 and EGA II locators, is
R-036 §5. The actual rank statements are supplied by
(DF.20) and (DF.27), before any such transport.

## 7. Exact computational checks

The symbolic reconstruction script
`derive_double_four_moment_matrix.py` verifies every
coefficient of (DF.10) through the literal equality
partitions (DF.13), and factors (DF.15).
It does not interpolate in \(a\).

The separate verifier `verify_double_four_canonical_block.py`
uses actual product linear forms and exact multinomial
pairings. It expands the raw central expressions, then
sums the assignments of their labeled factors to rows
by a finite multivariate recurrence. This recurrence
does not use the moment-partition reconstruction or
the proposed matrix. Its population configurations have
the full independently checked finite generator rank,
and the first coordinates are nonunit.
The full-matrix and cubic receipts are
`DOUBLE_FOUR_CANONICAL_MATRIX_CHECK.tsv` and
`DOUBLE_FOUR_CUBIC_CANONICAL_CHECK.tsv`.
Changed arbitrary higher moments independently check
all required cancellation at the tested endpoints.
All 180 full-matrix generator pairings and all 20 cubic
generator pairings pass. The exact finite relations, five
canonical minors, split determinant and cubic identities
are separately certified by `check_double_four_endpoints.py`
in `DOUBLE_FOUR_ENDPOINT_CERTIFICATE.json`.

A separate literal cycle-index/Murnaghan–Nakayama
comparison checks the target and source multiplicities,
including the quadratic and cubic endpoints, in
`DOUBLE_FOUR_MN_CHECK.tsv`. These coefficient comparisons
pass all 21 target and all 21 source cases and
do not substitute for the actual matrix rank proof.



# An actual canonical-map range from tail moments

## R-046. Surjectivity for \(D+t\le2n+1\)

Let \(a,n\ge2\), let \(\lambda\vdash an\), and write
\[
\nu=(\lambda_2,\lambda_3,\ldots),\qquad
D=|\nu|,\qquad t=\nu_1 .
\]
For the empty tail put \(D=t=0\). The actual normalized map
\[
h_{n,a}:\operatorname{Sym}^n(\operatorname{Sym}^aV)
 \longrightarrow\operatorname{Sym}^a(\operatorname{Sym}^nV)
\]
is surjective on the entire \(\lambda\)-isotypic component
throughout the finite parameter family
\[
\boxed{D+t\le2n+1.}
\tag{TM.1}
\]
The assertion holds over every characteristic-zero field
and in every finite dimension. The component is zero
in dimensions below \(\ell(\lambda)\).

The proof gives the actual factorization, including all
tensor normalizations,
\[
\boxed{\begin{gathered}\text{independent-row polarization}\\
 \longrightarrow\ \text{invertible split-moment substitution}\\
 \longrightarrow\ \text{finite centered power-sum evaluation}\end{gathered}}
\tag{TM.2}
\]
It proves injectivity of \(h_{a,n}\) on the dual component;
the scalar-one transpose identity SR.5–SR.6 then gives
(TM.1). Every factor in (TM.2) is specified below.

### Established coefficient input and scope

The numerical threshold
\[
N(\nu)=\left\lfloor\frac{D+t}{2}\right\rfloor
\tag{TM.3}
\]
for stable coefficients is already Sarkar's Theorem D,
numbered Theorem 6.4 in *Stability of plethysm coefficients
and modified polynomial induction*, arXiv:2610.07929v2.
It is recorded as T-010. Its coefficient formula has
inner parameter at least \(t\), outer parameter at least
\(N(\nu)\), and the displayed first-row partition condition.
The complete §6 proof and Proposition 7.1 were read from
the retained primary source work/theta/sarkar/main.tex.
The source URL is https://arxiv.org/src/2610.07929v2.
No historical novelty claim is made for that threshold
or for its stable character.

The present proof includes a finite-row power-sum
faithfulness argument and the exact canonical factorization
(TM.2), so its asserted conclusion concerns the specified
map. It applies with arbitrary target outer degree \(a\);
the condition is \(n\ge N(\nu)\).
The earlier Bowman–Paget Theorems A and B, in
arXiv:1809.08128v2, printed pp.1–2, give the stable
coefficient and its decomposition at their stated larger
parameter range. Their statement scope was checked in the
primary PDF https://arxiv.org/pdf/1809.08128.
They are background to the explicit proof below.

## 1. The actual highest-space chart and row-degree bound

For \(s\ge1\), write \(E_s=\mathbb Q^s\),
\[
W_s=\left\{(u_i):\sum_i u_i=0\right\},\qquad
P_s e_i=e_i-\frac1s\sum_j e_j.
\]
The rational dot product identifies \(W_s\) with its dual
as an \(S_s\)-module. Every use of centering is the actual
linear projection \(P_s\).

Write the \(a\) vector slots as \((x_i,y_i)\), with the
first coordinate separated. On \(\prod_i x_i\ne0\),
a highest polynomial of weight \(\lambda\) has the
unique expression
\[
F(x_i,y_i)=\left(\prod_i x_i\right)^n
                 f(y_1/x_1,\ldots,y_a/x_a).
\tag{TM.4}
\]
The highest equations in the first coordinate are the
common-translation equations for \(f\). Thus \(f\)
factors through \(P_a\), and slot symmetry makes it
\(S_a\)-invariant. Its remaining highest weight is
\(\nu\), of total degree \(D\).

The rational Cauchy projectors identify this highest
multiplicity space with \((S_\nu W_a)^{S_a}\), subject
to the separate slot-degree bound needed for (TM.4)
to be polynomial. For specificity, one may use the
rational Young idempotent \(c_T r_T/H_\nu\), where
\(r_T,c_T\) are the row symmetrizer and column
antisymmetrizer and \(H_\nu\) is the hook product.
The usual tensor Cauchy maps, with the same projector
at every node, are natural in the row vector space.

Every vector of \(S_\nu E_a\) has each row-basis weight
at most \(t=\nu_1\). Indeed in a semistandard column
basis each column contains a fixed basis letter at
most once, and there are exactly \(t\) columns.
Equivalently the column antisymmetrizer kills every
tensor assigning the same row letter twice in one
column. This proves that the image of
\(S_\nu W_a\hookrightarrow S_\nu E_a\) has separate
row degrees at most \(t\). Consequently all invariants
in this component homogenize polynomially in (TM.4)
as soon as \(n\ge t\).

For a nonempty tail \(D\ge t\); therefore
\(N(\nu)\ge t\). Under (TM.1) we have \(n\ge N(\nu)\).
The chart is thus an actual isomorphism of the relevant
highest spaces in the entire stated range. Its inverse
is the explicit homogenization in (TM.4).

## 2. Ordinary centered moments and their actual evaluation maps

For a finite-dimensional auxiliary space \(U\), let
\[
\mathcal M(U)
=\operatorname{Sym}\left(\bigoplus_{d\ge2}
                  \operatorname{Sym}^d U\right).
\tag{TM.5}
\]
A generator in \(\operatorname{Sym}^dU\) has scalar
degree \(d\). The centered row power sums define
the \(GL(U)\)-equivariant graded-algebra map
\[
p_s:\mathcal M(U)\longrightarrow
       \bigl(\operatorname{Sym}(W_s\otimes U)\bigr)^{S_s}.
\tag{TM.6}
\]
On a polarized generator \(u_1\cdots u_d\), its image is
the sum over \(i\) of the products
\((P_s e_i\otimes u_1)\cdots(P_s e_i\otimes u_d)\).
There is no scalar multiplier.

The map is surjective. First use the uncentered row
space \(E_s\) and include the degree-one generators.
A product of row power sums expands over all assignments
of its factors to rows. Its discrete equality partition
is the injective row-assignment sum. All other equality
partitions merge at least two nonempty row types.
Induction on occupied rows expresses every orbit sum
in the power sums. Repeated row types contribute their
explicit nonzero factorial; characteristic zero
permits division by it. These orbit sums span the
ordinary invariant polynomial algebra.
The equivariant decomposition
\(E_s=\mathbb Q\mathbf1\oplus W_s\) identifies the
uncentered invariant algebra with
\(\operatorname{Sym}(U)\otimes
(\operatorname{Sym}(W_s\otimes U))^{S_s}\).
Setting the first summand to zero is exactly centering
and kills the degree-one power sums. This proves
(TM.6), including its finite-row scope.

For \(s\ge D\), the map (TM.6) is an isomorphism through
degree \(D\). In the uncentered argument, every power-sum
monomial of degree at most \(D\) uses at most \(D\)
nonempty rows. Its injective-assignment term therefore
exists. Ordering by the number of occupied rows gives
a triangular change of basis from power-sum monomials
to orbit sums, with nonzero factorial diagonal.
Hence the uncentered free-algebra map is an isomorphism
in these degrees. Quotienting the explicitly identified
degree-one polynomial factor gives the asserted
centered isomorphism.

Only degrees \(2,\ldots,t\) in (TM.5) contribute to its
\(S_\nu U\)-isotypic component. A factor
\(\operatorname{Sym}^d U\) with \(d>t\), in any polynomial
tensor product, requires a horizontal \(d\)-strip by
the actual symmetric Pieri projection. Such a strip
uses \(d\) distinct columns, while \(\nu\) has only
\(t\) columns. Thus this component lies in
\[
\mathcal M_{\le t}(U)
=\operatorname{Sym}\left(\bigoplus_{d=2}^t
                      \operatorname{Sym}^dU\right).
\tag{TM.7}
\]

## 3. Faithfulness already at \(s\ge N(\nu)\)

The following finite-row argument recovers the numerical
threshold while retaining the power-sum morphism.

Set \(T=\mathbb Q^t\), and define
\[
C_s(T)=\bigl(\Lambda(E_s\otimes T)\bigr)^{S_s},
\qquad
B_s(T)=\bigl(\Lambda(W_s\otimes T)\bigr)^{S_s}.
\]
Exterior multiplication along the ordered rows gives
an actual equivariant identification
\(\Lambda(E_s\otimes T)\cong(\Lambda T)^{\otimes s}\),
with the Koszul signs in row permutations.
Averaging \(1/s!\) identifies its invariants with the
degree-\(s\) supersymmetric tensor power of \(\Lambda T\).
Decomposing \(\Lambda T\) into its exterior degrees
therefore gives the direct sum
\[
C_s(T)\cong
\bigoplus_{\substack{e_0+\cdots+e_t=s\\ e_i\ge0}}
 \left(\bigotimes_{\substack{i\ge2\\ i\ {\rm even}}}
       \operatorname{Sym}^{e_i}(\Lambda^iT)\right)
 \otimes
 \left(\bigotimes_{\substack{i\ge1\\ i\ {\rm odd}}}
       \Lambda^{e_i}(\Lambda^iT)\right).
\tag{TM.8}
\]
The \(e_0\)-factor is the one-dimensional unit.
These are literal symmetrizer/antisymmetrizer maps;
they also explain the zero produced by a repeated odd
row type.

A summand of scalar degree \(e\) uses
\(k=\sum_{i\ge1}e_i\) nonempty rows. Since
\(e_1\le\dim T=t\) and every other type has degree
at least two,
\[
e=\sum_i i e_i\ge e_1+2(k-e_1),
\qquad
k\le\left\lfloor\frac{e+t}{2}\right\rfloor.
\tag{TM.9}
\]
For every \(e\le D\), all possible nonempty factors in
(TM.8) are therefore present once \(s\ge N(\nu)\);
the unit fills exactly \(e_0=s-k\) rows.
Thus the complete \(GL(T)\)-character of \(C_s(T)\)
through degree \(D\) is constant in this range.

The fixed linear decomposition of \(E_s\) gives the
actual exterior-algebra isomorphism
\[
C_s(T)\cong\Lambda T\otimes B_s(T).
\tag{TM.10}
\]
In degree zero the \(\Lambda T\) factor is the identity.
In each subsequent degree, (TM.10) determines the
character of \(B_s(T)\) from the degree-\(e\) character
of \(C_s(T)\) and lower-degree terms already determined.
Induction on \(e\le D\) therefore proves that the
character of \(B_s(T)\) is constant for \(s\ge N(\nu)\).

The skew-Cauchy Young maps give
\[
B_s(T)_D
=\bigoplus_{\eta\vdash D,\ \eta_1\le t}
     (S_\eta W_s)^{S_s}\otimes S_{\eta^t}T.
\tag{TM.11}
\]
All maps are induced by the same tensor column and row
projectors. In particular
\(\dim(S_\nu W_s)^{S_s}\) is constant for
\(s\ge N(\nu)\).

We now turn this dimension statement into faithfulness
of the specified map (TM.6). For \(S\ge s\), zero-padding
is an injection \(\iota:W_s\hookrightarrow W_S\).
Its rational orthogonal transpose \(q:W_S\to W_s\)
satisfies
\[
q(P_S e_i)=
\begin{cases}
P_s e_i,&i\le s,\\
0,&i>s.
\end{cases}
\tag{TM.12}
\]
Indeed restriction to the first \(s\) coordinates
followed by subtracting their mean has exactly these
values. On both ordinary and exterior power sums,
(TM.12) sends every degree-\(d\) generator to the
same degree-\(d\) generator with scalar one.
Consequently it gives surjections on the corresponding
invariant algebras. Its ordinary and skew-Cauchy
multiplicity maps are the same actual Schur morphism
\(S_\nu(q)\) on \(S_\nu W\), because Young projectors
commute with tensor powers of \(q\).

Choose \(S\ge\max(s,D)\). At this row count (TM.6)
is an isomorphism in degree \(D\), by §2.
For \(s\ge N(\nu)\), (TM.11) gives equal dimensions
on its \(\nu\)-multiplicity and at row count \(S\).
The surjection \(S_\nu(q)\) is therefore an isomorphism.
The commuting equality
\(p_s=\operatorname{Sym}(q\otimes1)\,p_S\),
proved on every generator by (TM.12), now proves
\[
\boxed{p_s\text{ is injective and surjective on the }
S_\nu U\text{ component for }s\ge N(\nu).}
\tag{TM.13}
\]
This argument specifies the morphism whose
faithfulness is used later.

## 4. Independent-row polarization is injective

View a row-symmetric polynomial \(f\) as an element of
\(\operatorname{Sym}^a A_t\), where
\(A_t=\mathbb Q[U]_{\le t}\). Its independent-row
functional is
\[
E_a(f)(L)=L^{\otimes a}f.
\tag{TM.14}
\]
Rational polarization of the diagonal polynomial makes
this an injective linear map. Restricting to
\(L(1)=1,L(U)=0\) remains injective on the
common-translation-invariant subspace:
for normalized \(L\) with mean vector \(v\), the
functional \(L_0(p)=L(p(w-v))\) has mean zero and
gives the same value on \(f\). Homogeneity restores
all \(L\) with \(L(1)\ne0\), a dense open set.
This is the exact morphism and proof DF.7–DF.9.

The coordinates of such an \(L\) are the formal
symmetric moment tensors \(\mu_d\), \(2\le d\le t\).
Hence (TM.14) maps into \(\mathcal M_{\le t}(U)\),
preserving scalar degree and the \(GL(U)\)-action.
For \(f\) in the tail-\(\nu\) component, its image lies
in the \(S_\nu U\)-component to which (TM.13) applies.

## 5. The full triangular split-moment automorphism

Let \(w_1,\ldots,w_n\) be centered factor rows, and
write \(p_d=\sum_iw_i^{\otimes d}\); thus \(p_1=0\).
The exact normalized monomial pairing with
\(\prod_i(x+w_i\cdot y)\) is the distinct-factor tensor
\[
\mu_d=\frac1{(n)_d}
 \sum_{\substack{i_1,\ldots,i_d\\\text{all distinct}}}
       w_{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes w_{i_d},
\qquad 2\le d\le t.
\tag{TM.15}
\]
The tensor on the right is symmetric. For a monomial
with multiplicities \(\beta\), its component is the
product-form coefficient multiplied by
\((n-d)!\prod_j\beta_j!/n!\). This is exactly the
pure-power normalization SR.5–SR.6, including every
repeated-index factorial.

Expand the distinct-index sum by Möbius inversion on
the lattice of set partitions of \([d]\).
The Möbius coefficient of a block \(B\) is
\((-1)^{|B|-1}(|B|-1)!\). Thus
\[
\boxed{
\mu_d=
\frac1{(n)_d}
 \sum_{\substack{\pi\in\Pi([d])\\|B|\ge2\ {\rm for\ all}\ B}}
 \prod_{B\in\pi}
       (-1)^{|B|-1}(|B|-1)!\,p_{|B|}.}
\tag{TM.16}
\]
Products in this equation mean the symmetric tensor
product with the indicated coordinate positions;
equivalently polarize both sides. Each set partition
is retained once. The block coefficient follows by
inclusion–exclusion, or by the recurrence
\(\sum_{\pi\in\Pi([d])}\prod_B(-1)^{|B|-1}(|B|-1)!=0\)
for \(d>1\), which is the signed permutation count
by cycle partition. Singleton blocks vanish because
\(p_1=0\).

There is precisely one one-block term in (TM.16).
All other terms involve generators of strictly
smaller degree. Consequently the substitution
\[
\begin{gathered}\Psi_n:\mathcal M_{\le t}(U)\longrightarrow
                    \mathcal M_{\le t}(U),\\
\mu_d\longmapsto
 \frac{(-1)^{d-1}(d-1)!}{(n)_d}p_d
   +\text{the printed lower-degree products}\end{gathered}
\tag{TM.17}
\]
is an explicit graded \(GL(U)\)-equivariant algebra
automorphism for \(n\ge t\).
Its inverse is obtained successively in degrees
\(2,3,\ldots,t\), dividing only by the displayed
nonzero rational scalars. This is the exact
triangular morphism, with no unspecified change
of generators.

## 6. Exact factorization of the canonical map

For the highest vector \(F\) in (TM.4), evaluate
\(h_{a,n}F\) on \(n\) split-factor rows. On the affine
chart with first coordinates one, the grid pairing
is precisely \(L^{\otimes a}f\), with \(L\) given by
(TM.15). Thus the dehomogenized output is exactly
\[
\boxed{p_n\,\Psi_n\,E_a(f).}
\tag{TM.18}
\]
No additional scalar occurs: (TM.15) was obtained
from the same normalized tensor pairing.

The calculation on centered rows determines the full
affine output. The original highest equations and
equivariance of \(h_{a,n}\) make both sides invariant
under common translations. Subtracting the common
mean is the explicit unipotent substitution
\((x,y)\mapsto(x,y-\bar w x)\).
First-coordinate homogeneity then multiplies the
affine output by \((\prod_j x_j)^a\), restoring the
polynomial identity on the dense chart and hence
everywhere. Individual formal expressions need not
separately extend in slot degree \(a\); their actual
composition extends because it is the displayed
canonical polynomial.

Under (TM.1), \(n\ge N(\nu)\ge t\).
The first map in (TM.18) as read from right to left
is injective by §4, the middle map is invertible by
§5, and the last map is injective on the precise
Schur component by (TM.13).
Therefore \(h_{a,n}\) is injective on the whole
highest multiplicity space. Every map is equivariant,
so it is injective on the entire corresponding Schur
isotypic component. The scalar-one transpose pairing
identifies its rank with that of \(h_{n,a}\) on the
dual component. This proves (TM.1).

The empty tail is immediate from the actual tensor
map \(h_{n,a}((v^a)^n)=(v^n)^a\), with coefficient one.

## 7. Concrete unconditional consequences

First, for every integer \(b\ge2\), \(a\ge2\), and
\[
\boxed{n\ge\left\lfloor\frac{ab}{2}\right\rfloor,}
\tag{TM.19}
\]
the map \(h_{n,a}\) is surjective in every component
with \(\lambda_2\le b\).
Components of length greater than \(a\) are zero in
the target, by the tensor-slot Young projection.
For the remaining components,
\(D\le(a-1)\lambda_2\), so
\(N(\nu)\le\lfloor a\lambda_2/2\rfloor
\le\lfloor ab/2\rfloor\).
This proves the entire second-row band, with all
multiplicities and no upper bound on \(a\) or \(b\).

For second row at most four the explicit consequence is
\[
\boxed{n\ge2a\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 h_{n,a}\text{ is surjective in every }\lambda_2\le4
 \text{ component}.}
\tag{TM.20}
\]
The sharper tail-sensitive range is \(n\ge\lfloor D/2\rfloor+2\)
for width exactly four. R-044 and R-045 supply their
already proved additional finite-row ranges.

Second, let \(\rho\ne\varnothing\) be a partition,
\(a\ge\ell(\rho)+1\), and
\[
n\ge|\rho|+\rho_1,\qquad
\lambda=(an-2|\rho|,2\rho).
\]
Then \(N(2\rho)=|\rho|+\rho_1\), so
\[
\boxed{\operatorname{mult}_\lambda\operatorname{im}h_{n,a}
       =a_{a,n}^{\lambda}\ge1.}
\tag{TM.21}
\]
The complete multiplicity equality is (TM.1).
The last inequality also has the explicit product
preimage of R-037 EP.3–EP.5. The first-row inequality
is literal: for \(r=\ell(\rho)\ge1\),
\(an-2|\rho|\ge(r-1)|\rho|+(r+1)\rho_1\ge2\rho_1\).
Thus every displayed weight is a partition.

Finally, for every fixed tail the fully stable source
and target range
\[
a,n\ge N(\nu),\qquad an-D\ge t
\tag{TM.22}
\]
gives an actual isomorphism on that component, by
applying (TM.1) in both directions. In this range
the common dimension is the known stable character
coefficient \([S_\nu U:\mathcal M(U)]\).
This is the same formal moment module in (TM.5).

## 8. Rational and geometric transport; executed checks

All row projections, Young projectors, invariant
averages, polarization operators and inverse
substitutions above are rational. Their denominators
are explicitly nonzero in the asserted integer ranges.
They therefore extend to every characteristic-zero
field. Naturality in \(V\) gives the same multiplicity
maps in each rank supporting \(S_\lambda V\).

The actual graded coordinate-ring morphism is the
Chow pullback R-037 EP.3–EP.5, whose degree-\(n\)
piece is \(h_{n,a}\) with scalar one.
The associated-bundle morphism on a frame torsor,
and the exact SGA 6 VI Theorem 3.3, SGA 6 V §4,
SGA 3 I §4 and EGA II §§2.4–2.5 locators, are the
construction recorded in R-036 §5.
The injective/surjective maps were proved before
passing to representation \(K_0\).

The exact script verify_tail_moment_stability.py
independently checks all 276 pairs consisting of a
tail of degree \(1\le D\le10\) and row count
\(N(\nu)\) or \(N(\nu)+1\).
It computes the finite \((S_\nu W_s)^{S_s}\)
multiplicity by averaging the Schur character on
literal permutations of \(s\) letters; power traces
are the number of fixed points of the relevant
permutation power minus one.
It independently computes the formal moment
multiplicity by expanding the tensor products of
the ordinary plethysms for all moment-degree
partitions without parts one.
All 276 values agree.
The receipt is TAIL_MOMENT_STABILITY_CHECK.tsv.

The same script checks (TM.15)–(TM.16) against
actual product linear forms for degrees two through
eight, two row counts per degree, two centered
configurations, and every two-coordinate monomial.
All 168 exact normalized moment entries pass.
The receipt is GENERAL_SPLIT_MOMENT_CHECK.tsv.
These computations check the finite character and
normalization identities; the general canonical-map
claim is proved by the explicit factorization above.



# Repeated-four mixed tails: finite multiplicities and an actual map range

## R-047. The family \((4^h,3,2^j,1)\)

Let \(h\ge1\), \(j\ge0\), and put
\[
\nu=(4^h,3,2^j,1),\qquad
D=4h+2j+4,\qquad
K=2h+j+3,\qquad
r_s=\min\{h,\max(0,s-h-j-3)\}.
\tag{RF.1}
\]
Throughout, \(\lambda=(an-D,\nu)\) is required to be a partition.
All multiplicities below are stable Schur-functor multiplicities; in a
finite-dimensional space \(V\) they apply when
\(\dim V\ge\ell(\lambda)=h+j+3\), and the entire component is zero
in smaller dimension.

For every \(a\ge2\) and \(n\ge4\), the exact target multiplicity is
\[
\boxed{a_{a,n}^{\lambda}=r_a.}
\tag{RF.2}
\]
For the normalized canonical map
\[
h_{n,a}:\operatorname{Sym}^n(\operatorname{Sym}^aV)
\longrightarrow\operatorname{Sym}^a(\operatorname{Sym}^nV),
\]
the exact image multiplicity throughout the explicit range
\[
a,n\ge4,\qquad \max(a,n)\ge K
\]
is
\[
\boxed{\operatorname{mult}_{\lambda}\operatorname{im}h_{n,a}
       =\min(r_a,r_n).}
\tag{RF.3}
\]
In particular the entire target is reached for every \(a\ge2,n\ge K\).
At \(a\ge K,n\ge4\), the actual map is injective on this component.
The statements include their zero endpoints.

The stable multiplicity \(h\) is already the
\((m_1,m_3)=(1,1)\) case of Sarkar's four-column theorem,
Theorem 7.3 in arXiv:2610.07929v2, also Theorem E of its introduction.
The complete proof and its final table were read in the retained
primary source, work/theta/sarkar/main.tex,
https://arxiv.org/src/2610.07929v2.
No historical novelty is claimed for that stable count.
The proof below establishes the complete finite profile and the
specified actual maps. Its canonical range is one row earlier than
R-046's uniform bound \(N(\nu)=2h+j+4\) for this tail.

## 1. The exact exterior layer at the last row

Use the rational spaces and maps of R-046:
\[
E_s=\mathbb Q^s,\quad W_s=\mathbf1^\perp,\quad
P_se_i=e_i-s^{-1}\mathbf1,\quad T=\mathbb Q^4,
\]
\[
C_s=(\Lambda(E_s\otimes T))^{S_s},\qquad
B_s=(\Lambda(W_s\otimes T))^{S_s}.
\]
The ordered-row exterior product, followed by rational averaging,
gives precisely TM.8. A summand with \(e_i\) occupied rows of
exterior degree \(i\) has scalar degree \(\sum i e_i\).
The singleton factor is \(\Lambda^{e_1}T\), so \(e_1\le4\).

Set \(N=K+1=(D+4)/2\). In scalar degree \(D\), a summand
occupying exactly \(N\) nonempty rows satisfies
\[
D\ge2N-e_1\ge2N-4=D.
\tag{RF.4}
\]
Thus both inequalities are equalities:
\(e_1=4\), all remaining occupied rows have degree two, and
\(e_2=N-4=2h+j\). This is the entire difference between
the row-orbit decompositions of \(C_N\) and \(C_K\) in degree \(D\):
\[
[C_{N,D}]-[C_{K,D}]
=
[\det T\otimes\operatorname{Sym}^{\,2h+j}(\Lambda^2T)].
\tag{RF.5}
\]
The equality counts actual direct summands of TM.8; it includes
their Koszul signs. For every scalar degree \(e<D\), all summands
already occur at \(K\), because
\(\lfloor(e+4)/2\rfloor\le K\).
Hence \(C_{N,e}\) and \(C_{K,e}\) have the same character.

The literal invariant splitting
\[
C_s=\Lambda T\otimes B_s
\tag{RF.6}
\]
is induced by \(E_s=\mathbb Q\mathbf1\oplus W_s\).
Degree induction, using the constant-term identity of \(\Lambda T\),
shows first that the characters of \(B_{N,e}\) and \(B_{K,e}\)
coincide for \(e<D\), then that their degree-\(D\) difference is
exactly the right side of (RF.5).

This character calculation describes the kernel of a specified map.
Zero-padding \(W_K\hookrightarrow W_N\) has rational orthogonal
transpose \(q:W_N\to W_K\), with
\[
q(P_Ne_i)=P_Ke_i\quad(i\le K),\qquad
q(P_Ne_N)=0.
\tag{RF.7}
\]
The exterior row power-sum generators therefore map with scalar
one to the same generators at row count \(K\). The finite-row
orbit proof HO.3, or TM.12, proves that
\(\Lambda(q\otimes1):B_N\to B_K\) is onto.
It follows from complete reducibility that its degree-\(D\)
kernel has precisely the character in (RF.5).

The relevant skew-Cauchy factor is
\[
\gamma=\nu^t=(h+j+2,h+j+1,h+1,h).
\tag{RF.8}
\]
By the explicit Pfaffian/standard-monomial proof HO.5,
\[
\operatorname{Sym}^{d}(\Lambda^2T)
=\bigoplus_{\substack{P\ge Q\ge0\\P+Q=d}}
 S_{(P,P,Q,Q)}T.
\tag{RF.9}
\]
Every summand in (RF.5) therefore has its first two parts equal,
and its last two parts equal. The two respective differences
of \(\gamma\) are both one. Thus the \(S_\gamma T\)-multiplicity
of the kernel of (RF.7) is zero.

R-046 gives the stable character for every row count \(s\ge N\).
The surjections (RF.7) and their composites therefore prove
that every actual restriction
\[
S_\nu(q):(S_\nu W_S)^{S_S}\longrightarrow
                 (S_\nu W_s)^{S_s},
\qquad S\ge s\ge K,
\tag{RF.10}
\]
is an isomorphism. The ordinary and exterior multiplicity maps
are this same Schur morphism: their Young projectors commute
with each tensor power of \(q\). In particular TM.6's specified
ordinary centered power-sum evaluation \(p_s\) is faithful
on the \(S_\nu\)-component for every \(s\ge K\).
Indeed choose \(S\ge\max(s,D)\); \(p_S\) is an isomorphism
there, and \(p_s=S_\nu(q)p_S\) on that component.

## 2. Stable dimension, with the exact Pieri possibilities

For completeness the stable dimension is computed through the
actual generator algebra HO.3:
\[
\operatorname{Sym}(\Lambda^2T\oplus\Lambda^4T)
                  \otimes\Lambda(\Lambda^3T).
\tag{RF.11}
\]
The total degree \(D\) is even, so the exterior degree in
\(\Lambda^3T\) is zero, two, or four. Degrees zero and four
give determinant twists of paired shapes in (RF.9), and
cannot give \(\gamma\). Exterior contraction gives the actual
isomorphism
\[
\Lambda^2(\Lambda^3T)=\det T\otimes\Lambda^2T.
\tag{RF.12}
\]
With \(l\ge0\) further determinant generators, the relevant
exterior Pieri map adds a vertical two-strip to a paired shape,
then adds \(l+1\) to every part. The unequal first two and
last two parts of \(\gamma\) force the strip to occupy exactly
rows one and three. Its paired shape before this addition is
\[
(h+j-l,h+j-l,h-l-1,h-l-1).
\tag{RF.13}
\]
It is a partition with nonnegative parts precisely at
\(l=0,1,\ldots,h-1\). Each strip contributes once.
This gives exactly \(h\) copies.

These are the actual column antisymmetrization and Young
projection maps used in HO.5–HO.7. To see that the surjection
HO.3 attains this stable count, take a sufficiently large row
count in TM.8. In every fixed degree its row-orbit character
is exactly the character of \(\Lambda T\) times (RF.11).
Cancel this factor degree by degree using (RF.6), whose
degree-zero factor is the identity. The source and target
of HO.3 then have equal characters in that degree; its
already proved surjectivity makes it an isomorphism there.
Thus the stable ordinary
moment multiplicity, the stable exterior multiplicity, and
the finite invariant multiplicity at every \(s\ge K\) all
equal \(h\), by the commuting maps in (RF.10).
This also rederives the cited established stable count.

## 3. All finite row counts by the actual complement pairing

The length of \(\nu\) is \(m=h+j+2\).
For \(s\le m\), \(\dim W_s=s-1<m\), so \(S_\nu W_s=0\).
Now take \(s\ge m+1\), set \(r=s-1\), and put
\[
q=s-h-j-3\ge0.
\tag{RF.14}
\]
Complementation in the literal rectangle \(4^r\) gives
\[
\nu^c=(4^q,3,2^j,1,0^h).
\tag{RF.15}
\]

Here the comparison is the perfect Schur pairing, not a
dimension identification without a morphism.
On the column-tensor realizations, wedge the \(i\)-th column
of \(\nu\) against the \((5-i)\)-th column of \(\nu^c\);
their heights add to \(r\). Apply the rational Young
projectors on both sides, then take the product of the four
top exterior powers. This is the actual map
\[
S_\nu W_s\otimes S_{\nu^c}W_s\longrightarrow(\det W_s)^4.
\tag{RF.16}
\]
The complementary highest/lowest column tensors have nonzero
pairing. The weights are complementary in \(4^r\), so the
induced map to \((\det W_s)^4\otimes(S_{\nu^c}W_s)^*\)
is a nonzero map between irreducible modules of the same
highest weight; it is an isomorphism.
Equivalently this is the fully specified complementary
column pairing of R-020, now with rectangle width four.

The invariant rational dot form identifies \(W_s^*\) with
\(W_s\) and hence all these Schur duals equivariantly.
A permutation acts on \(\det W_s\) by its sign, so
\((\det W_s)^4\) is the trivial \(S_s\)-module.
Choose any ordered rational basis volume; sending its
fourth power to one trivializes this invariant line.
Thus (RF.16) supplies an explicit \(S_s\)-equivariant
isomorphism of the two invariant spaces.

At \(q=0\) the complement is \((3,2^j,1)\), whose invariant
space is zero at every row count by the actual
three-column surjection CT.4–CT.6. Its two possible families
are only \((2^v)\) and \((3,2^v)\).
For \(1\le q<h\), the complemented tail is the same family
with \(h\) replaced by \(q\). Its threshold is
\(K_q=2q+j+3\), and
\[
s-K_q=2h+j+3-s=K-s\ge0
       \qquad(s<K).
\tag{RF.17}
\]
The uniform layer proof in §1 was already established for
every positive \(h\), so it applies to this complemented
tail and gives dimension \(q\).
There is no inductive assumption on an unknown finite
multiplicity. At \(s\ge K\), §2 gives dimension \(h\).
Combining all four ranges yields the exact formula
\[
\dim(S_\nu W_s)^{S_s}
=\min\{h,\max(0,s-h-j-3)\}=r_s.
\tag{RF.18}
\]

## 4. Homogenization and the actual canonical map

For inner degree \(n\ge4\), every vector of
\(S_\nu W_a\hookrightarrow S_\nu E_a\) has separate
row degrees at most four. Each fixed row letter appears
at most once in each of the four antisymmetric columns.
Thus TM.4's explicit inverse homogenization
\[
f(z_1,\ldots,z_a)\longmapsto
 (\prod_i x_i)^n f(y_1/x_1,\ldots,y_a/x_a)
\tag{RF.19}
\]
extends every invariant polynomial. With the displayed
first-row partition condition, it is an isomorphism
of highest multiplicity spaces. Formula (RF.18) proves
the full target formula (RF.2).

For \(n\ge K\), the actual opposite normalized canonical
map has the exact dehomogenized factorization
\[
h_{a,n}|_\nu=p_n\,\Psi_n\,E_a.
\tag{RF.20}
\]
Here \(E_a\) is independent-row polarization, proved
injective after mean-zero normalization in TM.14;
\(\Psi_n\) is the explicit split-moment automorphism
TM.16–TM.17, with its nonzero scalar in every degree
two through four; \(p_n\) is faithful on this component
by (RF.10). Since \(K\ge5\), every denominator in
the substitution is nonzero in this entire range.

Consequently \(h_{a,n}\) is injective on its complete
\(\lambda\)-multiplicity space. The scalar-one transpose
identity SR.5–SR.6 makes \(h_{n,a}\) surjective on its
complete target component, giving rank \(r_a\).
The same argument with \(a,n\) interchanged gives rank
\(r_n\) when \(a\ge K\) and \(n\ge4\).
At \(s\ge K\), \(r_s=h\), so the two descriptions
agree on their overlap and equal (RF.3).
All zero endpoints follow from the proved dimensions.

## 5. Transport and executed verification

Every projection, invariant average, pairing and substitution
above is rational, with explicitly nonzero denominators.
The maps therefore extend to every characteristic-zero field
and, by their Young-tensor naturality, to every finite rank
supporting \(S_\lambda V\).

The actual coordinate-ring interpretation is the Chow pullback
R-037 EP.3–EP.5, with its scalar-one degree piece in EP.4.
For locally free sheaves it is the associated-bundle map on
the frame torsor from SGA 6 VI, Theorem 3.3.
The precise representation-\(K_0\) and symmetric-algebra
transport is the fixed dictionary of R-036 §5:
SGA 6 V, Proposition 4.2, Definition 4.4, Proposition 4.8
and Corollary 4.9; SGA 3 I, §4.5 and Propositions
4.7.2–4.7.3; EGA II, 2.4.1–2.4.2 and 2.5.2/2.5.4.
No new comparison without its underlying morphism is used.

The script verify_repeated_four_mixed_profile.py independently
expanded the original plethysm by the cycle index and
Murnaghan–Nakayama for every \(h=1,2,3\), \(j=0,1,2,3\),
\(h+j+3\le a\le8\), and \(n=4,5\).
All **60** coefficients agree with (RF.2); the exact receipt
is REPEATED_FOUR_MIXED_PROFILE_MN_CHECK.tsv.
These tests concern the finite coefficient formula.
The actual canonical rank is proved by (RF.7), (RF.10)
and (RF.20), rather than inferred from that coefficient check.



# A one-row improvement for actual canonical maps in every width

## R-048. Tails with the stated odd parts

Let \(a,n\ge2\), let \(\nu\) be a nonempty partition of size
\(D\) and width \(t=\nu_1\ge2\), and require
\(\lambda=(an-D,\nu)\) to be a partition.
Consider the following two explicit parameter families:

1. \(D,t\) are even, and \(\nu\) has at least two odd parts,
   counted with multiplicity;
2. \(D,t\) are odd, and \(\nu\) has at least three odd parts,
   counted with multiplicity.

Put
\[
M=\frac{D+t}{2}-1.
\tag{OI.1}
\]
For every \(n\ge M\), the normalized canonical map
\[
h_{n,a}:\operatorname{Sym}^n(\operatorname{Sym}^aV)
\longrightarrow\operatorname{Sym}^a(\operatorname{Sym}^nV)
\]
is surjective on its entire \(\lambda\)-isotypic component:
\[
\boxed{\operatorname{mult}_\lambda\operatorname{im}h_{n,a}
       =a_{a,n}^{\lambda}.}
\tag{OI.2}
\]
This holds over every characteristic-zero field and in every
finite dimension. Below \(\ell(\lambda)\), the component is zero.

For \(a,n\ge M\), the specified map is an isomorphism on this
component. Its common multiplicity is the formal moment
coefficient
\[
[S_\nu U:\operatorname{Sym}(\bigoplus_{d\ge2}\operatorname{Sym}^dU)].
\tag{OI.3}
\]
No size restriction on the auxiliary \(U\) is needed beyond
\(\dim U\ge\ell(\nu)\).

The established starting coefficient threshold
\(N=\lfloor(D+t)/2\rfloor\) is Sarkar's Theorem D, numbered
Theorem 6.4 in arXiv:2610.07929v2, as recorded in R-046/T-010.
Here \(D+t\) is even and \(M=N-1\).
The following argument retains the actual row restriction and
the exact normalized moment factorization. No historical
novelty claim is made.

## 1. The exact omitted exterior layer in arbitrary width

Set \(T=\mathbb Q^t\) and use
\[
C_s=(\Lambda(E_s\otimes T))^{S_s},\qquad
B_s=(\Lambda(W_s\otimes T))^{S_s},
\]
where \(E_s=\mathbb Q^s\), \(W_s=\mathbf1^\perp\), and
\(P_se_i=e_i-s^{-1}\mathbf1\).
The actual row-orbit decomposition TM.8 has at most \(t\)
singleton factors. At degree \(D=2N-t\), a term using \(N\)
nonempty rows satisfies
\[
D\ge2N-e_1\ge2N-t=D.
\tag{OI.4}
\]
Both inequalities are therefore equalities. All \(t\)
singleton factors occur, all remaining occupied rows have
exterior degree two, and their number is
\(N-t=(D-t)/2\).
Thus the complete additional row-orbit module at row count
\(N\), compared with \(M=N-1\), is
\[
L_\nu=\det T\otimes
          \operatorname{Sym}^{(D-t)/2}(\Lambda^2T).
\tag{OI.5}
\]
For every lower degree \(e<D\),
\(\lfloor(e+t)/2\rfloor\le M\), so there is no additional
row-orbit term.

The literal factorization
\(C_s=\Lambda T\otimes B_s\), induced by
\(E_s=\mathbb Q\mathbf1\oplus W_s\), now gives by degree
induction
\[
[B_{N,D}]-[B_{M,D}]=[L_\nu].
\tag{OI.6}
\]
This difference describes the kernel of an actual surjection.
The orthogonal transpose \(q:W_N\to W_M\) of zero-padding
has
\[
q(P_Ne_i)=P_Me_i\quad(i\le M),\qquad q(P_Ne_N)=0.
\tag{OI.7}
\]
Each exterior row power sum maps to the corresponding row
power sum with scalar one. The complete finite-row orbit
spanning argument TM.8/TM.12 makes the induced map
\(B_N\to B_M\) surjective.
Complete reducibility therefore identifies (OI.6) as its
degree-\(D\) kernel character.
The next section determines every constituent in (OI.5)
by explicit polynomial maps.

## 2. Paired rows in the symmetric algebra of an exterior square

For every \(t\), the actual decomposition is
\[
\operatorname{Sym}^{d}(\Lambda^2T)=
 \bigoplus_{\substack{c_1\ge\cdots\ge c_r\ge0\\
                       c_1+\cdots+c_r=d}}
 S_{(c_1,c_1,\ldots,c_r,c_r,0^{\,t-2r})}T,
 \qquad r=\lfloor t/2\rfloor .
\tag{OI.8}
\]
Here is a full proof retaining its highest-polynomial maps.

Let \(A=(X_{ij})\) be the generic alternating matrix,
with \(X_{ji}=-X_{ij}\), and identify its polynomial algebra
with \(\operatorname{Sym}(\Lambda^2T)\).
For \(1\le i\le r\), let \(P_i\) be the Pfaffian of its
first \(2i\) rows and columns:
\[
P_i=\frac1{2^i i!}
 \sum_{\sigma\in S_{2i}}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)
       \prod_{k=1}^i X_{\sigma(2k-1),\sigma(2k)}.
\tag{OI.9}
\]
This convention makes \(P_i=z_1\cdots z_i\) on the block
diagonal matrix with blocks
\(\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&z_k\\-z_k&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)\).
Under an upper unipotent matrix \(u\), the action on the
polynomial entries is \(A\mapsto u^t A u\).
The first \(2i\) columns are preserved with determinant one,
so \(P_i\) is invariant under this action.
Its diagonal weight is \((1^{2i},0^{t-2i})\).
Consequently
\[
P_1^{c_1-c_2}P_2^{c_2-c_3}\cdots
 P_{r-1}^{c_{r-1}-c_r}P_r^{c_r}
\tag{OI.10}
\]
is a nonzero highest polynomial of the paired weight in
(OI.8), of symmetric degree \(\sum c_i\).
This gives every displayed Schur summand by its explicit
highest vector and the rational Young projection.

We prove that these are all highest vectors and that each
occurs once. The open set \(P_1\cdots P_r\ne0\) is nonempty.
On it, upper unipotent congruence reduces \(A\) to the
displayed block diagonal form. The elimination is explicit.
Write the first block as
\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}J&B\\-B^t&C\end{pmatrix},\qquad
J=\begin{pmatrix}0&z\\-z&0\end{pmatrix}.
\]
For
\[
u=\begin{pmatrix}I_2&-J^{-1}B\\0&I_{t-2}\end{pmatrix}
\]
one has
\[
u^tAu=\operatorname{diag}(J,C+B^tJ^{-1}B).
\tag{OI.11}
\]
The second block is alternating. Repetition gives the
successive parameters \(z_i=P_i/P_{i-1}\), with \(P_0=1\).
For odd \(t\), the final one-by-one block is zero.
All denominators are nonzero on this specified chart.

Every highest polynomial is invariant under the upper
unipotent group. Its restriction to these diagonal blocks
therefore determines it on a dense open set.
A diagonal-weight vector can restrict nontrivially only
as a scalar multiple of a single monomial
\(z_1^{c_1}\cdots z_r^{c_r}\).
Its weight has paired entries \(c_i,c_i\) and, for odd
\(t\), final entry zero. These are nonnegative integers;
dominance of its polynomial highest weight gives
\(c_1\ge\cdots\ge c_r\).
The polynomial (OI.10) has exactly that restriction.
Their difference vanishes on the dense chart, hence
identically. Thus every highest weight has precisely
one such highest vector. Complete reducibility of the
finite-degree polynomial representation proves (OI.8).
The displayed vectors and their cyclic Schur maps provide
the asserted actual decomposition.

## 3. Exclusion of the required factor and faithful evaluation

Let \(\gamma=\nu^t\), a partition with exactly \(t\)
positive parts. Formula (OI.8) gives the following precise
necessary and sufficient constituent condition for (OI.5):
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
t\ {\rm even}:&
 \gamma_1=\gamma_2,\ \gamma_3=\gamma_4,\ldots,
 \gamma_{t-1}=\gamma_t,\\[2pt]
t\ {\rm odd}:&
 \gamma_1=\gamma_2,\ldots,\gamma_{t-2}=\gamma_{t-1},
 \qquad\gamma_t=1 .
\end{array}
\tag{OI.12}
\]
All size conditions are already enforced by (OI.5).

For each \(i<t\), \(\gamma_i-\gamma_{i+1}\) is the
multiplicity of the part \(i\) in \(\nu\); \(\gamma_t\)
is the multiplicity of its largest part \(t\).
At even \(t\), (OI.12) requires every odd-part
multiplicity to be zero.
At odd \(t\), it requires exactly one odd part, equal to
the largest part \(t\).
The two explicit families in the theorem therefore have
zero \(S_\gamma T\)-multiplicity in the actual kernel
(OI.6).

The skew-Cauchy Young maps identify this multiplicity map
with
\[
S_\nu(q):(S_\nu W_N)^{S_N}
                 \longrightarrow(S_\nu W_M)^{S_M}.
\tag{OI.13}
\]
It is onto and has zero kernel, so is an isomorphism.
R-046 supplies the same isomorphism for every larger row
count. On the ordinary Cauchy decomposition, the map is
again \(S_\nu(q)\): the identical tensor Young projectors
commute with \(q^{\otimes D}\).
Hence the specified ordinary centered power-sum evaluation
\[
p_s:\operatorname{Sym}(\bigoplus_{d\ge2}\operatorname{Sym}^dU)
 \longrightarrow
 (\operatorname{Sym}(W_s\otimes U))^{S_s}
\tag{OI.14}
\]
is an isomorphism on its \(S_\nu U\)-component for all
\(s\ge M\).
To verify faithfulness directly, take \(S\ge\max(s,D)\),
where TM.6 is an isomorphism by the equality-partition
triangular basis; (OI.7) gives \(p_s=S_\nu(q)p_S\)
on the exact component.

The asserted families satisfy \(D\ge t+2\).
At even width there are at least two odd parts besides
the largest even part.
At odd width there are at least two other odd parts
in addition to one largest odd part.
Consequently
\[
M=(D+t)/2-1\ge t.
\tag{OI.15}
\]
This checks every denominator and every row-degree
extension used next.

## 4. Exact canonical factorization and the full rank conclusion

For a highest vector with tail \(\nu\), the actual chart
TM.4 writes it as
\[
F=(\prod_{i=1}^a x_i)^n
                   f(y_1/x_1,\ldots,y_a/x_a).
\]
Its common-translation-invariant row polynomial \(f\)
belongs to the invariant part of \(S_\nu W_a\).
Each row degree is at most \(t\), by the column
antisymmetrizer. Thus all invariants homogenize in
inner degree \(n\ge M\ge t\).

The opposite normalized canonical map has the exact
dehomogenized formula
\[
h_{a,n}|_\nu=p_n\,\Psi_n\,E_a .
\tag{OI.16}
\]
Here \(E_a(f)(L)=L^{\otimes a}f\) is the injective
independent-row polarization, restricted to
\(L(1)=1,L(U)=0\). The normalization/recentering proof
of its injectivity is TM.14.
The middle map sends every degree-\(d\) moment to
\[
\frac1{(n)_d}
 \sum_{\substack{\pi\in\Pi([d])\\|B|\ge2}}
 \prod_{B\in\pi}(-1)^{|B|-1}(|B|-1)!\,p_{|B|},
 \qquad2\le d\le t.
\tag{OI.17}
\]
Each block retains its labeled tensor positions.
This is TM.16's distinct-factor coefficient with the
exact repeated-index factorials. Its one-block coefficient
is \((-1)^{d-1}(d-1)!/(n)_d\ne0\); the other terms use
strictly lower-degree generators. It is therefore the
explicit invertible triangular algebra morphism \(\Psi_n\).
Finally \(p_n\) is faithful on the required component
by (OI.14).
