Every factor of (OI.16) is injective there, so \(h_{a,n}\)
is injective on the complete highest multiplicity space
and hence the whole isotypic component.
The scalar-one transpose pairing SR.5–SR.6 identifies
this rank with that of \(h_{n,a}\), proving (OI.2).
With both \(a,n\ge M\), apply the same argument in both
directions; this proves the actual isomorphism and (OI.3).

## 5. An explicit positive varying-width family

For every
\[
\boxed{a\ge5,\qquad w=4\ {\rm or}\ w\ge6,\qquad n\ge w+1,}
\tag{OI.18}
\]
the partition
\[
\lambda=(an-w-4,w,3,1)
\]
has
\[
\boxed{\operatorname{mult}_\lambda\operatorname{im}h_{n,a}
       =a_{a,n}^{\lambda}\ge1}
\tag{OI.19}
\]
in every dimension at least four.

Here is an explicit nonzero highest vector proving the
last inequality. In centered three-dimensional rows
\(z_i=w_i-\bar w\), take the polynomial
\(F_{a,3}\) of R-040 HC.7–HC.8:
\[
S=\sum_i z_i z_i^t,\quad C_{pqr}=\sum_i z_{ip}z_{iq}z_{ir},
\quad
A_{ij,kl}=\det(S)((S^{-1})_{ik}(S^{-1})_{jl}
                        -(S^{-1})_{il}(S^{-1})_{jk}),
\]
\[
F_{a,3}=\sum_{i,j,k}
 (C_{11i}C_{2jk}-C_{12i}C_{1jk})A_{ij,k3}.
\tag{OI.20}
\]
The \(A\)'s are signed complementary minors, so this is
polynomial even at singular \(S\). The complete
HC.7–HC.14 calculation proves its highest weight
\((4,3,1)\), its translation and slot invariance, and
its nonzero value for every \(a\ge5\).
Put \(P_d=\sum_i z_{i1}^{\,d}\).
Both \(P_2\) and \(P_3\) are nonzero invariant highest
polynomials of weight \((2)\) and \((3)\), respectively.
For even \(w\ge4\) use
\[
F_{a,3}P_2^{(w-4)/2};
\]
for odd \(w\ge7\) use
\[
F_{a,3}P_3P_2^{(w-7)/2}.
\tag{OI.21}
\]
The raising operators are derivations, so these
products are highest of weight \((w,3,1)\).
The centered row polynomial algebra is an integral
domain, so they are nonzero.
Their row degrees are at most \(w\), either from their
column realization or directly from the factors.
Formula TM.4 homogenizes them in every \(n\ge w+1\).

For even \(w\), the tail has two odd parts; for odd
\(w\), it has three. In both cases
\(D=w+4\), \(t=w\), and \(M=w+1\), so (OI.2) applies.
The first-row inequality is explicit:
\(an-w-4\ge5(w+1)-w-4=4w+1\ge w\).
Thus every displayed parameter is a valid partition
and every nonvanishing statement is literal.

## 6. Transport and independent verification

All exterior restrictions, congruences, Young maps,
rational averages, and split-moment inverses have been
specified over \(\mathbb Q\). They extend to any
characteristic-zero field. Naturality gives the same
multiplicity map in every finite dimension supporting
\(S_\lambda V\).

The exact graded geometric map is the Chow pullback
R-037 EP.3–EP.5, with scalar-one homogeneous piece EP.4.
Its frame-torsor associated map and the representation
\(K_0\) dictionary are exactly those recorded in R-036 §5:
SGA 6 VI Theorem 3.3; SGA 6 V Proposition 4.2,
Definition 4.4, Proposition 4.8 and Corollary 4.9;
SGA 3 I §4.5 and Propositions 4.7.2–4.7.3;
EGA II 2.4.1–2.4.2 and 2.5.2/2.5.4.

The independent script verify_one_row_improved_stability.py
checks every tail of degree at most twelve satisfying
the stated parity and odd-part conditions, including five
auxiliary width-one zero cases outside the theorem's \(t\ge2\)
range.
It averages the literal Schur character on the permutation
standard representation at row count \(M\), and separately
expands the complete formal moment algebra by original
cycle-index/Murnaghan–Nakayama characters.
All **96** exact comparisons pass: **91** lie in the stated
width range and five are the auxiliary zero cases.
All **22** positive multiplicities lie in the stated range.
The receipt is
ONE_ROW_IMPROVED_STABILITY_CHECK.tsv.
This check concerns the faithful-evaluation dimensions;
the actual rank assertion is proved by (OI.7),
(OI.13), and (OI.16), with their full normalizations.



# Odd-part occupancy and an actual canonical-map bound

## R-049. A refined bound for every tail

Let \(a,n\ge2\), let \(\nu\) be a nonempty partition of
size \(D\) and width \(t=\nu_1\ge2\), and require
\(\lambda=(an-D,\nu)\) to be a partition.
Let \(o\) be the number of odd parts of \(\nu\), counted
with multiplicity, and put
\[
\epsilon=t\bmod2,\qquad
q=\left\lceil\frac{o-\epsilon}{3}\right\rceil,\qquad
M(\nu)=\left\lfloor\frac{D+t-q}{2}\right\rfloor.
\tag{OO.1}
\]
Then \(q\ge0\), \(M(\nu)\ge t\), and for every \(n\ge M(\nu)\)
the actual normalized map
\[
h_{n,a}:\operatorname{Sym}^n(\operatorname{Sym}^aV)
 \longrightarrow\operatorname{Sym}^a(\operatorname{Sym}^nV)
\]
is surjective on its entire \(\lambda\)-isotypic component:
\[
\boxed{\operatorname{mult}_\lambda\operatorname{im}h_{n,a}
       =a_{a,n}^{\lambda}.}
\tag{OO.2}
\]
The assertion holds over every characteristic-zero field
and in all finite dimensions. The component is zero below
dimension \(\ell(\lambda)\).

For \(a,n\ge M(\nu)\), the actual map is an isomorphism on
this component, with the formal centered-moment multiplicity
(TM.5). The explicit proof below supplies every restriction
and polarization morphism. It includes R-048's one-row
ranges and produces improvements of arbitrarily many rows
on the positive family in §5.
The starting numerical bound in R-046 is explicitly attributed
there to Sarkar Theorem 6.4; no historical priority claim
is made here.

## 1. The actual centered and uncentered restriction maps

For \(S\ge s\ge1\), set
\[
E_S=\mathbb Q^S,\quad
\bar e_S=S^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^S e_i,\quad
W_S=\mathbf1^\perp,\quad P_Se_i=e_i-\bar e_S,
\]
and analogously at \(s\). Define the following linear map:
\[
\widetilde q:E_S\longrightarrow E_s,\qquad
\widetilde q(e_i)=
 \begin{cases}e_i,&i\le s,\\ \bar e_s,&i>s.\end{cases}
\tag{OO.3}
\]
It satisfies, by direct summation,
\[
\widetilde q(\bar e_S)=\bar e_s,\qquad
\widetilde q(P_Se_i)=
 \begin{cases}P_se_i,&i\le s,\\0,&i>s.\end{cases}
\tag{OO.4}
\]
Thus its restriction to \(W_S\) is exactly the orthogonal
transpose \(q:W_S\to W_s\) of zero-padding used in TM.12.
The map (OO.3) is equivariant for \(S_s\) acting on the first
\(s\) rows, and therefore sends \(S_S\)-invariants to
\(S_s\)-invariants after taking exterior powers.

Fix \(T=\mathbb Q^t\), and write
\[
C_s=(\Lambda(E_s\otimes T))^{S_s},\qquad
B_s=(\Lambda(W_s\otimes T))^{S_s}.
\]
The specified vector \(\bar e_s\) identifies the literal
trivial-line factor with \(T\), giving
\[
C_s=\Lambda T\otimes B_s.
\tag{OO.5}
\]
Under these actual decompositions, (OO.3) induces precisely
\[
\Lambda(\widetilde q\otimes1)|_{C_S}
 =1_{\Lambda T}\otimes
          \bigl(\Lambda(q\otimes1)|_{B_S}\bigr).
\tag{OO.6}
\]
In particular this statement uses the displayed averaged
extra-row images, not coordinate deletion.

The centered map in (OO.6) sends every row power sum to
its counterpart with scalar one, by (OO.4).
The finite signed row-orbit spanning proof TM.8/TM.12
therefore makes it surjective, and so the uncentered map
is surjective as well. There is the actual graded
\(GL(T)\)-equivariant injection
\[
\ker(B_S\to B_s)_D
 \hookrightarrow \ker(C_S\to C_s)_D,\qquad v\longmapsto1\otimes v.
\tag{OO.7}
\]

The row-orbit decomposition of \(C_s\) is
\[
C_s=
\bigoplus_{\substack{e_0+\cdots+e_t=s\\e_i\ge0}}
 \bigotimes_{i\ {\rm even},\,i\ge2}
       \operatorname{Sym}^{e_i}(\Lambda^iT)
 \ \otimes\
 \bigotimes_{i\ {\rm odd}}
       \Lambda^{e_i}(\Lambda^iT).
\tag{OO.8}
\]
It comes from ordered-row exterior multiplication and
rational symmetrization with the literal Koszul signs;
the \(e_0\) unit factor is one-dimensional.
For a fixed tuple of nonempty row counts, the same module
occurs at every \(s\ge k=\sum_{i\ge1}e_i\).
It follows that the character difference
\([C_S]-[C_s]\) is exactly the sum of the row-orbit module
characters with \(s<k\le S\).
Surjectivity of (OO.6) makes this the character of its kernel.
We use this equality of characters; those omitted row-orbit
modules are not asserted to be literal kernel summands
for the particular map (OO.3).

## 2. The alternating highest-weight bound for each occupied tuple

For a rational \(GL(T)\) highest weight
\(\alpha=(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_t)\), define
\[
A(\alpha)=\alpha_1-\alpha_2+\alpha_3-\cdots
                         +(-1)^{t-1}\alpha_t .
\tag{OO.9}
\]
The paired-row decomposition OI.8, proved there by explicit
upper-unipotent Pfaffian elimination, says that every
constituent of \(\operatorname{Sym}^{e_2}(\Lambda^2T)\)
has \(A(\alpha)=0\).
Tensoring with \(\det T\) adds \(\epsilon\) to this number.

Consider one nonzero summand of (OO.8), of scalar degree
\(D\), with \(k\) occupied rows. Its singleton factor is
\(\Lambda^{e_1}T\), with \(e_1\le t\). Put \(u=t-e_1\).
The perfect exterior pairing gives the actual isomorphism
\[
\Lambda^{e_1}T=\det T\otimes\Lambda^uT^*.
\tag{OO.10}
\]
Every other factor at \(i\ge3\), whether symmetric or
exterior, injects into
\((\Lambda^iT)^{\otimes e_i}\) by its normalized averaging
or signed averaging projector. Thus each constituent of
the row-orbit module occurs in
\[
\det T\otimes\Lambda^uT^*\otimes
 \operatorname{Sym}^{e_2}(\Lambda^2T)
 \otimes\bigotimes_{i\ge3}(\Lambda^iT)^{\otimes e_i}.
\tag{OO.11}
\]
All these are explicit tensor maps.

The exterior Pieri maps add a vertical \(i\)-strip;
their dual maps remove a vertical \(u\)-strip.
They are the column insertion or contraction maps followed
by the rational Young projectors. The dual version also
follows immediately from (OO.10) and the usual exterior
Pieri map, with its determinant twist retained.
Each added or removed box changes (OO.9) by \(1\) or \(-1\).
Starting from a paired constituent in (OO.11), every possible
final highest weight \(\gamma\) therefore satisfies
\[
A(\gamma)\le
 \epsilon+u+\sum_{i\ge3}i e_i.
\tag{OO.12}
\]
This argument applies as written to the intermediate
rational highest weights as well; their individual last
entries need not be nonnegative.

The exact degree and occupancy identities are
\[
D=e_1+2e_2+\sum_{i\ge3}i e_i,\qquad
k=e_1+e_2+\sum_{i\ge3}e_i,
\]
hence
\[
D+t-2k=u+\sum_{i\ge3}(i-2)e_i.
\tag{OO.13}
\]
For every \(i\ge3\), \(i\le3(i-2)\), and \(u\le3u\).
Equations (OO.12)–(OO.13) imply
\[
\boxed{A(\gamma)\le\epsilon+3(D+t-2k).}
\tag{OO.14}
\]

For \(\gamma=\nu^t\), the alternating sum \(A(\gamma)\)
is exactly \(o\): a row of \(\nu\) of length \(j\)
contributes \(1-1+\cdots+(-1)^{j-1}\), equal to one
at odd \(j\) and zero at even \(j\).
Thus every row-orbit module containing \(S_{\nu^t}T\)
has
\[
D+t-2k\ge
 \left\lceil\frac{o-\epsilon}{3}\right\rceil=q,
\qquad
k\le M(\nu).
\tag{OO.15}
\]
This is the asserted occupied-row bound.

Finally \(o\ge\epsilon\), since the largest part supplies
an odd part when \(t\) is odd.
After removing one largest part, the remaining degree
\(D-t\) bounds the number \(o-\epsilon\) of remaining
odd parts. Therefore
\[
0\le q\le o-\epsilon\le D-t,\qquad
M(\nu)\ge t.
\tag{OO.16}
\]
This includes \(q=0\) and all small parameter endpoints.

## 3. Faithful centered evaluation at the refined row count

For \(S\ge s\ge M(\nu)\), (OO.15) says that no omitted
row-orbit term in the character difference \(C_S-C_s\)
contains \(S_{\nu^t}T\) in degree \(D\).
The kernel character in §1 has zero multiplicity there.
The actual injection (OO.7) gives the same vanishing for
the centered kernel.

Skew Cauchy identifies that multiplicity map with
\[
S_\nu(q):(S_\nu W_S)^{S_S}
          \longrightarrow(S_\nu W_s)^{S_s}.
\tag{OO.17}
\]
It is therefore an isomorphism.
In the ordinary Cauchy decomposition the map is again
the identical Schur map \(S_\nu(q)\), because the tensor
Young projectors commute with every tensor power of \(q\).

Take \(S\ge\max(s,D)\). The centered power-sum evaluation
\(p_S\) of TM.6 is an isomorphism through degree \(D\),
by the full equality-partition triangular-basis proof.
Its generator identity with \(q\) is scalar one.
Consequently
\[
\boxed{p_s\text{ is an isomorphism on the }S_\nu
       \text{ component for every }s\ge M(\nu).}
\tag{OO.18}
\]
No dimension comparison is used without the specified
surjection and its kernel.

## 4. The actual canonical map

For \(n\ge M(\nu)\ge t\), every \(S_\nu W_a\) invariant
extends to its homogeneous highest polynomial by TM.4.
The separate row-degree bound \(t\) follows from the
column antisymmetrizer, exactly as in TM.4/OI.15.

The normalized opposite canonical map is the literal
composition
\[
h_{a,n}|_\nu=p_n\Psi_nE_a.
\tag{OO.19}
\]
The independent-row polarization \(E_a\) is injective,
including after \(L(1)=1\) and mean-zero restriction,
by TM.14.
The split-moment substitution \(\Psi_n\) is the complete
set-partition expression TM.16/OI.17. Its degree-\(d\)
leading coefficient is
\((-1)^{d-1}(d-1)!/(n)_d\), nonzero for \(2\le d\le t\),
and its other terms use lower-degree generators.
It is the explicit triangular automorphism proved in
TM.17. The final factor is injective on the precise
component by (OO.18).
Thus the composition is injective on the entire
highest multiplicity space, with no scalar omitted.
The scalar-one transpose identity SR.5–SR.6 proves
(OO.2). Applying it in both directions gives the
two-sided isomorphism range stated at the beginning.

## 5. Positive hook families with unbounded row improvement

Let
\[
r\ge1,\quad a\ge r+2,\quad u,v\ge0,\quad
t_0=\frac{r^2+3r+4}{2},\quad t=t_0+2u+3v.
\tag{OO.20}
\]
For every
\[
n\ge t+\left\lfloor
                \frac{r-\lceil r/3\rceil}{2}\right\rfloor
\]
the actual map reaches the complete target component
\[
\boxed{\lambda=(an-t-r,t,1^r),\qquad
 \operatorname{mult}_\lambda\operatorname{im}h_{n,a}
 =a_{a,n}^{\lambda}\ge1.}
\tag{OO.21}
\]
These statements hold in every dimension at least \(r+2\).
The partition is automatic:
\(n\ge t\), \(a\ge r+2\), and
\(an-t-r\ge(r+1)t-r\ge t\).

Here is the actual invariant tensor proving positivity.
On \(E=W_a\), with coordinates \(x_i\) satisfying
\(\sum_i x_i=0\), put
\[
p_d(x)=\sum_{i=1}^a x_i^d,\qquad
\Omega_r=\iota_x(dp_2\wedge dp_3\wedge\cdots\wedge dp_{r+2}).
\tag{OO.22}
\]
The symbol \(\iota_x\) is contraction with the Euler
vector \(x\). This polynomial \(r\)-form is invariant
under \(S_a\), has coefficient degree \(t_0\), and
satisfies \(\iota_x\Omega_r=0\).

To identify its exact Schur module, exterior Pieri gives
\[
\operatorname{Sym}^{t_0}E^*\otimes\Lambda^rE^*
=S_{(t_0+1,1^{r-1})}E^*
 \oplus S_{(t_0,1^r)}E^*.
\]
Contraction \(\iota_x\) maps the first summand nontrivially
to the equal Schur summand in
\(\operatorname{Sym}^{t_0+1}E^*\otimes\Lambda^{r-1}E^*\):
on its highest polynomial
\(x_1^{t_0}dx_1\wedge\cdots\wedge dx_r\), the
\(x_1^{t_0+1}dx_2\wedge\cdots\wedge dx_r\) term is nonzero.
The second Schur summand is absent from that codomain,
so contraction kills it.
Complete reducibility and the displayed multiplicity-one
Pieri maps show
\[
\ker\iota_x=S_{(t_0,1^r)}E^*.
\tag{OO.23}
\]
The rational invariant dot form identifies \(E^*\) with
\(E\) as an \(S_a\)-module.

For an explicit nonzero evaluation take \(a_0=r+2\),
\(x_i=i-(a_0+1)/2\) on the first \(a_0\) rows and
zero thereafter. Let \(b_j=e_j-e_{a_0}\).
The value on \(b_2,\ldots,b_{a_0-1}\) is
\[
\begin{aligned}
\Omega_r(x)(b_2,\ldots,b_{a_0-1})
 &=x_1\det\bigl[d(x_j^{d-1}-x_{a_0}^{d-1})\bigr]_{
                   2\le d\le a_0,\ 1\le j<a_0}\\
 &=(-1)^{a_0}\frac{a_0-1}{2}\,a_0!\!
                   \prod_{1\le i<j\le a_0}(x_j-x_i)\ne0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{OO.24}
\]
To check the second equality, factor \(x_j-x_{a_0}\)
from each column; the remaining row polynomials are monic
of degrees zero through \(a_0-2\), so their determinant
is the Vandermonde on \(x_1,\ldots,x_{a_0-1}\).
The remaining factors give the displayed sign and \(a_0!\).
All \(x_j-x_i=j-i\) are nonzero. This calculation also
proves nonvanishing after adding zero rows.

Multiply (OO.22) by \(p_2^u p_3^v\).
Both scalar polynomials are nonzero on \(E\) for \(a\ge3\),
and the polynomial form module is free over its integral
domain of coefficients. The product is therefore nonzero,
still horizontal, with coefficient degree \(t\).
The same exact contraction argument gives
\(S_{(t,1^r)}E^*\). Evaluating the form on \(r\)
auxiliary centered columns realizes its highest polynomial:
raising a later column into the first inserts \(x\)
and gives zero; raising between the later columns repeats
an exterior argument and gives zero.
This specifies the actual highest-vector map.

Its separate row degrees are at most \(t\) by the Young
column bound. Homogenization TM.4 supplies a nonzero
target highest vector in every asserted inner degree.
For \(\nu=(t,1^r)\), its odd-part count is
\(o=r+(t\bmod2)\), so \(q=\lceil r/3\rceil\).
Formula (OO.1) is exactly the bound in (OO.21).

In particular, choose any \(s\ge0\) and set
\[
r=6s+2,\qquad
t=18s^2+21s+7+2u+3v,\qquad
a\ge6s+4,\qquad n\ge t+2s .
\tag{OO.25}
\]
Then (OO.21) is a positive full-image family.
The previous uniform threshold for its tail is
\(t+3s+1\); the displayed actual-map proof reaches
\(s+1\) additional rows below that value.
For example \(s=1,u=v=0,a=10,n=48\) gives the literal
positive component \((426,46,1^8)\).

## 6. Transport and independent finite checks

All maps above are rational. The two mean vectors in
(OO.3), the exact exterior duality, Young projectors,
invariant averages and triangular moment inverses have
nonzero denominators in the displayed ranges.
Naturality extends the result to each supporting finite
rank and every characteristic-zero field.

The exact geometric map is the Chow pullback R-037
EP.3–EP.5, with scalar-one degree piece EP.4.
The frame-torsor and representation-\(K_0\) transport
is the fixed dictionary R-036 §5:
SGA 6 VI Theorem 3.3; SGA 6 V Proposition 4.2,
Definition 4.4, Proposition 4.8 and Corollary 4.9;
SGA 3 I §4.5 and Propositions 4.7.2–4.7.3;
EGA II 2.4.1–2.4.2 and 2.5.2/2.5.4.

The independent script verify_odd_part_occupancy_stability.py
compares the literal standard-representation Schur average
at \(M(\nu)\) with the separately expanded formal moment
character for every tail of degree two through fourteen
and width at least two.
All **493** comparisons pass; **248** use an improved
row count, and **58** of those have positive multiplicity.
The exact receipt is ODD_PART_OCCUPANCY_STABILITY_CHECK.tsv.
These checks concern character values. The actual rank
is proved by (OO.3)–(OO.7), (OO.17) and (OO.19).

The separate script verify_odd_part_hook_form.py evaluates the
literal contracted wedge of power-sum differentials and independently
compares its determinant with (OO.24), for \(r=1,\ldots,10\)
and row counts \(a=r+2,r+4\).
All **20** exact nonzero scalars pass, including the added-zero-row
realization. The receipt is ODD_PART_HOOK_FORM_SCALAR_CHECK.tsv.



# Actual canonical isomorphisms on every hook tail

## R-050. Complete hook-tail rank law

Let \(a,n\ge1\), \(t\ge1\), \(r\ge0\), and require
\[
\lambda=(an-t-r,t,1^r)
\tag{HM.1}
\]
to be a partition. Over every characteristic-zero field, the actual
normalized Foulkes–Howe maps in both directions are isomorphisms on
their complete \(\lambda\)-isotypic components:
\[
\boxed{\begin{gathered}
h_{a,n}:\operatorname{Sym}^{a}(\operatorname{Sym}^{n}V)
\longrightarrow\operatorname{Sym}^{n}(\operatorname{Sym}^{a}V),\\
\operatorname{mult}_{\lambda}\operatorname{im}h_{a,n}
=a_{a,n}^{\lambda}=a_{n,a}^{\lambda}
=\operatorname{mult}_{\lambda}\operatorname{im}h_{n,a}.
\end{gathered}}
\tag{HM.2}
\]
Every multiplicity is zero below dimension \(r+2\).
The proof uses the actual subspace of highest polynomials with
separate row degree at most \(n\); it does not impose \(n\ge t\).

The known ingredients are identified precisely. The hook-specialization
identity is Langley–Remmel, *The plethysm \(s_\lambda[s_\mu]\) at hook
and near-hook shapes*, Theorem 3.1 and its complete proof, printed
pp.6–8 (2004), DOI https://doi.org/10.37236/1764. Its primary PDF is
https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/v11i1r11/pdf.
The invariant-form input is Solomon, *Invariants of finite reflection
groups*, §3, unnumbered Theorem p.59, proof pp.59–61, and formula (4)+p.62 (1963), DOI https://doi.org/10.1017/S0027763000011028.
Its primary PDF is
https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/160748DDB7C9D17C5379F6FF65BB5B98/S0027763000011028a.pdf/invariants-of-finite-reflection-groups.pdf.
The precise special cases and all comparison maps used here are proved
below. The two-row case \(r=0\) has the known canonical Hermite
interpretation already located in R-038's opening. No historical
priority claim is made for any coefficient identity or rank statement.
The present result is the explicitly proved canonical-map form (HM.2).

## 1. A finite power-sum morphism generated in degrees at most the row count

For \(s\ge1\), put
\[
W_s=\{(x_1,\ldots,x_s):\sum_i x_i=0\},\qquad
P_s e_i=e_i-s^{-1}\sum_j e_j,
\]
and, for an auxiliary space \(U\), define
\[
\mathcal M_{\le s}(U)=
\operatorname{Sym}\!\left(\bigoplus_{d=2}^{s}\operatorname{Sym}^dU\right).
\]
The empty sum at \(s=1\) gives \(\mathbb Q\).
The degree of a generator in \(\operatorname{Sym}^dU\) is \(d\).
Define the actual graded algebra morphism
\[
\begin{split}
\mathsf p_s:\mathcal M_{\le s}(U)&\longrightarrow
\bigl(\operatorname{Sym}(W_s\otimes U)\bigr)^{S_s},\\
u_1\cdots u_d&\longmapsto
\sum_{i=1}^s(P_s e_i\otimes u_1)\cdots(P_s e_i\otimes u_d).
\end{split}
\tag{HM.3}
\]
The scalar on each polarized generator is one.

This map is surjective in every degree. To see the finite bound on
generators directly, first work with \(s\) uncentered vector rows.
The equality-partition expansion of a product of power sums expresses
every row-orbit sum in polarized power sums of unrestricted degrees:
its distinct-row term is the desired orbit sum times the nonzero
factorial for repeated row types; every other term has fewer occupied
rows. Induction on that number proves generation.

For a formal covector \(\ell\), let \(y_i=\ell(w_i)\). Write
\(q_d(\ell)=\sum_i y_i^d\) and let \(e_j(\ell)\) be the elementary
symmetric polynomials in these \(s\) quantities. The explicit Newton
recursion is
\[
j e_j=\sum_{i=1}^{j}(-1)^{i-1}e_{j-i}q_i,
\qquad e_0=1\quad(1\le j\le s).
\tag{HM.4}
\]
The polynomial \(\prod_i(X-y_i)\) gives, for \(d>s\),
\[
q_d=e_1q_{d-1}-e_2q_{d-2}+\cdots+(-1)^{s-1}e_s q_{d-s}.
\tag{HM.5}
\]
Thus each \(q_d(\ell)\) is a specified polynomial in
\(q_1(\ell),\ldots,q_s(\ell)\). Taking every coefficient in the
coordinates of \(\ell\) proves that all polarized power sums are
generated in degrees at most \(s\). The actual projection to \(W_s\)
kills degree one and sends the remaining generators to (HM.3).
Rational averaging, or the literal fixed-line splitting, proves
surjectivity after this projection. This establishes the asserted
finite-degree generating map without an unspecified change of algebra.

## 2. Hook multiplicities in the source of (HM.3)

Fix a nonzero moment multidegree
\(\beta=(\beta_2,\ldots,\beta_s)\), and put
\[
D=\sum_{d=2}^{s}d\beta_d,\qquad
J=\{d:\beta_d>0\},\qquad k=|J|.
\]
The corresponding actual tensor factor is
\(\bigotimes_d\operatorname{Sym}^{\beta_d}(\operatorname{Sym}^dU)\),
with character \(\prod_d h_{\beta_d}[h_d]\).
The specialization \(1-z\) is the ring homomorphism specified on power
sums by \(p_j\mapsto1-z^j\). In particular the minus sign has its
virtual-alphabet meaning, with this displayed value for every \(j\).

The generating function
\[
\sum_{d\ge0}h_d[1-z]v^d=\frac{1-zv}{1-v}
\]
gives \(h_d[1-z]=1-z\) for \(d\ge1\). Adams substitution commutes
with this identity: explicitly,
\(p_j[h_d][1-z]=h_d[1-z^j]=1-z^j\).
Consequently, for every \(b,d\ge1\),
\[
h_b[h_d][1-z]=1-z.
\tag{HM.6}
\]
The skew-Schur coproduct, obtained by splitting the alphabet in the
Young-tableau construction, gives
\(s_\eta[X-Y]=\sum_{\rho\subseteq\eta}
s_\rho[X](-1)^{|\eta/\rho|}s_{(\eta/\rho)'}[Y]\).
At \(X=1,Y=z\), a nonzero term requires \(\rho\) to be a row and
\(\eta/\rho\) to be a vertical strip. These are exactly the hook shapes.
For the hook \(\eta=(D-r,1^r)\), the two possible rows have lengths
\(D-r\) and \(D-r-1\), including the empty row at its endpoint. Hence
\[
s_\eta[1-z]=
\begin{cases}(-z)^r(1-z),&\eta=(D-r,1^r),\\0,&\eta\text{ is not a hook}.
\end{cases}
\tag{HM.7}
\]
Equations (HM.6)–(HM.7), in this fixed degree \(D\), compare
\((1-z)^k\) with \((1-z)\sum_r m_r(-z)^r\). They prove the exact
nonnegative multiplicity
\[
\boxed{
[S_{(D-r,1^r)}U:
 \bigotimes_d\operatorname{Sym}^{\beta_d}(\operatorname{Sym}^dU)]
=\binom{k-1}{r}.}
\tag{HM.8}
\]
The value is zero for \(r>k-1\). This derives the needed special case
of the cited hook theorem and specifies the character substitution.

## 3. Hook multiplicities in the target and faithfulness of the actual map

Here is a direct form of the invariant differential-form calculation.
On \(\mathbb Q^s\), the basic power sums \(p_1,\ldots,p_s\) have
Jacobian \(s!\prod_{i<j}(x_j-x_i)\). Every polynomial differential
form therefore has a unique rational expansion in wedges of the
\(dp_j\). For an invariant form, wedge with the complementary
differentials to extract one coefficient. Its numerator, relative to
\(dx_1\wedge\cdots\wedge dx_s\), is alternating, and is divisible
by every \(x_j-x_i\); the quotient by the Jacobian is a symmetric
polynomial. This proves existence and uniqueness over the invariant
polynomial ring. Split off the mean coordinate and its differential.
On \(W_s\), the resulting invariant form algebra is
\[
I_s\otimes\Lambda(dq_2,\ldots,dq_s),\qquad
I_s=\mathbb Q[q_2,\ldots,q_s],\qquad q_d=\sum_i x_i^d.
\tag{HM.9}
\]
The mean splitting and the triangular Newton identities are the actual
maps in this special case of Solomon's theorem.

Identify \(W_s\) with its dual by its invariant rational dot product.
Let \(\partial=\iota_x\) be contraction by the Euler vector, and set
\(\xi_d=dq_d/d\). Then
\[
\partial\xi_d=q_d,\qquad \deg q_d=\deg\xi_d=d.
\tag{HM.10}
\]
On \(\operatorname{Sym}^tW_s^*\otimes\Lambda^rW_s^*\), the kernel
of \(\partial\) is the actual Young image of \(S_{(t,1^r)}W_s^*\).
For \(r>0\), exterior Pieri gives the two shapes
\((t+1,1^{r-1})\) and \((t,1^r)\). The first highest vector has
a nonzero contraction term; the second shape is absent from the
target. This specifies the kernel through the rational row and column
Young projectors. At \(r=0\), retain positive polynomial degree.
The equality \(\partial d+d\partial=D\) also gives the explicit
contracting homotopy \(D^{-1}d\) in positive total degree.
Taking invariants is exact by the actual averaging projector.

Give \(q_d\) and \(\xi_d\) the same \(d\)-th unit multidegree.
For \(\beta\ne0\) and \(J,k\) as above, choose \(i=\min J\).
The multidegree-\(\beta\) complex has basis
\(q^{\beta-\mathbf1_S}\xi_S\) for \(S\subseteq J\), and its
differential is exterior contraction \(v_j\mapsto1\).
An explicit basis for the exterior-degree-\(r\) kernel is
\[
q^\beta\bigwedge_{j\in T}
 \left(\frac{\xi_j}{q_j}-\frac{\xi_i}{q_i}\right),
\qquad T\subseteq J\setminus\{i\},\quad |T|=r.
\tag{HM.11}
\]
These are polynomials: each surviving wedge term has at most one
factor of each denominator, and its exponent in \(\beta\) is positive.
In the basis \(v_i,v_j-v_i\), contraction kills exactly the exterior
algebra on the latter vectors. This proves both spanning and
independence, with dimension \(\binom{k-1}{r}\).

Summing over \(\beta\) proves that the target of (HM.3) has exactly
the hook multiplicity computed in (HM.8). The ordinary Cauchy maps
identify that multiplicity with \((S_{(t,1^r)}W_s)^{S_s}\); these
are the same normalized Young projectors used in R-046. Since (HM.3)
has already been proved surjective, equality of these dimensions proves
faithfulness of this specified morphism:
\[
\boxed{\mathsf p_s\text{ is an isomorphism on every hook }
S_{(t,1^r)}U\text{ component, for every }s\ge1.}
\tag{HM.12}
\]
There is no multigrading assertion about \(\mathsf p_s\): the two
multigraded counts establish equality after summation in total degree.
The actual isomorphism is the power-sum morphism (HM.3).

For later use its common dimension is the explicit finite sum
\[
H_s(D,r)=
\sum_{\substack{\beta_2,\ldots,\beta_s\ge0\\
                 \sum d\beta_d=D}}
\binom{|\{d:\beta_d>0\}|-1}{r},\qquad D>0.
\tag{HM.13}
\]
In particular all terms vanish when \(r\ge s-1\).

## 4. Exact canonical factorization with its actual row-degree bound

Let \(F\) be any highest polynomial in
\(\operatorname{Sym}^a(\operatorname{Sym}^nV)\) of weight (HM.1).
Write its slots as \((x_i,y_i)\). On the dense chart \(\prod_i x_i\ne0\),
\[
F=\left(\prod_i x_i\right)^n f(y_1/x_1,\ldots,y_a/x_a).
\tag{HM.14}
\]
The actual polynomial \(F\) has separate slot degree \(n\), so
\(f\) has separate row degree at most \(n\). The first-coordinate
highest equations say exactly that \(f\) is invariant under common
translations. Slot symmetry gives \(S_a\)-invariance, and the remaining
highest weight is the hook \((t,1^r)\). Thus (HM.14) is an injection
into the relevant centered invariant space, with the stated row bound.
At \(n<t\) it is this actual bounded subspace that is used.

Let \(A_n=\mathbb Q[y]_{\le n}\). The independent-row morphism is
\[
E_a(f)(L)=L^{\otimes a}f,\qquad L(1)=1,\quad L(y)=0.
\tag{HM.15}
\]
It is injective on common-translation-invariant polynomials.
Indeed, for a normalized functional of mean \(v\), replace it by
\(L_0(p)=L(p(y-v))\); translation invariance preserves its value on
\(f\). Homogeneity in \(L\) restores all \(L(1)\ne0\), a dense
open set. Diagonal polarization of the resulting homogeneous degree
\(a\) polynomial recovers \(f\). The separate degree bound puts the
image in \(\mathcal M_{\le n}(U)\), preserving the exact hook type.

For centered split-factor rows \(w_1,\ldots,w_n\), put
\(p_d=\sum_iw_i^{\otimes d}\). The normalized tensor pairing gives
the order-\(d\) moment
\[
\mu_d=\frac1{(n)_d}
\sum_{\substack{i_1,\ldots,i_d\text{ distinct}}}
w_{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes w_{i_d}
=\frac1{(n)_d}
\sum_{\substack{\pi\in\Pi([d])\\|B|\ge2\ \forall B}}
\prod_{B\in\pi}(-1)^{|B|-1}(|B|-1)!\,p_{|B|}.
\tag{HM.16}
\]
All \(2\le d\le n\) are allowed. The first equality follows from
the monomial pairing: a coordinate monomial of lower degree \(d\)
and multiplicity vector \(\alpha\) is multiplied by
\((n-d)!\prod_j\alpha_j!/n!\). The second equality is the
set-partition inclusion–exclusion expansion, with the displayed
Möbius block factors; singleton blocks vanish after centering.
This is the same normalized pairing as TM.15–TM.16.

There is one single-block term, with scalar
\[
c_{n,d}=\frac{(-1)^{d-1}(d-1)!}{(n)_d}\ne0.
\]
Every other term uses smaller moment degrees. Therefore (HM.16)
defines the explicit graded equivariant automorphism
\(\Psi_n\) of \(\mathcal M_{\le n}(U)\), whose inverse successively
solves for the generators in degrees \(2,3,\ldots,n\).

Direct grid pairing now gives the exact dehomogenized canonical map
\[
\boxed{h_{a,n}F\quad\longleftrightarrow\quad
\mathsf p_n\,\Psi_n\,E_a(f).}
\tag{HM.17}
\]
Every scalar in this equality is fixed by (HM.16); there is no extra
factor. Subtracting the common row mean is an actual unipotent
substitution, so the identity on centered rows determines the entire
affine output. Multiplication by \((\prod_j x_j)^a\) restores the
homogeneous polynomial on the dense chart and hence everywhere.

The first map from right to left is injective by (HM.15), the middle
map is invertible, and the last is injective on the exact hook component
by (HM.12). Thus \(h_{a,n}\) is injective on the full highest
multiplicity space. Equivariance gives injectivity on the entire
\(\lambda\)-isotypic component. Interchanging \(a,n\) proves the
opposite injection. The two finite-dimensional multiplicity spaces
therefore have equal dimensions and both maps are bijective.
This proves (HM.2), including all unstable inner degrees.

The actual inverse on highest spaces is specified by (HM.17): use
the inverse of (HM.3) on its hook component, the recursive inverse
of (HM.16), and diagonal polarization inverse to (HM.15), then
homogenize by (HM.14). The first inverse can be implemented directly
on rational Young-projected monomial bases: evaluate (HM.3) on each
basis element and invert its now proved nonsingular rational matrix.
Bijectivity just proved ensures that the resulting formal expression
lies in the image of (HM.15), with its required row-degree bound.
This description does not assert that the two canonical maps are
mutual inverses.

## 5. An explicit unit family and the complete normalized scalar

Let \(m\ge2\), \(a,n\ge m\), and put
\[
T=\binom m2+1,\qquad D=\binom{m+1}{2}-1,
\qquad\lambda=(an-D,T,1^{m-2}).
\tag{HM.18}
\]
The first-row inequality follows from \(an\ge m^2=D+T\).
For \(s\ge m\) and rows \(z_i=(u_i,v_{i1},\ldots,v_{i,m-2})\), define
\[
\begin{split}
P_{s,m}(z)&=
\sum_{\substack{I\subseteq[s]\\|I|=m}}
\left(\prod_{\substack{i<j\\i,j\in I}}(u_j-u_i)\right)
\det\bigl[(1,u_i,v_{i1},\ldots,v_{i,m-2})\bigr]_{i\in I}.
\end{split}
\tag{HM.19}
\]
Both factors change by the same sign under reordering \(I\).
Their product and the sum are row symmetric. Differences and the
affine determinant prove common-translation invariance. Each factor
has separate row degree at most \(m-1\) and \(1\), respectively.
The determinant is the exterior highest tensor of weight
\((1^{m-1})\), while the Vandermonde uses only the first coordinate
and has degree \(\binom m2\). Hence their product is a highest
polynomial of tail weight \((T,1^{m-2})\) and separate row degree
at most \(m\), by the displayed determinant and upper-unipotent
column operations.

It is nonzero: on the moment-curve rows
\((u_i,u_i^2,\ldots,u_i^{m-1})\), with distinct rational \(u_i\),
every summand is the square of its nonzero Vandermonde. Thus
\[
F_{a,n;m}=\left(\prod_{i=1}^a x_i\right)^n
P_{a,m}(y_i/x_i)
\tag{HM.20}
\]
is an actual nonzero polynomial highest vector. Its weight is
(HM.18). Formula (HM.13) has exactly one contribution in degree
\(D\) and exterior leg \(m-2\): its support must have at least
\(m-1\) distinct degrees, whose least possible sum is
\(2+3+\cdots+m=D\). Equality forces these degrees to occur once
each. Consequently the entire centered highest space has dimension
one. The vector (HM.20) attains it in every \(a,n\ge m\), proving
that both plethysm multiplicities and the canonical rank are one.

Here is an independent direct calculation of the map scalar.
For a normalized mean-zero functional \(L\), define
\[
J_m(\mu)=
\det\bigl[L(u^p b_q)\bigr]_{
             1\le p\le m-1,\ 0\le q\le m-2},
\qquad(b_0,b_1,\ldots,b_{m-2})=(u,v_1,\ldots,v_{m-2}).
\tag{HM.21}
\]
In each row the entries are formal moments of degree \(p+1\).
Expanding both determinants in (HM.19) and pairing independent rows
gives \(m!\) times the determinant of their one-row pairings. Its
first row is \((1,0,\ldots,0)\), so the remaining determinant is
(HM.21). There are \(\binom am\) subsets. This proves exactly
\[
E_a(P_{a,m})=(a)_m J_m(\mu).
\tag{HM.22}
\]

For centered \(s\)-row power sums, append the degree-zero row to
the matrix with entries \(\sum_i u_i^p b_q(z_i)\), and append the
constant column. The top row is \((s,0,\ldots,0)\).
The ordinary rectangular Cauchy–Binet identity, with its increasing
subset convention, gives
\[
s J_m(p)=P_{s,m}.
\tag{HM.23}
\]
This also identifies the invariant Euler form exactly:
\(\iota_u(dq_2\wedge\cdots\wedge dq_m)=m!J_m(p)
=(m!/s)P_{s,m}\).

The hook component of \(\mathcal M_{\le n}\) in this degree is one
dimensional for every \(n\ge m\), as just proved, and \(J_m\)
is a nonzero vector in it by (HM.23). The substitution \(\Psi_n\)
acts there by the product of the single-block coefficients in
degrees \(2,\ldots,m\). Indeed its original multidegree, one
factor in each of those degrees, has that coefficient. Every term
using a lower-degree substitution loses its highest replaced degree
and cannot restore that multidegree. The one-dimensionality and
equivariance then give the entire identity, not only one coefficient.
Using (HM.22)–(HM.23) in (HM.17) proves
\[
\boxed{\begin{aligned}
h_{a,n}F_{a,n;m}&=C_m(a,n)F_{n,a;m},\\
C_m(a,n)&=
(-1)^{\binom m2}\frac{(a)_m}{n}\,
\frac{\prod_{j=1}^{m-1}j!}{\prod_{d=2}^{m}(n)_d}\ne0.
\end{aligned}}
\tag{HM.24}
\]
The reciprocal gives the complete unit-component inverse.
In the square case this simplifies by the displayed factorial
products to the exact scalar
\[
\boxed{C_m(m,m)=
(-1)^{\binom m2}\frac{\bigl(\prod_{j=1}^{m-1}j!\bigr)^2}
{(m!)^{m-1}}.}
\tag{HM.25}
\]
For \(m=2,3,4,5\), these values are respectively
\(-1/2,-1/9,1/96,1/2500\).
Thus the actual square map has a nonzero unit component of weight
\((T,T,1^{m-2})\) in every rank \(m\), with a specified preimage
and complete scalar.

## 6. Further positive ranks, endpoints, and transport

The earlier Euler-form family also improves without any bound
depending on the number of odd tail parts. Let
\[
r\ge1,\quad a\ge r+2,\quad u,v\ge0,\quad
t=\frac{r^2+3r+4}{2}+2u+3v,\quad n\ge t.
\tag{HM.26}
\]
In (HM.11), use support \(\{2,3,\ldots,r+2\}\), every exponent
one, and the full \(r\)-element exterior subset; multiply by
\(q_2^u q_3^v\). This gives a nonzero invariant hook tensor.
The column-wise row bound \(t\) from TM.4 makes its homogenization
polynomial at every \(n\ge t\). Its first row is at least \(t\),
since \((a-2)t\ge r\). Therefore the actual common rank is
\[
\operatorname{mult}_{(an-t-r,t,1^r)}\operatorname{im}h_{n,a}
=H_a(t+r,r)\ge1.
\tag{HM.27}
\]
These are stable Schur-functor multiplicities; a literal nonzero
component requires \(\dim V\ge r+2\).
The R-049 bound on this family was
\(t+\lfloor(r-\lceil r/3\rceil)/2\rfloor\). In particular
\(r=6s+2\) gives an improvement by \(2s\) rows at the positive
endpoint \(n=t\). The unit family (HM.18) reaches the smaller
actual endpoint \(a=n=m\) as well.

For \(t=1\), (HM.8) has no contributing multidegree:
\(D=r+1<2+\cdots+(r+2)\). Both actual components vanish.
For \(a=1\) or \(n=1\), the tensor map is the identity on
\(\operatorname{Sym}^{an}V\); every nonempty tail component is
zero. The empty tail has coefficient one and its pure-power map
has scalar one. These observations also follow from the empty
moment algebra at one row.

All averages, Young projectors, row projections, moment coefficients,
and inverses above are rational, with nonzero displayed denominators.
Naturality gives the actual maps in every finite dimension that
supports \(S_\lambda V\), and scalar extension gives every
characteristic-zero field. The graded coordinate-ring map is exactly
the Chow pullback R-037 EP.3–EP.5, with EP.4 its actual morphism.
The frame-torsor and representation-\(K_0\) transport uses the exact
SGA 6 VI Theorem3.3 and V §4, SGA 3 I §4, and EGA II §§2.4–2.5
locators and maps recorded in R-036 §5. Every rank assertion is
proved before that transport.

## 7. Executed independent checks

The reproducible script verify_hook_moment_faithfulness.py records:

- HOOK_MOMENT_FINITE_ROW_CHECK.tsv: all4,650 hooks of degrees1–30
  at row counts1–10. Direct cycle-eigenvalue complete/exterior
  characters and hook Jacobi–Trudi averaging agree with the
  independently counted support formula (HM.13).
- HOOK_MOMENT_MULTIDEGREE_CHECK.tsv: all729 hook comparisons
  for moment multidegrees of total degree2–12. Literal power-sum
  plethysm products and Murnaghan–Nakayama agree with (HM.8).
- HOOK_TAIL_RECIPROCITY_MN_CHECK.tsv: all457 valid hook-tail
  weights for \(2\le a\le n\le6\), with every leg up to the
  source length cutoff and every admissible second row. Both original
  plethysms agree, including181 positive pairs. These checks concern
  coefficients; the actual rank is proved by (HM.17).

The separate verify_hook_tail_canonical_scalar.py expands both
determinant permutations in (HM.19), pairs each resulting original
row monomial with the coefficients of an actual product of linear
forms, and uses its exact multinomial denominator. It does not call
the moment determinant on the literal side. All75 pairings in
HOOK_TAIL_CANONICAL_SCALAR_CHECK.tsv agree with (HM.24), for
\(m=2,3,4,5\), \(n=m,m+1,m+2\), two configurations, and
\(a=m,m+1,m+3\), plus \(m=n=6\) at those three outer degrees.
First coordinates are nonunit, including alternating signs, and the
target Vandermonde-square evaluation is nonzero in every sample.


# Current map ranges and the exact remaining transfer

## M-001. Canonical maps, coefficient inequalities, and the checked parameter ranges

Use the actual normalized grid morphism
\[
h_{b,a}:\operatorname{Sym}^{b}(\operatorname{Sym}^{a}V)
 \longrightarrow\operatorname{Sym}^{a}(\operatorname{Sym}^{b}V),
\qquad

The symbol `WG` on 133/006 is explicitly the group completion of the orthogonal-sum monoid of isometry classes. Write it `GW^⊕` here. Write `GW` for the quotient that also imposes the metabolic relation `[M]=[H(L)]` for a Lagrangian `L`. There is a concrete surjective ring map

\[
q:GW^\oplus\longrightarrow GW,
\quad [M,b]\longmapsto[M,b],
\]

with kernel generated by the differences `[M]-[H(L)]`. The corresponding forgetful maps land respectively in the split Green ring `K_0^⊕` and the exact Grothendieck ring `K_0`. ## A-001. Cote 133, scan 019: symmetric powers, subsets, and the supplied study's counterexample

**Statements on the page.** The page displays `σ_t(E)λ_{−t}(E)=1`, `λ_t(L)=1+tL`, `σ_t(L)=(1−tL)^{-1}`, `σ²(E)=E²−λ²(E)`, `σ²(E)=λ²(E)+E`, and `2λ²(E)+E=E²`. The last numerical check is `2 binom(d,2)+d=d²`. It also asks for `λ^i(xy)`.

For a locally free sheaf, the first four formulas are the standard exterior/symmetric-power identities in exact `K_0`. The short exact sequence

\[
0\longrightarrow\Lambda^2E\xrightarrow{u\wedge v\mapsto u\otimes v-v\otimes u}
E\otimes E\longrightarrow\operatorname{Sym}^2E\longrightarrow0
\]

is locally split as a sequence of underlying modules and proves the degree-two identity. Exterior-power operations on this exact `K_0` satisfy the universal special-λ identities; see SGA 6, V, Lemma 2.2.1 and VI, Theorem 3.3. The line identities follow directly from the one-dimensional tensor powers. These are known identities, not novelty claims.

**Refutation in the finite-set reading used by the supplied study.** Let `G=C_2` and let `E={0,1}` with the nonidentity element interchanging the points. In the Burnside ring `B(G)`, write `1` for the singleton. The unordered two-element subsets form `1`. The two-element multisets form `E+1`: two doubled points are interchanged and the mixed pair is fixed. Ordered pairs form two free orbits, so `E²=2E`. Consequently

\[
\lambda^2_{\rm subset}(E)=1,\qquad
\sigma^2_{\rm multiset}(E)=E+1,\qquad E^2=2E.
\]

The boxed equality would assert `2+E=2E`. Apply the fixed-point ring homomorphism

\[
\phi_G:B(G)\longrightarrow\mathbb Z,
\qquad [X]\longmapsto|X^G|.
\]

Its two sides are `2` and `0`. This is a counterexample, including after group completion. The numerical cardinality map `φ_1` sends both sides to `4`; that explains exactly what the last numerical line verifies.

**Exact dictionary.** Linearization `\ell:B(G)→R_\mathbb Q(G)` sends `E` to `1+ε`, with `ε` the sign character. It commutes with symmetric powers because the monomial basis of `Sym^n\mathbb Q[E]` is the multiset basis. It does not carry the unsigned-subset operation to exterior powers: `\ell(\lambda^2_{subset}E)=1`, whereas `\Lambda^2\ell(E)=ε`. The Burnside pre-λ operation determined by `λ_t=σ_{−t}^{−1}` has

\[
\lambda^2(E)=E^2-\sigma^2(E)=E-1,
\]

whose linearization is `ε`. Thus the discrepancy is exhibited by actual maps and a nonzero element, rather than by a claimed absence of mathematical relations.

**Plethysm consequence.** The page's valid `K_0` identities supply λ-polynomial arithmetic. The unsigned finite-subset identity cannot be used to derive equivariant multiplicities: the `C_2` counterexample already changes an irreducible constituent. The source `SA17`, section “Scan 19: λ- and σ-operations”, incorrectly records the simultaneous equivariant equalities as checked.

## A-002. Cote 133, scan 006: the rank obstruction in characteristic two

**Statements on the page.** The group completion of strictly nondegenerate quadratic modules is asserted to have a pre-λ structure augmented by rank; on a connected base where `2` is not invertible the ranks are even; with `2` invertible there is a unit. It asks whether the universal product and iterate formulas hold, and reduces their study to classifying topoi of orthogonal groups.

**Proof of the parity statement.** Over a characteristic-two residue field, the polar bilinear form of a quadratic form is alternating. A nondegenerate alternating matrix has even size (successive hyperbolic-pair elimination proves this). On a connected ringed space, the rank of a locally free module of finite constant rank is constant. A point with characteristic-two residue field therefore forces its rank to be even. The assertion needs such a point; saying merely “2 not invertible” for an arbitrary locally ringed topos still requires the usual stalk interpretation.

**Counterexample to the stated pre-λ augmentation.** Already over `Spec\mathbb F_2`, every object in the specified monoid has even rank, hence every element of its group completion has even rank. The hyperbolic plane has rank two. A pre-λ augmentation to the binomial λ-ring would give

\[
\operatorname{rk}(\lambda^2H)=\binom22=1,
\]

which is impossible in that group. This refutes the pre-λ assertion with precisely the exterior/rank compatibility written on the page. Also the standard unital definition has `λ^0=1`, whose rank is one. The nonunital parenthesis does not repair the displayed rank compatibility.

With `2` invertible, use the explicit inverse maps `q↦b_q/2` and `b↦(v↦b(v,v))` between quadratic forms and symmetric bilinear forms. Tensor products, the form on exterior powers, and the rank-one unit are defined through this equivalence. The quadratic hyperbolic form `q_H(v,φ)=φ(v)` corresponds to the bilinear matrix with off-diagonal entries `1/2`; scaling one of the two summands by `2` identifies it with the customary bilinear hyperbolic matrix with off-diagonal entries `1`. This fixes the convention used below. The remaining special-λ question for the literal group completion is answered by A-003.

## A-003. Cote 133, scan 006: the literal split ring fails the special-λ identities even with 2 invertible

This is a complete counterexample to the page's general special-λ question for `GW^⊕`.

Let `k=\overline{\mathbb F}_3`, `G=C_3`, and `S=BG` with structure sheaf `k`. The associated vector-bundle category is finite-dimensional `kG`-modules. Let `J_i`, `1≤i≤3`, denote the indecomposable module whose generator acts as a single unipotent Jordan block of size `i`. Every module is a direct sum of these three, uniquely, because `(g−1)^3=0`. Thus the additive group of the split Green ring is free on `1=[J_1]`, `y=[J_2]`, and `x=[J_3]`.

Choose `J_3=k[G]` with its permutation basis and nondegenerate invariant dot-product bilinear form; denote the symmetric form class by `X`. Let `Z=H(J_2)`. Under forgetting forms, `F(X)=x` and `F(Z)=2y`.

The split Green-ring identities are

\[
x^2=3x,\qquad xy=2x,\qquad y^2=x+1,
\quad \lambda^2x=x,\quad\lambda^3x=1,
\quad\lambda^2y=1,\quad\lambda^3y=0.
\tag{A3.1}
\]

The first two follow from the equivariant isomorphism `kG⊗M≅kG^{dim M}`: the map on basis vectors is `g⊗m↦g⊗g^{-1}m`, with the group acting on the first factor in the codomain. For the third, take `g=[[1,1],[0,1]]`. On `J_2⊗J_2`, `N=g⊗g−1` has rank two, `N²` has rank one, and `N³=0`; hence the Jordan type is `(3,1)`. On `\Lambda^2J_3`, the action is again a 3-cycle on the basis `e_1∧e_2,e_2∧e_3,e_3∧e_1`, so it is `J_3`. Both determinants are one. These computations prove (A3.1); `check_archive.py` additionally verifies the finite-field matrix ranks and exterior matrices exactly.

In every pre-λ ring, Newton's polynomial gives

\[
\psi^3(a)=a^3-3a\lambda^2(a)+3\lambda^3(a),
\]

and `ψ³` is additive; this follows by extracting the third coefficient of `t(d/dt)logλ_t`. The special-λ product polynomials force `ψ³(ab)=ψ³(a)ψ³(b)`: over universal line elements both sides are `\sum_{i,j}u_i^3v_j^3`, an integral symmetric-polynomial identity.

Equation (A3.1) gives

\[
\psi^3(x)=3,\qquad \psi^3(y)=2x-2y.
\]

The forgetful map commutes with every exterior power and hence with `ψ³`. Since `F(XZ)=x(2y)=4x`, the two required sides after forgetting are

\[
F(\psi^3(XZ))=12,
\qquad F(\psi^3(X)\psi^3(Z))=12x-12y.
\]

Their difference is `12(x−y−1)`, a nonzero element of the free abelian group on `J_1,J_2,J_3`. The coefficients here are integers in a Grothendieck group, not scalars in `k`. Consequently `GW^⊕(BC_3)` with its exterior powers is not a special λ-ring.

The separate iterate identity is now refuted in **A-015**, `ITERATE_COUNTEREXAMPLE.md`. For the actual object `A=X⊥H(J₂)`, the underlying class is `a=x+2y`. Its second exterior power is `6x+3`, and its iterated third exterior power is `441x+7`. The universal polynomial `Q_(3,2)=e₁²e₄−2e₂e₄−e₁e₅+e₆+e₃²` instead evaluates to `445x−4y+3`, giving the nonzero defect `−4(x−y−1)`. The universal polynomial was verified coefficient by coefficient in six variables; this is injective in symmetric-function degree six. Both the product and iterate questions therefore have separate explicit counterexamples for the literal split ring.

**Exact geometric transfer.** The representations with forms define homomorphisms of group schemes `C_3→O_3` and `C_3→O_4`, and hence a classifying-topos map `BC_3→B(O_3×O_4)`. Restriction pulls back the two universal quadratic modules to `X,Z`. This is the concrete instance of the universal orthogonal-group reduction proposed in the margin.

**Relation with the modern theorem.** Zibrowius, *Symmetric representation rings are λ-rings*, NYJM 21 (2015), Definition 1.2, p.1060, defines `GW` by orthogonal-sum and metabolic relations; its main theorem, p.1056, establishes the special-λ structure on that quotient. For the present `C_3`, exact `K_0` sends `J_i` to `i[J_1]`, and therefore sends `x−y−1` to zero. The counterexample establishes precisely why the split statement cannot be substituted for that cited theorem. Zibrowius, *The γ-filtration on the Witt ring of a scheme*, arXiv:1411.3198v2, Theorem 2, extends the theorem to schemes over a field of characteristic different from two; Proposition 2.15 supplies the `O_n×O_m` torsor construction. These known theorems are cited, not reproved.

**Plethysm consequence.** Passing to exact `K_0` retains the usual Schur operations by SGA 6 VI 3.3. Working in the uncorrected split quadratic ring would invalidate even the degree-three universal product relation. The correcting quotient is explicit.

## A-004. Cote 133, scan 008: hyperbolic sums and the proposed equivalence relation

### A-004a: explicit isometry with 2 invertible

For a strictly nondegenerate quadratic form `q` with polar form `b` over a ringed topos in which `2` is invertible, define

\[
\Phi:(M,q)\perp(M,-q)\longrightarrow H(M),
\quad (x,y)\longmapsto(x+y,\tfrac12 b(x-y,-)).
\]

The hyperbolic quadratic form evaluates this image to
`b(x−y,x+y)/2=q(x)−q(y)`. Nondegeneracy of `b` and invertibility of `2` give an inverse by solving for `x+y` and `x−y`. This formula is natural in isometries, hence works on classifying topoi as well. The page's classifying-topos caveat therefore has no example in this range. The symmetric-bilinear version appears as Zibrowius 2015, Lemma 1.1, p.1059; the displayed formula here translates it into the page's quadratic convention.

### A-004b: a characteristic-two classifying-topos counterexample

Let `k=\overline{\mathbb F}_2`, `M=k²`, and `q(x,y)=xy`. Its polar form `b((x,y),(x',y'))=xy'+x'y` is nondegenerate. Let `G=O(q)=\mathbb G_m\rtimes C_2`, with the torus acting by `diag(t,t^{-1})` and the involution interchanging coordinates. The module `M` is simple: a torus-stable submodule is a sum of its two distinct weight lines, and the involution exchanges those lines. Its equivariant endomorphism ring is `k`. Its invariant bilinear forms are exactly the multiples of `b`, hence alternating.

For every `G`-module `E` and every `G`-map `f:M→H(E)=E⊕E^∨`, write `f=(i,j)`. The bilinear form `B(u,v)=j(v)(i(u))` on `M` is `G`-invariant, so `B(v,v)=0`. Therefore `q_H(f(v))=0` for every such map.

The first-summand map `M→(M,q)⊥(M,q)` has pullback `q≠0`. Thus `(M,q)⊥(M,q)` cannot be isometric to `H(E)` for any `E`. The same argument, using the first summand, proves

\[
(M,q)\perp(M,q)\perp H(F)\not\simeq H(E)
\]

for all `E,F`. This proves the page's suggested failure on `BO(2)` with full characteristic and form data.

The proposed relation on scan 008 requires `q⊥(−q')⊥H(F)≅H(E)`. In this example `−q=q`. Taking `q'=q`, the displayed impossibility says that the proposed relation is not even reflexive. Consequently it cannot describe a quotient in the stated generality. It does describe the usual stable-hyperbolic relation in the range of A-004a: adding negative forms removes the extra group-completion stabilizer because every `P⊥(−P)` is hyperbolic.

## A-005. Cote 133, scan 008: the hyperbolic ideal and failure of λ descent

Over a base with `2` invertible, let `F` forget the form and `H` be the hyperbolic functor. The exact identity

\[
(M,b)\otimes H(E)\simeq H(M\otimes E)
\tag{A5.1}
\]

uses `b:M≅M^∨` to identify the second summand `M⊗E^∨` with `(M⊗E)^∨`. The hyperbolic pairing is carried to the tensor-product pairing. Thus the image of `H` is an ideal in the corresponding form ring. The two available additive maps are `H:K_0^⊕→GW^⊕` and `H:K_0→GW`. The map from exact `K_0` to the split form ring need not be well-defined: in characteristic three, `J_2=2J_1` in exact `K_0`, while the split forgetful images of `H(J_2)` and `H(2J_1)` are `2J_2` and `4J_1`.

The rank of `H(E)` is even, so rank modulo two descends to the Witt quotient. Exterior powers do not descend, already over any field of characteristic different from two: the hyperbolic plane is zero in the Witt ring, but its determinant form is

\[
\lambda^2 H(1)=\langle-1\rangle.
\]

In the quadratic convention fixed in A-002, the determinant coefficient is initially `−1/4`, and the change of basis by `2` gives the displayed isometry to `\langle-1\rangle`. The latter has odd rank, hence nonzero rank modulo two in the quotient. Since `λ²(0)=0`, no operation on the quotient can commute with both the quotient map and this exterior-power operation. This completely answers the page's descent question for the ordinary Witt quotient.

## A-006. Cote 133, scan 009: characteristic classes and the struck-out claim

The page specifies naturality, normalization on symmetric lines, and `w(x+y)=w(x)w(y)`, then states universal product and exterior-power formulas. For schemes over `\mathbb Z[1/2]`, the exact modern input is the étale-cohomology splitting morphism of Zibrowius 2016, Proposition 3.3: it splits a symmetric bundle into symmetric lines and is injective on `H^*_{et}(-,\mathbb Z/2)`. This is sufficient for the following precise restatement of the page.

Write the degree-one classes of the split lines of `E,F` as `u_1,…,u_r` and `v_1,…,v_s`. Naturality and injectivity carry back the formulas

\[
w(E)=\prod_i(1+u_i),\qquad
w(E\otimes F)=\prod_{i,j}(1+u_i+v_j),
\]
\[
w(\Lambda^a E)=\prod_{|I|=a}\left(1+\sum_{i\in I}u_i\right).
\tag{A6.1}
\]

The products are symmetric in each root family, so each coefficient is a universal polynomial in the elementary symmetric functions and the ranks. Tensoring symmetric lines adds their degree-one Kummer classes, which proves the root substitution in (A6.1); exterior powers select subsets. The injective pullback proves the formulas before splitting. For virtual classes total `w` takes values in the completed group `1+\prod_{i>0}H^i`; the completion is needed to invert total classes without a cohomological-dimension bound. SGA 6, V §6 describes the associated Chern-ring universal construction. The page does not specify such a ring structure on its displayed target, and its assertion of a λ-homomorphism is read through this universal construction.

The struck-out claim `w∘H=1` is false. Over `Spec\mathbb R`, `H(1)≅\langle1,-1\rangle`, and normalization gives `w_1(H(1))=(-1)≠0` in `H^1_{et}(\mathbb R,\mathbb Z/2)`. Thus total `w` does not factor through the Witt quotient. This counterexample suffices without relying on the more elaborate formula in the supplied SA17 study. The study's formula for hyperbolic bundles is not used in this run.

**Plethysm consequence.** Applying (A6.1) to iterated Schur operations computes characteristic classes of those bundles. The exact morphism `GW→H^0(\mathbb Z)×(1+\widehat H^+)` does not provide the full irreducible-character expansion; e.g. the characteristic-three defect in A-003 already maps to zero after exact passage. No assertion about all possible geometric ways to recover that expansion is made.

## A-007. Cote 133, scan 028: tensor-power identity and its positivity test

Let `X` be a commutatively ringed topos over `\mathbb Q`, `E` a finite locally free object, and `ν=(1^{α_1}2^{α_2}…)⊢n`. Put

\[
\rho_i=[\mathbf1_{S_i}],\qquad
\rho_\nu=\prod_i\rho_i^{\alpha_i}
=[\operatorname{Ind}_{\prod_jS_{\nu_j}}^{S_n}\mathbf1].
\]

The product here is induction. With `m_ν` expressed as an integral polynomial in `e_1,…,e_n`, the page's formula is

\[
[E^{\otimes n}]=\sum_{\nu\vdash n}m_\nu(E)\rho_\nu.
\tag{A7.1}
\]

**Proof in this fully specified setting.** The split semisimple algebra `\mathbb Q[S_n]` decomposes into matrix algebras indexed by partitions. Its rational idempotents act on `E^{⊗n}` and give the functorial decomposition

\[
E^{\otimes n}\simeq\bigoplus_{\lambda\vdash n}S_\lambda(E)\otimes[\lambda].
\tag{A7.2}
\]

Thus `K_0(BS_{n,X})≅\bigoplus_{λ⊢n}K_0(X)`. The Frobenius-characteristic map sends `[λ]` to `s_λ` and `ρ_ν` to `h_ν`. Apply evaluation at `E` to the first factor of the Cauchy identity

\[
\sum_\lambda s_\lambda(x)s_\lambda(y)
=\prod_{i,j}(1-x_i y_j)^{-1}
=\sum_\nu m_\nu(x)h_\nu(y).
\]

The equality of coefficients in this direct sum is precisely (A7.1). This is a proof of the page's formulation from the known Cauchy and Schur–Weyl theorems, not a new proof of those theorems. The exact primary locators in Macdonald, *Symmetric Functions and Hall Polynomials*, 2nd ed., are I (4.2), p.62, and (4.3), p.63, for the two Cauchy expansions; I (7.3)–(7.6), pp.113–114, for the characteristic map and irreducible characters; Appendix A (5.6), p.156, for the tensor-power decomposition. These equations were inspected in the primary PDF.

The coefficients singled out in the supplied study are `m_(1^n)=e_n` and `m_(n)=p_n`, hence exterior and Adams operations. The `m_ν` are integral and isobaric of weight `n` by the fundamental theorem of symmetric polynomials. This confirms the polynomial claim.

**Counterexample to the direct-summand reading of the margin.** Take `X=BGL_{2,\mathbb Q}` and `E` the standard rank-two bundle. In degree two,

\[
\tau^2(E)=\psi^2(E)\rho_2+\Lambda^2(E)\rho_1^2,
\qquad \psi^2(E)=\operatorname{Sym}^2(E)-\Lambda^2(E).
\]

The character of `ψ²(E)` is `x_1²+x_2²=s_(2)−s_(1,1)`. A genuine characteristic-zero `GL_2` representation decomposes into irreducibles with nonnegative multiplicities; the coefficient `−1` proves that this virtual class is not such a representation. Therefore the first summand in the displayed monomial expansion cannot be realized as an actual direct summand of `E^{⊗2}`. The exact change of basis `ρ_1²=1+sgn` cancels that negative term and gives the positive decomposition (A7.2): `Sym²(E)⊗1 ⊕Λ²(E)⊗sgn`.

**Modular polynomial-ring question reported by SA17.** In exact `R_{\mathbb F_2}(S_2)`, the regular module has a filtration with two trivial factors. Hence `ρ_1²=2ρ_2`, refuting polynomial independence of the indicated generators. The map from the split Green ring to the exact representation ring sends the indecomposable regular module to this class; the relation is asserted in the latter. The general integral/ringed-topos version of (A7.1) is now proved in **A-012**, `TENSOR_POWER_INTEGRAL.md`, using the ABW integral Cauchy filtration and three exact torus-weight extractions. It holds for exact K₀ of bounded-rank finite locally free modules on every commutatively ringed topos; no semisimplicity or polynomial independence of the Young classes is assumed.

The coefficient-ring question has two further explicit answers. **A-021**, `MIXED_CHAR_LATTICES.md`, proves that rationalization gives `K₀(O[S_n]-lattices)≅R_K(S_n)` for every characteristic-zero discrete valuation ring `O` with fraction field `K`. The inverse is specified on the Specht classes, and compatibility with induction yields the polynomial ring `Z[ρ₁,ρ₂,…]`. This includes the study's expressly open `Z_p` case. **A-023**, `LOCAL_RING_COUNTEREXAMPLE.md`, takes the characteristic-zero local ring `A=Z_(2)[ε]/(2ε,ε²)` and the rank-one `S₂` action `g↦1+ε`. Its determinant character lies outside the subgroup generated by the determinants of `ρ₂` and `ρ₁²`, proving failure of generation. **A-020** also verifies `rank R_(F_p)(S_p)=p(p)−1` from James's all-field simple-module classification. OriginalPDFpage29 was inspected; the remaining question is the full classification of coefficient rings.

**Plethysm consequence.** Schur–Weyl gives positive Schur objects; the monomial expansion supplies signed universal λ expressions. Further composition `s_μ[s_ν]` is well-defined in the same free λ-ring. A-007 does not identify a lattice-point basis for its coefficients. It refutes specifically the proposed direct-summand reading of (A7.1), while giving the exact basis morphism that relates the formulas.

The subsequent constructions G-009–G-012 complete the finite positive-count calculation by explicit invariant-algebra and coherent-module presentations. In particular, G-010 treats every Schur plethysm coefficient through the actual wreath-product covariant module, and G-011 presents the image of the actual canonical-map projector. G-012 evaluates the outer-degree-three algebra with six generators and two relations, giving four explicit bounded polytopes. These constructions and their independent complete proof reviews are recorded in `ROOT_PROOF_REVIEW.md`; no generic unevaluated-projector gate remains for terminating finite positive counts. Bounds polynomial in varying input size and global open injectivity families require additional results not asserted by those constructions.

## A-008. Cote 43, scan 037: Witt-series formulas

The page's series ring is represented by `Spec\mathbb Z[a_1,a_2,…]`, with addition given by multiplication of series. Use the explicit isomorphism to the conventional big Witt series

\[
\alpha(f)(t)=f(-t)^{-1}.
\]

It sends the page's line element `1+at` to the conventional Teichmüller series `(1−at)^{-1}`. Transporting the conventional Witt multiplication gives `(1+at)*f(t)=f(at)`. This fixes the convention without identifying two products silently.

For an `\mathbb F_p`-algebra `A`, define `F(\sum a_i t^i)=\sum a_i^p t^i` and `V(f)=f(t^p)`. The ring-scheme multiplication has integer coefficients, so coefficient Frobenius preserves it. Direct multiplication of series in characteristic `p` gives

\[
f(t)^p=F(f)(t^p),\qquad FV=VF=[p].
\]

Here `[p]` is multiplication by `p` in the additive Witt group, hence the ordinary `p`th power of a series. Also `V(fg)=V(f)V(g)`, proving its additivity. Iterating and applying the line-element rule yields

\[
(1+x t^{p^i})*f(t)=F^i(f)(x t^{p^i}).
\]

To justify the page's substitution `x=a^{p^i}` for arbitrary `x`, adjoin `a` using the monic algebra `A[a]/(a^{p^i}−x)`. It is free as an `A`-module, so `A` injects into it; the equality checked there descends coefficient by coefficient. This fills the explicit algebraic step in the page.

The map to `p`-typical Witt vectors is the truncation map associated with the divisor-stable set `{1,p,p²,…}` after `α`; its ghost coordinates retain the indices `p^r`, and it sends `1+at` to the Teichmüller vector `(a,0,…)`. This is the standard big-to-typical construction, cited rather than reproved; see Hazewinkel, *Witt vectors. Part 1*, §§14.1–14.8, pp.71–73. Those paragraphs explicitly establish that the operation polynomials in coordinate `n` involve only coordinates whose indices divide `n`, and hence that selecting the `p`-power coordinates defines the quotient functor on every commutative ring. The page's assertion that line values determine the map needs naturality and continuity in the series filtration; those are part of this specified natural Witt morphism.

**Plethysm consequence and Borger dictionary.** The representing symmetric-function algebra is the free special λ-ring. In the character algebra `R(GL_r)=\mathbb Z[x_1^{±1},…,x_r^{±1}]^{S_r}`, the Adams map is `ψ^p(f)=f(x_1^p,…,x_r^p)` and is congruent to `f^p` modulo `p`. This proves the commuting Frobenius-lift property on `Spec R(GL_r)` directly. Borger, supplied `lrfoe13.tex`, §§1.1–1.2, identifies the free λ-ring with the arithmetic jet space of the affine line and describes its topos adjunctions; §2.2 gives the monoid-algebra Frobenius action. These are explicit morphisms connecting the page to the supplied Borger framework. The character coefficient-extraction problem remains present in the Schur-basis expansion.

The remaining uniqueness claim is now proved in A-018, `WITT_UNIQUENESS.md`: finite coordinate dependence, additivity on universal products of line series, and the injective map from elementary symmetric functions show that an additive affine-scheme morphism is determined by its line values. This applies to the big-to-p-typical map over every characteristic.

## A-009. Cote 2, scan 017: restriction, induction, external tensor products

For a homomorphism of finite groups `u:H→G`, restriction preserves tensor products. On all modules over a commutative ring `R`, the induction projection formula has the isomorphism

\[
R[G]\otimes_{R[H]}(M\otimes\operatorname{Res}N)
\longrightarrow (R[G]\otimes_{R[H]}M)\otimes N,
\quad g\otimes(m\otimes n)\longmapsto(g\otimes m)\otimes gn.
\]

Its inverse sends `(g⊗m)⊗n` to `g⊗(m⊗g^{-1}n)`. The `H`-balancing relations prove both maps are well-defined; their displayed composites are identities. Restriction along `G→G×G`, `g↦(g,g)`, takes `M\boxtimes N` to `M⊗N`. Extension of scalars identifies iterated induction with induction along the composite. These formulas also apply sheafwise.

OriginalPDFpage16/site15 now explicitly verifies the convention: it defines the all-module category with group action and calls `u_*` extension, with `u*` restriction. Originaltargetpage17 and followingpage18 were also inspected; the displayed formulas and induction product match the transcription.

For subgroup inclusions, `R[G]` is free over `R[H]`, so induction preserves finite locally free underlying objects and exact sequences. For arbitrary group homomorphisms, the corresponding preservation claim is false: `C_2→1` applied to the rank-one sign module over `\mathbb Z` gives coinvariants `\mathbb Z/2`. Thus the page's arbitrary-group-map functors are unproblematic on all modules, but an induced map on the exact `K_0` of locally free objects needs a stated category or an admissibility restriction. The exterior/symmetric/Schur constructions on tensor powers give the finite-operator realization of λ operations mentioned also on cote12/041.

## A-010. The λ-ring and γ-filtration dictionary

The free-ring fact is SGA 6, V, Proposition 4.2 and Definition 4.4: for every special λ-ring `R`, evaluation at `x∈R` is the unique λ-map

\[
\operatorname{ev}_x:\Lambda=\mathbb Z[e_1,e_2,…]\longrightarrow R,
\qquad e_i\longmapsto\lambda^i(x).
\]

Composition of these operations is plethysm. Finite rank is the explicit quotient `Λ→\mathbb Z[e_1,…,e_r]`, with kernel generated by `e_i`, `i>r`; SGA 6 V, Proposition 4.8 and Corollary 4.9 verify its λ-ideal property. Inverting `e_r` gives the full `GL_r` character ring. A rank-`r` bundle `E` with frame torsor `P` supplies the homomorphism `R_\mathbb Z(GL_r)→K_0(X)`, `[W]↦[P×^{GL_r}W]`, used in SGA 6 VI, Theorem 3.3. It carries `S_λ` to `S_λE`, so it carries the universal plethysm identity to the same `K_0` identity on sheaves.

For the rank augmentation, SGA 6 V 3.2–3.4 defines `γ_t(x)=λ_{t/(1−t)}(x)` and V 3.10 defines the filtration generated by products `\prod γ^{i_j}(x_j)` with rank-zero `x_j` and `\sum i_j≥n`. On a splitting pullback with line classes `L_1,…,L_r`, direct substitution gives

\[
\gamma_t(E-r)=\prod_{j=1}^r(1+(L_j-1)t).
\]

The pullback injection and passage to associated graded give the Chern-class interpretation in SGA 6. This supplies an exact translation of every universal Schur expression into γ coordinates.

The map induced by `Spec\mathbb C→BGL_r` sends a representation to its dimension. In characters it is evaluation `x_i↦1`. The nonzero element `[V]-r` lies in its kernel. Thus ordinary rank at a point does not determine the character, with the loss measured by this actual map. Equivariant `K_0(BGL_r)` retains the full character. This is the specific distinction needed when transferring a coefficient statement to geometry; no claim about the impossibility of other geometric constructions is involved.

## A-011. Cote 89, scan 018: the exterior pairing in the rank-two reconstruction

The public original PDFpages16–18 now supply the definitions: `V` is free of rank two over a commutative ring `Λ`, and the disjoint line generators `u,v` form a basis. Write `w=au+bv`. Then

\[
u\wedge v=v\wedge w=w\wedge u
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad a=b=-1
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad u+v+w=0.
\]

Indeed the middle two wedges are `−a(u∧v)` and `−b(u∧v)`, and `u∧v` is a generator of the free determinant line, so its coefficients can be compared over `Λ`. Over a field, the zero vector, the scalar action on each punctured line torsor, and this reconstruction of addition on independent pairs recover addition on all pairs: dependent pairs lie on one scalar line. The target explicitly discusses this field reconstruction. Although supplied scan018 omits `=0` after `u+v+w`, the preceding original PDFpage17/site16, formula(8), writes the full equation. Thus the repair is supplied by the neighboring manuscript itself. The precise geometric map is `\Lambda² V→\det V`, the identity in rank two. An arbitrary-ring reconstruction of every nonunimodular vector is not claimed from the field argument.

# A-012. Integral completion of archive cote 133, scan 028

This completes the exact-K₀ gate left in A-007. The asserted identity holds on every commutatively ringed topos `(X,A)`, with `K₀` formed from finite locally free modules of bounded rank and short-exact-sequence relations. The integral construction below specifies both the map and the exact category. It does not assert polynomial independence of the Young generators in a modular representation ring.

## Statement and conventions

Let `K_n(X)=K₀(BS_(n,X),A)`, the exact Grothendieck group of finite locally free `A`-modules with `S_n` action, and put `K_*(X)=⊕_(n≥0)K_n(X)`. Products from degrees `a,b` to `a+b` are external tensor product followed by induction from `S_a×S_b` to `S_(a+b)`. A class of `K₀(X)` acts on each `K_n(X)` by tensor product with trivial `S_n` action.

For a partition `ν=(ν_1,…,ν_l)` of `n`, define the actual Young permutation module

`ρ_ν = [A[S_n/(S_(ν_1)×⋯×S_(ν_l))]]`.

The orbit basis identifies this with the product of the degree-`ν_i` trivial classes. Let `m_ν` be the ordinary monomial symmetric function, expressed as its integral polynomial in the elementary functions. For every `ξ∈K₀(X)`,

\[
\tau^n(\xi)=\sum_{\nu\vdash n}m_\nu(\xi)\,\rho_\nu
\quad\text{in }K_n(X).
\tag{A12.1}
\]

On an effective class `[E]`, `τⁿ([E])=[E^⊗n]` with the place-permutation action. On virtual classes, `τ` is the homomorphism from addition in `K₀(X)` to the degree-completed multiplicative group `1+∏_(n>0)K_n(X)` constructed below.

## Primary integral input and its exact translation

K. Akin, D. A. Buchsbaum, J. Weyman, *Schur functors and Schur complexes*, Adv. Math. 44 (1982), 207–278, DOI 10.1016/0001-8708(82)90039-1. The original paper was downloaded from the author's current research page and inspected in full around the relevant statements. Local copies: `ABW1982.pdf`, `ABW1982.txt`.

- Theorem II.2.16, printed p.232, supplies a universal free basis of each Schur module by standard tableaux.
- Theorem III.1.4, printed pp.245–246, supplies a natural filtration of `Symⁿ(F⊗G)` by `GL(F)×GL(G)` submodules, with associated graded `⊕_(η⊢n)L_η(F)⊗L_η(G)`.

The paper uses exterior-row notation: `L_(a)=Λᵃ`. To match the partition convention of the archive and Macdonald, **define** `S_λ^int=L_(λ′)`. This is an explicit conjugation of the indexing partition. After this relabeling, its standard tableau basis has weight multiplicities `K_(λν)`, the usual Kostka integers, and the Cauchy associated graded is `⊕_(λ⊢n)S_λ^int(F)⊗S_λ^int(G)`.

Every graded factor is finite free over Z. The filtration is defined by natural exterior-diagonalization and symmetric-multiplication maps, so it is stable under change of bases and scalar extension. Exactness over Z with free successive quotients is preserved by arbitrary base change. Applied locally to free sheaves and glued by this naturality, it gives the same filtration on a commutatively ringed topos. This is the precise transfer used here.

## Three weight extractions from the same filtration

Take `W=Z^n`, with its standard diagonal torus and permutation-matrix `S_n`. Write

`C_λ=(S_λ^int(W))_(1,…,1)`.

This is a finite free Z-lattice with `S_n` action: permuting the torus weights fixes the all-ones weight. No identification of `C_λ` with an irreducible module is required. Taking a torus weight is exact over Z, since a torus comodule is a direct sum of its weight modules, by SGA 3 I Proposition 4.7.3.

**First extraction: the tensor power.** The `W`-weight `(1,…,1)` component of `Symⁿ(E⊗W)` is equivariantly isomorphic to `E^⊗n` through

`e_1⊗⋯⊗e_n ↦ (e_1⊗w_1)⋯(e_n⊗w_n)`.

Permuting the `w_i` is the place-permutation action through this map. Extracting that weight from the Cauchy filtration gives

\[
[E^{\otimes n}]=\sum_{\lambda\vdash n}[S_\lambda^{\mathrm{int}}(E)]\,[C_\lambda]
\quad\text{in }K_n(X).
\tag{A12.2}
\]

**Second extraction: the integral Young relation.** Apply (A12.2) to `E=Z^n`, now equipped with its own diagonal torus, and select the weight `ν` padded by zeroes. The tensor-word basis on the left is the set of words with each letter `j` appearing `ν_j` times. Its permutation action is the Young coset action, since the stabilizer of the ordered word is `∏_jS_(ν_j)`. On the right, the standard tableau basis gives a free weight module of rank `K_(λν)`. Therefore, already over Z,

\[
\rho_\nu=\sum_{\lambda\vdash n}K_{\lambda\nu}[C_\lambda].
\tag{A12.3}
\]

This proof uses the exact filtration; it does not infer integral equality from rational characters.

**Third extraction: the class of the integral Schur functor.** Return to `Symⁿ(E⊗W)` and take an arbitrary `W`-weight `ν`. The left side is the tensor product `⊗_jSym^(ν_j)(E)`, and the graded factors on the right have multiplicities `K_(λν)`. Hence

\[
h_\nu(E)=\sum_{\lambda\vdash n}K_{\lambda\nu}[S_\lambda^{\mathrm{int}}(E)].
\tag{A12.4}
\]

Here `[Symᵃ(E)]=h_a(E)` follows from the exterior/symmetric Koszul identity in exact K₀, including in positive characteristic. The corresponding symmetric-function identity is `h_ν=Σ_λK_(λν)s_λ`. The Kostka matrix is integral triangular with diagonal entries one, so its transpose is invertible over Z. Comparing and inverting (A12.4) gives

`[S_λ^int(E)]=s_λ(E)`.

This proves the needed Schur/λ polynomial dictionary without a character-injectivity assumption over Z or a semisimplicity assumption.

Now substitute into (A12.2) and use `s_λ=Σ_νK_(λν)m_ν`, followed by (A12.3):

`Σ_λs_λ(E)[C_λ]=Σ_νm_ν(E)Σ_λK_(λν)[C_λ]=Σ_νm_ν(E)ρ_ν`.

This proves (A12.1) on effective classes for every commutatively ringed topos in the declared exact category.

## Exact-sequence relations and virtual classes

For `0→E′→E→E″→0`, filter `E^⊗n` by the number of factors in `E′`. The associated graded degree with `a` such factors is

`Ind_(S_a×S_(n−a))^(S_n)((E′)^⊗a ⊗ (E″)^⊗(n−a))`.

The submodules and quotients are finite locally free: this is checked after a local splitting of the original sequence, and the filtration itself is natural and `S_n` stable. Thus, with the induction product,

`τ(E)=τ(E′)τ(E″)`.

Consequently `τ` descends to the exact Grothendieck group and extends to differences by inversion of a series with constant term one.

Define `Φ_n(ξ)=Σ_(ν⊢n)m_ν(ξ)ρ_ν`. The universal alphabet-splitting identity

`m_ν(x+y)=Σ_(α∪β=ν)m_α(x)m_β(y)`

and the actual induction identity `ρ_αρ_β=ρ_(α∪β)` give `Φ(ξ+η)=Φ(ξ)Φ(η)`. The alphabet identity is an integral symmetric-function identity and evaluates in the special λ-ring `K₀(X)` of SGA 6 VI Theorem 3.3. Thus `Φ` is the same kind of homomorphism as `τ`. They agree on effective classes by the preceding proof, hence on their entire group completion. This proves (A12.1) for all `ξ`.

## Consequences for the audit

The polynomial `Σ_(α_1,…,α_n)` on scan 028 is exactly `m_ν`, with `ν=(1^α_1⋯n^α_n)`, in every characteristic under the exact-K₀ convention now fixed. This is a proved current-run reformulation using the known ABW integral filtration. The page's direct-summand margin remains refuted by A-007's rank-two example; the equality established here lives in the exact Grothendieck group. The modular relation `ρ_1²=2ρ_2` in exact `R_(F_2)(S_2)` also remains valid: no independence of the `ρ_ν` was used in the proof.

The unsigned-subset counterexample A-001 and the split quadratic counterexample A-003 are unaffected. Their explicit comparison maps still determine the exact targets of the identities.
