## 1. The exact general chart and its linearization

The chart T-032 takes a smaller flag polynomial \(F\) to
\[
u^{n-\lambda_2}F(v(X)),\qquad
v_{j,I}=\left(\prod_{i\notin I}x_i\right)p_{j,I},
\quad u=\prod_i x_i.
\]
The map \(w\mapsto\mathbf1\wedge w\) identifies the smaller exterior coordinates with the displayed minors. Row permutations fix \(\mathbf1,u\), commute with centering, and act on every exterior power by its literal permutation matrix. Thus the chart preserves the exact \(S_m\) action. The full-height smaller flag factor is \(\det E\); its sign character is the last factor of \(\mathcal L_\tau\), not a separate omitted twist.

The highest-weight and row-weight calculation in C.12–C.13 gives precisely \(\lambda_2\) factors of height at least two and the common residual exponent \(n\) for every \(x_i\). The inverse dense chart C.14 recovers any prescribed smaller matrix and any nonzero \(u\). Consequently polynomial extension is exactly divisibility by \(u^k\), as asserted in GF.8. The invariant form on \(E\) is nondegenerate and equivariant over \(\mathbf Q\), so its Schur functor gives the specified map from the section convention \(S_\tau E^*\) to \(S_\tau E\).

## 2. Every higher flag frame is independent of the leading normal directions

At \(x_m=\varepsilon\), with \(s_m=S\ne0\), the first-line coordinates are exactly
\[
a_j=\varepsilon\frac{r_j-r_1}{S-\varepsilon r_1},
\qquad 2\le j\le m-1.
\]
The (m-2) coordinates are a regular parameter system at \([\ell_m]\) in \(\mathbf P(E)\). Pullback along the flag bundle gives a regular parameter system transverse to its whole fiber.

The subfamily \(X_{mj}=0\) for \(j\ge3\) is sufficient to test the possible leading-coefficient cancellation. At \(\varepsilon=0\), a nonzero minor must contain row \(m\); expansion along that row uses only the entry \(S\) in column two. After factoring out the \(x_i\), every remaining minor is an exterior coordinate in the columns
\[
\mathbf1,\quad (X_{i3}/x_i)_{i<m},\quad\ldots,
(X_{im}/x_i)_{i<m}.
\]
No such coordinate depends on the \(r_j\). The quotient \(E/\mathbf Q\ell_m\) is exactly \(\mathbf Q^{m-1}/\mathbf Q\mathbf1\): restricting the first (m-1) coordinates is surjective onto that quotient, with kernel \(\mathbf Q\ell_m\). The remaining ratio columns are arbitrary, so their classes realize every generic flag and every choice of nonzero successive frame scalings in the quotient. Varying \(S\prod_{i<m}x_i\) supplies the first-line frame; successive column scalings supply all higher exterior frames. The last one is nonzero whenever those quotient columns form a basis, so the determinant factor also has valuation zero.

Meanwhile the (m-2) differences \(r_j-r_1\) vary freely with all those image flag and frame coordinates fixed. This proves the required algebraic independence over the image fiber's function field. It is stronger than independence of only the first line: it includes every higher coordinate which can occur in \(F\).

## 3. Equality of orders and the ordinary ideal powers

Choose local nonzero Plücker coordinates at the generic fiber point. On the exhibited family each has valuation zero, so the local trivialization of \(\mathcal L_\tau\) introduces no extra factor of \(\varepsilon\). A section with lowest nonzero transverse term of degree \(h\) has leading coefficient equal to that nonzero polynomial evaluated at the independent \((r_j-r_1)/S\). It cannot vanish. The opposite inequality follows because every transverse parameter is divisible by \(\varepsilon\). This proves exact equality of the original coordinate-divisor valuation and the fiber-ideal order.

The special subfamily used here need not dominate the entire original divisor: the lower-order divisibility is valid on its full open chart, and nonvanishing on this subfamily proves nonvanishing of the universal leading coefficient. Its independence statement is exactly what is needed for the reverse inequality.

The generic order detects the ordinary sheaf power everywhere on the fiber. Indeed the fiber is a regular embedding and its graded normal quotients are locally free over an integral flag variety. A section of such a quotient which is zero at the generic point is zero globally. Induction through the first \(k\) graded pieces therefore gives membership in \(\mathcal I_i^k\) at every point, not just symbolic membership at one generic point.

The original \(x_i\) are pairwise nonassociate primes. Hence the \(m\) valuations are equivalent to divisibility by \(\prod_i x_i^k\). The fibers are disjoint, so their powers are pairwise comaximal and intersection equals product. Flatness of the flag projection identifies that product with \(\pi^*\mathcal I_{Z_m}^k\). Applying the actual chart map proves GF.4, and the specified Specht covariant functor proves GF.5.

The cases \(k=0\), \(n=0\), and \(m=3\) cause no change in the argument. For \(m=3\), the quotient flag fiber is a point, the transverse system has one parameter, and the same independence test still applies.

## 4. The full quadratic ideal and its action

Set \(r=m-1\ge3\) and use the \(r\) coordinate points plus \([1:\cdots:1]\). In degree two, vanishing at the coordinate points removes every square, while vanishing at the last point imposes exactly one sum-zero relation on the mixed coefficients. This gives the listed differences \(z_i z_j-z_1z_2\).

In their quotient, write \(z=z_1z_2\). For distinct (i,j), choose \(a\notin\{i,j\}\); then
\[
z_i z=z_i(z_jz_a)=z_j(z_i z_a)=z_jz.
\]
Every mixed degree-\(C\) monomial contains a cross-product, and this identity replaces every remaining factor by \(z_1\). Thus the pure powers \(z_i^C\) and the single mixed class \(zz_1^{C-2}\) span. Evaluation at the coordinate points isolates the coefficients of the pure powers, and evaluation at the last point then isolates the mixed coefficient. They are independent. This proves the asserted basis in every degree, including the low degrees separately.

The resulting graded map to the product of line coordinate rings is injective. Its kernel before quotienting is exactly the intersection of the homogeneous linear prime ideals of those lines. Hence the generated ideal is radical and saturated as well as the full projective ideal. The dimension of its quadratic piece is \(m(m-3)/2\).

Returning to the exact affine representatives \(\ell_i\), evaluation is equivariant without a scaling character. The two eigenvalues for the matrix of the values of \(q_i^2\) are \((m-2)/m\) and \((m-1)/m\); for \(q_i^3\) they are \(1-3/m+3/m^2\) and \((m-1)(m-2)/m^2\). These are nonzero for the stated \(m\). The invariant quadratic has the same nonzero value at each point and propagates surjectivity by two degrees. The established dimensions make evaluation an isomorphism onto \(\operatorname{Perm}_m\) for every \(C\ge2\). Degrees zero and one give its constant and standard submodules. All the actions in GF.15 are therefore literal evaluation maps.

For \(m=3\), the three differences \(q_i-q_j\) are distinct line equations on \(E\), each vanishing at one frame point. Their product gives exactly the reduced degree-three divisor ideal and changes by sign under permutations. This is the stated separate cubic formula.

# The exact two-row quotient complex and its cohomology

Reviewer/contributor: GPT-6 Astra Pro, run /root/archive_audit; reasoning setting not exposed.

Work over \(\mathbf Q\). Let \(L\hookrightarrow E\) be an inclusion of a line bundle into a rank-four bundle with locally free quotient \(Q\). For integers \(a\ge b\ge0\), the following construction fixes every map in the two-row Schur complex. On the five-point projective space it also proves all cohomology assertions in the region \(c\ge2k\).

## 1. The signed tensor construction

Put \(N=a+b\), and regard
\[
C=[L\longrightarrow E]
\]
as a cochain complex with \(L\) in degree \(-1\) and \(E\) in degree zero. The symmetric group \(S_N\) acts on \(C^{\otimes N}\) by the **Koszul signed** permutation of tensor positions. Interchanging two \(L\)-positions contributes a minus sign; interchanging an \(L\)-position with an \(E\)-position does not.

For a tensor whose \(L\)-positions form \(J\subset\{1,\ldots,N\}\), the differential is the specified map
\[
d(v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_N)
=\sum_{r\in J}(-1)^{|J\cap\{1,\ldots,r-1\}|}
v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes\iota(v_r)\otimes\cdots\otimes v_N.
\tag{S.1}
\]
Here \(\iota:L\to E\) is the given inclusion. The two terms that replace any fixed pair of \(L\)-positions cancel, so \(d^2=0\). The signed permutation action commutes with this differential.

Take the row-filled standard tableau \(T\) of shape \((a,b)\). Let \(r_T\) be its row symmetrizer, \(c_T\) its column antisymmetrizer, and \(h_{a,b}\) its hook-length product. Use the explicit primitive Young idempotent
\[
e_T=h_{a,b}^{-1}c_Tr_T\in\mathbf Q[S_N].
\]
For \(N=0\), use the identity on the tensor unit. Define the Schur complex to be the image
\[
\mathcal S_{a,b}(C)=e_T C^{\otimes N},
\tag{S.2}
\]
with differential the restriction of (S.1). Its degree-zero term is the same Young-idempotent realization of \(S_{(a,b)}E\), and its augmentation is induced by the actual quotient \(E\to Q\).

### Exactness and tensoring by a nonflat ideal

Locally choose a splitting \(E=L\oplus Q\). The complex \(C\) then contracts onto \(Q\) in degree zero. Tensoring the contraction gives a homotopy of \(C^{\otimes N}\) onto \(Q^{\otimes N}\). Average that homotopy over \(S_N\). The augmentation and the chosen inclusion of \(Q^{\otimes N}\) commute with the signed action, so the averaged homotopy still satisfies the same contraction identity and now commutes with \(e_T\).

Restricting it to the idempotent image proves that (S.2) contracts locally onto \(S_{(a,b)}Q\). In particular its augmented complex is locally split exact. The homotopy is \(\mathcal O\)-linear; tensoring it with any specified ideal preserves the identity. Thus tensoring this complex with \(\mathcal I^k(c)\) preserves exactness without a flatness requirement on the ideal.

## 2. The three terms and completely specified comparison maps

The term of tensor degree \(-j\) is, before applying \(e_T\),
\[
\operatorname{Ind}_{S_{N-j}\times S_j}^{S_N}
\left(E^{\otimes(N-j)}\otimes L^{\otimes j}\otimes\operatorname{sgn}_{S_j}\right).
\tag{S.3}
\]
The induction map places the \(j\) line factors into the selected tensor positions; its signs are those of (S.1). The sign in (S.3) is essential. In particular the two-line term for an exterior square contains \(L^2\).

Frobenius reciprocity and the exterior Pieri rule identify the idempotent image with
\[
L^j\otimes
\bigoplus_{\nu:\ (a,b)/\nu\text{ is a vertical strip of size }j}S_\nu E.
\tag{S.4}
\]
For completeness, the Pieri multiplicities are exactly one by the alternant identity. Multiplying the alternant for \(s_\nu\) by \(e_j\) is the sum of alternants obtained by increasing \(j\) distinct exponents by one. An exponent collision makes the alternant zero. All other terms remain in decreasing order and correspond precisely to adding at most one box in each row. Dividing by the Vandermonde alternant gives
\[
e_j s_\nu=\sum_{\lambda/\nu\text{ vertical }j\text{-strip}}s_\lambda.
\]
The Frobenius-character isometry used for the Specht projector therefore gives the multiplicity-one branching in (S.4).

Here is an exact finite prescription for the maps in (S.4), which avoids leaving their scalar choices implicit. Realize every Specht module as the rational polytabloid span, with tableaux in lexicographic order. Apply the sign averaging projector on the last \(j\) letters to the Specht module of shape \((a,b)\). For each allowed \(\nu\), solve the intertwiner equations for the adjacent transpositions of \(S_{N-j}\) by rational Gaussian elimination. The preceding multiplicity calculation proves that this solution space is one-dimensional. Choose its first nonzero solution with first nonzero coordinate equal to one. The direct sum of these intertwiners is an isomorphism onto the sign-projected space; invert its rational matrix.

Composition with these inverse projections gives the maps between the corresponding Schur functors. The Frobenius-reciprocity map itself is explicit: an intertwiner \(f\) to the subgroup module is sent to
\[
v\longmapsto\sum_{gH\in S_N/H}g\otimes f(g^{-1}v),
\qquad H=S_{N-j}\times S_j,
\]
and its inverse is projection to the identity coset. Finally the identification with the primitive-idempotent image is evaluation at \(e_T\):
\[
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf Q[S_N]}(\mathbf Q[S_N]e_T,V)
\longrightarrow e_TV,\qquad f\longmapsto f(e_T),
\]
with inverse \(v\mapsto(ae_T\mapsto av)\).

These prescriptions use rational matrices independent of the local frame of \(E\). They commute with frame change, so they define actual bundle isomorphisms. Conjugating (S.1) by them specifies the displayed Schur-functor differentials.

There are at most two rows, so no vertical strip has more than two boxes. The complex is consequently
\[
0\longrightarrow L^2\otimes S_{(a-1,b-1)}E
\longrightarrow
L\otimes\left(S_{(a-1,b)}E\oplus S_{(a,b-1)}E\right)
\longrightarrow S_{(a,b)}E
\longrightarrow S_{(a,b)}Q\longrightarrow0,
\tag{S.5}
\]
with only the valid partition terms retained. The vanishing in degrees \(j>2\) can also be seen directly: three odd line entries in two rows force two identical odd entries in one row, whose graded row symmetrizer is zero.

The boundary conventions are explicit:

- At \(a=b>0\), omit \(S_{(a-1,b)}E\); retain \(S_{(a,b-1)}E\) and the two-line term.
- At \(b=0<a\), the complex is the ordinary symmetric-quotient sequence \(L\operatorname{Sym}^{a-1}E\to\operatorname{Sym}^aE\to\operatorname{Sym}^aQ\).
- At \(a=b=0\), the augmentation is the identity on \(\mathcal O\).
- At \(a=b=1\), the maps are \(l^2\mapsto l\otimes l\) and \(l\otimes e\mapsto l\wedge e\).
- At \(b=1\), decomposing \(E\otimes\operatorname{Sym}^{a-1}E\) by polarization identifies (S.5) with the complete hook complex already checked in A-035.

## 3. Higher cohomology on the five-point projective space

Now take \(E=\mathfrak h_5\) on \(\mathbf P(E)\), \(L=\mathcal O(-1)\), and the actual five-point ideal \(\mathcal I\). Let \(k\ge0\) and \(c\ge2k\). Tensor (S.5) by \(\mathcal I^k(c)\), and place its three terms \(F_2,F_1,F_0\) in cochain degrees \(-2,-1,0\).

The scalar cohomology facts needed here are complete:

1. \(H^{q>0}(\mathcal I^k(c))=0\). For \(k\ge2\) this follows from A-029; for \(k=1\), the degree-two evaluation and its higher-degree versions give it; for \(k=0\), it is the usual cohomology of \(\mathcal O(c)\).
2. \(H^2(\mathcal I^k(m))=0\) for all the twists in the complex. The finite-support quotient \(\mathcal O/\mathcal I^k\) has no higher cohomology, and \(H^2(\mathcal O(m))=0\) on \(\mathbf P^3\).
3. \(H^3(\mathcal I^k(m))=0\) for these twists, because \(m\ge c-2\ge-2\) and \(H^3(\mathcal O(m))=0\) there.

The cohomology spectral sequence for this bounded complex has no term of positive total degree: \(F_0\) has only \(H^0\), and the only possible additional cohomology of \(F_1,F_2\) is \(H^1\), in total degrees zero and minus one. The complex is quasi-isomorphic to the displayed quotient sheaf in degree zero. Therefore
\[
\boxed{
H^{q>0}\!\left(\mathbf P(E),
\mathcal I^k(c)\otimes S_{(a,b)}Q\right)=0
\quad(a\ge b\ge0,\ k\ge0,\ c\ge2k).
}
\tag{S.6}
\]
This proof includes \(k=1,c=2\). Possible \(H^1(\mathcal I(0))\) and \(H^1(\mathcal I(1))\) appear only in nonpositive total degrees; no additional assertion about a map between them is needed for (S.6).

## 4. The exact Euler representation and jet evaluation

Write \(\chi(\mathcal I^k(m))\) for the exact alternating cohomology class. The locally split complex and (S.6) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
[H^0(\mathcal I^k(c)\otimes S_{(a,b)}Q)]
={}&[S_{(a,b)}E]\,\chi(\mathcal I^k(c))\\
&-\left([S_{(a-1,b)}E]+[S_{(a,b-1)}E]\right)
\chi(\mathcal I^k(c-1))\\
&+[S_{(a-1,b-1)}E]\,\chi(\mathcal I^k(c-2)),
\end{aligned}
\tag{S.7}
\]
with the same valid-partition convention.

Every twist here is at least \(-2\). The actual jet-coordinate map of A-033 gives
\[
\operatorname{tr}\bigl(g\mid\chi(\mathcal I^k(m))\bigr)
=h_m(g)-m_1(g)h_{k-1}(g),
\tag{S.8}
\]
where \(h_m=0\) for negative \(m\). The invariant form identifies the symmetric powers of \(E^*\) with those of \(E\). At \(k=0\), the jet term is zero. At \(k=1,c=2\), the three scalar classes are respectively \(U,-\mathbf1,-E\), so (S.7) retains both exceptional scalar cohomology contributions exactly.

Equations (S.1)–(S.8) provide the maps, all boundary cases, the required vanishing and the exact finite-group Euler character for every two-row quotient shape in the stated region.

\[

=(-1)^{a+\gcd(a,b)}
 (A^{b/\gcd(a,b)}-B^{a/\gcd(a,b)})^{\gcd(a,b)}.
\]
The numerator has the same resultant sign, so it cancels in the ratio.

\(r+1\); its permutation sign is exactly the stated \(\kappa\).

denominator remains nonzero over independent cycle parameters. Under

exponent integral. Thus ST.6 includes every sign and exponent.

initial values, including zero.

For every partition \(\eta\) of \(mq\) with at most \(m\)
parts, the report constructs a nonzero invariant
\[
f_\eta\in B_{2\eta}(2q)
\]
and the actual injection
\[
B_\lambda(n)\longrightarrow B_{\lambda+2\eta}(n+2q),
\qquad v\longmapsto f_\eta v.
\tag{ER1}
\]
The domain property of the polynomial ring proves injectivity;
the element's literal \(S_m\)-invariance proves equivariance.
Taking the finite-group multiplicity functor therefore gives
the claimed inequality simultaneously for every outer label.

Here is an independent constructive check that the required
balanced tableau exists. For a partition \(\eta\vdash mq\),
choose integers
\[
\eta_{i+1}\le\beta_i\le\eta_i\quad(1\le i<m),
\qquad |\beta|=(m-1)q.
\]
The lower-end sum is \(mq-\eta_1\le(m-1)q\);
the upper-end sum is \(mq-\eta_m\ge(m-1)q\).
Every integer between these two sums is realized by choosing
coordinates in the indicated integer intervals, and the
interlacing inequalities make \(\beta\) a partition.
The skew diagram \(\eta/\beta\) is a horizontal strip of size
\(q\). Label that strip by \(m\), and repeat on \(\beta\).
This gives a semistandard tableau with exactly \(q\) copies
of each label. The construction includes \(q=0\).

Its product of flag minors \(h_T\) has the required right
weight \(\eta\) and balanced row content. At the matrix
\(X_{ij}=i^{j-1}\), each selected initial-column minor is a
nonzero Vandermonde determinant. Hence \(h_T(X)\ne0\).
The explicit element
\[
f_\eta=\sum_{g\in S_m}(g h_T)^2
\]
has weight \(2\eta\), content \((2q)^m\), and is invariant
under literal row permutation. Its value at that real
matrix is positive, because one summand is already positive.
This proves nonvanishing over \(\mathbf Q\) without any
unidentified projection. At \(q=0\), it is the nonzero
constant \(m!\).

Multiplication by a determinant power gives the stated
additional translation and the sign twist
\(\operatorname{sgn}^d\). The translated staircase families
therefore follow from the already checked G022/G023 by
composition of actual injections.

## A-047. Every five-row interior weight, G025

**Result: complete proof PASS; all seventy-six seeds and the

### The finite reduction and its actual transport

Write the four gaps as \(2+p_i+2t_i\), with \(p_i\in\{0,1\}\).
Choose a coordinate-minimal \(u\le t\) satisfying the stated
size congruence modulo five. Such a minimal vector has
\(\sum_i u_i\le4\): from any five residues among \(1,2,3,4\),
two of the six partial sums coincide, giving a nonempty
zero-sum submultiset. Subtracting it preserves the congruence
because two is invertible modulo five, contradicting
coordinate minimality. This proves the completeness of
the finite enumeration over sixteen parity vectors and
seventy vectors of total size at most four.

For the resulting minimal partition \(\sigma\), put
\(d=\lambda_5\) and
\(\eta=(\lambda-d\mathbf1-\sigma)/2\).
Its consecutive gaps are \(t_i-u_i\), so it is a partition.
Its size is a multiple of five, since
\(2|\eta|=5(n-d-n_\sigma)\).
Thus the exact injection (ER1), followed by determinant
multiplication, transports every seed multiplicity to
the desired component, with its precise sign twist.

### Independent sign and coefficient checks

The single-cycle alternant has exponents
\(e_i=\alpha_i+\ell-i\). Repeated residues modulo \(\ell\)
give zero. Distinct residues give the row-permutation
sign relative to ascending residues, multiplied by
\((-1)^{\ell(\ell-1)/2}\), the denominator's descending
order sign. Total degree \(\ell n\) then gives exactly
the power \(T^n\). Fixed-point removal is the actual
Pieri expansion by a horizontal \(n\)-strip, with
interlacing and total-size constraints. Its branching
formula has no extra cycle sign.

For two two-cycles, separating the even and odd exponents
in the four-row determinant gives the two two-variable
Schur factors in IN10. The permutation sign is
\((-1)^{N+3}\), where \(N\) counts odd-before-even pairs;
the denominator has three such pairs. The interval
coefficient formula therefore has the displayed sign
and endpoint constraints.

For a three-cycle and a two-cycle, Laplace expansion on
the first three columns has sign
\((-1)^{\sum_{i\in I}i+6}\), with one-based row indices.
The cross resultant is \(T_1^2-T_2^3\), with positive
leading term. Its Laurent expansion is
\[
(T_1^2-T_2^3)^{-1}
=\sum_{v\ge0}T_1^{-2v-2}T_2^{3v}.
\]
Consequently the numerator exponents satisfy
\(A=n+2v+2,\ B=n-3v\), exactly as in the report.
The ten row subsets give the claimed finite expression.
The program's zero-based exponent differs from the
one-based expression by an even integer, so the signs agree.

The independent program check_gap2_seeds_independent.py
does not use these alternant residue formulas. It
enumerates minimal congruence vectors independently,
uses interlacing strips, evaluates literal integer
Jacobi–Trudi determinants for single cycles, and uses
Jacobi–Trudi interpolation over \(\mathbf F_{61}\) for
the two-cycle cases. The interpolated degree is at most
twenty-four. The actual two-two trace has absolute
value at most \(n+1\le13\), and the three-two trace
has absolute value at most ten. Centering the residue
therefore recovers the unique exact integer.

The execution compared all seventy-six seeds, all
532 class traces and all 532 multiplicities. It used
1,394 single-cycle determinants and 976 two-cycle
interpolations. Every result agrees; the smallest
multiplicity is two and the largest seed inner degree
is twelve. The separate degree-four source and target
multiplicities are one and three. The full receipt is
GAP2_SEEDS_INDEPENDENT_RECEIPT.json.

### Exact degree-four grid-map calculation

The polynomial \(F_0\) in IN16 is a product of the stated

and its right highest weight is \((8,6,4,2)\). Averaging

(\operatorname{Sym}^5 V)\).

Polarizing each row gives the coefficient of all twenty

normalized transpose-grid projection. Thus the
denominator in IN17 is exactly \((5!)^4\).

=21,210,071,040,
\]
with 1,048,576 Boolean points, 502,432 nonzero summands,

This is a 118-bit integer, strictly less than \(2^{127}\);

### Exact primary-source range and propagation

Cheung–Ikenmeyer–Mkrtchyan, Symmetrizing tableaux and the
5th case of the Foulkes conjecture, arXiv:1509.03944v1,
defines its map on printed p. 2 by symmetric-tensor

and symmetric projection. This is the actual map used

and read. Their original large evaluation matrices

Christian Ikenmeyer, On McKay's propagation theorem for

same grid map on printed p. 2. Theorem 1.3 is on that
page, and its complete proof is §§2–6, printed pp. 3–8.
All of this proof was read. The following precise
normalization clarifications make its auxiliary maps
literal without changing any kernel:

1. In tensor degree \(D=ab\), the source defines
   \(\phi_{ij}=D^{-1}\sum_p\zeta_{ij}^{(p)}\).
   Hence its two-operator coefficient is \(D^{-2}\),
   rather than the printed \(1/[D(D-1)]\). Terms with
   the same tensor position vanish, and the remaining

2. Removing the \(a\) fixed \(f_b\) positions in §4
   multiplies the lower raising product by exactly

3. In §5, fixing positions of the other letters leaves

   the weight vector maps with coefficient
   \((b-\eta_2)/D\). Since
   \(\eta_2\le i-1<a<b\), it is nonzero.

One can also identify the source's raising map with
the normalized transversality map exactly. Index a
source basis by unordered partitions into \(a\)
blocks of size \(b\), and a target basis by unordered
partitions into \(b\) blocks of size \(a\); use averages
over the block labels. The raising-product entry is
\(b!/D^D\) precisely when every source-target block

therefore establishes injectivity of the actual

The normalized symmetric-tensor projectors are

# Exact finite-normal audit of the stable defect formula

Statement **A-048**. Complete proof review of T047, performed on
21 November 2026 by GPT-6 Astra Pro, run /root/archive_audit;
effort setting not exposed.

**Result: complete proof PASS.** The entire report
work/theta/outer5/stable_defect_cohomology_report.md, D.1–D.17,
and both its evaluator and check program were read. The proof
establishes its actual higher-cohomology isomorphism for every
\(s\ge2,\ k\ge3s-1,\ a=b+x,\ b,x\ge0\), with \(c=2k-s\).
Its stated zeroth-cohomology consequence is the exact Euler
character plus the evaluated correction. This audit gives that
assertion its precise stated scope.

## 1. The directional interpolation maps

The four tangent directions at a frame point form a projective
frame in \(\mathbf P^2\). The two quadrics
\[
f=z_1z_2-z_1z_3,\qquad
g=z_1z_2-z_2z_3
\]
have exactly the four displayed projective zeros and independent
gradients there. Their complete intersection is reduced and has
length four. In particular they form a regular sequence.
For \(r=s-1\), the generators \(f^{r-i}g^i\) and the adjacent
relations \(g e_{i-1}-f e_i\) give the exact complex
\[
0\longrightarrow S(-2r-2)^r
\longrightarrow S(-2r)^{r+1}
\longrightarrow J^r\longrightarrow0.
\]
The proof by successive division modulo \(f\) checks every
syzygy. Injectivity on the left follows in order from the
coordinates, since \(f\) and \(g\) are nonzero divisors.
After sheafification and twist \(d\ge2r\), the left summands
have twist at least \(-2\). Projective-plane cohomology proves
that evaluation onto all order-\(r\) directional jets is
surjective. This is the literal polynomial-evaluation map.

The independent calculation also formed those matrices directly
in affine charts for the four direction points. For every
\(1\le r\le8\), their ranks at \(d=2r\) are the full
\(4\binom{r+1}{2}\) row ranks. At \(d=2r-1\), their ranks are
the full column ranks, giving the predicted failure to cover
all jets at that lower degree. Each rank is witnessed by a
maximal nonzero minor modulo \(1000003\), and therefore proves
the same maximal rank over \(\mathbf Q\). These sixteen checks
are additional computations; the displayed resolution proves
the interpolation statement for every \(r\).

## 2. Finite normal restriction as an exact morphism

Fix a pair \(e\), use the stabilizer splitting \(E=P_e\oplus W_e\),
and set \(r=s-1\). The complement of \(\mathbf P(W_e)\) in
\(\mathbf P(E)\) is the total space of
\(W_e\otimes\mathcal O_{\mathbf P(P_e)}(1)\).
The image \(\mathcal B^r_{e,k}(c)\) of the ideal sheaf in the
order-\(r\) normal quotient is, as a module on the base line,
\[
\bigoplus_{0\le j<r}
\operatorname{Sym}^jW_e^*
\otimes (XY)^{k-j}\mathcal O(c-j-2(k-j)).
\tag{SD1}
\]
The exponent \(k-j\) is exactly the remaining endpoint
Taylor order. The other three frame points lie off this line
and impose no condition on its finite normal sheaf.

For precision, define a finite morphism of truncated normal
neighborhoods
\[
t:\operatorname{Tot}_{<r}(W_e\otimes\mathcal O(-1))
\longrightarrow
\operatorname{Tot}_{<r}(W_e\otimes\mathcal O(1)),
\qquad w=XYv.
\tag{SD2}
\]
The notation means that all monomials of normal degree at
least \(r\) have been set to zero. The map is finite because
both structure algebras are finite over the base line.
The coefficient map
\[
F\longmapsto (XY)^{-k}F(X,Y,XYv)
\]
defines an isomorphism
\[
\mathcal B^r_{e,k}(c)\simeq t_*\mathcal O(-s)
\tag{SD3}
\]
of modules for the original normal-neighborhood algebra.
Indeed each normal degree \(j\) in (SD1) contains
\((XY)^{k-j}\); substitution contributes \((XY)^j\),
and cancellation leaves an ordinary regular coefficient.
The inverse multiplies that coefficient by
\((XY)^{k-j}\). The original normal coordinate acts on the
right side by \(XYv\). This proves (SD3) at the endpoints
without inverting \(X\) or \(Y\) in their local rings.

The projection formula consequently gives the actual comparison
\[
\mathcal B^r_{e,k}(c)\otimes S_{(a,b)}Q
\simeq
t_*\bigl(\mathcal O(-s)\otimes S_{(a,b)}t^*Q\bigr).
\tag{SD4}
\]
This identifies exactly the bundle to which the report's
unipotent automorphism is applied.

Write \(p=X\ell_i+Y\ell_j\). On the source of (SD2), put
\[
T=I-\frac12\bigl((Yv)\otimes X^*+(Xv)\otimes Y^*\bigr).
\]
The products \(Xv,Yv\) are global regular \(W_e\)-valued
functions: their two homogeneous degrees cancel. Its
correction has square zero, since both coordinate
functionals vanish on \(W_e\). Thus \(T\) is invertible
with the displayed sign-reversed inverse, and
\[
T(p+XYv)=p.
\]
It is symmetric under endpoint interchange and equivariant
under the other three letters. The induced actual quotient
bundle isomorphism is
\[
t^*Q\simeq
(\det P_e)\mathcal O(1)\oplus W_e.
\tag{SD5}
\]
Equations (SD2)–(SD5) verify all normal couplings, including
the original linear-form differential.

## 3. The global cohomology comparison

For both twists \(C=c\) and \(C=c-1\), the report's binary
overlap functionals compare the coefficients of exponents
\(t\) and \(C-j-t\), with
\[
C-k+1\le t\le k-j-1.
\]
For a normal monomial of degree \(j<r\), its point Taylor
degree is \(t+j\). In the source it is at least \(k-s\),
which is at least \(2s-1\) in the stated range and hence
at least \(2r\). At each fixed total Taylor degree the
leading functionals are exactly a subset of the directional
jets from §1. Chart changes are triangular in the total
degree, with invertible leading coordinate changes.
Taking a largest degree in a proposed relation and descending
therefore proves that every overlap coefficient vanishes.
This proves surjectivity of both scalar restriction maps.

The target dimension is established by the already verified
Cox grading from A-028. Its six binary weights are
\((k-s)^5,k-3s\). For \(k\ge3s\), the binary weight difference is
\[

\frac{(1-z^{k-s+1})^5}{(1-z)^4}
=
\binom{2k-s+3}{3}
-5\binom{k+2}{3}
+10\binom{s+1}{3}.
\]
Terms of numerator order at least three have negative
residual degree. At \(k=3s-1\), the sixth binary weight is
\(-1\); the component is zero. The displayed coefficient
also vanishes by the equality of binary weights \(-1\)
and \(1\), or by direct substitution into the binomial
expression. Hence the endpoint has the same formula.

Subtracting the fat-point length proves
\[

\]
Each normal image has first-cohomology dimension
\[
\sum_{j=0}^{s-2}(j+1)(s-j-1)=\binom{s+1}{3}.
\]
The target scalar restriction is therefore an isomorphism
and the preceding source restriction is onto. The two
maps form the commuting diagram with the actual
locally split Schur complex. Its scalar twists have no
\(H^2,H^3\), so the cokernel on first cohomology gives
the full Schur-bundle first cohomology, and all groups
of degree at least two vanish. This verifies the
global-to-finite-normal comparison in full.

The factor \(\det P_e\) comes from

counts precisely the three possible symmetric-power

### The normal-order map and Cauchy extraction

Put \(r=m-2\). The degree-\(N\) Cauchy decomposition of
\(\operatorname{Sym}(E\otimes F)\) contains precisely the
partitions with at most \(r\) rows. The quotient
\(E\to Q\) gives an actual map
\(S_\alpha E\to H^0(S_\alpha Q)\).
The primitive-idempotent image of
\([\mathcal O(-1)\to E]^{\otimes N}\), with its Koszul
signs, has degree-\(j\) terms indexed by vertical
\(j\)-strips. Thus \(j\le r\). Every negative line
twist \(\mathcal O(-j)\), \(1\le j\le r\), is acyclic
on \(\mathbf P^r\). The locally split tensor
contraction proves exactness before taking sections,
so the quotient map itself induces the asserted
section isomorphism.

At the frame point represented by \(e_0=\ell_i\),
the moving quotient sends
\[
e_0\longmapsto-\sum_jx_je_j.
\]
Its induced algebra map is exactly
\[
Y_{0a}\longmapsto-\sum_jx_jY_{ja}.
\tag{FR1}
\]
Over the fraction field in the remaining rows, the
\(r\times r\) matrix \(Y=(Y_{ja})\) is invertible.
Consequently the least nonzero homogeneous degree
in the \(Y_0\) variables survives (FR1) as exactly
the same \(x\)-degree. Later homogeneous pieces have
larger degree and cannot cancel it. The polynomial
coefficients in the other rows encode the entire
Schur component faithfully. Therefore membership in
\(I_i^k\) is equivalent to order-\(k\) vanishing
of the section, and intersection over all frame
points gives the actual isomorphism FA.2. This
checks the order, rather than merely the value at
the point.

### Product, saturation and the signed complex

At a homogeneous prime different from the irrelevant
ideal, at most \(m-2\) of the \(I_i\) are contained
in that prime: any \(m-1\) frame vectors span \(E\).
Their independent vectors can be completed to a
basis, making their ideals disjoint variable blocks.
Every other ideal is a unit at the prime. For
disjoint blocks, membership in all \(k\)-th powers
is equivalent to degree at least \(k\) in every
block, which is exactly product membership.
Thus the product and intersection have the same
ideal sheaf.

Each block power is saturated: a complementary
variable does not change membership, so a class
killed by an irrelevant-ideal power is already
zero. Intersections preserve saturation. This
proves that the saturation of \(P_k\) is \(J_k\).
Conca–Herzog applies to the \(mk\) repeated nonzero
linear ideals, giving regularity \(mk\) and saturation
degree at most \(mk\). Hence FA.3 and the required
higher-cohomology vanishing hold in the exact
stated range.

The differential in the restriction complex adds
one index with its ordered-subset sign. A frame
permutation has the sign of reordering the image
subset. This is its actual equivariant orientation
line. On a disjoint-block chart, a monomial survives
in the term for \(A\) precisely when every index
in \(A\) belongs to the set of block powers that
do not contain that monomial. Its augmented complex
is the full simplex on that set, contracted by
inserting its least index. This proves sheaf
exactness with the specified maps.

For a subset of size \(s\le m-2\), the quotient
is free over the polynomial ring in the complementary
variables, with normal-monomial shifts at most
\(s(k-1)\). At \(N\ge mk\), all residual twists are
nonnegative; higher cohomology vanishes and global
sections equal the indicated graded pieces. For
\(s\ge m-1\), already \(m-1\) independent truncated
blocks have maximum degree \((m-1)(k-1)<mk\);
their degree-\(N\) component and sheaf vanish.
Regularity also makes the union sheaf acyclic
in these twists and its sections equal to
\(S_N/(J_k)_N\). These observations prove that
taking global sections gives exactly FA.4,
including its last term and all endpoints.

For a subset \(A\), the explicit complement \(W_A\)

### The coherent and locally free \(K_0\) maps

The revised dictionary paragraph is valid.
For completeness, its equivariant resolution
construction terminates by the following direct
argument. At each syzygy \(M_i\), choose an invariant
graded lift of \(M_i/S_+M_i\). Each such space is
finite dimensional, and reductivity of
\(S_m\times GL(F)\) over \(\mathbf Q\) supplies
the lift. The resulting maps
\(S\otimes W_i\to M_i\) are surjective by graded
Nakayama. Their kernels are finitely generated
because \(S\) is Noetherian. This constructs a
minimal equivariant graded free resolution.

If \(D=\dim(E\otimes F)\), the variable Koszul
complex resolves \(\mathbf Q\) in \(D\) steps.
Its exactness follows successively because each
variable is a nonzero divisor modulo its predecessors.
It computes \(\operatorname{Tor}_i^S(M,\mathbf Q)\),
which is zero for \(i>D\). The minimal resolution
has zero differentials after tensoring with
\(\mathbf Q\), so
\[
F_i/S_+F_i=\operatorname{Tor}_i^S(M,\mathbf Q)=0
\quad(i>D).
\]
Graded Nakayama gives \(F_i=0\). Thus the displayed
equivariant resolution is finite, with actual maps.

Sheafification sends each free term to a locally
free equivariant sheaf, and alternating sum gives
its exact \(K_0\) class. Comparison lifts between
resolutions are equivariant because
\(\operatorname{Hom}_{S,G}(S\otimes W,-)\)
is exact; their acyclic mapping cones have zero
alternating class. The same construction on a
short exact sequence gives additivity. This
proves the stated coherent-to-locally-free map,
with its independence of choices.

## 1. Tensor pairings and the actual incidence map

The nested symmetric pairing is the restriction of the ordinary

h_{d,e}(V)^*=h_{e,d}(V^*)
\]
with scalar one. In particular, each subsequent use of transpose
identifies the rank of the particular map being studied.

row arrangement. A transverse unordered column partition has
exactly \(v!u!\) such arrangements: choose the order of its rows
and columns, after which each cell is prescribed by the unique
intersection element. Hence its coefficient is
\[
(u!)^{1-v}.
\]
A nontransverse column partition cannot arise. Thus the incidence
matrix is related to the normalized canonical map by the exact
formula OF.8, and in the fourth square the scalar is \(24^{-3}\).

## 1. Validity, grading and the canonical point-jet map

inequality. The determinant identity for \(Q\), of rank three,
gives \(S_\alpha Q=\mathcal O(c)S_{(a,b)}Q\), since
\((\det E)^c\) is trivial for even \(c\). The actual chart map
then gives exactly the sign \(\operatorname{sgn}^{d+a}\).

The bundle \(S_{(a,b)}Q\) is generated by the quotient of
\(S_{(a,b)}E\). At a fixed point, select global sections spanning
its fiber. Every homogeneous tangent monomial of degree \(j<k\)
is the leading jet of a scalar degree-\(c\) section that vanishes
to order \(j\), because \(c\ge k-1\). Multiplication by the
selected bundle sections spans the entire degree-\(j\) jet
quotient. Correcting jets in increasing order changes none of
the already prescribed lower degrees. This proves surjectivity
onto the full one-point jet space.

The map itself is the canonical restriction map. G-027's
least-normal-degree substitution identifies its kernel with

literal frame-permutation action. No simultaneous independent

argument; the subsequent exact complex computes precisely its
global cokernel.

## 2. The pair term and its actual maps

At subset size three, the complementary space has dimension one.

\[

term is zero. The larger subset terms vanish in degree \(N\ge5k\)
as already proved in G-027.

At size two, the complementary factor has at most two rows.
It must omit the third row of \(\alpha\), of length
\(c=2(k-1)\). This already uses the entire maximum degree of
the two truncated factors. Thus their degrees are each \(k-1\);
the complementary partition is exactly \((a+c,b+c)\);
and the removed skew shape is a single horizontal row of
length \(c\). Its only Schur type is \((c)\).

The multiplication map
\[

\longrightarrow\operatorname{Sym}^{c}F
\]
therefore induces an isomorphism on the required component.
Its restriction to that unique top summand is nonzero, as seen
on a pure power; normalized symmetric comultiplication supplies

fixes multiplication, so no extra pair sign occurs here.

Multiplication of the Cauchy copy in rows \(z_1,z_2\) by

Its \(F\)-type is \(S_\alpha F\), and its \(W\)-type is

multiplicity space. Since \(c\) is even, its determinant

is exactly \(\operatorname{sgn}_{S_2}\).
Induction over the ten pairs gives the module in ER.2.

## 4. Traces and polynomial bounds

The signed tensor Schur complex gives the three scalar Euler

nonzero increment has total at most five. A longer element

further monoid increment.

The graph is best interpreted as a set of actual inputs:
an unstable node represents one point, and a stable node
represents its whole nonnegative first-axis progression of
step ten. Every deficient seed belongs to this represented set.

successor in that set or in the upward-closed full-support set.

For a stable point \(g+10q(1,0,0)\), adding a generator gives
\[

\]
The multiplier for \(h\) and the first-axis multiplier commute
as elements of the same polynomial algebra. First use the stored
edge for \(g+2h\). If it is a full-support exit, all further
axis increments preserve full support. Otherwise retain its
normal representative and any actual stable offset already
removed. Apply the recorded first-axis edge successively for
the remaining finite number of increments. While the state is
unstable, this increases its first gap until it either exits or
reaches the new threshold. At a stable state, the further
increments are isomorphisms and its first-axis edge is a loop
in the represented set.

This explicitly treats an increment that raises \(b,c\) and
raises the stability threshold. It never assumes that the
normal form commutes with that increment. Induction on a finite
generator expression proves that every deficient input is
represented by a listed point or ray. Conversely every listed
point has a deficient computed module, and every represented
stable point has that same module by the actual isomorphism.

## 1. Validity, jet maps and cohomology

Write \(a=b+x\), \(c=2k-3\), and

=\operatorname{sgn}_5\mathcal O(c)S_{(a,b)}Q.
\]
The chart sign is therefore \(\operatorname{sgn}^{d+a}\),
as stated, since \(\lambda_2=d+a+c\) and \(c\) is odd.

Because \(c\ge k-1\), every scalar homogeneous tangent jet
of order less than \(k\) occurs as the leading jet of a section
of \(\mathcal O(c)\). Global sections of \(S_{(a,b)}Q\)
generate its fiber. Multiplying these sections and correcting
jets successively gives the canonical surjection onto each full
point-jet module. This is the individual point map; its direct
sum has exactly the cokernel computed by the arrangement complex.
G-027's normal-order substitution identifies its kernel with the
displayed Schur component of the point ideal power.

The ambient bundle is acyclic, and a finite point-jet sheaf has

zero. The exact degree-\(|\alpha|\) arrangement complex now
identifies this cokernel with the kernel of the actual signed
quotient \(K_2\to K_3\). Its later terms vanish in the proved
degree range. This establishes ET.4 with the stated maps, not

## 1. Exact map and kernel membership

The averaged tensor evaluation pairing gives
\(h_{b,a}^*=h_{a,b}\) on the dual space, with scalar one.
Consequently the actual image annihilator is the displayed lower
canonical kernel; its Schur multiplicity equals the cokernel
multiplicity being bounded. This is the same exact pairing already

The normalized outer comultiplication \(\delta\) has
multiplication as a left inverse. For \(r+1\) outer slots,

\[
\Theta F(v_1,\ldots,v_r;x,y)=
\binom br^r\mathcal A_F
(x^rv_1^{b-r},\ldots,x^rv_r^{b-r},y^b).
\]
There is no unspecified scalar in this formula.

The lower-kernel membership proof was reread in full in R-024
P.9–P.16. A split form \((x^r+c y^r)Q\) is a product of
\(b\) linear forms over \(\mathbf C\). Its first coefficient
in \(c\) gives the vanishing with last argument \(y^rQ\).
Applying the \(b-r\) directional derivatives corresponding
to the factors of \(Q\) to the last argument \(y^b\)
gives exactly the scalar \(b!/r!\) times this vanishing.
Before derivative \(i\), the exchanged variables have degrees
\(b-i+1\) and \(r\), with positive difference
\(b-r-i+1\). On a two-letter string
\(\det^j\operatorname{Sym}^{p+q-2j}\), the derivative
has nonzero coefficient \(p-j\), since \(j\le q<p\).
It is therefore injective on the full bidegree and on every
multiplicity space. The other variables are spectators. Removing
the derivatives successively proves the required vanishing with
last argument \(y^b\). Evaluation in \(x,y\) separates
the two exterior symmetric factors, so the image lies in the
tensor product with the actual lower canonical kernel.

All maps and coefficients are rational; proving the polynomial
identities over \(\mathbf C\) proves their rational identities.
Extension to every characteristic-zero field preserves the kernels
and the injectivity of the resulting linear maps.

## 2. Full-multiplicity injection and its iteration

For \(b_{r+1}=C_{r+1}+t\), the exact recurrence gives
\(b_{r+1}-r=b_r\ge t\ge1\). After \(\delta\),
every first-factor type \(\nu\) contributing to a
\(\lambda\)-type is contained in \(\lambda\), by the
horizontal-strip Pieri rule. Thus \(\nu_2\le t\le b_r\).

the stated range. Division by these exact factors gives an inverse
on the polynomial subspace. The equivariant kernel therefore has
no highest vector of the indicated type, proving injectivity on
the entire isotypic space rather than on a selected vector.

The direct sum of these first-factor types is still injective:

last symmetric factor. Tensoring preserves injectivity. In the
resulting codomain every lower kernel type is contained in the
output type by two applications of Pieri, and hence has second

Iterating this specified map on its middle factor, using ordinary
factor permutations, gives FK.10. The degree identity
\((r+1)b_{r+1}-r b_r=r^2+b_{r+1}\) checks at every stage.
No projection onto an unspecified image or multiplicity basis is
needed in this iteration.

The independent script `check_finite_base_tails_independent.py`

# Primary oscillator source audit

Statement **A-059**. Checked 21 November 2026 by GPT-6 Astra Pro,
run `/root/archive_audit`; effort setting not exposed.

Primary source: T. Basile, E. Joung, K. Mkrtchyan and M. Mojaza,
*Dual Pair Correspondence in Physics: Oscillator Realizations and
Representations*, arXiv:2006.07102v2, subsequently JHEP 09 (2020) 020,
DOI 10.1007/JHEP09(2020)020.
https://arxiv.org/pdf/2006.07102v2

The web PDF fetch returned a disabled-fetch error. A direct request
to that same primary URL then returned an actual 952017-byte PDF,
saved as `OSCILLATOR_DUALITY_2020V2.pdf`; extracted text is saved
alongside. This audit read the text and mathematical formulas,
without claiming new visual inspection of the page images.

## Exact passages read

- §5.1, (5.7)–(5.20), printed pp.28–29: compact oscillator
  realization, central shifts, Young conditions and Cauchy duality.
- Entire §5.2, (5.21)–(5.30), printed pp.29–31: the
  \(U(M_+,M_-)\), \(U(N)\) differential operators, minimal
  oscillator state, contraction conditions and mixed highest weight.
- Appendix A, (A.21)–(A.28), printed pp.76–77, together with
  the surrounding derivation: the mixed tensor, exterior-column
  contraction and the resulting complementary highest weight.
- The representation convention (1.16), printed p.7; the
  explicit cover discussion (2.12)–(2.18), printed p.10; and
  (2.23)–(2.25), printed p.11. These specify the source's use
  of double-cover compact groups and its half-integral weights.

## Statements established by these passages

The differential operators in (5.21) have diagonal shifts
\(+N/2\) in the positive block and \(-N/2\) in the
negative block. The compact partner (5.22) has scalar diagonal
shift \((M_+-M_-)/2\). The contraction equations (5.28)
identify the mixed traceless tensor of (5.29), whose unshifted
highest weight is
\[
(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_p,0,\ldots,0,-m_q,\ldots,-m_1).
\]
The exterior-column Levi–Civita contraction in (A.25) is the
actual map to the polynomial highest weight obtained after a
determinant twist; (A.26)–(A.28) display that weight explicitly.
The strict range \(p+q<N\) proposed for T-052 lies within
all the dimensional inequalities used in this passage.

The source explicitly includes the covering-group convention.
Its symbols must retain that convention when the displayed
half-integral generators are used literally. For example a
positive-block vacuum coordinate of weight \(N/2\) acquires
\((-1)^N\) around the corresponding \(2\pi\) circle. This
is an exact monodromy calculation, and (2.12)–(2.18) explains
the analogous issue in the source. A proposed unshifted action
or an honest-group identification needs its actual changed
generators and integration, rather than suppressing the shifts.
No objection to the source's stated cover convention is claimed.

## A precise equality-boundary correction

The sentence immediately before (A.23), printed p.76, says that
traceless tensors vanish at \(p+q\ge N\). At equality this
is false. For \(N=2\), let \(e_1,e_2\) be the standard
basis and \(e_1^*,e_2^*\) its dual. The actual contraction
\[
\mathbf C^2\otimes(\mathbf C^2)^*\longrightarrow\mathbf C,
\qquad v\otimes\phi\longmapsto\phi(v)
\]
kills the nonzero tensor \(e_1\otimes e_2^*\). It has
the two one-box symmetries, so \(p=q=1\) and \(p+q=N\).
It is the highest vector of weight \((1,-1)\) for the usual
upper-triangular convention. Thus the equality claim is refuted
by the displayed morphism. The source's later paragraph before
(A.28) correctly permits \(p+q\le N\), as does (A.21).
The intended T-052 range is strict and does not use the rejected
equality sentence.

This is a source audit and an explicit boundary correction. It
does not certify the entire new T-052 construction, which had
not yet been supplied when these checks were recorded.

## 1. Parameters and first-row endpoints

For \(e=0\), summation gives
\[
N=(m-1)\lambda_2+\lambda_1-mn,\qquad
N-mk=\lambda_1-\lambda_2.

For \(e>0\), \(n_0=\lambda_2,k=0\), and

The first-row map is literal multiplication by \(u^e\), where

in every block. Each first coordinate therefore has excess

## 2. Operators, adjoints and real dual pair

The Weyl relations give exactly
\[
[C_a,R_b]=\sum_iX_{bi}\partial_{X_{ai}}
+\delta_{ab}(N_Y+m)=A_{ba}-\delta_{ab}A_{00}.
\]
Together with the compact brackets this verifies every block
of the matrix-unit relation. The two terms of \(G_{ij}\)
are the standard and dual \(\mathfrak{gl}_m\) actions.
Their commutators with \(R_a\) cancel literally, as do
their derivative commutators with \(C_a\). The common center
has exactly the scalar \(m(r-1)/2\), and every \(A\)
preserves each individual charge.

The factorial monomial form gives \(R_a^\dagger=C_a\)
and all adjoints in OC.11. In \(\mathfrak u(r,1)\),
the two mixed matrix coefficients are complex conjugates,
while the represented operators are negative adjoints.
This gives the asserted skew-adjoint real action. The compact
real form follows from \(B_{ij}^\dagger=B_{ji}\).

A real-linear commutant of \(U(r,1)\) commutes with its
scalar \(i\), hence is complex-linear. The phases, positive
unitaries and a mixed boost span the matrix units on
\(H=\mathbf C^{r,1}\), so its complex commutant on
\(H\otimes W\) is \(1\otimes\operatorname{End}W\).
Preserving the imaginary Hermitian form and complex linearity
recovers its real part, giving exactly \(U(m)\). The reverse
centralizer is obtained by the same calculation.

The positive compatible complex structure is \(i\) on the
positive part and \(-i\) on the negative part. The latter
turns its creation representation into \(W^*\), giving
\(F\otimes W\oplus W^*\). Its determinant is
\[
(\det a)^m z^{-m}(\det g)^{r-1}.
\]
The vacuum square and its half derivatives therefore give
every shift in OC.7, including the negative-block sign.

The source cover convention was checked in A-059, and this
report retains it. Removing the compact vacuum character gives

tensoring by its inverse on the pullback cover cancels the
central kernel and descends to literal permutation matrices.
For odd \(r\), the integral determinant character gives the
stated section and sign. No fractional sign character of

## 3. Charge, quotient and harmonic projection

A block-homogeneous monomial of degree \(d_i\ge k\) has
forced \(Y_i\)-exponent \(d_i-k\). Hence OC.14 is a
bijection, with inverse erasing \(Y\), and commutes with
row changes and column permutations. Raising the block degree

multiplication is transported to the \(R_a\)'s.

The all-degree T-049 quotient theorem applies at

On the finite charge-degree space, the denominator's
orthogonal complement is exactly the common lowering kernel.
The operator \(T=\sum_aR_aC_a\) is positive semidefinite;

For \(\det(t-T)=t^s q(t)\), \(q(0)\ne0\),
diagonalizability proves that \(q(T)/q(0)\) is identity
on the zero eigenspace and zero elsewhere. Its coefficients
are rational. Harmonic inclusion followed by the quotient is

The rightmost derivative in
\((N_i-k+1)\partial_{Z_{ai}}\) acts first; the resulting
coefficient is \(d_i-k\). It vanishes at the truncation
boundary. The transported norm
\(\prod_i u_i!(d_i-k)!\) independently verifies its adjoint

## 4. Harmonic irreducibles and all dual maps

Cauchy extraction gives a row type \(S_\alpha F\) and the
mixed tensor \(S_\alpha W\otimes\operatorname{Sym}^bW^*\).
The row contraction equations are exactly the traceless
conditions after Young projection. The primary §5.2 and

At \(b>0\), \(\ell(\alpha)+1\le m-1<m\), strictly

The vector \(Y_m^b\prod_j\Delta_j^{\alpha_j-\alpha_{j+1}}\)

The identity

The remaining dual is handled by the displayed Gram map.
The rational Young image and its balanced subspace have

The one-column homogenization gives the four operators OC.29

OC.20 assigns a compact weight

## 1. Rees multiplication and the affine quotient

For block degrees \(d_i\ge k\), the charge homogenization

unit and the coefficient algebra at degree zero. In particular,
\(\ell_i\otimes f_a\) maps to \([X_{ai}Y_i]\), while
\(t\prod_i(\ell_i\otimes f_{a_i})\) maps to

The substitution and homogenization commute with row changes
and column permutations. They preserve row weight, \(X\)-degree
and charge; \(Y\)-degree is forced to be \(N-mk\).

## 2. Complete direct normal forms and flat family

Replacing \(M_a\) by the negative remainder therefore strictly
decreases the total diagonal-variable degree. Termination holds

The leading monomials \(M_a\) are pairwise coprime.
The two reductions from \(qM_aM_b\) both reach
\(qT_aT_b\); repeated occurrences of one rule are identical.
Induction on the decreasing diagonal degree proves uniqueness
of every linear normal form. Such a form kills every multiple
of a relation, and each reduction preserves the ideal residue.
The standard monomials are therefore a basis. Because every
step also lowers the displayed monomial order, the initial ideal
is exactly \((M_1,\ldots,M_r)\).

For a nonzero standard representative modulo the first \(a-1\)

from the previous leading monomials, so it remains indivisible

required nonzerodivisor step, hence the regular sequence.

The same diamond proof works over \(\mathbf Q[s]\),

## 3. Literal bounded polytopes and smaller-row transport

A standard monomial has exponents \(u_{ai},v_i\).

# A064 — independent review of the two-column unit family

## 1. Exterior kernel and the unique invariant

The map UT.3 is the literal raising operator on the two summands in the exterior algebra of \(W\otimes\mathbf Q^2\). With all first-copy wedge factors placed before second-copy factors, moving the \(l\)-th second-copy vector to the first copy gives exactly the sign \((-1)^{l-1}\) in the report. In skew Cauchy, the source weight \((j,j)\) occurs in the \(\mathrm{GL}_2\)-factor of shape \((2j-k,k)\), with raising scalar \(j-k\). It vanishes exactly at \(k=j\). Thus the kernel is the actual embedded \(S_{(2^j)}W\), including the endpoint \(j=\dim W\), where the target exterior power vanishes.

For \(W=\mathfrak h_a\), the hook identification is explicit. The ordered-singleton tabloid map to \(e_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge e_{i_q}\) sends the column antisymmetrizer to

\[
q!\,(e_{i_1}-e_{i_0})\wedge\cdots\wedge(e_{i_q}-e_{i_0}).
\]

Fixing \(i_0=a\) gives a spanning set of \(\Lambda^q\mathfrak h_a\). Its dimension is \(\binom{a-1}{q}\), so this is the stated hook Specht isomorphism, with its scalar and all ranks checked. The hooks in \(\Lambda^{j+1}\mathfrak h_a\) and \(\Lambda^{j-1}\mathfrak h_a\) differ; their tensor product has no invariant. The determinant inner products identify each exterior power with its dual. Consequently the source of UT.3 has a one-dimensional invariant line, and its invariant line lies in the kernel. This proves the claimed one-dimensional invariant space in \(S_{(2^j)}\mathfrak h_a\).

The inverse Gram tensor \(\Omega_j\) is nonzero and realizes this line. The tensor \(J=(P\otimes P)\sum_i e_i\otimes e_i\), with \(P=1-a^{-1}\mathbf1\mathbf1^t\), is the ordinary coevaluation tensor of \(\mathfrak h_a\). Applying the two exterior maps to \(J^{\otimes j}\) produces \(j!\Omega_j\): the ordered choices of a fixed increasing index set contribute precisely \(j!\). This verifies the matching, Gram, and invariant constructions as actual maps, not only dimension equalities.

## 2. The balanced flag morphism

The displayed minors \(v_{j+1,I}\) have row weight one and right weight \((a-j,1^j)\). On \(u\ne0\), they are the components of

\[
u\,\mathbf1\wedge\bar w_2\wedge\cdots\wedge\bar w_{j+1}.
\]

The map \(\Lambda^j\mathfrak h_a\to\Lambda^{j+1}\mathbf Q^a\), \(z\mapsto\mathbf1\wedge z\), is injective; on its image its inverse is contraction by \(\mathbf1/a\). Hence the smaller flag coordinates used by the report have the claimed ordinary permutation action. The smaller flag relations follow by evaluating on the centered column matrix.

The map on \(S_{(2^j)}\mathfrak h_a\) is multiplication by \(u^{n-2}\) after substitution of these minors. It has the stated balanced row weight and highest weight \((an-2j,2^j)\). Its injectivity has a concrete dense inverse: prescribe nonzero \(u_0\), select the first coordinates with product \(u_0\), and choose subsequent columns by dividing the first centered column by \(u_0\). This realizes arbitrary smaller flag matrices on the open chart.

Surjectivity follows because the shape has exactly two columns of height greater than one. Replacing those two ordinary minors by their balanced expressions leaves exactly \(u^{n-2}\); all remaining first-column factors cancel by row balance. The exponent is nonnegative for every \(n\ge2\), including \(n=2\). This proves the exact balanced-module isomorphism and its \(S_a\)-equivariance, with no unaccounted determinant sign. ## 3. Canonical-image and rectangular consequences

The stated canonical rank-one ranges follow from the already audited second-row-two specialization of R034. Both the full band restriction and its finite-base hypotheses are satisfied.

For UT.18–UT.19 I independently opened the primary Ikenmeyer–Panova PDF, *Rectangular Kronecker coefficients and plethysms in geometric complexity theory*, arXiv:1512.03798v2, and read Theorem 2.1 on printed p.5, the definitions and complete Proposition 2.5–2.6 proofs on p.6, and Lemma 2.7 plus the complete Proposition 2.8 proof on p.7:

## 1. The actual highest vectors

The polynomial \(F_{a,n,j}\) is symmetric in the \(a\) slots, has degree \(n\) in each slot, and has right highest weight \((an-2j,2^j)\). These statements follow directly from the initial minors and the factors of the first coordinates in SR.4. Its nonzero value is established by setting all first coordinates to one and including \(0,e_1,\ldots,e_j\) among the remaining slot vectors; it becomes a sum of squared real minors with a nonzero term. A064 proves that its highest-weight multiplicity is one, so it spans the specified highest line.

## 2. Exact polarization scalar

The report's normalized pairing sends \(\ell_1^a\cdots\ell_n^a\) under the grid regrouping map to \((\ell_1\cdots\ell_n)^a\) with scalar one. Thus the transposed map evaluates the polarized form at \(a\) copies of \(Q=\ell_1\cdots\ell_n\), exactly as in SR.5.

On the affine chart \(\ell_k=(1,v_k)\), put \(s=\sum_kv_k\), \(T=\sum_kv_kv_k^t\), and \(\mu=s/n\). The one-slot degree-two moment matrix is

\[
B=\begin{pmatrix}1&\mu^t\\ \mu&M\end{pmatrix},
\qquad M=\frac{ss^t-T}{n(n-1)}.
\]

I checked both distinct and repeated coordinate indices against the factorial pairing \((n-|\beta|)!\prod_i\beta_i!/n!\). The same matrix is obtained in both cases. Expanding the two determinants of one squared minor and applying the slot functionals gives \((j+1)!\det B\). Summing over its \(\binom a{j+1}\) slot sets therefore gives \((a)_{j+1}\det B\), with every outside factor contributing one.

The Schur complement is literally

\[
M-\mu\mu^t=-\frac{T-ss^t/n}{n(n-1)}.
\]

For the \(n\)-row matrix whose rows are \((1,v_k)\), Cauchy–Binet gives

\[
F_{n,a,j}(1,v_1;\ldots;1,v_n)
=n\det(T-ss^t/n).
\]

Combining these equalities gives the exact scalar, including its sign and both denominator exponents:

\[
h_{a,n}F_{a,n,j}
=\frac{(-1)^j(a)_{j+1}}{n^{j+1}(n-1)^j}\,F_{n,a,j}.
\]

The identity on the open first-coordinate chart extends to the full polynomial identity by multihomogeneity and density. At \(j<n\), choosing \(e_1,\ldots,e_j\) and zero remaining vectors gives centered determinant \((n-j)/n\ne0\). At \(j\ge n\), all corresponding minors vanish because the matrix has only \(n\) rows. This matches the row-length obstruction for the opposite plethysm and proves every scalar endpoint without division by a vanishing quantity; throughout this part \(n\ge2\).

The canonical map in the rank statement is the transpose grid map. Rational invariant perfect pairings identify each finite multiplicity block with the transpose block, so their ranks agree. The target multiplicity is one by A064. Hence the actual map has rank one exactly at \(j<n\), and rank zero at \(j\ge n\).

## 3. All other partitions in the band

For a tail \(\nu=(2^j,1^k)\) with \(k>0\), the stable balanced chart is valid because \(n\ge2\ge\lambda_2\). Skew Cauchy gives the literal Young-component embedding

\[
S_{(2^j,1^k)}\mathfrak h_a
\lhook\joinrel\longrightarrow
\Lambda^{j+k}\mathfrak h_a\otimes\Lambda^j\mathfrak h_a.
\]

The two exterior factors are distinct self-dual hook Specht modules by the explicit polytabloid map checked in A064. Their tensor product has zero invariant space. The injection consequently proves the full ones-tail vanishing, including \(j=0\) and maximal admissible exterior degrees.

The remaining nonzero tails are the pure two tails and the empty tail. The latter is the one-row component, on which the grid map takes the pure-power generator to itself. Partitions with more than \(a\) rows have zero target multiplicity by the iterated Pieri filtration. The displayed cokernel sum is therefore exactly the sum of the missing pure-two components \(n\le j\le a-1\), each once; characteristic-zero semisimplicity justifies the direct sum. Terms whose Schur functor vanishes in a chosen smaller vector-space rank are zero there, as asserted. The separate degree-one cases are the literal symmetric-power identity.

All constructions use normalized tensor permutations, multiplication, minors, and rational pairings. Their naturality with respect to the vector space proves the stated bundle transport by descent through frame changes. No assertion of exactness after an arbitrary pullback is required.

G_{n,a,s}.

# A071 — independent review of the higher-row width-four canonical family

## 1. The invariant algebra and the unit bound

The signed row-power-sum induction used in HO.3 works for all finite row counts. Its discrete equality partition is the injective row-assignment sum; all other nonzero terms have fewer occupied rows with their literal exterior signs. Equal odd row types have an odd stabilizer transposition and average to zero. Projection to the sum-zero representation is equivariantly split and removes the singleton generators. This proves the actual surjection in HO.3.

In the six two-form variables, the only incomparable pair of two-subsets under componentwise order is \((1,4),(2,3)\). The displayed Plücker replacement removes one copy of each offending factor and introduces neither. It terminates. Comparable products correspond to the two-row semistandard tableaux, and their diagonal monomials in a generic two-by-four matrix are distinct: the two sorted row multisets determine the tableau. A diagonal-leading term order therefore proves their independence.

The Pfaffian is an irreducible quadratic because its bilinear matrix has rank six, whereas a factored quadratic has rank at most two. On its \(X_{12}\ne0\) chart, the minor map realizes every permitted coordinate and solves for \(X_{34}\). Primality then gives the exact kernel globally. The nonzero highest-column map and the semistandard dimension count identify the degree-\(d\) quotient with \(S_{(d,d)}T\). Multiplication by the determinant-weight Pfaffian, followed by characteristic-zero complete reducibility, gives exactly
\[
\operatorname{Sym}^d(\Lambda^2T)
=\bigoplus_{q=0}^{\lfloor d/2\rfloor}
S_{(d-q,d-q,q,q)}T.
\]

The exterior contraction also gives \(\Lambda^3(\Lambda^3T)=(\det T)^2\otimes T\). Since the target total degree is odd, only exterior degrees one and three occur. Degree three has fourth part at least two and cannot produce \(\gamma_4=1\). For degree one, a determinant generator can occur at most once; after one such factor, the remaining target has only two nonzero rows, so it cannot contain the required vertical three-strip. With no determinant generator, the only strip adds in rows \(1,3,4\) to \((m-1,m-1,0,0)\). This remains an admissible unique strip at \(m=2\). Hence the invariant space has dimension at most one, with the actual Schur maps specified in the report.

## 2. The centered highest vector and its affine minor formula

The tensor contraction in HO.9 transforms by
\[
(\det\mathbf Q^m)^2\otimes
\operatorname{Sym}^2(\mathbf Q^m)\otimes(\mathbf Q^m)^*.
\]
The two covariant indices \(1,1\) and the final dual index \(m\) give an actual highest component. Its weight is \((4,2^{m-2},1)\). Common translations and row permutations preserve the centered formula.

For HO.10, both centering column operations have determinant one. The operation on the quadratic column is available because \(m\ge2\) and its linear \(w_1\) column is present. The centered \(R^tB\) has first column \((a,0,\ldots,0)^t\), and its remaining block is \(S\) with its final column replaced by \((C_{i11})\). Last-column cofactor expansion gives \(aH_{a,m}\); the written indices \(\operatorname{adj}(S)_{im}\) agree with the cofactor indices because \(S\), hence its adjugate, is symmetric. Cauchy–Binet gives exactly the product of the two minors, with no additional orientation sign.

Each row has degree at most three in this product. On the specified centered configuration,
\[
\operatorname{adj}(S)=(m+1)I-\mathbf1\mathbf1^t,\qquad
(C_{11i})=(0,-1,\ldots,-1).
\]
Their final component is \(-(m+1)+(m-1)=-2\). Thus \(H=-2\) and \(A=-2a\), including the minimal number \(a=m+1\) of rows.

The homogenized minor formula has denominator cancellation exactly as printed: the first determinant contributes one power of every inside \(x_i\), the second contributes two, and \(u^n\) leaves the factors in HO.13. Every slot has degree \(n\). The two row-permutation determinant signs cancel. The common-translation and lower-coordinate highest equations give precisely HO.1's weight.

Dehomogenization is injective in the fixed slot degrees. Common translation invariance identifies its image with polynomials on the sum-zero row quotient through the explicit centering projection. Cauchy Young extraction then embeds its highest space into the invariant module bounded in §1. The nonzero homogeneous vector extends at \(n=3\) because its per-row degree is three, even though the largest tail part is four. This proves multiplicity one throughout the stated target domain.

## 3. Exact determinant pairing, scalar, and inverse

Expanding both determinants in HO.14 and fixing the first permutation leaves the determinant of the moment-pairing matrix, with the same sign. There are exactly \((m+1)!\) first permutations. The first column is \((1,0,\ldots,0)^t\), so the lower block has \(m-1\) second-moment columns and one third-moment column. Summing over its \(\binom a{m+1}\) subsets gives exactly \((a)_{m+1}\), with every outside slot contributing \(L(1)=1\).

The normalized split-form pairing gives the second moment \(-S/[n(n-1)]\) and the third moment \(2C/[n(n-1)(n-2)]\). These are ordered-distinct-index identities, including repeated coordinate labels. Factoring the scalars from the \(m-1\) second-moment columns and the one third-moment column gives
\[
\frac{2(-1)^{m-1}}{n^m(n-1)^m(n-2)}.
\]
The remaining determinant is \(H_{n,m}=A_{n,m}/n\), so the exact final scalar is
\[
c_{a,n,m}
=\frac{2(-1)^{m-1}(a)_{m+1}}
{n^{m+1}(n-1)^m(n-2)}.
\]
Translation and separate homogeneity extend the computation on first coordinates one to the full polynomial identity.

For the desired map with parameters reversed, the reciprocal of \(c_{n,a,m}\) is exactly

{2(n)_{m+1}},
\]
as in HO.18. It gives the actual rational preimage when \(a,n\ge m+1\).

For \(3\le n\le m\), the opposite minor sum is empty. Independently, its source sits in the tensor product of \(n\) one-row symmetric powers, and the actual iterated Pieri inclusions give at most \(n\) rows. The specified \(\lambda\) has \(m+1\) rows, so the source multiplicity is zero while the target remains the proved unit line. This proves the entire zero-image range. All displayed denominators remain nonzero in their declared domains.

## 4. Coordinate and bundle maps

R037 EP.3–EP.5 gives the product morphism \(V^a\to\operatorname{Sym}^aV\), its algebra pullback, and its degree-\(n\) component with scalar-one normalized grid convention. I reread this passage: the evaluation tensor \(v_1^n\cdots v_a^n\) maps under the transposed grid to \((v_1\cdots v_a)^n\). Thus the nonzero cases of HO.17–HO.18 give the claimed nonzero Chow coordinate-ring classes through this exact morphism.

The Young and tensor maps are natural in the vector space and therefore have these same multiplicity matrices in every dimension at least \(m+1\). The actual perfect-pairing maps give

projection therefore give the uniform unit upper bound.

S_{(3,2^{m-3},1,0)}W^*$. The four exterior-column pairings

## 2. The tensor, highest weight and exact affine identity

The complementary-minor tensor

$$
A_{ij,kl}=\det(S)(G_{ik}G_{jl}-G_{il}G_{jk}),\qquad G=S^{-1},
$$

is polynomial at singular $S$ by its complementary-minor expansion.
It transforms as $\det^2$ times four contravariant indices.
Contracting it with two third-moment tensors leaves three covariant
and one contravariant indices. In
$F=\mathcal F_{112}^{\,m}-\mathcal F_{121}^{\,m}$, the

All other raising operators kill the two terms: the only covariant
labels are one and two, while the dual label is already $m$.
The exact weight is
$(2,\ldots,2)+2e_1+e_2-e_m=\nu$.
Centering proves translation invariance and the row sums prove
row-permutation invariance.

The weighted determinant identity has the reported sign and factor.
After centering, the upper-left entry of $R^tB_t$ is $a$,
its bottom first column is zero, and its remaining bottom columns

Weighting rows by $1+\epsilon z_{i2}$ for $B_1$ and
$1+\epsilon z_{i1}$ for $B_2$ gives identical fourth-moment
last-column variations, which cancel. The Schur-complement
corrections in the last column are multiples of $S_{:2}$ and
$S_{:1}$; both are among the retained columns because $m\ge3$.
Their determinants vanish separately.

The remaining derivative is

$$
a\left(v_1^t(d\,\operatorname{adj}_S[C_2])e_m
-v_2^t(d\,\operatorname{adj}_S[C_1])e_m\right)=-aF.
$$

Substituting
$d\,\operatorname{adj}_S[M]
=\det S\{\operatorname{tr}(GM)G-GMG\}$
gives exactly the negative of the two stated cofactor contractions.
Polynomiality then extends the identity to singular matrices.

Weighted Cauchy–Binet computes that derivative as the subset sum
with inside weights $\sum_{i\in I}z_{ip}$. Multiplication by $a$
and substitution $z=w-\bar w$ gives

displayed $L_{I,p}$. Thus $D=-a^2F$ with no omitted scalar.

The per-row degree-four cancellation is termwise. Such a term
must use that row's linear entry in $R$, its quadratic last-column
entry in $B_t$, and its own entry in $L_{I,p}$. The two last-column
cofactors coincide; the residual row factors
$w_{i2}w_{i1}^2$ and $w_{i1}(w_{i1}w_{i2})$ coincide.
Their signs and coefficient $a-m-1$ are the same, so the

For the displayed centered configuration,

The scalar products give

Thus every printed entry is correct. In the expression for $F$,

Appending zero rows preserves these centered moments. The

## 4. The normalized canonical scalar and every endpoint

For an independent-row functional with zero first moments,
all outside-row weights in HC.10 have expectation zero.
For a fixed inside subset, the two-determinant permutation expansion
gives $(m+1)!$ times the moment determinant. Its upper-left entry

Substituting the normalized split-form moments

For $a,n\ge m+2$, both generators and the scalar are nonzero,

## 1. Exact kernel and invariant-algebra section

The stable-chart and determinant-column maps give the stated sign-twisted first hook. The multiplication map $P\otimes E\to P_+$ is the actual differential, and the natural polarization satisfies $\delta\nabla=D$ in total degree $D$. Thus $1-\nabla\delta/D$ is the indicated projection onto its hook kernel.

The homogeneous coinvariant section is chosen over $\mathbb Q$ and averaged over the finite group; multiplication gives the graded equivariant free $I$-module isomorphism. For a nontrivial Specht label, its isotypic component contains no degree-zero target, so the kernel sequence surjects onto the full free multiplicity module.

For each homogeneous free target generator, the lift $\nabla/D$ is specified. Extending these chosen lifts $I$-linearly is an actual section. The proof does not require the gradient itself to be $I$-linear on arbitrary products. Its resulting direct summand is a finitely generated graded projective module.

Choosing lifts of a basis modulo $I_+$ gives a graded free cover. Graded Nakayama gives surjectivity; the projective splitting makes the quotient sequence exact modulo $I_+$. Its kernel has zero quotient, so graded Nakayama makes the kernel zero. This proves the claimed graded freeness through the actual chosen maps. Rational row reduction specifies every lift in finite degree. No polynomial-time claim is attached to constructing this potentially large free basis.

## 2. Numerator and trivial cycle module

The exterior trace specialization removes the factor at $(1,1)$. In exterior degree one, the nontrivial label has the specified $(2,1)$ term of content $-1$; multiplying by $q$ and subtracting the target cancels precisely that term. The remaining shifted fake degrees are nonnegative, with nonnegative exponents. The numerator degree bound $M+1$ follows from its exact coinvariant expression, whose two fake degrees lie in degrees at most $M$.

For the trivial label, Solomon's actual differential basis has scaled generators $\xi_i=de_i/i$ with $\delta\xi_i=e_i$. In a fixed positive invariant monomial degree, all available basis vectors map to the same monomial. Subtracting the unique least-support-index vector gives the explicit star basis FH.15. At $m=4$, multiplying that exact series by the specified invariant denominator gives $q^5+q^6+q^7-q^9$. A finite graded free module over this invariant algebra would have a numerator equal to the sum of its homogeneous basis degrees with nonnegative coefficients. The negative coefficient therefore proves precisely the stated failure of graded freeness for this trivial module. The positive star basis supplies its actual alternative presentation.

## 3. Support, polytopes and complexity

For every non-row label with $m\ge4$, the numerator has both its lowest degree and the next one. # A-089. Whole-proof audit of R046
