## 1. Exact highest-space chart and degree bound

For a nonempty tail, $D\ge t$, so
$N=\lfloor(D+t)/2\rfloor\ge t$.
The integer inequality $D+t\le2n+1$ is exactly $n\ge N$. Thus the stated range guarantees the slot-degree bound needed by the chart.

The dehomogenized highest vector is translation invariant and factors through the actual sum-zero projection. The Cauchy and fixed rational Young projectors identify its lower highest component with the invariant Schur space. Every row-basis weight in $S_\nu E_a$ is at most $\nu_1=t$: each of the $t$ columns contains a given basis letter at most once. Since the inclusion $W_a\hookrightarrow E_a$ and its Schur map are actual linear maps, this bounds the separate row degrees of every vector under consideration. Hence the displayed homogenization is an inverse on the entire invariant highest space for $n\ge t$.

## 2. Ordinary moment algebra and its evaluation

The degree-$d$ generator map is the literal centered row power sum, with scalar one. In the uncentered algebra, products expand by equality partitions of occupied rows. The discrete partition gives the corresponding injective row-assignment sum, and every other term merges row types. The induction and the nonzero factorial multiplicities give surjectivity in every finite row count.

When $s\ge D$, all row assignments needed in scalar degrees at most $D$ exist. Ordering the monomial types by occupied rows gives a triangular basis change with nonzero diagonal, proving injectivity as well. The fixed decomposition into the trivial row line and $W_s$ gives the degree-one polynomial factor; setting it to zero is precisely centering. Quotienting that identified factor proves the centered isomorphism through degree $D$.

A generator of degree $d>t$ cannot contribute to the $S_\nu U$ component. The actual Pieri projection from a factor $\operatorname{Sym}^dU$ requires a horizontal strip with $d$ distinct columns, whereas $\nu$ has only $t$ columns. This proves the precise formal moment truncation used in the factorization.

## 3. Finite-row faithfulness of the specified power-sum map

The ordered-row exterior identification carries the true permutation action to supersymmetric tensor permutations with their Koszul signs. Decomposing by row exterior degree gives TM.8 through literal symmetric and alternating projectors. A nonzero term has at most $t$ degree-one rows, because that factor is an exterior power of $T=\mathbb Q^t$. All other nonempty rows have degree at least two. Therefore a degree-$e$ term uses at most $\lfloor(e+t)/2\rfloor$ rows.

For $e\le D$ and $s\ge N$, every possible term occurs, with the remaining rows filled by the unit. The full $GL(T)$ character of the uncentered invariant exterior algebra is consequently constant in these degrees. The actual decomposition
$C_s(T)=\Lambda T\otimes B_s(T)$
has constant term one in its first factor. Degree induction therefore proves constancy of the centered character, and skew-Cauchy extracts constancy of the precise $\nu$ multiplicity.

The proof then supplies the required morphism. The orthogonal transpose $q$ of zero-padding satisfies
$q(P_Se_i)=P_se_i$ for $i\le s$ and zero otherwise.
This identity makes both ordinary and exterior power-sum generators restrict with scalar one. The ordinary restriction is surjective; the equality-partition argument gives the same conclusion for the exterior generators. Tensor powers of $q$ commute with the fixed Young projectors, so both Cauchy descriptions induce the same $S_\nu(q)$ on row multiplicity spaces.

Choose $S\ge\max(s,D)$. At $S$, the ordinary moment map is an isomorphism by the basis argument above. The invariant restriction onto row count $s\ge N$ is surjective and its domain and target multiplicities have the equal dimensions just proved. Thus it is an isomorphism on this precise component. The generator identity
$p_s=\operatorname{Sym}(q\otimes1)p_S$
then proves injectivity and surjectivity of this particular $p_s$. This is the actual finite-row faithfulness needed later.

## 4. Independent-row polarization and triangular moment substitution

The independent-row evaluation is injective by rational polarization of its diagonal functional. On translation-invariant polynomials it remains injective after normalization and setting first moments to zero: recenter a normalized functional by its own mean, then restore nonnormalized functionals by homogeneity on the dense open set $L(1)\ne0$. This is the same exact argument already checked in A085, in arbitrary finite auxiliary dimension.

Its output is a polynomial in the formal moments of degrees two through $t$, preserves scalar degree and is $GL(U)$-equivariant. It therefore remains in the $S_\nu U$ component on which the preceding faithfulness applies.

For a repeated-coordinate monomial with multiplicities $\beta$, the ordered distinct-factor sum is $\prod\beta_j!$ times the corresponding coefficient of the product linear form. Dividing by $(n)_d$ gives exactly $(n-d)!\prod\beta_j!/n!$, the scalar-one normalized pairing. This verifies every repeated-index normalization in TM.15.

Möbius inversion on equality partitions gives the block coefficient
$(-1)^{|B|-1}(|B|-1)!$.
The signed permutation count by cycle partition verifies its recurrence. Each set partition occurs once with its coordinate positions retained. The first moments vanish, so singleton blocks disappear. The one-block contribution is
$(-1)^{d-1}(d-1)!p_d/(n)_d$;
every other contribution uses lower-degree generators. For $n\ge t$, all displayed leading scalars are nonzero. Recursive substitution in degrees $2,\ldots,t$ therefore gives an actual graded equivariant algebra automorphism and its inverse.

## 5. Exact canonical factorization and rank

On the first-coordinate chart, the normalized grid pairing on a row-symmetric highest polynomial is exactly the same row functional in each of its $a$ rows. Hence the output is
$p_n\Psi_nE_a(f)$,
with no extra scalar. The calculation on centered rows determines the entire affine output: common translation is the explicit first-coordinate unipotent substitution. The actual output is highest and satisfies these equations by equivariance. Restoring separate first-coordinate homogeneity proves the global polynomial identity. Only this actual composition is required to extend to the target slot degree.

The first factor is injective on the input highest space, the middle is invertible, and the last is injective on its exact Schur component for $n\ge N$. Thus $h_{a,n}$ is injective on the whole highest multiplicity space. Equivariance and complete reducibility make it injective on the full isotypic component. The actual scalar-one transpose pairing then gives full target rank for $h_{n,a}$.

The empty tail is supplied directly by the pure-power tensor identity. Insufficient ambient rank gives zero by the actual column antisymmetrizer. Rational definitions and nonzero displayed denominators give the same result after every characteristic-zero scalar extension.

## 6. Consequences and source scope

For a target component of length at most $a$, one has $D\le(a-1)t$. Therefore $n\ge\lfloor ab/2\rfloor$ reaches every target with $t\le b$; longer target shapes are already zero by the tensor-slot Young map. The width-four and tail-sensitive bounds follow by substitution.

For tail $2\rho$, the threshold is exactly $|\rho|+\rho_1$. The report's first-row calculation proves validity of the displayed partition, and the previously checked actual even-tail product construction supplies nonzero multiplicity. Applying the theorem in both directions gives the asserted stable-range canonical isomorphism.

This agrees with the report's attribution. The present proof obtains faithfulness of the actual power-sum map by the independent finite-row construction above. check_tail_moment_independent.py expands three-coordinate product linear forms directly and independently computes the set-partition Möbius sum by choosing the block containing the first labeled factor through submultisets. It uses exact fractions and imports no source implementation.

## 1. The section model, line factors, and evaluation

Write $E=\mathfrak h_m$, $d=m-1$, and
$v_i=e_i-m^{-1}\mathbf 1$. The original partition and balanced degree are
$$
\lambda=((m-1)a+t-m-r,a+t,(t+1)^r,t^{m-2-r}),
\qquad n=a+t-1.
$$
Their sum is $mn$, their first gap is $(m-2)a-m-r$, and the ideal
order in G015 is exactly $\lambda_2-n=1$.
After removing the full determinant factor, the smaller flag weight is
$(a,1^r,0^{d-r-1})$. For $r>0$ its line is
$$
(\mathcal S_1^*)^{a-1}\otimes\det\mathcal S_{r+1}^*.
$$
On the flag fiber over a line, the factor
$\det\mathcal S_{r+1}^*$ splits into $\mathcal S_1^*$ and the
exterior Young line for the quotient. Its degree-zero pushforward
is therefore $\mathcal O(a)\Lambda^rQ^*$. For $r=0$ this is simply
$\mathcal O(a)$.

The determinant factor is $\det(E^*)^t=\operatorname{sgn}^t$.
It has not acquired an extra sign from the quotient exterior factor.
Locally trivializing the quotient bundle makes the remaining flag
calculation a product over the base. Its Čech vector-space complex
over $\mathbb Q$ stays exact after tensoring with the base ideal
module. This proves the stated degree-zero pushforward with
$\mathcal I_Z$, without asserting that this ideal is a flat module.
The comparisons glue through the actual Young/Plücker maps.

Since $Q^*=\Omega^1(1)$, the section module before imposing the
point ideal is the Koszul kernel
$$
H^0(\mathcal O(a)\Lambda^rQ^*)
=H^0(\Omega^r(a+r))
\simeq S_{(a,1^r)}E^*.
$$
Here the Euler contraction is the multiplication differential used
in G037. Its coefficient degree is $a$ and its total Koszul degree
is $a+r$. Evaluation at the specified affine representatives is
the actual map
$$
F\longmapsto (F(v_i))_i:
S_{(a,1^r)}E^*\longrightarrow
\bigoplus_i\Lambda^r\operatorname{ann}(v_i).
$$
The horizontal equation puts the values in the indicated
annihilators. The vectors $v_i$ are literally permuted, so these
fiber trivializations introduce no scalar character.

The sum of fibers is the induced representation
$\operatorname{Ind}_{S_{m-1}}^{S_m}\Lambda^r\mathfrak h_{m-1}$.
An explicit coset comparison sends $g\otimes\phi$ to $g\phi$ in
the component indexed by $g(m)$. The stabilizer identification is
the zero-sum subspace of the first $m-1$ coordinates in
$\operatorname{ann}(v_m)$, using the invariant dot form.
Choosing the transpositions $(i\,m)$ gives an inverse coset
description. Thus the kernel of the displayed map is precisely
the G015 vanishing section space, with its full outside sign
$\operatorname{sgn}^t$.

## 2. Both actual evaluation splittings

The degree-$a\ge3$ right inverse in UH.8 checks directly.
At every frame point,
$s_2(v_j)=(m-1)/m$,
$z_i(v_i)=(m-1)/m$, and
$z_i(v_j)=-1/m$ for $i\ne j$. Substitution in UH.7 gives
$p_i(v_j)=\delta_{ij}$ and $\ell_i(v_i)=1$.
For $\phi_i\in\Lambda^r\operatorname{ann}(v_i)$,
$$
p_i\ell_i^{a-3}\iota_z(\ell_i\wedge\phi_i)
$$
has coefficient degree $a$, is horizontal because
$\iota_z^2=0$, and takes the prescribed value $\phi_i$ only at
$v_i$. The identity at that point is
$$
\iota_{v_i}(\ell_i\wedge\phi_i)
=\ell_i(v_i)\phi_i-\ell_i\wedge\iota_{v_i}\phi_i
=\phi_i.
$$
Every factor is permuted by the group, so summing these maps gives
an equivariant rational right inverse.

At $a=2$, the adjoint of
$l\otimes\theta\mapsto(l(v_i)\iota_{v_i}\theta)_i$
is exactly
$$
(\psi_i)_i\longmapsto
\sum_i v_i\otimes(v_i\wedge\psi_i),
\qquad
\psi_i\in\Lambda^r(E/\mathbb Qv_i).
$$
The map from each quotient exterior power to
$v_i\wedge\Lambda^rE$ is well defined and injective.
The only relation among the $v_i$ is their constant relation.
Consequently a vector in the adjoint kernel has
$v_i\wedge\psi_i=\eta$ independent of $i$.
Choosing $d$ frame vectors as a basis shows that an element of
every corresponding principal exterior ideal must contain every
basis vector. The intersection is zero for $r+1<d$.

It follows that evaluation is surjective for $r\le m-3$.
Every declared degree-two input has $r\le m-4$ by the first-gap
inequality. At the excluded endpoint $r=m-2$, the common
intersection is exactly $\det E$, so the cokernel is the
one-dimensional sign representation. This endpoint statement
also retains the actual group action on the common wedge.

The invariant positive forms and the displayed adjoint give the
rational splitting $B^*(BB^*)^{-1}$ followed by
$l\otimes\theta\mapsto l\iota_z\theta$. Surjectivity makes this
inverse well defined. No numerical-rank hypothesis enters the proof.

## 3. The correction types and the degree-two kernel

The hook identification
$\Lambda^r\mathfrak h_{m-1}\simeq[(m-1-r,1^r)]$
agrees with the standard alternating difference-vector Young map.
Its characteristic can also be checked from the actual splitting

the exterior power of the permutation module is the induced

Jacobi–Trudi recurrence.

Inducing this hook one further letter adds a single box.
With $q=m-1-r$, its possible shapes are exactly

(q+1,1^r),\qquad(q,1^{r+1}),\qquad
(q,2,1^{r-1})\quad(r\ge1,\ q\ge2).

They are distinct, including $r=0$ and $q=1$.
The coset module followed by rational Young projections supplies

single Specht kernel, including its actual inclusion obtained

zero-dimensional positive polytope at that endpoint.

For every non-row correction shape, the row-superstandard
tableau has comajor degree $b(\nu)$. This follows by summing

Thus each special construction raises the numerator degree by

For the row shape, $r=0$ and $D=a\ge3$. The chosen two/three

zero targets at the smaller values of $a$.

## 1. The entire final row layer and its actual restriction

Set $N=K+1=(D+4)/2$ and take $T=\mathbb Q^4$.
In the ordered-row exterior decomposition of
$C_s=(\Lambda(\mathbb Q^s\otimes T))^{S_s}$, a degree-$D$
term occupying $N$ nonempty rows has
$$
D\ge 2N-e_1\ge 2N-4=D.
$$
Equality forces $e_1=4$ and every other occupied row to have
exterior degree two. Thus $e_2=N-4=2h+j$. These are all
the new terms between row counts $K$ and $N$ in degree $D$.
Their module is exactly
$$
\det T\otimes\operatorname{Sym}^{2h+j}(\Lambda^2T).
$$
There are no changes at any scalar degree below $D$, since
the occupancy bound there is at most $K$.

The actual splitting
$C_s=\Lambda T\otimes B_s$, with
$B_s=(\Lambda(W_s\otimes T))^{S_s}$, has constant term one
in its first factor. Recursive comparison of degrees first
gives equality below $D$, then gives the same displayed
difference in degree $D$ for the two $B_s$.

The proof then uses a specified map. Zero-padding
$W_K\hookrightarrow W_N$ has orthogonal transpose $q$,
and direct coordinate computation gives
$q(P_Ne_i)=P_Ke_i$ for $i\le K$ and $q(P_Ne_N)=0$.
Every exterior row power sum therefore maps with scalar
one to its corresponding generator at row count $K$.
The full finite-row orbit spanning proof makes the
restriction $B_N\to B_K$ surjective. Its kernel has exactly
the character just computed.

The relevant skew-Cauchy highest weight is
$\gamma=(h+j+2,h+j+1,h+1,h)$. The retained Pfaffian and
standard-monomial proof decomposes
$\operatorname{Sym}^d(\Lambda^2T)$ into the shapes
$(P,P,Q,Q)$ with $P+Q=d$. Every kernel summand therefore
has equal first two parts and equal last two parts, whereas
both corresponding gaps of $\gamma$ are one. The actual
restriction has no kernel on this Schur multiplicity space.

The same argument together with R046 stability at $s\ge N$
proves that every restriction from $S\ge s\ge K$ is an
isomorphism on $(S_\nu W_s)^{S_s}$. The ordinary and
exterior realizations use the same Schur morphism $S_\nu(q)$:
the rational tensor projectors commute with every tensor
power of $q$. Choosing $S\ge\max(s,D)$ gives the commuting
identity $p_s=S_\nu(q)p_S$, so the particular ordinary
moment map $p_s$ is faithful. This is the exact map needed
for the canonical-factorization argument.

## 2. Stable multiplicity and the recorded clarification

The free stable generator algebra is
$$
\operatorname{Sym}(\Lambda^2T\oplus\Lambda^4T)
\otimes\Lambda(\Lambda^3T).
$$
Its only possible exterior degrees contributing to the
even scalar degree $D$ are zero, two and four. Exterior
degrees zero and four give determinant twists of paired
shapes and cannot give $\gamma$. The actual contraction
isomorphism
$$
\Lambda^2(\Lambda^3T)\simeq\det T\otimes\Lambda^2T
$$
reduces the remaining contribution to a vertical two-strip
and a determinant shift. The two gaps of $\gamma$ force
the strip to occupy rows one and three. With $l$ additional
determinant generators, the paired starting shape is
$$
(h+j-l,h+j-l,h-l-1,h-l-1),
$$
which is allowed exactly for $0\le l\le h-1$.
These are $h$ distinct multiplicity-one Pieri contributions.

The audit requested one precision: HO.3 is initially a
surjection, so its source count alone would supply only

times the displayed free generator algebra. Cancelling

shows equal source and target characters for HO.3. Its
surjectivity therefore makes it an isomorphism in each fixed
stable degree. This inserted argument was read after editing.
It justifies exactly $h$ copies, with the actual generator
morphism retained.

The primary retained Sarkar source was also reread through

thm-four-columns and its complete proof and final table.
The section theorem counters confirm the numeric locator.
The row $(m_1,m_3)=(1,1)$ gives $m_4=h$ exactly.

https://arxiv.org/src/2610.07929v2.
This is attribution of the established stable count; the
finite restriction and canonical map are checked above and

## 3. Every finite row count through the perfect pairing

The tail length is $m=h+j+2$. For $s\le m$ the Schur
functor vanishes because $\dim W_s=s-1<m$.
For $s\ge m+1$, write $q=s-h-j-3$. Padding to exactly
$s-1$ rows and complementing in $4^{s-1}$ gives
$$
\nu^c=(4^q,3,2^j,1,0^h).
$$
This follows by reversing the padded list and subtracting
each entry from four, so it includes the exact zero-row count.

The comparison is the perfect column pairing
$$
S_\nu W_s\otimes S_{\nu^c}W_s\longrightarrow(\det W_s)^4.
$$
Column $i$ of the first tensor pairs by exterior multiplication
with column $5-i$ of the other. Their heights add to $s-1$.
Applying the rational Young projectors gives the usual
complementary highest/lowest pairing, which is nonzero.
The induced irreducible Schur map to the determinant twist
of the dual is therefore an isomorphism. The invariant dot
form then identifies the dual with the same Schur functor
on $W_s$. The determinant character is $\operatorname{sgn}$,
so its fourth power is trivial. A fixed rational volume
trivializes that fourth power. These are actual
$S_s$-equivariant maps, not only a dimension identity.

At $q=0$, the complementary shape $(3,2^j,1)$ is excluded
by the proved three-column algebra surjection: its only
possible families are $(2^v)$ and $(3,2^v)$.
For $1\le q<h$, the complement is the same family with
$h$ replaced by $q$. Its stable threshold is
$K_q=2q+j+3$, and
$$
s-K_q=K-s=h-q>0.
$$
The already proved uniform stable layer calculation applies
to this smaller positive parameter and gives multiplicity
$q$. There is no circular finite-profile induction.
For $s\ge K$ the multiplicity is $h$. Combining the dimension,
zero-complement, intermediate-complement and stable ranges
gives exactly $r_s$.

## 4. Homogenization and the full canonical rank

The Young-column inclusion into $S_\nu\mathbb Q^a$ uses
four columns. Every fixed row letter can occur at most once
in each column, hence every corresponding invariant has
separate row degree at most four. For inner degree $n\ge4$,
the inverse highest-space chart
$$
f\longmapsto\left(\prod_i x_i\right)^n
f(y_1/x_1,\ldots,y_a/x_a)
$$
extends polynomially. The stipulated first-row partition
condition is exactly the remaining highest-weight condition.
Thus the target multiplicity is $r_a$.

For $n\ge K$, R046 gives the actual opposite canonical map

$$
h_{a,n}|_\nu=p_n\Psi_n E_a.

The independent-row expectation $E_a$ is injective on the
translation-invariant highest space. The all-degree split
moments give the equivariant triangular automorphism

$K\ge5$, all its normalized falling-factorial denominators
are nonzero. The final particular evaluation $p_n$ is
faithful by §1. Their composition is injective on the
whole multiplicity space.

The established scalar-one transpose identity therefore
makes $h_{n,a}$ surjective on its whole target. This gives

arguments apply and equal $\min(r_a,r_n)$ throughout RF.3.
For $a=2,3$ the whole-target assertion is the actual zero
Schur component, as its length is at least four.

All maps are rational and natural under the relevant Young

The coherent/local-free, frame-torsor and Chow-coordinate
transport follows the already checked maps cited in §5.

## 1. Original partitions and the exact stable transport

For $m\ge3$, $a\ge2$, $t\ge0$, and $n\ge a+t$, the output

$m(n-t)-2a-2\ge(m-2)a-2\ge a-2$; its second gap is $a-2$.
Thus every declared tuple is a partition. The stable chart
condition is exactly $\lambda_2\le n$.

The T032/G015 chart sends the balanced module to the full

gives $S_{(a,2)}W$ and the actual character
$\operatorname{sgn}^t$. This proves the stated effective
outer label and uses the already specified chart inverse
and exterior-column pairing. The remaining calculation is
on this exact Schur module, not merely its dimension.

## 2. The complete polarization kernel and cokernel

With tensor degrees two and one respectively, the map
$$
\phi:P\otimes\operatorname{Sym}^2W\longrightarrow P\otimes W,
\qquad
f\otimes uv\longmapsto fu\otimes v+fv\otimes u
$$
is $P$-linear, homogeneous and $GL(W)$-equivariant.
Its factors of two at repeated vectors are retained.

For total degree $D\ge4$, Pieri gives exactly the three
domain summands $(D)$, $(D-1,1)$, $(D-2,2)$ and the first
two target summands. The three displayed highest vectors
were checked with the literal raising derivation $y\mapsto x$.
The first has nonzero image $2x^{D-1}\otimes x$.
The second has nonzero image
$x^{D-1}\otimes y-x^{D-2}y\otimes x$.
The three terms in the third image cancel exactly, with
the stated coefficient minus two. Its weight is $(D-2,2)$.
The Young inclusions and semisimplicity therefore identify
the actual kernel with $S_{(D-2,2)}W$.

At degree three, the first two summands are still present
once each and their same nonzero images prove surjectivity.
At degree two, the map is the symmetric inclusion into
$W\otimes W$, so its cokernel is $\Lambda^2W$.
At degree one its cokernel is $W$. No other degree occurs.
These arguments include $\dim W=2$; every displayed
highest vector exists, and irrelevant Schur summands
vanish through their column antisymmetrizers.

As $I=\mathbb Q[e_2,\ldots,e_m]$ has no positive element
below degree two, its positive ideal kills the whole
cokernel. Under the actual exterior-hook maps the two
cokernel representations are the distinct Specht labels
$(m-1,1)$ in degree one and $(m-2,1,1)$ in degree two.
For $m=3$ these are the standard and sign representations,
so the smallest outer degree has exactly the stated
exceptional labels.

## 3. Freeness outside the exceptional labels

The invariant averaged coinvariant section gives the
graded multiplication isomorphism $I\otimes H\to P$.
Consequently the covariants of both free $P$-modules are
finite graded free $I$-modules. Their homogeneous basis
polynomials are precisely
$A_\nu=q^2f_{[\nu]\otimes\operatorname{Sym}^2W}$ and
$B_\nu=qf_{[\nu]\otimes W}$. The rational invariant perfect
Specht forms justify the tensor multiplicity notation.

Away from the two cokernel labels, the covariant map is
surjective by the exact rational averaging functor.
Choosing a homogeneous lift of every free target basis
element gives an actual graded $I$-linear section.
The kernel is therefore graded projective.

The stated freeness proof is valid without an unstated
projective-module theorem. Lift a homogeneous basis modulo
$I_+$, map the corresponding graded free module onto the
kernel, and use graded Nakayama for surjectivity.
Graded projectivity splits this surjection. After reduction
modulo $I_+$ its kernel is zero; another graded Nakayama
application gives zero kernel. All modules are finite and
bounded below, so both applications have their required
hypotheses. This supplies the actual free basis and proves
coefficientwise nonnegativity of $A_\nu-B_\nu$.

## 4. The exceptional decomposition, checked as actual modules

Fix an exceptional label and its degree $d=1$ or $2$.
Its cokernel is the single graded residue field $(I/I_+)[d]$.
A homogeneous free basis of $\mathcal B_\nu$ can be adapted
to the quotient: one degree-$d$ vector $e_0$ maps to one and
the others map to zero. Reduction of basis vectors in that
degree is ordinary rational row reduction. The image is
therefore exactly
$$
I_+e_0\oplus\mathcal B'.
$$
Lift the free basis of $\mathcal B'$ through the actual
surjection onto this image and split it off. The remaining
graded projective domain is free by the preceding argument
and maps onto $I_+e_0$.

Choose $x_i$ mapping to $e_ie_0$, in degree $d+i$.
Their residue classes are linearly independent in
$\mathcal A_0/I_+\mathcal A_0$, because their images in
$I_+/I_+^2$ are its independent minimal generators.
The map on these quotients is onto. Choose a homogeneous
complementary residue basis in its kernel and lift it to
vectors $y_j$. The $x_i,y_j$ form a free homogeneous basis
by the same graded Nakayama and projective splitting argument.

Each image of $y_j$ is in $I_+^2e_0$ and can be written
$\sum_i g_{ji}e_ie_0$ with homogeneous $g_{ji}\in I_+$.
The basis change
$y_j\mapsto y_j-\sum_i g_{ji}x_i$ fixes all $x_i$ and is
invertible triangular over $I$. It makes those images
zero. The exact kernel thus becomes
$$
K_\nu\simeq\mathcal F_\nu\oplus Z_1(I)[d],
\qquad
Z_1(I)=\ker\left(\bigoplus_{i=2}^m I\xi_i
\xrightarrow{\xi_i\mapsto e_i}I\right).
$$
This decomposition is on the specified polarization kernel.

The intermediate free domain has basis polynomial
$A_\nu-B_\nu+q^d$. Removing the $x_i$ gives
$$
F_\nu=A_\nu-B_\nu+q^d\left(1-\sum_{i=2}^m q^i\right),
$$
exactly SR2.3. It is the basis polynomial of the remaining
free span, so its coefficients are nonnegative.
Their degrees are at most $N+2$ with $N=\binom m2$:
coinvariant degrees are at most $N$, and the correction
degrees $d+i$ also obey the bound because $m\le N$.

As a check on the signs, the Hilbert numerator of $Z_1(I)$
is $\sum_iq^i-1+\prod_i(1-q^i)$. Adding its shifted
numerator to $F_\nu$ gives
$A_\nu-B_\nu+q^d\prod_i(1-q^i)$, precisely the kernel
Hilbert series obtained from the actual residue-field
cokernel. This is a consequence of the decomposition,
not a substitute for its basis construction.

## 5. The actual weighted cycle basis and positive polytopes

For a fixed monomial multidegree $\beta$, let
$J=\{i:\beta_i>0\}$ and $i=\min J$.
The degree-$\beta$ domain basis is
$e^\beta\xi_j/e_j$ for $j\in J$, all mapping to
$e^\beta$. Its kernel basis consists exactly of the
differences with the distinguished index $i$:
$$
e^\beta(\xi_k/e_k-\xi_i/e_i),\qquad k\in J\setminus\{i\}.
$$
Both quotients are polynomial. This proves the claimed
series by an explicit basis, with no unproved cancellation:
$$
\sum_{2\le i<k\le m}
\frac{q^{i+k}}{\prod_{l=i}^m(1-q^l)}.
$$

Each positive coefficient $c_{\nu,j}$ of the free polynomial
is encoded by one bounded coordinate from zero to
$c_{\nu,j}-1$, together with the invariant monomial exponents
satisfying $\sum ib_i=D-j$. Fixing the homogeneous basis
described above makes this an actual indexing of its vectors.
The matrices need only the integer basis counts, not
construction of every vector.

The exceptional cycle uses G037's single trivial-hook
polytope at total degree $D-d$, with hook parameter
$D-d-1\ge1$. This includes $m=3$, where the cycle is a
free generator of degree five and degree six is absent.
For $m\ge4$, its support is every degree at least five.
The free coin support is exactly degree zero or degree at
least two, since sizes two and three are available.
These give the stated complete support test, including
small $a$ and all exceptional endpoints.

There are at most $N+3$ free-degree pieces and one cycle
piece. Each free piece has $m$ variables, and the cycle
piece has $3m-3$. All upper bounds and degree equations
are literal bounded integer constraints. The positive
coefficient and support formulas follow from the actual
free/cycle basis decomposition.

## 6. Corner paths, pair module, and polynomial bounds

The ordinary tensor-coset isomorphism
$v\otimes gH\mapsto g\otimes g^{-1}v$ and its displayed
inverse prove the remove-one/add-one rule for
$[\nu]\otimes(\mathbf1\oplus W)$. Subtracting its actual
trivial direct summand gives the standard tensor rule.

The unordered-pair map
$$
\{i,j\}\longmapsto(P_me_i)(P_me_j)
$$
is equivariant and bijective. Indeed a putative kernel

The pair stabilizer is $S_{m-2}\times S_2$. Restriction
followed by induction and the two Pieri rules give exactly
the remove-two/add-two formula of SR2.15. Horizontal and
vertical branches are counted separately when both occur;
different corner orders leading to the same strip are not
double counted. The code's sets of intermediate and upper
shapes, followed by its two independent strip tests,
implement precisely this convention.

Only polynomially many candidate corner paths are used.
The already proved fake-degree formula is truncated through
degree $N$, giving its entire polynomial. Its coefficient
bound by $m!$, multiplied by the polynomial path counts,

The coefficient evaluator applies the previously proved

Both degrees are $O(m^2)$ and the same established

The code retains the full numerator, validates the
physical inputs, and uses the correct determinant parity.
The stated explicit-$m$ encoding convention is appropriate.

## 1. Parameters and the complete jet sheaf

The first gap of the partition in HJ.1 is
$(m-2)a-mk-r$. At $a=2k+1$ and $r=m-2$ it is
$(m-4)k\ge0$; every other allowed parameter increases it.
The tuple has size $mn$ for $n=a+t-k$.
Its ideal order is exactly $\lambda_2-n=k$.
The exterior flag pushforward therefore gives
$\mathcal I_Z^k\otimes\mathcal O(a)\Lambda^rQ^*
=\mathcal I_Z^k\otimes\Omega^r(a+r)$, with the outside
character $\operatorname{sgn}^t$ from the full determinant
columns.

The points are disjoint and reduced. At each point their
ordinary sheaf ideal power is the maximal-ideal power.
The kernel of restriction to order-less-than-$k$ jets is
therefore exactly the displayed sheaf section space.
The T061 product-chart pushforward argument remains valid
after tensoring its vector-space Čech maps with this ideal
module. No flatness of the ideal module is assumed.

## 2. Every quadratic derivative and its actual inverse

After a projective frame change, the points are the
coordinate points of a space of dimension $m-1$ and
the all-ones point. The quadrics
$x_jx_l-x_1x_2$, omitting the zero member, are precisely
the spanning presentation from G016.

At a coordinate point $e_h$ with $h>2$, the pairs $(h,j)$
give all transverse coordinate derivatives. At $e_1$,
the pairs $(1,j)$ and $(2,j)$, $j\ge3$, give
$dx_j-dx_2$ and $-dx_2$, hence every transverse direction.
The calculation at $e_2$ is its exchanged version.
At the all-ones point the derivatives are
$dx_j+dx_l-dx_1-dx_2$. Taking the pairs $(1,j)$ and
$(2,j)$ gives every difference relative to coordinates
one and two, including their difference. They span the
full sum-zero projective cotangent space. This works
already with three affine coordinates, so includes $m=4$.

Changing to the specified chart $\ell_i=1$ only changes
these differentials by the invertible coordinate map
and a nonzero trivialization factor, since the quadrics
vanish at the point. Thus HJ.4 is the actual surjective
derivative map at every frame point.

Its Gram right inverse
$\partial_i^*(\partial_i\partial_i^*)^{-1}$ is rational.
The invariant positive forms make the inverse well
defined after extension to $\mathbb R$, hence over
$\mathbb Q$ as the inverse of a rational nonsingular
matrix. Both forms and the chart are fixed by the point
stabilizer, so the inverse is stabilizer-equivariant.
Literal frame permutations carry one such map to another.

## 3. The all-order simultaneous interpolation

The separators $p_i$ have value one at their own affine
frame vector and zero at all others, as checked in A090.
For $f_h=\sigma_i(u_h)$, the quotient $y_h=f_h/p_i$
has zero constant term and linear term $u_h$ on the
chart $\ell_i=1$. Hence it gives an automorphism of
the truncated local algebra. Its inverse is obtained
by successively removing homogeneous terms of orders
one through $k-1$; all maps are finite rational
polynomial substitutions.

For each multiindex $|\beta|<k$, the polynomial
$$
p_i^{\,k-|\beta|}\prod_h f_h^{\beta_h}
$$
has homogeneous degree $2k$. At its own point it is
$p_i^k y^\beta$, and multiplication by $p_i^k$ is a
unit on the finite local algebra. These jets thus form
a basis. At every other point every displayed factor
is in its maximal ideal, and their total number,
counting multiplicity, is exactly $k$. Consequently
the polynomial has order at least $k$ at that point.
This proves simultaneous scalar jet interpolation.

For $\phi\in\Lambda^r\operatorname{ann}(v_i)$, the form
$H_i(\phi)=\iota_z(\ell_i\wedge\phi)$ has coefficient
degree one and is horizontal. On $\ell_i(z)=1$, it is
$$
\phi-\ell_i\wedge\iota_z\phi.
$$
Restriction to $W_i=\ker\ell_i$ is exactly $\phi$.
Every horizontal form is uniquely determined by that
restriction, because $E=\mathbb Qz\oplus W_i$ on

## 4. Order-two correction and its bounded branching

## 2. General Pfaffian highest maps, including action conventions

In the abstract polynomial algebra
$\operatorname{Sym}(\Lambda^2T)$, the variable
$X_{ij}$ represents $e_i\wedge e_j$.
For a matrix acting on basis columns, its action
on the alternating matrix of these variables is
$A\mapsto u^tAu$. In particular an upper unipotent
matrix preserves the span of its first $2i$
columns with determinant one. Each leading
Pfaffian $P_i$ is consequently a highest polynomial
of weight $(1^{2i},0^{t-2i})$. On the displayed
alternating blocks it is $z_1\cdots z_i$, with
the sign convention in OI.9.

The exact block multiplication was checked:
for
$A=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}J&B\\-B^t&C\end{smallmatrix}\right)$
and
$u=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}I&-J^{-1}B\\0&I\end{smallmatrix}\right)$,
$$
u^tAu=\operatorname{diag}(J,C+B^tJ^{-1}B).
$$
The plus sign follows from $J^{-t}=-J^{-1}$.
The lower block is alternating. The matrix $u$
is upper unipotent in the original ordered basis.
Repeated elimination is therefore an allowed
highest-weight group operation, with denominators
nonzero on the specified open set.

This open set is nonempty, as witnessed by nonzero
alternating blocks, and hence is dense in the
generic alternating matrix space. Successive
leading Pfaffians give the block parameters
$z_i=P_i/P_{i-1}$. For odd dimension the final
one-dimensional alternating block is zero.

A highest polynomial is invariant under these
upper unipotent substitutions. Its restriction
to the blocks determines it on the dense open
set. A diagonal-weight vector restricts either
to zero or to one scalar monomial
$z_1^{c_1}\cdots z_r^{c_r}$, because those
variables have independent paired torus weights.
Polynomiality gives nonnegative integer exponents;
dominance gives $c_1\ge\cdots\ge c_r$.
The product
$P_1^{c_1-c_2}\cdots P_r^{c_r}$
has exactly the same restriction and weight.
Subtracting it leaves a highest polynomial
vanishing on a dense open set, hence zero.

Thus every possible paired weight occurs once
and no other highest weight occurs. The explicit
products and rational Young/cyclic Schur maps
give the actual decomposition OI.8 by complete
reducibility. The proof covers both parities
of $t$, including $t=2$ and $3$.

The cubic transfer

$$
is homogeneous, $P$-linear and $GL(W)$-equivariant.
In the two-letter highest-vector calculation,

## 2. The actual quadratic action and the Ricci inverse

The four-index tensor map
$$
\mathcal K(A,B)_{ijkl}
=A_{ik}B_{jl}+A_{jl}B_{ik}
-A_{il}B_{jk}-A_{jk}B_{il}
$$
has both pair antisymmetries, pair interchange,
and the cyclic Bianchi identity. It is
symmetric in its two symmetric inputs,
so it kills the $(3,1)$ factor. Its
full four-slot symmetrization is zero,
so it kills $(4)$. Its value on
$x^2\otimes y^2$ is nonzero.
The exact three-term Pieri decomposition

specified $S_{(2,2)}W$ realization.

$e_2=-\tfrac12\sum z_i^2$.

$$
\operatorname{Ric}\mathcal K(g,B)
=(d-2)B+(\operatorname{tr}_gB)g.
$$
Its trace is $2(d-1)\operatorname{tr}_gB$.
The displayed formula in SR3.13 therefore
recovers $B$ exactly for every $d\ge3$.
For an arbitrary curvature tensor $R$,

Subtracting it is the equivariant projector
onto $\mathcal R=\ker\operatorname{Ric}$.
The denominators $d-2$ and $2(d-1)$ are
nonzero for all declared $m\ge4$.

All maps are equivariant under the rational
orthogonal group of the form and therefore

complement and inverse, not only their
dimension relation.

# A097. Independent review of the fixed-second-part construction

## Scope and result

**PASS after the explicit distinct-shape clarification in G040 §7.** I read the whole saved report `work/root/fixed_second_part_report.md`, FS.1–FS.18 and all eight sections, including the amended restriction–induction formula. The review covers the actual maps, every finite-degree endpoint, the positive basis construction and the claimed fixed-parameter bit bounds. General execution of the proposed algorithm has not been performed in this audit, and no generic execution receipt is asserted.

The effective outer label is changed by the actual determinant pairing already checked in the stable balanced chart. For the parameters in FS.1, the first partition gap is nonnegative: at the smallest allowed $n=a+t$ it is $(m-2)a-b\ge0$. The second gap is $a-b\ge0$. Thus the transport applies to every displayed input, including $m=3$, $a=b$ and $t=0$.

## 1. Complete transfer and cokernel

The map is the actual multiplication–derivative map
$$
\phi_b(f\otimes v_1\cdots v_b)
 =\sum_i fv_i\otimes\prod_{j\ne i}v_j.
$$
For source first-factor degree $u$, the two-row Pieri summands have highest vectors
$x^{u-i}X^{b-i}(xY-yX)^i$.
The derivative $x\partial_X+y\partial_Y$ annihilates the bracket and multiplies the remaining highest vector by $b-i$. In the target, the same summand occurs precisely in the corresponding Pieri range. It follows that the kernel is zero for $u<b$, and is exactly $S_{(u,b)}W$ for $u\ge b$. For target first-factor degree $j\le b-1$, the one missing summand is $S_{(b-1,j)}W$; for $j\ge b$ there is none. This proves the complete finite cokernel in FS.4, including degree $b-1$, the last degree $2b-2$, and the two-dimensional standard module at $m=3$.

Writing $L=2b-2$, its smallest nonzero degree is $b-1$. Therefore every $e_i$ with $i\ge b$ kills that actual cokernel: its image would have degree at least $2b-1$. The tightened choice $B=\min(m,b-1)$, $J=\mathbb Q[e_2,\ldots,e_B]$ and $Y=(e_{B+1},\ldots,e_m)$ is valid. The low-variable action is induced from multiplication on the first symmetric factor of the displayed map. It is not chosen from a character calculation.

## 2. Finite covariants and rational size bounds

Every required raw symmetric-factor degree is bounded in terms of $b$. Hence the raw matrix dimensions are polynomial in $m$ for fixed $b$. The centered permutation action and the elementary invariant formulas have polynomially many rational coefficients of polynomial bit length in the basis $e_i-e_m$.

The near-row test $\nu_1\ge m-L$ is justified by an injection through rational Young projectors into $W^{\otimes e}\subset(\mathbb Q^m)^{\otimes e}$. A word orbit with $l$ different letters is the coset representation for $S_{m-l}$; its one-box induction chains contain the row $(m-l)$. Thus no discarded label can occur in the finite cokernel.

For a surviving label, at most $L$ letters lie outside its first row in a row tabloid. Its tabloid realization has polynomial dimension. Every nonsingleton column contains a lower box; there are at most $2L$ boxes in all nonsingleton columns, so the size of the column group depends only on $b$. The orbit-span algorithm can retain actual integer orbit polytabloids, rather than repeatedly replacing them by rational combinations. Their coefficients remain bounded by that fixed column-group size. All adjacent-permutation matrices can then be obtained by solving against a single retained orbit basis. This gives the stated polynomial coefficient heights as well as polynomial dimensions; repeated elimination does not require an unsupported bound on exponentially growing intermediate rational vectors.

The equations $T\rho_\nu(s_i)=\rho_C(s_i)T$ compute the covariant spaces exactly because the adjacent transpositions generate $S_m$. The invariant multiplications commute with those transpositions and descend to those exact solution spaces. The number of low degrees and low invariant variables is bounded by $b$, so their quotient and intertwining computations have polynomial bit size. When $m\le L$, any finite dimension absorbed in this argument is bounded by a function of $b$.

## 3. Minimal covers and actual free cancellation

Choose the generator basis of $C_\nu/J_+C_\nu$ and homogeneous lifts. Each generator degree is at most $L$. The greedy normal-monomial argument can be performed separately in each weighted degree; multiplication preserves the chosen module term order. Consequently the retained monomials form the complement of the initial relation module and have weight at most $L$.

No basis vector of the minimal cover is a leading relation with constant coefficient: that would contradict minimality in $C_\nu/J_+C_\nu$. Every minimal monomial in the leading relation module therefore has a variable divisor whose removal is normal. Its weight is at most $L+B$. The corresponding relation has a remainder consisting of earlier retained monomials in the same weighted degree. These leading terms generate the entire initial module, so the relations generate the full kernel. This proves the finite degree bound used to obtain $F_1\to F_0$.

Over $I=J[Y]$, the relations are generated by the low relations and $y_i$ times the generators of $F_0$. At $Y$-degree zero, their minimality is the minimality of $F_1$. At a single high-variable degree, it is the independence of the free-generator residues of $F_0$. Higher $Y$-degrees add no generators. Thus FS.8 is the actual minimal first pair of covers of $C_\nu$.

The two cover cancellations from G039 apply without any additional freeness assertion about the relation module. In the first cancellation, a basis of the target free module is adapted to its minimal cokernel generator residues; subtracting homogeneous combinations of those selected generators makes the complementary basis vectors have zero image. They can be lifted through the transfer, and their free pairs cancel. In the remaining domain, a basis is adapted to the minimal relation residues. Complementary images are positive-degree combinations of the selected relations and are killed by the corresponding triangular basis change. Both changes are invertible homogeneous changes of free bases. Their complementary free summand has precisely FS.11 as its basis polynomial. Its coefficientwise nonnegativity follows from these actual cancellations, including the case $C_\nu=0$.

## 4. The high-variable kernel decomposition

For a fixed nonzero high-variable exponent vector $\beta$, put $S=\{j:\beta_j>0\}$ and choose its first element $i$. The degree-$\beta$ map is exactly
$$
F_1\oplus F_0^S\longrightarrow F_0,\qquad
(u,(v_j))\longmapsto d_Ju+\sum_jv_j.
$$
The inverse pair displayed in FS.13 is literal:
$$
(u,(v_j)_{j\ne i})\longmapsto
(u,-d_Ju-\sum_{j\ne i}v_j,(v_j)_{j\ne i}),
$$
and its inverse reads the unrestricted coordinates. Multiplying the first component by $y^\beta$ and the $j$th relation component by $y^{\beta-e_j}$ preserves all weighted degrees and gives polynomial vectors. This verifies the exact decomposition even when $d_J$ has a kernel.

At $\beta=0$ the remaining module is $K_J$. For $\beta\ne0$ the free choices are one copy of $F_1$ and $|S|-1$ copies of $F_0$. The latter choices are exactly the previously checked least-support star-cycle basis. This proves FS.14, with both high terms zero for an empty variable list and the cycle term zero for a one-variable list.

## 5. Primary degree bounds and their exact use

I opened and read Aschenbrenner, *Ideal membership in polynomial rings over the integers*, §3 through Theorem 3.2, including the complete homogeneous reduction, its recurrence and finite-field descent. The precise locator is PDF pp.13–16, Theorem 3.2 on printed/PDF p.16:

https://www.mat.univie.ac.at/~maschenbrenner/pdf/ideal2.pdf

The theorem bounds generators of the solution module of an $r_0$-row polynomial matrix of degree at most $\delta$ over a field by $(2r_0\delta)^{2^\ell}$. This is exactly the use in FS.15 after taking harmless maxima for zero ranks. In the proof's division paragraph, the free coordinates are the coordinates $r+1,\ldots,n$ associated to its displayed vectors (3.1); the isolated printed range $n-r+1,\ldots,n$ is an indexing slip and is not used literally in this audit.

I also opened Liang, *Degree bounds for Gröbner bases of modules*, arXiv:1905.07517v3; I read the statements and intervening proof passage containing Theorem 37/Corollary 38, §8, Theorems 40–41 and Corollary 42, and visually checked Corollary 42 on PDF p.19 (printed p.19):

https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.07517

Corollary 42 bounds the reduced basis degree by $2(Dr)^{2^\ell}$ for a submodule of a rank-$r$ free module generated in degrees at most $D$, with any module monomial order. Here ordinary basis degrees are deliberately set to zero. Applying it with $D=H$, $r=r_1$ gives exactly FS.16. The zero and full kernels are treated directly. This use does not identify the ordinary grading with the original weighted grading.

These are source checks of the stated passages; this audit does not claim to reconstruct every earlier theorem in Liang's paper.

## 6. A polynomial bit algorithm, not only a degree existence bound

For fixed $b$, the tightened bound $\ell=B-1\le b-2$ is fixed, and $r_0,r_1$ and their coefficient heights are polynomial in $m$. At $b=2$, $J=\mathbb Q$, $F_0=C_\nu$ and $F_1=K_J=0$; the high-variable formula reduces to the ordinary weighted-star cycle term. I reread this amendment in the author's report. Therefore $H$ and $G$ are polynomial in $m$, with computable exponents depending only on $b$. The ambient coefficient system for all vector polynomials of ordinary degree at most $G$ has polynomial dimensions:
$$
r_1\binom{G+\ell}{\ell}
\quad\hbox{unknowns, and at most}\quad
r_0\binom{G+\delta+\ell}{\ell}
\quad\hbox{coefficient equations}.
$$
Its entries are the already bounded coefficients of $d_J$. Exact rational nullspace and row-reduction operations have polynomial bit complexity; the final numerator and denominator heights are bounded by minors of these polynomial-size matrices.

Every element of the full reduced Gröbner basis lies in this solution space. Row reduction followed by divisibility-minimal leading-term selection therefore finds its leading generators. More explicitly, each globally reduced basis element has no trailing term in the full initial module; hence it has no trailing pivot in this finite solution space. Its pivot row is consequently the same unique reduced row in that space. This justifies the proposed finite search even for a term order that is not ordinary-degree-compatible.

Weighted-homogeneous components are preserved by the matrix equation and never increase ordinary degree. The reduced basis may therefore be chosen weighted homogeneous. All its ordinary exponent cuts are at most $G$.

The high- and low-degree character calculations do not require constructing exponentially large Specht modules for arbitrary $\nu$. For the free input characters, the number of distinct shapes at distance at most $b$ is polynomial in $m$; all small LR tableaux have at most $b$ boxes. Fake-degree polynomials have degree at most $\binom m2$ and coefficients bounded by the finite representation dimensions, whose binary lengths are polynomial in $m$. The signed arithmetic used to calculate the free numerator is separate from its positive basis interpretation proved above.

## 7. Correction to the restriction–induction enumeration

The initial wording about corner-removal paths could have counted a skew branching multiplicity twice. I requested an explicit distinct-shape convention. The author inserted it, and I reread the amended paragraph.

For the orbit indexed by $\rho$, let $l=\ell(\rho)$ and let $\sigma_d\vdash m_d(\rho)$ be the small-factor labels. Each shape $\eta\subseteq\nu$ of size $m-l$ is enumerated once. For each output $\kappa\supseteq\eta$ of size $m$, its multiplicity contribution is
$$
c^\nu_{\eta,\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\ldots}
c^\kappa_{\eta,\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\ldots}.
$$
Summing over the displayed distinct shapes and labels is exactly restriction followed by induction through
$S_{m-l}\times\prod_d S_{m_d(\rho)}$, under the tensor–coset map. Intermediate shapes for the ordered subgroup factors are counted inside the iterated LR coefficient. The order in which individual corner boxes were removed supplies no further factor.

The complete primary LR proof and the executable reading convention were independently read for A096 at Macdonald I§9, pp.142–147. The amended formula uses that precise coefficient and fixes the only counting ambiguity found here.

## 8. Positive bases, polytopes, exact values and scope

The exponent-grid construction counts monomials **inside** the initial kernel module. Cutting each axis at every generator exponent makes divisibility constant in a box. There are at most $(s+1)^\ell$ boxes per component, and both $s$ and the number of components are polynomial in $m$ for fixed $b$.

In each weighted degree, choose the first Gröbner element dividing an initial monomial and multiply it to that leading monomial. Distinct resulting leading terms prove independence. Gröbner reduction proves spanning and terminates within the finite weighted degree. Thus these lattice points index actual kernel vectors through a triangular basis lift; they do not merely reproduce a formal Hilbert series.

All weights are positive. Intersecting the boxes with FS.17 makes the pieces bounded, with the stated floor bounds. The other three types of terms are the nonnegative free numerator, the $F_1$ term with a distinguished first positive high exponent, and the $F_0$ least-support cycle term. Their tags are disjoint, and the inverse in §4 supplies the exact vector for every high-variable tag. The variable bound $3m+2b$ is a safe upper bound on every type.

For exact evaluation, use the original unbounded geometric series for the infinite box intervals, extracting only the requested degree. The finite cutoffs have polynomial size and create at most $2^\ell$ numerator shifts. The final degree-dependent upper bounds used to display bounded polytopes need not be inserted into these generating-series numerators. The rational-function degrees and coefficient heights are polynomial in $m$ for fixed $b$. The previously proved parity-extraction method in G037 then gives polynomial bit time in these sizes and $\log(D+1)$. The output coefficients themselves have polynomial binary length by the same finite-variable rational-series bound. Equality to zero decides support because the formula has already been carried to positive basis pieces.

The actual balanced chart, determinant map, transfer, finite quotient, cover changes, high-variable inverse and initial-term lift all preserve the asserted gradings. No scheme-theoretic pullback exactness or characteristic-$p$ rank assertion is needed. The result is a proved and specified finite algorithm for every fixed $b$, with general-purpose implementation still a separate task. This independent audit records a whole-proof and primary-source check, not an unexecuted computation.


# A098. Closed endpoint for the hook jet map

## Result and reviewed scope

**PASS.** I read the complete T065 report, HE.1–HE.7 and all three proof sections, the complete endpoint evaluator and checker, the reused bounded-point enumerator in T064, and the saved endpoint receipt. I also independently opened the publisher's primary PDF and read the proof chain through Nagel–Trok Theorem 5.3, with the exact regularity convention. No repetition of the author's numerical sweep is claimed.

The result extends the actual jet-surjection map to every valid endpoint $a=2k$. For $m\ge4$, the allowed legs are exactly $0\le r\le\min(m-2,(m-4)k)$, which is the first-partition-gap condition for HE.1. The partition sum is $m(k+t)$, and the determinant comparison changes the outer label by conjugation precisely for odd $t$.

## 1. Primary input and the complete numerical specialization

The primary source is Uwe Nagel and Bill Trok, *Segre's regularity bound for fat point schemes*, Ann. Sc. Norm. Super. Pisa Cl. Sci. (5), XX (2020), 217–237:

https://journals.sns.it/index.php/annaliscienze/article/download/674/660/892

The exact locators are Lemma 3.1(a), p.225; Remark 4.3, p.228; and Theorem 5.3, p.233. I read §§2–5 through that theorem, including the matroid partition construction, the residual induction lemmas, the reduced-point step and Proposition 5.2. I visually checked pp.225 and 233 in the publisher PDF. The source retained by the author is `work/theta/unstable_hook/nagel_trok_2020.pdf`, with its extracted text beside it.

The regularity index is the degree of surjective restriction, rather than the ideal's regularity shifted by one. For a fat point scheme it is bounded by the maximum, over positive-dimensional linear spaces, of $\lceil(w_L-1)/\dim L\rceil$. The use in HE.4 therefore has the correct shift.

For the frame of $m$ points in $\mathbf P^{m-2}$, every $m-1$ representing vectors are independent. A proper $q$-plane has at most $q+1$ points, so its contribution at uniform multiplicity $k$ is at most
$$
k+\left\lceil\frac{k-1}{q}\right\rceil\le2k-1.
$$
The full-space contribution has the same bound because
$$
(2k-1)(m-2)-(mk-1)=(m-4)k-m+3\ge m-5\ge0
$$
for $m\ge5$, $k\ge2$. This checks both equality endpoints $m=5,k=2$ and the entire asserted range. It proves the rank of the exact scalar restriction map in degree $2k-1$.

In the source's final induction on p.233, the minimal generators of $I_P^{m-1}$ are the products $\ell_i h_j^{(i)}$, and the factors nonzero at $P$ are $q_j^{(i)}$. These are respectively the $g$ and $f$ roles of the stated claim and of Lemma 3.5. The intervening swapped letters are a notation slip; keeping these roles proves the claimed residual equality and does not change either product. In this application the exponent in Lemma 3.5 is $m-1$. The representable quotient constructions choose auxiliary points outside $P$, so the quotient vectors used in the matroid argument are nonzero.

## 2. The rational equivariant scalar splitting

The Taylor matrix $B$ uses actual homogeneous monomials and the specified affine charts $\ell_i=1$. The projective frame and all their representatives are rational. Its target is the direct sum of the local rings modulo their $k$th maximal-ideal powers, with the homogeneous line trivialized by the chosen representative.

The stabilizer of a frame vector fixes that vector exactly. It therefore acts trivially on this trivialized line, and its action on the transverse affine coordinates is the standard action already used in T062. There is no additional character in the scalar jet target.

The regularity result proves surjectivity over $\mathbb Q$: one can either apply its arbitrary-field formulation directly or extend the rational matrix to characteristic zero and descend its rank. Rational invariant positive forms are obtained by finite averaging. Hence
$$
S=B^*(BB^*)^{-1}
$$
exists, is rational, satisfies $BS=1$ and commutes with the group action. The adjoint is taken using those invariant forms. This supplies an exact map and a proved inverse matrix; its invertibility is not a remaining hypothesis.

## 3. Horizontalization and all exceptional endpoints

At point $i$, let $\phi$ lie in the exterior power of the transverse covectors and use
$$
H_i(\phi)=\iota_z(\ell_i\wedge\phi).
$$
This polynomial form has coefficient degree one and is horizontal because $\iota_z^2=0$. On the affine chart $\ell_i(z)=1$, restriction to tangent vectors in $\ker\ell_i$ gives exactly $\phi$: the term containing $\ell_i$ vanishes on those tangent vectors. Thus these are a genuine free local frame for the horizontal bundle, including all jets, rather than only its fiber at the central point.

Express the prescribed form jet in that frame. Apply $S$ to each scalar coefficient, supported at the one point, and multiply its scalar polynomial by the corresponding $H_i(\phi)$. The degree is exactly $(2k-1)+1=2k$. At every other point its scalar factor belongs to the $k$th maximal-ideal power; multiplication by a regular form preserves that vanishing. Summing over all points gives the required right inverse.

The construction is independent of the temporary exterior basis: it is evaluation and multiplication of the corresponding identity tensor. The charts and their transverse spaces are transported by permutations of the specified frame vectors. Since $S$ is equivariant, the resulting horizontal right inverse is also equivariant.

For $m=4$, the validity inequality forces $r=0$. The scalar degree-$2k$ interpolation map from T062 applies directly, with no horizontal factor. For $k=1$, validity forces $r\le m-4$, exactly the nonexceptional range of T061's degree-two adjoint map. These two cases cover all endpoints excluded from the scalar regularity calculation.

The kernel remains the same ideal-sheaf section space as in T062. The flag projection and determinant pairing therefore give HE.2, with the unchanged jet representation FK.6–FK.11 and the unchanged parity twist. No equality of characters is substituted for this map argument.

## 4. Positive point deletion and complexity

The endpoint enumerator calls the same complete bounded-point routine with $a_0=2k$. For a nontrivial label its lowest numerator degree is at least $r+1$, so the available excess is at most $2k-1$. This is inside the previously proved $2k+1$ bound. The hook-plus-at-most-$k$-boxes argument still bounds the diagonal width by $k+1$.

For the invariant label, a nonzero correction forces $r\le k-1$, and the total degree is at most $3k-1$. Its coin and retained-subset enumeration is likewise within the earlier fixed-order bounds. The actual surjection proves that there are at least $d_{m,k,r}(\nu)$ complete points available for deletion.

The code selects those distinct complete points directly at the endpoint; it applies no parity transport. Each lies in a unique current cell. Replacing that cell by its first-differing-coordinate alternatives partitions its lattice points after removing exactly the selected point. Every replacement adds $2N_{\rm poly}-1$ cells. Thus the final number is exactly
$1+d(2N_{\rm poly}-1)$, including $d=0$.

The rational scalar right inverse is part of the proof of availability. The numerical evaluator and exported matrices do not construct that potentially large interpolation matrix. They use the already bounded LR correction and tableau/coin enumeration. Consequently the fixed-order construction and binary-degree bounds are inherited from T064 with smaller search ranges.

I checked the endpoint parameter validator, partition size, determinant conjugation, coefficient branch, direct base-point call, unique-owner deletion loop and full-range routing. The complete checker compares to independent standard-hook and jet traces and checks the literal exported cells; its saved receipt reports 5,366 coefficient/parity comparisons, 1,378 point-selection cases and 133 literal-polytope cases. Those are the author's executed checks, read here and not rerun.

## Audit classification

This is a complete independent proof/code reading plus a primary-source application check. It establishes the exact endpoint map and positive-cell construction. It is not an independent rerun of the saved finite certificate and does not claim a new scalar regularity theorem.


# A099. Odd-part occupancy and the actual canonical-map range

## Complete review

**PASS.** I read all of R049, OO.1–OO.25 and its six sections, both verification scripts, and the exact supporting passages TM.4, TM.8, TM.12, TM.14 and TM.16–TM.18 in R046. This is an independent whole-proof check of the map and its improved range. The author's finite sweeps are not rerun here.

The central conclusion is the actual isotypic surjectivity of $h_{n,a}$ for
$$
n\ge M(\nu)=\left\lfloor
\frac{|\nu|+\nu_1-\lceil(o-(\nu_1\bmod2))/3\rceil}{2}
\right\rfloor.
$$
The proof supplies the needed actual restriction map, its kernel injection, the faithful moment evaluation and the normalized canonical factorization. It does not infer a rank from matching numerical multiplicities.

## 1. The specified restriction and its kernel

The linear map $\widetilde q$ sends the first $s$ basis vectors to their counterparts and each extra basis vector to $\bar e_s$. Its sum on all $S$ basis vectors is $S\bar e_s$, so it sends $\bar e_S$ exactly to $\bar e_s$. It consequently sends $P_Se_i$ to $P_se_i$ for $i\le s$ and to zero for $i>s$. This is the orthogonal transpose of zero-padding on the mean-zero summands.

The decomposition $E_s=\mathbb Q\bar e_s\oplus W_s$ is specified by these vectors. Its exterior-algebra decomposition is natural for this very map, so the induced map on invariant exterior algebras is literally
$$
1_{\Lambda T}\otimes\Lambda(q\otimes1).
$$
The map is equivariant for the subgroup permuting the first $s$ rows, which is enough to take $S_S$-invariants to $S_s$-invariants.

The centered map is surjective: its row-power-sum generators go to the target generators with scalar one. Their generation follows either from the signed row-orbit proof of TM.8/TM.12 or from its explicit row inclusion–exclusion followed by the centering projection. Thus the uncentered map is also onto. There is consequently the actual injective map on kernels $v\mapsto1\otimes v$ used in OO.7.

The row-orbit decomposition is the symmetric or exterior power of each row type, according to its parity. Its unit factor fills the unused rows. For a fixed occupied tuple, the same $GL(T)$ module occurs at every row count at least its occupancy. Hence the difference of source and target characters is exactly the sum of the tuples that do not fit in $s$ rows. Since the specified map has already been proved onto, that difference is its actual kernel character. This proves the use of the omitted tuple modules without claiming that they are the coordinate subspaces of this particular kernel.

## 2. The alternating-weight bound

For a dominant rational weight $\alpha$, write
$A(\alpha)=\alpha_1-\alpha_2+\cdots+(-1)^{t-1}\alpha_t$.
The full paired-row decomposition of $\operatorname{Sym}(\Lambda^2T)$, independently checked in A094, has $A=0$.

In a row-orbit tuple, the singleton exterior factor is $\Lambda^{e_1}T$ with $e_1\le t$. Put $u=t-e_1$. The perfect exterior pairing gives the exact determinant-twisted duality
$$
\Lambda^{e_1}T=\det T\otimes\Lambda^uT^*.
$$
Every symmetric or exterior factor at a row degree $i\ge3$ embeds by its rational normalized projector into $(\Lambda^iT)^{\otimes e_i}$. No enlargement of a coefficient is assumed without this injection.

The determinant twist changes $A$ by $\epsilon=t\bmod2$. The dual exterior Pieri map removes a vertical $u$-strip, and each other exterior map adds a vertical $i$-strip. Each affected box changes the fixed alternating sum by $1$ or $-1$. Thus every resulting highest weight satisfies
$$
A(\gamma)\le\epsilon+u+\sum_{i\ge3}ie_i.
$$
The assertion remains valid for rational intermediate weights. Indeed dual exterior Pieri follows from
$\Lambda^uT^*=\det^{-1}T\otimes\Lambda^{t-u}T$; adding the complementary vertical strip and then subtracting the full determinant subtracts exactly one in the complementary $u$ rows. No positivity of the last intermediate coordinate is required.

The occupancy and degree identities give
$$
D+t-2k=u+\sum_{i\ge3}(i-2)e_i.
$$
Since $i\le3(i-2)$ for every $i\ge3$, the displayed bound implies
$A(\gamma)\le\epsilon+3(D+t-2k)$.

At $\gamma=\nu^{\mathsf t}$, $A(\gamma)$ is exactly the number $o$ of odd parts of $\nu$: each row contributes the alternating sum across its own boxes. Therefore
$$
k\le\left\lfloor\frac{D+t-q}{2}\right\rfloor,
\qquad q=\left\lceil\frac{o-\epsilon}{3}\right\rceil.
$$
The largest part contributes an odd part exactly when $t$ is odd. Removing that largest part also proves $0\le q\le o-\epsilon\le D-t$, so $M(\nu)\ge t$. This verifies every small and zero-improvement endpoint.

This contains R048's one-row improvements: in its equal-parity cases, $D+t$ is even and the required odd-part hypothesis gives $q\ge1$, lowering the floor by at least one.

## 3. Faithful evaluation and the exact canonical map

For $S\ge s\ge M(\nu)$, no omitted tuple in the actual uncentered kernel character contains $S_{\nu^{\mathsf t}}T$. The injection of centered kernels then proves zero kernel on that component. Surjectivity was already supplied by the row generators, so the same actual Schur map
$$
S_\nu(q):(S_\nu W_S)^{S_S}\longrightarrow(S_\nu W_s)^{S_s}
$$
is an isomorphism.

The ordinary and skew-Cauchy multiplicity maps are identical because the rational tensor Young projectors commute with tensor powers of $q$. With $S\ge\max(s,D)$, the full equality-partition triangular basis makes the ordinary moment evaluation $p_S$ an isomorphism in degree $D$. Its commutative relation with $q$ is scalar one on every generator. This proves precisely the componentwise isomorphism of $p_s$ used in OO.18.

The remaining factorization is the already checked literal map
$h_{a,n}|_\nu=p_n\Psi_nE_a$.
The Young column bound gives separate row degree at most $t$, so the highest-vector homogenization is polynomial at every $n\ge M(\nu)\ge t$. Independent-row polarization $E_a$ remains injective after normalizing the constant and mean coordinates. The split-moment substitution has diagonal coefficient
$(-1)^{d-1}(d-1)!/(n)_d$ in every generator degree $2\le d\le t$. Those denominators and coefficients are nonzero in this range, and its lower terms only use smaller-degree generators. It is the explicit triangular automorphism, with its recursive inverse.

Faithful $p_n$ therefore makes the opposite canonical map injective on the full highest multiplicity space. The scalar-one transpose identity gives the asserted surjectivity of $h_{n,a}$. Applying the same reasoning in both directions proves the isomorphism when $a,n\ge M(\nu)$. These statements are natural in the ambient vector space and extend over every characteristic-zero field through the rational maps.

## 4. The positive family and its full scalar

The wedge $dp_2\wedge\cdots\wedge dp_{r+2}$ has coefficient degree
$(r+1)(r+2)/2$ and form degree $r+1$. Euler contraction therefore has coefficient degree
$t_0=(r^2+3r+4)/2$, form degree $r$, and square-zero contraction makes it horizontal. Each $p_d$ is invariant under the row permutations, so the form is invariant.

Exterior Pieri has exactly the two displayed Schur summands in the polynomial-form domain. Contraction is nonzero on the highest vector of $S_{(t_0+1,1^{r-1})}$: the coefficient of
$x_1^{t_0+1}dx_2\wedge\cdots\wedge dx_r$ is nonzero. The other summand has no occurrence in the target. This identifies the whole kernel with $S_{(t_0,1^r)}$ by the actual contraction map, including $r=1$.

For the nonzero evaluation, set $a_0=r+2$ and use the centered consecutive coordinates in OO.24. The vector $x$ is
$\sum_{j<a_0}x_j(e_j-e_{a_0})$. On the listed $r$ arguments, all terms except $j=1$ repeat an exterior argument. The determinant is therefore exactly $x_1$ times the displayed derivative determinant.

Factoring the row constants gives $a_0!$. Factoring the column differences $x_j-x_{a_0}$ gives sign $(-1)^{a_0-1}$ times the missing Vandermonde factors. The remaining monic polynomials have successive degrees $0,\ldots,a_0-2$, hence determinant equal to the smaller Vandermonde. Finally $x_1=-(a_0-1)/2$ gives precisely
$$
(-1)^{a_0}\frac{a_0-1}{2}\,a_0!
\prod_{i<j}(x_j-x_i),
$$
with no scalar or sign omitted. The chosen arguments and coordinates remain in the centered subspace after adding zero rows, and the same value proves nonvanishing there.

Multiplication by $p_2^up_3^v$ preserves horizontality and the invariant action. Both factors are nonzero for $a\ge3$; the polynomial-form module is free over an integral domain, so their product with the form is nonzero. Evaluation on the auxiliary centered columns is the actual highest-vector map: a raising operation into the first column inserts the Euler vector, while a raising operation between later columns repeats an alternating argument. Both give zero. Homogenization then supplies the required target vector at every stated inner degree.

For the hook tail, $o=r+\epsilon$, so its threshold is exactly
$t+\lfloor(r-\lceil r/3\rceil)/2\rfloor$. Substituting $r=6s+2$ gives $t=18s^2+21s+7+2u+3v$ and threshold $t+2s$. The previous $t+3s+1$ threshold is larger by $s+1$. The example $(426,46,1^8)$ has total degree $480=10\cdot48$, the required first gap and a nonzero actual target vector.

# A100. The first pair correction for hook jets

## Scope and conclusion

**PASS.** I read the complete T066 report, PB.1–PB.15 and all five sections, its full positive evaluator and checker, and the saved receipt. I reread the exact-complex, normal-order, stabilizer and determinant passages FA.4, FA.6, FA.8–FA.9 and FA.13–FA.15 in G027. The proof has the required exact maps at the singleton and pair terms, and the stated last-map surjectivity follows from the already proved exact complex.

The conclusion is the complete valid boundary $a=2k-1$, $k\ge2$. It has the stated stable-hook multiplicity minus the jet multiplicity plus the horizontal-two-strip pair indicator. The difference between the latter two correction multiplicities is itself the multiplicity of an actual image representation, hence is nonnegative. This supports the explicit positive deletion construction.

## 1. Parameter range and concentration

Write $R=m-2$ and $\alpha=(a^{R-r},(a-1)^r)$. Then
$$
|\alpha|-mk=(m-4)k-(m-2)-r.
$$
The valid range PB.1 is exactly $|\alpha|\ge mk$, the degree range of FA.4 and the first-gap condition on the original partition. The other parts are ordered, nonnegative, and sum to $m(k-1+t)$. The formal $m=4$ range is empty, as its upper leg bound is negative. The omitted $k=1,a=1$ endpoint has no valid partition.

Taking the $S_\alpha F$ multiplicity is exact over $\mathbb Q$, since these finite polynomial representation spaces are completely reducible. It preserves the actual signed restriction differential and the subset orientations.

At a selected subset of size $q$, the residual space has dimension $d=R-q+1$. A nonzero semistandard skew character $S_{\alpha/\rho}\mathbb Q^d$ requires
$\rho_i\ge\alpha_{i+d}$ for $1\le i\le q-1$. To check this directly, a column present in row $i+d$ of $\alpha$ but absent from row $i$ of $\rho$ remains in every skew row $i,\ldots,i+d$, giving $d+1$ boxes in that column. This is impossible with only $d$ entries.

The normal degree is bounded above by $q(k-1)$. Its necessary lower bound is
$(q-1)(a-1)=2(q-1)(k-1)$, which is strictly larger for $q\ge3$ because $k\ge2$. Thus all terms after the pair term vanish. Terms with still larger subsets have already vanished in the original degree-$|\alpha|$ complex. This proves actual concentration rather than an alternating-character simplification.

## 2. Ambient and singleton comparisons

The full exterior-column complement in the width-$a$ rectangle of height $\dim E=m-1$ sends the padded $\alpha$ to $(a,1^r)$ and gives
$S_\alpha E=\det(E)^a\otimes S_{(a,1^r)}E^*$.
The invariant rational form identifies the dual standard module with the standard module. Tensoring the complex by the determinant factor removes the exponent $a$ and leaves precisely the common determinant exponent $t$ on the original balanced module.

At a singleton, complementary pairing in height $R$ changes the residual horizontal-strip rule into multiplication of $(1^r)$ by a row of length $u$. Every resulting first part is at most $u+1\le k\le a$, so none is lost outside the rectangle. This proves the whole module identity
$$
S_{\alpha/(u)}W
=\det(W)^a\otimes
  \bigl(\operatorname{Sym}^uW^*\otimes\Lambda^rW^*\bigr)
$$
for $0\le u<k$, including $u=0$, $r=0$ and $r=R$. At the top leg, the determinant factors reduce to the same identity, so there is no hidden missing constituent.

The comparison with the actual jet map is specified by FA.8. Its substitution
$Y_{0a}\mapsto-\sum_jx_jY_{ja}$ preserves the least normal degree: over the fraction field of the generic complementary matrix it is an invertible linear substitution. Hence its degree-$u$ coefficient map is injective on the relevant Schur multiplicity.

The preceding complementary Pieri identity identifies the dimension of that source with the full degree-$u$ horizontal-form jet space. Thus this particular coefficient map is an isomorphism. The exterior pairing is a bundle isomorphism, and the local horizontal frames from HJ.7 are honest frames on the whole affine chart. The comparison of truncated jets is consequently filtered triangular with invertible diagonal blocks; finite triangular elimination gives its inverse. This proves that the singleton differential is the original hook jet evaluation, not merely a map between representations having the same character.

After the common determinant twist is removed, the singleton term is exactly the induction in PB.11. Its positive multiplicity is the previously verified monomial-orbit/exterior/LR formula FK.11.

## 3. The pair term and its determinant signs

At $r=0$, the pair residual dimension requires $\rho_1\ge a=2k-1$, beyond the maximum normal degree $2k-2$. There is no pair term.

At $r\ge1$, the necessary lower bound is $\rho_1\ge a-1=2k-2$. Consequently both normal slots must have their maximum degree $k-1$, and their only surviving normal shape is the single row $(2k-2)$. The Cartan projection is ordinary multiplication of the two symmetric powers. Its inverse on that summand is the bidegree polarization divided by $\binom{2k-2}{k-1}$. This scalar is nonzero over $\mathbb Q$. Slot interchange is therefore the trivial action on this summand.

For the residual Pieri factor, dimension forces the bottom row of $\alpha$ to be removed in full. It already contains all $2k-2$ normal boxes, so every other row remains unchanged. The residual partition is precisely
$(a^{R-r},(a-1)^{r-1})$.
Its rectangle complement is $(1^{r-1})$, giving the exact determinant-twisted exterior module on $\mathfrak h_{m-2}$.

The pair orientation contributes $\operatorname{sgn}_{S_2}$. The global determinant factor contributes $\operatorname{sgn}_{S_2}^{a+t}\operatorname{sgn}_{S_{m-2}}^{a+t}$, and the residual determinant contributes $\operatorname{sgn}_{S_{m-2}}^a$. Since $a$ is odd, both resulting exponents are $t$ modulo two. Removing the same common twist leaves
$$
\operatorname{Ind}_{S_2\times S_{m-2}}^{S_m}
\bigl(\mathbf1\otimes\Lambda^{r-1}\mathfrak h_{m-2}\bigr).
$$
This verifies the trivial $S_2$ action, including the orientation; using only the normal multiplication without that orientation would not establish it.

The standard exterior power is the hook $(m-r-1,1^{r-1})$. Frobenius induction with the trivial $S_2$ factor is multiplication by $h_2$, so its multiplicity is precisely the horizontal-two-strip indicator in PB.3. At $r=R$, its complementary exterior power is the top standard exterior power and the same hook becomes the sign partition of $m-2$, as required.

## 4. Exactness, image multiplicity and positive cells

The original exact restriction complex and the preceding actual comparisons give PB.15 with left term $\operatorname{sgn}^t$ times the balanced module. One can also check that twist directly: the original kernel is $\operatorname{sgn}^{a+t}$ times the balanced module, and making the ambient module the untwisted stable hook tensors everything by $\operatorname{sgn}^a$.

The last differential remains signed polynomial restriction, followed by the stated Cartan and exterior identifications. Since the next complex term is zero, it is surjective. Its kernel, the image of the original hook jet map, has multiplicity $d-e$. Therefore $0\le d-e\le d\le D_k$, and the first kernel has multiplicity $c_{\rm stable}-d+e$.

For a positive correction, the label occurs in the jet term. The diagonal-width and invariant-label leg bounds from T064 therefore apply without change. At $a=2k-1$, the nonrow excess is at most $2k-2$, and the invariant total degree is at most $3k-2$. Both are smaller than the earlier proved bounded enumeration ranges.

Exactness proves that enough complete stable-hook points exist to remove $d-e$ of them. The bounded enumerator lists such points directly at the endpoint; no translation in degree is used. The first-differing-coordinate partition of the unique owner cell removes exactly one selected lattice point. All pieces retain the original bounded constraints, and each deletion increases the number of tags by $2N_{\rm poly}-1$. This verifies the count, disjointness and variable bound in PB.5.

The evaluator implements these exact branches: the valid parameter test, determinant conjugation, jet multiplicity, one horizontal-two-strip LR test, direct bounded point enumeration, unique-owner deletion and routing to the higher endpoints. Its runtime does not construct the restriction matrices. The earlier fixed-order bit bounds therefore apply with the stated smaller budgets.
